《大美晚报》、《中美日报》、《国民新闻》、
《新闻报》：

美国律师提出改善工部局
行政管理的建议

据外籍人士方面消息，一位知名美国律师昨日向记者发表如下声明：
“我将向将于4月17日开始履职的新任工部局董事提出建议。这些建议是根据工部局目前的财务状况和本地现有政治局势提出的。我希望尽早公开这些建议，并在适当时机提交给工部局。
“我的建议如下：
(1) 工部局的支出应以在上海流通的货币为基础。
(2) 应禁止投机、操纵、囤积和其他不当行为，以保护租界居民的生计。
(3) 应对动产和不动产征税。
(4) 工部局的所有决定和方案应予以公开。
(5) 工部局职员的津贴不应由董事会直接负责。
(6) 应废除提篮桥监狱，并将所有囚犯驱逐出租界。（关于这一点，尚未仔细考虑，也未决定是否将其提交董事会审议。）”

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
APR 1 2 1940

Five Economy Resolutions For
New Council Mapped Out

A recommendation that S.M.C. employee pension funds be taken out of the general municipal treasury and allocated with American and British insurance firms will be made to the incoming Council shortly after it takes office on April 17, a prominent American lawyer informed THE CHINA PRESS yesterday.

Asking that his name be kept out of print for the present, the lawyer said he had a list of five recommendations and was working on a sixth which he would submit simultaneously in an attempt to bring about some re-orientation of municipal affairs in view of the present financial and political situation.

Besides segregation of pension funds, the proposals will recommend payment of S.M.C. pensions in local dollars, passage of a non-profiteering ordinance to protect local residents, taxation of all real property unoccupied as well as occupied, and greater publicity to the Council's deliberations and decisions. The sixth recommendation which has not been fully worked out will ask that Ward Road Jail be abolished and its prisoners banned from the Settlement.

Security Guaranteed

The first recommendation advocating separation of the superannuation fund now lumped with the general S.M.C. monies, will be made with a view to the future security of the pensions. Were the municipal government to go bankrupt at any time under the present system the pensions of all employees would be wiped out. To avoid such an eventuality the five per cent of his salary paid into the superannuation fund by each employee and the 10 per cent added by the S.M.C. should be deposited each month with a large insurance company which would not be affected by financial collapse of the municipality, the lawyer pointed out.

Group insurance for all S.M.C. employees will be asked in order that the heirs of men who die or are killed on duty may receive full policy value instead of the non-statutory six months pay which is usually awarded by the S.M.C.

Local Currency

— It will further be advocated that all future S.M.C. employment contracts be made in local currency to be supplemented during periods of abnormal exchange by a cost of living allowance.

The lawyer will also propose that each employee be permitted to designate the currency in which his superannuation fund is to be kept under the proposed scheme. When payment is made in Shanghai currency to the insurance company each month it can thus be exchanged into the designated foreign currency at the prevailing rate, he explained.

The second recommendation will ask that all pensions due to former employees of the S.M.C. be paid in local dollars, subject to actual contractual obligations of the municipality.

Rage Profiteering

Recommendation No. 3 will advocate that the S.M.C. immediately pass a non-profiteering ordinance to protect foreign and Chinese residents earning small salaries from unfair increases in rent, food and other necessary commodities. The lawyer pointed out yesterday that the French Concession already has such an ordinance and that a similar one here would make it possible for the two municipalities to co-operate.

On the subject of rent profiteering he foresaw an S.M.C. Housing Committee to license every dwelling in the Settlement and fix the rent on it.

The fourth recommendation of the list reads: That all real property in the International Settlement be taxed including unoccupied property." Commenting, the lawyer stated that Shanghai is the only city in the world where property is only taxed when occupied.

Publicity Demanded

Finally the proposal will be made that all important matters and decisions by the S.M.C. be made public and that the individual vote of the councillors on these important issues be made public. This recommendation asks that if councillors disagree with the majority the dissenting opinions be made in writing and published for the information of the ratepayers and the general public.

"There is no reason for secrecy," the lawyer told THE CHINA PRESS. "The ratepayers will be better able to understand and appreciate the decisions of the S.M.C. in important matters and know if they are told about it."

The sixth recommendation concerning the doing away with Ward Road Jail which was described as costing the Settlement more than $600,000 a year, has not been defined yet.

《字林西报》。
1940年4月12日

为新工部局董事会规划的五项节约决议

一位知名美国律师昨日向《字林西报》透露，即将于4月17日就职的新任董事会不久后将收到一项建议，即把上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）雇员的养老基金从市政总库中分离出来，交由美国和英国的保险公司管理。

这位律师要求暂时不公开其姓名，他表示自己有一份包含五项建议的清单，并正在拟定第六项建议，将一并提交，试图鉴于当前的财政和政治局势，促使市政事务进行某种重新定位。

除了分离养老基金外，这些提案还将建议以本地货币支付工部局养老金，通过一项反暴利条例以保护当地居民，对所有空置及已占用的房地产征税，并加强对董事会审议过程和决策的宣传。尚未完全拟定的第六项建议将要求废除华德路监狱，并禁止其囚犯进入租界。

保障安全

第一项建议主张将目前与工部局一般资金混同的退休基金分离出来，其目的是为了确保未来养老金的安全。律师指出，在现行制度下，如果市政府在任何时候破产，所有雇员的养老金都将化为乌有。为避免这种意外情况，每位雇员存入退休基金的薪水的百分之五，以及工部局追加的百分之十，每月应存入一家大型保险公司，这样就不会受到市政财政崩溃的影响。

还将要求为所有工部局雇员办理团体保险，以便在执行公务中死亡或遇害者的遗属能够获得全额保单价值，而不是通常由工部局发放的非法定六个月薪水。

本地货币

——此外还将主张，今后所有的工部局雇佣合同均以本地货币订立，并在汇率异常期间辅以生活津贴。

该律师还将提议，允许每位雇员指定其退休基金在拟议方案下以何种货币存放。他解释说，每月向保险公司支付上海货币时，可以按现行汇率兑换成指定的外币。

第二项建议将要求，根据市政府的实际合同义务，以本地美元支付欠前工部局雇员的所有养老金。

遏制暴利

第三项建议将主张工部局立即通过一项反暴利条例，以保护赚取微薄薪水的外国和中国居民免受租金、食品和其他必需品的不公平上涨的影响。该律师昨日指出，法租界已有此类条例，在此实行类似的条例将使两个市政当局能够进行合作。

关于租金暴利问题，他预见工部局将设立一个住房委员会，对租界内的每一处住所颁发许可证并核定租金。

清单上的第四项建议写道：“对国际租界内的所有房地产征税，包括空置房产。”对此，该律师评论说，上海是世界上唯一一个仅在房产被占用时才征税的城市。

要求公开

最后，将提出一项建议，要求公开工部局的所有重要事项和决定，并公开董事在这些重要问题上的个人投票情况。这项建议要求，如果董事不同意多数意见，应将异议写成书面形式并予以公布，以供纳税人和公众知晓。

“没有理由保密，”该律师告诉《字林西报》。“如果告知纳税人，他们将能够更好地理解和欣赏工部局在重要事项上的决定，并了解这些决定。”

关于废除华德路监狱的第六项建议据称每年使租界花费超过60万美元，目前尚未明确界定。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. S. No. D. 7834

OUTCOME OF MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS

Commenting on the outcome of the recent Municipal
elections the "Rus" writes:-

"Thus all preliminary calculations made by the various
groups have been upset. Each group has secured a greater num-
ber of votes than it was expected. Now that the excitement cre-
ated by the election campaign has died away, the voice of com-
mon sense and prudence is audible in the local foreign press.
Comments of various foreign newspapers and, particularly, of the
"Evening Post", deserve full attention.

Stressing, in a series of articles, the fact that the
struggle was conducted not against any individual candidates,
but for certain principles, namely: preservation of the status
quo ( Anglo-American group ) and revision of the present status
of the Municipal Council ( Japanese group )- foreign press now
recognize the correctness of the Japanese slogans.

The time is ripe for a revision of the status of the
Municipal Council. The new Council is obliged to carry out this
revision in a painless manner during the course of the current
year in order to extend the international basis of the Settle-
ment.

Foreign press are now of the opinion that representa-
tives of the three main powers in the Council, i.e. Japanese,
British and American, should discuss in a friendly manner the
possibility of a change in the system of national representa-
tion, taking into consideration the increase of the Japanese
community and the interests of the population.

The press admit that full consideration should be gi-
ven to the suggestions made by the Japanese regarding natio-
nal representation in the Council and that certain changes
should be carried out in accordance with these suggestions.

This moral victory of the Japanese group is, perhaps,

上海公共租界警务处
档案号 S. S. No. D. 7834
日期 1940年4月18日

市政选举结果

《罗斯》报在评论最近的市政选举结果时写道：

“因此，各团体所做的所有初步计算均被打乱。每个团体获得的选票都比预期的要多。现在，由竞选活动引起的激动情绪已经平息，在当地外文报刊中可以听到常识和谨慎的声音。各种外文报纸，特别是《晚邮报》（Evening Post）的评论，值得充分关注。

外文报刊在一系列文章中强调，斗争并非针对任何个别候选人，而是为了某些原则，即：维持现状（英美集团）和修改工部局董事会的现有地位（日本集团）——现在外文报刊承认日本口号的正确性。

修改工部局董事会地位的时机已经成熟。新董事会有义务在本年度内以无痛的方式执行这一修改，以扩大租界的国际基础。

外文报刊现在认为，董事会中三个主要大国的代表，即日本、英国和美国代表，应当友好地讨论改变国籍代表制的可能性，同时考虑到日本侨民数量的增加和民众的利益。

报刊承认，应充分考虑日本方面关于董事会中国籍代表的建议，并根据这些建议进行某些变更。

日本集团的这一道德胜利，或许

There is no doubt that the present status of the Mu-

比并未给现有局势带来任何变化的选举结果更为重要。

毫无疑问，如果事态发展和战争影响不改变上海目前的民族平衡，工部局董事会的现有地位将在本年度内得到修改。

随后是一段针对《今日新闻》（Novosti Dnia）的猛烈抨击，该报被指控在‘总体上以正确方式进行的’选举运动中引入了‘肮脏手段’。

“利用《今日新闻》开展选举运动的外国团体现在应该感到羞愧。不用说，Chilikin先生及其同伙的全部工作引起了普遍的厌恶”

据《罗斯》报称，Chilikin的报纸多年来一直从事抹黑俄罗斯移民社区的运动，试图证明俄罗斯移民是一群毫无价值的人。然而，在最近的选举运动中，《今日新闻》改变了其惯常策略，仔细收集所有论据，以证明俄罗斯社区在上海发挥的巨大作用、其稳健的经济地位和文化影响力。

“关于《今日新闻》对日本的猛烈抨击，我们认为日本人会在他们认为合适的时候给出适当的回应”。

《罗斯》报在文章结尾重申了对《今日新闻》的指控，称该报由共产国际指挥，并陈述道：

SHANGHAI TIMES.
MAR 25 1940
（批：D. 7834 / 15 4 140）

Japanese Given Change
In Election Procedure
For Ballot This Year

Six Out Of Seven Requests Made To Council Are
Virtually Conceded; Scrutineers For Each
Booth Will Include One Nippon Official

REQUEST FOR EXTENSION OF VOTING TIME
NOT GRANTED; “COACHES” PERMITTED

Possibly forecasting something in the nature of a real lively election for Shanghai Municipal Councillors this year is the report appearing in the Shanghai "Mainichi," stating that several requests by Japanese ratepayers have been acceded to by the S.M.C., through Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner-General. Requests reported to have been granted by the S.M.C. include Japanese scrutineers at each polling booth; Japanese "coaches" to be permitted at each poll; Japanese ratepayers to be permitted to sign ballot papers in Japanese, and the names of Japanese candidates to be printed on ballot papers in Japanese.

One request, that the voting hours be extended, was not granted, according to the same source of information.

Efforts to confirm this report through Council sources yesterday proved fruitless, but it is generally understood that certain changes in election procedure for the ballot on April 10 and 11 have been agreed to by officials of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

Japanese Enigma

Although the Japanese have not yet indicated whether there will be an attempt on their part to increase Japanese representation on the Council during the coming Municipal year, there is a belief existing that additional representation will be sought in view of the increased number of Japanese residing within the jurisdiction of the S.M.C. No names of Japanese candidates for election have yet been announced, but in view of the requests for increased Japanese supervision of the ballot, it is taken for granted that something in the nature of an attempt to secure a third seat will be made next month.

In certain well-informed circles it is understood that the present ratio and "gentlemen's agreement" of five British, two American, two Japanese and five Chinese members may be upset at the forthcoming elections. There is not expected to be any alteration in the number of Chinese Councillors. As the result of the straw vote among the British community, the five candidates for election have been selected. The outcome of the straw vote among the American community is still awaited. Three candidates have been nominated for this vote, two of whom will be selected for the American quota on the Council. The question naturally has arisen whether the Japanese community intend to nominate more than their two customary candidates. If so, there will be the necessity for an election and, hence, the anxiety on the part of Japanese ratepayers to have scrutineers and "coaches" at the various polling booths.

"Mainichi" Report

The following report regarding change in election procedure appears in the Shanghai "Mainichi":

Six out of seven requests to facilitate voting by Japanese ratepayers at the forthcoming elections for councillors were acceded to by the Shanghai Municipal Council, the Shanghai "Mainichi" said in a featured report yesterday.

The requests were, the newspaper said, that:

1.—One of the two members of the election committee at each poll should be a Japanese because of the increase in the Japanese vote;
2.—One of the two scrutineers at each poll should be a Japanese;
3.—Japanese "coaches" be present at each poll to give necessary information regarding voting procedure to Japanese ratepayers who are not familiar with S.M.C. rules;
4.—Election forms of Japanese ratepayers, who cannot be easily located be sent to the Japanese Residents' Corporation in bulk for delivery;
5.—Voting hours be extended;
6.—Ratepayers be allowed to sign in Japanese.
7.—The names of Japanese candidates be written in Japanese on the voting forms.

Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, in an interview with Mr. Yuzo Hayashi, chairman of the Amalgamated Federation of Japanese Street Unions, on Tuesday, the "Mainichi" continued, agreed to requests 3, 6, and 7.

A "virtual agreement" on the remaining points, with the exception of request 5, was reached on Wednesday when Mr. Yochiaki Miura, Japanese Consul-General, conferred with Mr. C. S. Franklin, chairman of the Council, according to the daily.

《上海泰晤士报》。
1940年3月25日
（批注：D. 7834 / 15 4 140）

日本人在今年投票选举程序方面获得变更

向工部局提出的七项请求中有六项实际上已获准许；每个投票站将包括一名日本官员作为监票员

延长投票时间的请求未获批准；允许“指导人员”在场

据上海《每日新闻》报道，工部局秘书兼总办 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生已同意日本纳税人提出的几项请求，这或许预示着今年上海公共租界工部局董事的选举将出现某种真正激烈的竞争局面。据报道，工部局已批准的请求包括：在每个投票站设置日本监票员；允许日本“指导人员”在每个投票站在场；允许日本纳税人在选票上用日文签名，以及选票上日本候选人的姓名用日文印刷。

据同一消息来源称，有一项要求延长投票时间的请求未获批准。

昨日试图通过工部局方面证实这一报道的努力未果，但人们普遍了解到，工部局官员已同意对4月10日和11日的投票选举程序进行某些更改。

日本之谜

尽管日本人尚未表明是否会在即将到来的市政年度中试图增加其在工部局的代表人数，但有一种看法认为，鉴于居住在工部局管辖范围内的日本人数量增加，他们将寻求增加代表名额。目前尚未公布任何日本候选人的名字，但鉴于其要求加强对投票的日本监督，可以想见，下个月将会出现某种性质的尝试，以争取第三个席位。

在某些消息灵通的圈子里，人们了解到，目前的比例和“君子协定”——即五名英国人、两名美国人、两名日本人和五名中国人——可能会在即将到来的选举中被打破。预计中国董事的人数不会有任何改变。由于英国侨民社区进行了意向性投票，五名当选候选人已经选出。美国侨民社区的意向性投票结果仍有待揭晓。此次投票提名了三名候选人，其中两人将被选中填补工部局中的美国人名额。自然产生的问题是，日本社区是否打算提名超过其惯常的两名候选人。如果是这样，就有必要进行选举，因此日本纳税人急于在各个投票站安排监票员和“指导人员”。

《每日新闻》的报道

关于选举程序变更的以下报道出现在上海《每日新闻》上：

上海《每日新闻》昨日在一篇专题报道中称，上海公共租界工部局已同意了七项旨在便利日本纳税人在即将举行的董事选举中投票的请求中的六项。

该报称，这些请求是：

1.—鉴于日本选票的增加，每个投票站的选举委员会两名成员中应有一名日本人；
2.—每个投票站的两名监票员中应有一名日本人；
3.—在每个投票站安排日本“指导人员”，为不熟悉工部局规则的日本纳税人提供有关投票程序的必要信息；
4.—难以轻易找到的日本纳税人的选举表格，应批量发送至日本居留民团以便分发；
5.—延长投票时间；
6.—允许纳税人用日文签名。
7.—选票上的日本候选人姓名应用日文书写。

《每日新闻》继续报道，周二，G. Godfrey Phillips 先生在接受日本街道联合会主席林勇三（Yuzo Hayashi）先生采访时，同意了第3、6和7项请求。

据该日报称，周三，当日本总领事三浦义明（Yochiaki Miura）先生与工部局主席 C. S. Franklin 先生会晤时，除第5项请求外，就其余各点达成了“实际协议”。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. I. M. C. LIBRARY
No. S. B. D. 7834
Date 15 / 4 / 40

China Evening News published the following comment on April 6:-

AMBITION

The newspapers have told us that the municipal elections of the S.M.C. have come to a critical stage. The competition in the elections has drawn the attention of the general public in Shanghai and clearly shows the ambition of a certain party to seize the police rights of the International Settlement.

Up to the present, nobody can foretell the result of the competition. A united movement has now been formed against the ambition of a certain party. Speaking frankly, it is desired to consolidate the united front of Britain and America and to combat the mean attempt to seize the power of the S.M.C.

The Chinese residents can do nothing about the municipal elections. The competition reveals the ambition or aggression of a certain party. No doubt, the elections have some connection with the Far Eastern policy of Britain and America. So, no matter what consequences the municipal elections may have, the British and American authorities should intensify their support to China in her war of resistance.

When the real face of the so-called establishment of a new order in East Asia is disclosed, the word ambition will at once be exposed.

上海公共租界工部局
S. I. M. C. 图书馆
编号 S. B. D. 7834
日期 1940年4月15日

《中国晚报》于4月6日发表了以下评论：-

野心

报纸告诉我们，工部局的市政选举已进入关键阶段。选举中的竞争引起了上海公众的关注，清楚地显示了某一方企图夺取国际租界警务权的野心。

到目前为止，无人能预测竞争的结果。目前已形成一场联合运动，以反对某一方的野心。坦率地说，人们希望巩固英美统一战线，并对夺取工部局权力的卑鄙企图进行斗争。

中国居民对市政选举无能为力。这场竞争揭示了某一方的野心或侵略性。毫无疑问，选举与英美在远东的政策有一定联系。因此，无论市政选举产生何种后果，英美当局都应加强对中国抗战的支持。

当所谓建立东亚新秩序的真面目被揭露时，“野心”一词将立即暴露无遗。

page_data.en:
APP 1 3. 1940

NIPPON PRESS
DISAPPOINTED
ON POLL COUNT

LOSING CANDIDATES
TAKE UP CALM
ATTITUDE

Hardened observers are of the
opinion that things in Hongkew will
tighten up as a reaction over the
outcome of the Municipal Election.
Although the Japanese press has
been disappointed and has gone so
far as to state that the sacredness
of elections and principles of demo-
cracy have been violated by the
S.M.C. Revenue Office and the Bri-
tish Election Committee, this is not
the consensus of opinion in Japan-
ese business circles. On the con-
trary, like good sportsmen, they
have congratulated the winners and
have decided to let the matter rest.

Japanese Paper's Charges

Various charges have been hurled
at the Council by the Tairiku
Shimpo over the handling of the
election. The paper stated that
over 2,000 additional British votes
had been brought into play by the
co-operation of the Revenue Office
and the British Election Committee;
that obstructions had been put in
the way of Japanese seeking to
vote; that the method of voting
worked against the Japanese and
that foreign voters had been admit-
ted to the polling booths at the
S.V.C. Drill Hall after three o'clock.
Such charges hold no ground what-
soever as Japanese coaches with
yellow arm-bands were prominent
at both polling stations.

Hayashi's Views

However, the Japanese are more
determined than ever, for, according
to Mr. Y. Hayashi, President
of the Japanese Residents' Corpora-
tion, preparations are now under
way to obtain a landslide in next
year's election.

"It is to be regretted that the
results of the election fall short of
our expectations in spite of our solid
unity and I, as the chairman of the
Election Committee, lack words to
apologise for this the Japanese
residents. The irrationalities of
the present election system and the
question of whether the elections
were fairly conducted would require
study. However, I believe that ap-
propriate steps should be taken for
their study and reform" stated Mr.
Hayashi.

He concluded by saying: "We
Japanese shall not complain over
the results of the election now that
the struggle is over. Our aims to-
wards the International Settlement
are to internationalise it on the
basis of friendly relations and co-
operation among various communi-
ties, busting the monopolisation of
the Settlement's administration by
one national group so as to make
Shanghai an ideal international
city."
page_data.zh:
附件 1 1940年3月

《日本新闻》
对计票结果
感到失望

落选候选人
采取冷静
态度

经验丰富的观察家认为，虹口地区的局势将因市政选举结果而出现紧张反应。尽管日本媒体感到失望，甚至声称工部局财务处和英国选举委员会违反了选举的神圣性和民主原则，但这并非日本商界的普遍意见。相反，他们像优秀的运动员一样，祝贺获胜者，并决定让此事就此作罢。

日本报纸的指控

《大陆新报》就选举处理方式向工部局提出了各种指控。该报称，在财务处和英国选举委员会的合作下，额外引入了2,000多张英国选票；日本人的投票受到阻碍；投票方法对日本人不利；下午三点后，外国选民被允许进入工部局义勇队大厅的投票站。这些指控毫无根据，因为佩戴黄色臂章的日本指导人员在两个投票站都非常显眼。

林氏的观点

然而，日本人比以往任何时候都更加坚定，因为据日本居留民团总裁 Y. Hayashi（林氏）称，目前正着手准备在明年的选举中获得压倒性胜利。

“令人遗憾的是，尽管我们团结一致，但选举结果仍未达到我们的预期，我作为选举委员会主席，无言以对日本居民表示歉意。现行选举制度的不合理之处以及选举是否公平进行的问题需要研究。然而，我认为应采取适当措施对其进行研究和改革，”林氏表示。

他最后说：“既然斗争已经结束，我们日本人不会对选举结果抱怨。我们对国际租界的目标是在各社区友好关系和合作的基础上使其国际化，打破单一民族群体对租界行政管理的垄断，使上海成为理想的国际城市。”

April 14, 1940.
Morning Translation.

MAINICHI :-

BRITISH CAST VOTES AFTER CLOSURE OF POLLING BOOTH.

The result of the recent election of
the Municipal Council was against the expectation of
the 70,000 local Japanese residents, the 5.2.2 ratio
for Britain, America and Japan being retained.
Prior to the election, the number of votes enjoyed by
Japanese residents was expected to be from 3,700 to 3,800
while the votes of the British and Americans would be from
3,500 to 3,600. However, the great increase of votes
cast by Britons, which was disclosed after the election,
astonished Japanese residents. Behind the increase of
the British votes there was a cunning method employed by
British residents. From late at night on April 10 to
the early morning of April 11 Mr. Middleton, Chairman of
the Municipal Election Committee, is said to have
created votes amounting to ,000 which were cast on
April 11. Further Mr. L□□ne, Chairman of the British
Election Committee, visited a polling booth shortly
before the closure on April 10 in company with some
13 British people, each of whom possessed votes ranging
from 100 to 200, and these notes are said to have been
cast up till 7.30 p.m.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月14日。
晨间译文。

《每日新闻》：-

英国人在投票站关闭后投票。

最近工部局选举的结果出乎当地7万日本居民的意料，英、美、日 5:2:2 的比例得以保留。选举前，预计日本居民的票数将在3,700至3,800票之间，而英美选民的票数将在3,500至3,600票之间。然而，选举后披露的英国人选票的大幅增加令日本居民感到震惊。在英国选票增加的背后，是英国居民采用的一种狡猾手段。据说，从4月10日深夜到4月11日凌晨，市政选举委员会主席米德尔顿（Middleton）先生制造了多达 ,000 张选票，并于4月11日投出。此外，英国选举委员会主席 L□□ne 先生在4月10日投票结束前不久，与大约13名英国人一起访问了一个投票站，每人拥有100至200不等的选票，据说这些选票一直投到晚上7点30分。

page_data.en:
April 13, 1940.
Morning Translation.

MAINICHI :-

BRITISH CREATE SEVERAL THOUSAND VOTES IN
ONE NIGHT BY CHANGING CHINESE PROPERTY TO
BRITISH NAMES.

A heated struggle was staged in
the recent election of the Municipal Council between the
Japanese on one side and the British and Americans on
the other. The result of the election shows a great
gap between the number of Japanese votes and those of the
British and Americans, although the number of votes
enjoyed by Japanese residents and those of the British
and Americans were expected to be almost the same. The
British residents employed a cunning method to bring such
a result in order to maintain the status quo.
They arranged impartial equipment
in the polling booths but, immediately prior to the
election days, they temporarily transferred houses and
other immovable estate owned by Chinese to foreigners'
names, thus securing a large number of votes. By
employing such a method some 150 votes were cast by one
person representing various corporations. For instance,
Mr. V. H. Bourne, who is claimed to be an ex-employee of
the Municipal Council, cast some 1,000 votes alone at
3 p.m. on April 10. Such a cunning method on the part
of the British residents has aroused great indignation.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月13日。
晨间译文。

《每日新闻》：-

英国人一夜之间通过将中国房产改为英国人名义制造数千张选票。

在最近举行的工部局选举中，一方是日本，另一方是英美，双方展开了激烈的斗争。选举结果显示，日本选票数量与英美选票数量之间存在巨大差距，尽管此前预计日本居民享有的选票数量与英美选民的选票数量几乎相同。英国居民为了维持现状，采用了一种狡猾的手段来造成这种结果。
他们在投票站安排了看似公正的设备，但在选举日前夕，他们将中国人拥有的房屋和其他不动产暂时转移到外国人名下，从而获得了大量选票。通过采用这种方法，代表各个公司的一人投出了约150张选票。例如，据称曾是工部局雇员的 V. H. Bourne 先生，仅在4月10日下午3点就独自投出了约1,000张选票。英国居民的这种狡猾手段引起了极大的愤慨。

N. F. ALLMAN CHOSEN

Primary Election Among

With the nomination of Mr. N.

特别分部登记处
编号：S. B. D. 7834
日期：1946年5月15日

1946年

N. F. 奥尔曼被选为
增补候选人

为选出工部局董事
需在美国人中举行初选

随着美国协会昨日提名著名美国律师 N. F. 奥尔曼先生，在沪美国人有必要举行初选投票，以选出今年上海工部局的候选人。美国协会委员会已为上海工部局的两个席位选定的两位候选人是前董事 J. W. 卡尼先生和现任董事 R. T. 麦克唐纳先生。

目前尚无迹象表明是否会有其他名字被列入将于下周举行的初选名单。根据该协会的附则，工部局候选人必须由十名美国纳税人提名，但从对奥尔曼先生提名的响应来看，签署该提名表的人数可能在80至100人之间。

协会全体委员会在遴选首批两名候选人时，充当了市政选举小组委员会的角色。标准真空石油公司助理经理卡尼先生去年从工部局辞职，经劝说后决定作为候选人参加即将到来的选举。

麦克唐纳先生是威廉·亨特公司（William Hunt and Company）总经理，在卡尼先生辞职后被增补进入工部局。

CHINA PRESS.
MAR 8 1940
Three Candidates
Americans To
Vote Soon For
SMC Nominees
The name of Mr. N. F. Allman
was added to the list of candidates
for posts on the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council yesterday, making it
necessary for Americans here to
hold a primary election soon to
choose two of a group of three
nominees proposed by the American
Association.
The other two candidates are
Mr. R. T. McDonnell, present Coun-
cillor, and Mr. J. W. Carney, former
Councillor.
Until yesterday, it was not be-
lieved likely that a primary ballot
would have to be held, since only
two nominees had been put for-
ward. However, with the nomina-
tion of Mr. Allman, it was believed
possible that the American com-
munity may witness a primary
election campaign between more
than the three who are already
candidates. Nominations for the
primary ballot need the signatures
of 10 American ratepayers. Dead-
line for nominations is Monday,
when all petitions must reach the
secretary of the American Associa-
tion, Mr. James M. Howe.
Events in the last week have
provided a drastic change in the
list of nominations put up by
Americans for the S.M.C. Mr.
Cornell S. Franklin, present chair-
man of the Council, was expected
to stand for re-election until he
disclosed last week that he would
not be a candidate in the elections
this year. Mr. J. W. Carney was
then put forward, and until yes-
terday, only he and Mr. McDonnell
were expected to run for the posts.

《字林西报》
1940年3月8日
三名候选人
美国人即将投票
选出工部局提名人

N. F. 奥尔曼先生的名字于昨日被加入上海工部局职位候选人名单，这使得在沪美国人有必要尽快举行初选，以便从美国协会提出的三名提名人中选出两人。
另外两名候选人是现任董事 R. T. 麦克唐纳先生和前董事 J. W. 卡尼先生。
直到昨天，人们还认为不太可能必须举行初选投票，因为此前仅提出了两名提名人。然而，随着奥尔曼先生的提名，人们认为美国侨民社区可能会见证一场涉及多于目前这三名候选人的初选竞选活动。初选提名需要10名美国纳税人的签名。提名截止日期为星期一，届时所有请愿书必须送达美国协会秘书詹姆斯·M·豪先生处。
过去一周的事态发展为美国人提交给工部局的提名名单带来了剧烈变化。现任工部局主席康奈尔·S·富兰克林先生原本预计将寻求连任，直到他上周披露今年不会成为选举候选人。随后 J. W. 卡尼先生被推举出来，直到昨天，预计只有他和麦克唐纳先生会角逐这些职位。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

S.M.C. Election:
Increasing Occidental Vote:

To the Editor of the
"NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—During the recent Municipal
Election, the British, American and
other voters of Western nationality
were able, by making a supreme
effort, to maintain the status quo
as regards national representation on
the Municipal Council. It must be
obvious, however, that we cannot
depend on achieving an equally sa-
tisfactory result next year, and it is
therefore imperative to adopt im-
mediately whatever measures are pos-
sible for increasing the foreign voting
power.

There is a large reservoir of
foreign potential voters residing in
the French Concession, and it is de-
sirable that efforts be made to induce
a large quantity of these residents
of the French Concession to transfer
their domicile to the International
Settlement. It is regrettable that,
with their interests so closely linked
with the security of the International
Settlement, so many British, Ameri-
can and other foreigners are com-
pelled by force of circumstances to
reside in the French Concession,
where, of course, they have no power
to assist in selecting the governing
body for the International Settlement.

I suggest that one or more of the
following measures should be adopted
for the purpose of encouraging more
foreigners to reside in the Inter-
national Settlement:—

(a) The large real estate com-
panies, who have been so active in
developing certain areas of the
French Concession as a residential
neighbourhood, should immediately
plan the building of foreign style
dwellings and apartment houses on a
large scale in the International Settle-
ment.

(b) The Municipal Council should
specify certain areas in the Inter-
national Settlement as "Residential
Areas" in the same way as the
French Municipal Council have done
in the French Concession.

(c) The American and British
Consuls could charge a larger annual
registration fee to their Shanghai
nationals who are living outside the
International Settlement.

(d) American and British firms
might consider offering a monetary
inducement to their employees to take
up residence in the International
Settlement.

If any improvement is to be effected
in time to influence the 1941 Munici-
pal Election, it is important that early
action should be taken on the above
lines.

PUBLIC AFFAIRS.
Shanghai, Apr. 13.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

工部局选举：
增加西方人选票：

致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——在最近的市政选举中，英国、美国及其他西方国籍的选民通过做出最大努力，维持了工部局中各国代表权的现状。然而，显而易见的是，我们不能指望明年也能取得同样令人满意的结果，因此必须立即采取一切可能的措施来增加外国人的投票权。

在法租界居住着大量潜在的外国选民，理应设法促使大量法租界居民将其住所迁至公共租界。令人遗憾的是，尽管许多英国、美国及其他外国人的利益与公共租界的安全紧密相连，但他们却因形势所迫不得不居住在法租界，在那里，他们当然无权协助选拔公共租界的管理机构。

我建议应采取以下一项或多项措施，以鼓励更多外国人居住在公共租界：

(a) 那些在开发法租界某些区域作为住宅区方面一直非常活跃的大型房地产公司，应立即计划在公共租界大规模建造西式住宅和公寓楼。

(b) 工部局应像法国公董局在法租界所做的那样，指定公共租界内的某些区域为“住宅区”。

(c) 美国和英国领事馆可对其居住在公共租界以外的本国公民收取更高的年度注册费。

(d) 美国和英国公司可以考虑向其员工提供金钱激励，以促使其在公共租界定居。

如果要及时产生影响1941年市政选举的效果，重要的是要尽早按照上述方针采取行动。

公共事务。
上海，4月13日。

page_data.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS

APR 15 1940

Sinister Tactics Seen
In Local Election
Japanese Papers Critical
Of Methods

Tokyo, Apr. 14.
The Japanese press today launched an attack against "sinister" electioneering tactics in Shanghai and ascribed the Japanese defeat in the election for Municipal Councillors to the "constitution of the International Settlement."
The powerful Tokyo "Nichi Nichi" said the Japanese defeat was attributable to "sinister tactics of the British," but added that the recent failure "will not and must not" prevent the Japanese from continuing their efforts.
The "Yomiuri Shimbun" claimed the fundamental cause of the Japanese failure was the "anachronistic existence of land regulations and the International Settlement's constitution."
The "Asahi Shimbun" blamed the Japanese failure to place five candidates on the Council to overzealousness, pointing out that if the Japanese had restricted their number of candidates to three instead of five "the outcome might have been quite different."--United Press.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

1940年4月15日

当地选举中被指
使用阴险策略
日本报纸批评
其手段

东京，4月14日。
日本媒体今日发起攻击，指责上海存在“阴险”的竞选策略，并将日本人在工部局董事选举中的失败归咎于“公共租界的章程”。
影响力巨大的东京《日日新闻》称，日本的失败归因于“英国的阴险策略”，但补充说，最近的失败“不会且绝不能”阻止日本人继续努力。
《读卖新闻》声称，日本失败的根本原因是“土地章程和公共租界章程的过时存在”。
《朝日新闻》将日本未能将五名候选人送入工部局归咎于过度热心，指出如果日本人将候选人数量限制为三名而不是五名，“结果可能会截然不同”。——合众社。

1947年4月

日本人可能反对
增加税收

《大陆新报》昨日预测，当周三的外国纳税人会议上讨论该议题时，一位日本发言人可能会提出紧急动议发言，以此表达在沪日本同胞对上海工部局拟议增加捐税和执照费的反对意见。
该日报称，这位日本发言人将不得不提出紧急动议，因为他未按程序规则要求在4月9日前向工部局总办通知其意向。

page_data.en:
Japanese Will Start
Immediate Preparations
For 1941 S. M. Elections

Chairman Of Election Committee States That
Japanese Will Not Abandon Fight To Give
Greater Voice To Ideas On Council

AIM IS TO INTERNATIONALIZE ON BASIS
OF FRIENDLY RELATIONS

Japanese residents in Shanghai will not abandon their fight
to give a greater voice to their ideas on how the administra-
tion of the International Settlement should be conducted, Mr.
Yukichi Hayashi, chairman of the Japanese Election Committee,
said yesterday in a post-election statement.

“We will begin preparations now to obtain a landslide in
next year’s elections,” he declared.

“It is not in mortals to com-
mand success,” he said. “We Jap-
anese shall not complain over the
results of the election now that
the struggle is over. The import-
ance of an election lies not upon
its outcome, but in the righteous-
ness of the platforms at issue.”

Study Fairness

Mr. Hayashi, however, pointed
out that the question of whether
or not the election was conducted
fairly and justly would require
study, together with “the irration-
ality of the present election sys-
tem of elections.”

“I believe that appropriate steps
should be taken separately for
their study and reform,” he added.

In discussing the election re-
turns for membership in the
S.M.C., Mr. Hayashi remarked:
“It is to be regretted that the re-
sults of the election fell short of
our expectations in spite of our
solid unity and I, as the chairman
of the Election Committee, lack
words to apologize for this to the
Japanese residents.

Oust Monopolization

“Our aims towards the Interna-
tional Settlement is to internation-
alize it on the basis of friendly
relations and co-operation among
various communities, ousting the

monopolization of the Settlement’s
administration by one national
group so as to make Shanghai an
ideal international city,” the state-
ment said.

In promoting the common wel-
fare of the residents in the Settle-
ment by carrying out gradual re-
forms in the administration of the
Settlement and by re-examining
its organization which has not kept
pace with this progressive age,”
the Japanese sought to improve
existing conditions Mr. Hayashi
pointed out.

“Our insistence springs from a
noble ideal, unlike one based upon
egoistic national self-interest. We
feel that the results of the elec-
tion have eloquently shown that
our assertions were just and ap-
propriate. In spite of the smaller
number of Japanese in the Council
against the British and the Amer-
icans, we sincerely hope that our
opinions will be put into practice
before long,” the Election Chair-
man declared.
page_data.zh:
日本人将立即开始
筹备1941年工部局选举

选举委员会主席表示，
日本人不会放弃争取在工部局
发出更大声音的斗争

目标是在友好关系基础上实现国际化

上海日本居民不会放弃他们的斗争，即争取让他们关于如何管理公共租界的想法发出更大的声音，日本选举委员会主席林裕吉先生昨日在选后声明中表示。

“我们将现在开始准备，以便在明年的选举中获得压倒性胜利，”他宣称。

“谋事在人，成事在天，”他说。“既然斗争已经结束，我们日本人不会对选举结果抱怨。选举的重要性不在于其结果，而在于所争论政纲的正义性。”

研究公平性

然而，林先生指出，选举是否公平公正进行的问题，连同“现行选举制度的不合理性”，都需要进行研究。

“我认为应分别采取适当步骤对其进行研究和改革，”他补充道。

在讨论工部局成员的选举结果时，林先生评论道：“尽管我们团结一致，但选举结果未达到我们的预期，对此我作为选举委员会主席，无言以对在沪日本居民表示歉意。

消除垄断

“我们对公共租界的目标是在各社区友好关系与合作的基础上使其国际化，消除单一民族群体对租界行政管理的垄断，从而使上海成为理想的国际城市，”声明称。

林先生指出，日本人通过在租界行政管理中实施渐进式改革，并重新审视其未能跟上这个进步时代步伐的组织结构，以促进租界居民的共同福利，从而寻求改善现有状况。

“我们的坚持源于崇高的理想，而非基于自私的民族私利。我们认为，选举结果有力地表明，我们的主张是公正和适当的。尽管与英国人和美国人相比，工部局中的日本人数量较少，但我们真诚希望我们的意见不久后能得到实施，”选举委员会主席宣称。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES
APR 1 3 1940

Preparations Under Way
For Ratepayers' Meeting
As Election Fever Ends

No Special Resolutions To Be Presented At The
Meeting; Annual Orchestra Discussion Will
Not Be Brought Up; Deficit Main Issue

CHAIRMAN WILL GIVE ACCOUNTING FOR
CONDUCT OF 1939 AFFAIRS

With the excitement over the most hard-fought and most
widely commented Municipal Election in the history of the
International Settlement now over, attention is now being
focussed on the forthcoming annual meeting of ratepayers to
be held next Wednesday, April 17, at 2.30 p.m. at the Race Club
Public Stand.

There will be no special resolutions proposed by ratepayers
at the annual meeting, as new resolutions had been forwarded
to Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner-General
of the Council, by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, April 9, the dead-line set
for all resolutions. However, it is understood that the Chair-
man, Mr. Cornell S. Franklin will be asked a number of ques-
tions in the course of the meeting.

General satisfaction among the
British, American and other Occid-
ental communities was expressed
yesterday over the result of the
elections and the retention of the
status quo. The total of 13,008
votes polled surpassed all expecta-
tions of competent observers and
the national election committees.
It was first estimated that about
8,000 votes would be cast, but,
later, when an effort was made to
get all indirect voters to exercise
their right as ratepayers it was
estimated that about 10,000 would
turn out at the polls. The final
total of 13,008 even with 96 votes
being invalid, was very encourag-
ing, showing that Shanghailanders
at present are taking interest in
Municipal affairs.

Japanese Comment

The Chairman of the Japanese
Election Committee stated yester-
day that the Japanese residents in
Shanghai will not abandon their
fight to give a greater voice to
their ideas on how the administra-
tion of the Settlement should be
conducted. He added: "We will be-
gin preparations now to obtain a
landslide in next year's elections."

No Orchestra Debate

The regular annual debate on
the question of the Municipal
Orchestra will not be brought up
as a resolution at the Ratepayers'
Meeting this year. The main reso-
lution will be the proposal for the
adoption of the Budget for 1940
and authorization for the Council
to raise a sum of $16,000,000 by
various loans.

The question of the large deficit
will be the main point of discus-
sion and it is expected that a num-
ber of questions will be asked on
this point.

Mossop To Preside

The retiring chairman of the
Council, Mr. Cornell S. Franklin
will give the accounting for the
year 1939. He will be assisted by
Mr. W. J. Keswick, Vice-Chair-
man. The chair at the meeting
will be occupied by Judge Sir
Allan Mossop of the British Sup-
reme Court for China.

The following are the resolutions
and their proposers:

No. 1.—That our esteemed fellow-
ratepayer, His Honour Judge Sir Allan
Mossop, be invited to take the Chair.
Proposer: Mr. C. S. Franklin.
Seconder: Mr. W. J. Keswick.

No. 2.—That Mr. E. T. Nash be ap-
pointed Secretary to the meeting.
Proposer: Mr. C. S. Franklin.
Seconder: Mr. W. J. Keswick.

No. 3.—That the Rules of Procedure
in force at the previous annual meet-
ing be adopted for use at this meet-
ing.
Proposer: Mr. C. S. Franklin.
Seconder: Mr. W. J. Keswick.
(Note:—These Rules of Procedure
will be set forth in the Agenda papers
to be furnished to ratepayers at the
meeting, in which they will be describ-
ed as the "existing Rules of Pro-
cedure).

No. 4.—That Mr. Erik Crone be elect-
ed a Land Commissioner for the
ensuing year.
Proposer: Mr. H. S. Poulsen.
Seconder: Mr. E. Treck.

No. 5.—Election of four Governors
of the General Hospital for the ensu-
ing year.

No. 6.—That the Report and Accounts
for the year ended December 31, 1939,
be passed.
Proposer: Mr. C. S. Franklin.
Seconder: Mr. W. J. Keswick.

No. 7.—That the estimated expendi-
ture for the year 1940 contained in the
Budget proposed by the retiring
Council together with the recommenda-
tions attached thereto be approved
and adopted and that the Council be
hereby authorized to impose, collect
and recover the rates taxes dues and
fees recommended therein and to raise
should it be considered expedient to
do so upon such terms and in such
manner as the Council may in its dis-
cretion think fit a sum not exceeding
$16,000,000 of the equivalent thereof for
the purpose defined in the estimate
of Extraordinary Expenditure.
Proposer: Mr. C. S. Franklin.
Seconder: Mr. W. J. Keswick.

No. 8.—That the new Rules of Proce-
dure already published be adopted and
remain in force until the adoption of
Rules of Procedure at the next An-
nual Meeting.
Proposer: Mr. C. S. Franklin.
Seconder: Mr. W. J. Keswick.
(Note:—These new Rules of Proced-
ure will be set forth in the Agenda
papers to be furnished to ratepayers
at the meeting, in which they will be
described as the "proposed new Rules
of Procedure").

《上海泰晤士报》
1940年4月13日

选举热潮消退
纳税人大会筹备工作正在进行中

大会上将不提出特别决议案；年度乐队议题不会提上日程；赤字成为主要议题

主席将就1939年事务的处理情况作出说明

随着国际租界历史上竞争最激烈、评论最广泛的市政选举的兴奋劲头现已过去，人们的注意力现在集中在即将于下周三（4月17日）下午2时30分在跑马总会公共看台举行的年度纳税人大会上。

在年度大会上，纳税人将不会提出任何特别决议案，因为新的决议案已在4月9日（星期二）下午4时前送交工部局秘书兼总办 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生，这是所有决议案提交的截止日期。然而，据悉在会议过程中，主席 Cornell S. Franklin 先生将被问及若干问题。

昨日，英、美及其他西方侨民社区对选举结果及维持现状表示普遍满意。总计13,008张投票数超出了资深观察家和国家选举委员会的所有预期。最初估计约有8,000张选票投出，但后来，当努力促使所有间接选民行使作为纳税人的权利时，估计约有10,000人前往投票站。最终总数为13,008票，即使其中有96票无效，也令人非常鼓舞，表明目前的上海外侨正对市政事务产生兴趣。

日本方面的评论

日本选举委员会主席昨日表示，在上海的日本居民不会放弃争取让他们关于如何管理租界的意见拥有更大发言权的斗争。他补充说：“我们现在开始准备，以便在明年的选举中获得压倒性胜利。”

无乐队辩论

今年纳税人大会上不会将关于工部局乐队的常规年度辩论作为决议案提出。主要决议案将是提议通过1940年预算，并授权工部局通过各种贷款筹集16,000,000美元款项。

巨额赤字问题将成为讨论的主要焦点，预计在此问题上将提出若干质询。

Mossop 主持

卸任的工部局主席 Cornell S. Franklin 先生将对1939年度的工作进行述职。他将由副主席 W. J. Keswick 先生协助。会议主席将由英国在华最高法院法官 Allan Mossop 爵士担任。

以下是各项决议案及其提案人：

第1号——邀请我们尊敬的纳税人同仁，Allan Mossop 法官爵士担任大会主席。
提案人：C. S. Franklin 先生。
附议人：W. J. Keswick 先生。

第2号——任命 E. T. Nash 先生为大会秘书。
提案人：C. S. Franklin 先生。
附议人：W. J. Keswick 先生。

第3号——本次大会采用上一次年度大会生效的议事规则。
提案人：C. S. Franklin 先生。
附议人：W. J. Keswick 先生。
（注：这些议事规则将在提供给与会纳税人的议程文件中列明，其中将其描述为“现行议事规则”。）

第4号——选举 Erik Crone 先生为下一年度的土地委员。
提案人：H. S. Poulsen 先生。
附议人：E. Treck 先生。

第5号——选举下一年度广慈医院（General Hospital）的四名董事。

第6号——通过截至1939年12月31日止年度的报告和账目。
提案人：C. S. Franklin 先生。
附议人：W. J. Keswick 先生。

第7号——批准并通过卸任工部局提出的预算中所含的1940年度预计支出以及随附的建议，并据此授权工部局征收、收取和追缴其中建议的捐税、税款、债务和费用；且若认为权宜，授权工部局以其自行斟酌认为合适的条款和方式，筹集不超过16,000,000美元或等值金额的款项，用于非常支出估算中所界定的目的。
提案人：C. S. Franklin 先生。
附议人：W. J. Keswick 先生。

第8号——通过已公布的新议事规则，并使其保持有效，直至下一次年度大会通过新的议事规则为止。
提案人：C. S. Franklin 先生。
附议人：W. J. Keswick 先生。
（注：这些新议事规则将在提供给与会纳税人的议程文件中列明，其中将其描述为“拟议的新议事规则”。）

page_data.en:
APR 1 3 1940

CONGRATULATIONS TO
ELECTED CANDIDATES
BY SPOKESMAN HERE

Retrocession
Of Settlement
Final Object

Abolition Of Extra-
territoriality In
China Desired

CONSTITUTION CHANGE
IS SOUGHT BY JAPAN

While extending congratula-
tions to victorious candidates in
the Shanghai Municipal Council
elections, Mr. Ken Tsurumi,
Embassy spokesman for the
Japanese Consulate in Shang-
hai, at a press conference held
last evening, announced that
the final object of the Japanese
Government was the retroces-
sion of the foreign Concessions
and Settlements in China and
return of them to the Chinese
people.

The results of the election, con-
tinued Mr. Tsurumi, only further
convinces the Japanese community
that they must continue in their
efforts to "internationalise" the
Settlement and make it a place
suitable for everybody to live in.

In congratulating the five British,
two Americans and two Japanese
candidates successful in the Muni-
cipal elections, the spokesman
stated that the election was a sort
of game that should be conducted
according to the rules of sports-
manship, whereby the loser should
congratulate the winner. However,
as a result of the election, namely,
that again five British, two Ameri-
cans and two Japanese form the
Council, the feeling among the
Japanese people of Shanghai that
the administration of the Inter-
national Settlement ought to be
more international, has only been
greatly intensified.

Should Be More Suitable

The Japanese community in
Shanghai would continue its efforts
to carry out its convictions that
the International Settlement should
be a place suitable for everybody
to live in, said the spokesman.
This could only be accomplished

when the place lived up to its
name—that of an "international
settlement."

Asked by a correspondent whe-
ther the Japanese had any criticism
on the way the election was con-
ducted or in the manner in which
the Anglo-Saxon bloc obtained such
a striking increase in votes over
previous years, the spokesman
replied that an election was always
carried out on the assumption that
it was conducted justly and fairly.
He stated that facts of the elec-
tion would have to be investigated
before comment could be made as
to the fairness of the election. As
stated before, said the spokesman,
the object of the Japanese was to
secure a fair representation in the
affairs of the Shanghai International
Settlement and this objective he
hoped, would be achieved by law-
ful means.

Asked if it was hinted that the
Japan might resort to unlawful
means to secure this objective, the
spokesman replied that the Japan-
ese would not resort to any unlaw-
ful means.

In Shanghai Alone

The tendency in the world to-
day was to permit suffrage to be
carried out on a universal basis
and not under restrictions of pro-
perty owned by certain people,
said the spokesman. However, in
Shanghai—and Shanghai alone—
there still seemed to be an ana-
chronic system whereby a man was
allowed to vote if he possessed
sufficient property. That Shanghai
was still allowing this system to
operate only showed how anachro-
nic the regulations in the Settle-
ment were.

Asked whether the Japanese
planned to change the Land Re-
gulations or whether it was ex-
pected this would by done by the
new Chinese regime, the spokesman
replied the Japanese objective was
to obtain a reform of the Land
Regulations but this matter would
have to be decided with the Coun-
cil and the Consular Body before
taken up by the Chinese authori-
ties.

If he went to extremes, the
spokesman stated, he could easily
say that the Council should be run
by the nine largest landowners in
the Settlement or by the nine
richest millionaires, if there were
nine. The Land Regulations were
archaic, he said, and were intro-
duced in 1846 and were revised a
long time ago. In a world that is
moving forward it is a pity that
such a statute governed the ruling
of the International Settlement to-
day.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月13日

驻沪发言人
向当选候选人致贺

归还租界
是最终目标

希望废除
在华治外法权

日本寻求
修改章程

日本驻上海领事馆使馆发言人 Ken Tsurumi（音译）先生在昨晚举行的记者招待会上，在向上海工部局选举中的获胜候选人表示祝贺的同时，宣布日本政府的最终目标是归还外国在华租界和居留地，并将其交还给中国人民。

Tsurumi 先生继续说道，选举结果只是进一步使日本侨民确信，他们必须继续努力使租界“国际化”，使其成为一个适合所有人居住的地方。

该发言人在祝贺五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人在市政选举中胜出时表示，选举是一种应按照体育精神规则进行的游戏，据此，失败者应向胜利者表示祝贺。然而，由于选举结果，即再次由五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人组成工部局，上海日本民众中认为国际租界的管理应当更加国际化的情绪，反而大大加剧了。

应当更加适宜

该发言人称，上海的日本侨民将继续努力贯彻其信念，即国际租界应当成为一个适合所有人居住的地方。这只有在该地方名副其实——即成为一个真正的“国际居留地”时——才能实现。

当被一名记者问及日本方面是否对选举的进行方式，或盎格鲁-撒克逊集团票数较往年显著增加的方式有任何批评时，该发言人回答说，选举总是基于公正公平进行的假设而开展的。他表示，在对选举的公平性发表评论之前，必须调查选举的事实。正如之前所述，该发言人称，日本的目标是在上海国际租界事务中获得公平的代表权，他希望这一目标能通过合法手段实现。

当被问及这是否暗示日本可能采取非法手段来实现这一目标时，该发言人回答说，日本人不会诉诸任何非法手段。

仅在上海如此

该发言人称，当今世界的趋势是允许在普遍基础上进行选举，而不是受限于某些人拥有的财产。然而，在上海——且仅在上海——似乎仍然存在一种过时的制度，即如果一个人拥有足够的财产，就允许其投票。上海仍然允许这种制度运作，只表明租界的规章是多么过时。

当被问及日本是否计划修改《土地章程》，或者是否期望由新的中国政权来完成此事时，该发言人回答说，日本的目标是获得《土地章程》的改革，但在由中国当局处理此事之前，必须与工部局和领事团决定此事。

该发言人表示，如果走极端，他可以轻易地说，工部局应由租界内九大地主，或者如果有九位的话，由九位最富有的百万富翁来管理。他说，《土地章程》是陈旧的，引入于1846年，并在很久以前进行过修订。在一个不断前进的世界里，遗憾的是，如今国际租界的治理仍受如此法规的管辖。

CHINA PRESS
APR 1 3 1940

Japanese Calm, Restrained
Over Outcome Of Elections

An atmosphere of calm and restraint yesterday characterized the post-election attitude of several Japanese leaders as they surveyed the results of the polling which swept the "status quo" candidates into office.

While observers here believe that getting rich rapidly and then going home to Japan, according to this same businessman.
The army, he maintained, had only a disinterested by-stander's outlook on the election results and would certainly not attempt any forcible seizure of power because Japanese aims had been thwarted. The Tokyo Foreign Office, however, was stated to have been deeply interested in the campaign.
A quiet "I told you so" atmosphere pervaded British business offices yesterday and was explained by one taipan in the succinct words of a pseudo-Confucius saying: "He who have property win election."

British Opinion
Another British businessman ventured the opinion that never so long as government of the Settlement is conducted according to the Land Regulations will the British and Americans lose control of it. This is because the franchise is based solely on property qualifications. The British and American interests here control about four times the amount of Japanese owned property and to amend the Land Regulations requires the assent of all treaty powers as well as the Chinese National Government at Chungking.

With the election decision known, Shanghai is already seeking the sequel. "What of the next 12 months?" was a question asked almost universally by those whom THE CHINA PRESS interviewed.
Statements were not flowing very freely from the lips of new councillors yesterday but one of them, Mr. N. P. Allman, American, declared that a matter of primary importance to the 1940 Council would be the dissemination of greater publicity as to its problems and actions. "Publicity is the Council's best weapon against unjust criticism," he said.

S.M.C. Publicity
Approached on the same question Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Commissioner-General and Secretary of the Council, pointed out that aside from political matters he would co-operate with the press to the fullest extent in the future as in the past in giving out publicity on Council affairs.
Where politics were concerned, he continued, it should be realized that they often involve international susceptibilities and in the public interest could not be revealed. Another consideration was the presence of the five Chinese Councillors who are able to give invaluable advice to the Council in its dealings with local Chinese matters, but who would be embarrassed to keep silence because of their political connections if their views were made public.

《字林西报》
1940年4月13日

日本人对选举结果表现冷静克制

昨日，几位日本领导人在审视将“维持现状”候选人送入选政厅的投票结果时，其选后态度呈现出一种冷静与克制的氛围。

尽管此地的观察家认为，据这位商人所说，迅速致富然后回日本去。他坚持认为，军队对选举结果仅持有一种无私的旁观者视角，绝不会因为日本的目标受挫而试图强行夺取权力。然而，据悉东京外务省对此次竞选活动深感兴趣。
昨日，英国商号办公室里弥漫着一种安静的“我早就告诉过你”的氛围，一位大班用一句伪孔子格言简洁地解释道：“有产者赢得选举。”

英国人的观点
另一位英国商人大胆发表意见称，只要公共租界的政府管理遵循《土地章程》，英美就不会失去对其的控制权。这是因为选举权完全基于财产资格。此地的英美利益集团控制的财产数额约为日本人所控财产的四倍，而修改《土地章程》需要所有条约国以及位于重庆的中国国民政府的同意。

随着选举结果揭晓，上海已经在寻求后续发展。“未来12个月会怎样？”这是《字林西报》采访对象几乎普遍提出的问题。
昨日，新当选的董事们并未轻易发表声明，但其中一位美国籍董事N. P. Allman先生表示，1940年度工部局的首要事项之一是加大对其面临的问题及行动的宣传力度。“宣传是工部局应对不公正批评的最佳武器，”他说。

工部局的宣传
就同一问题询问工部局总办兼秘书G. Godfrey Phillips先生时，他指出，除政治事务外，他在未来将像过去一样，在发布有关工部局事务的宣传方面与新闻界充分合作。
他继续说，涉及政治问题时，应当意识到这些往往牵涉到国际敏感性，出于公共利益考虑不能公开。另一个考量因素是五位华董的存在，他们在工部局处理本地华人事务时能提供宝贵的建议，但如果他们的观点被公开，由于他们的政治关系，保持沉默会使他们感到尴尬。

关于向其审议过程公开的可能性，Phillips先生提出，此类性质的决议对工部局的约束力可能不如例如预算决议那样强。他说，如果是这样，将使上海在世界城市中处于独特的地位。

来年展望
昨日，日本选举委员会相当关注未来12个月的问题，其主席Yukichi Hayashi（音译）先生宣布：“我们将现在开始准备，以便在明年的选举中获得压倒性胜利。”
Hayashi先生继续说道：“既然斗争已经结束，我们日本人不会对现在的选举结果抱怨。我们对国际公共租界的目标是在各社群友好关系与合作的基础上使其国际化，消除由单一民族群体垄断租界行政管理的局面，从而使上海成为理想的国际城市。”
他说，“当前选举制度的不合理之处”以及选举是否公平进行的问题都需要研究。“我相信应采取适当措施对其进行研究和改革，”他补充道。

Hayashi的谈话
在讨论选举结果时，Hayashi先生 remarked：“令人遗憾的是，尽管我们团结一致，选举结果仍未达到我们的预期，作为选举委员会主席，我无言以对日本居民表示歉意。”
亲日的《大陆新报》昨日发表了反英和反工部局财务处的谩骂言论，宣称财务处与英国选举委员会联手违反了“选举的神圣性和民主原则”。

指控舞弊
该报指控称，直到4月10日，选举委员会还对公投结果感到担忧，并在财务处的密切配合下，在一天内制造了2000张英国选票。
该报还指控称，选举给寻求投票的日本人设置了障碍；在英美辖区的投票方式对日本人不公，但却不利于租界；以及居住在直接向S.V.C.（原文如此，应为S.M.C.即工部局）缴纳地税而非通过……（原文不清）……投票截止时间等，但在实施许多欺诈性选举方面，《大陆新报》称。

日本舆论对市政选举结果的看法尚未有足够时间形成定论，此地主要日本居民的声明普遍表明，他们准备以“良好的失败者”精神接受选举结果。在几种情况下，《字林西报》记者在征询日本舆论时，听到主要日本居民向他提及“良好的体育精神”这一短语。
昨日日本人对选举的具体意见表达可归纳为四类。

发言人观点
日本大使馆官方发言人在昨日的记者招待会上发表了如下声明。
“我们的目标仍然是更公平的代表权，我希望通过合法手段实现这一目标。”在此声明之前，他说，假设选举是以公平公正的方式进行的。“在发表评论之前，必须调查选举是如何进行的，”他说。
来自日本选举委员会主席Yukichi Hayashi先生的选后声明如下：
“既然斗争已经结束，我们日本人不会对选举结果抱怨……我们将现在开始准备，以便在明年的选举中获得压倒性胜利。”
来自据称为军方喉舌的《大陆新报》的评论如下：

“违反原则”
工部局财务处和英国选举委员会违反了选举的神圣性和民主原则。据这家日本报刊称，后者组织在财务处的协助下，在一天内增加了2000张英国选票。此外，该报指控称，非日本籍的外国选民在下午3点投票结束后被非法允许进入投票站。
一位要求记者不要使用其姓名的日本商人发表了如下评论：
“许多‘战前’就在上海的日本居民对选举结果暗中感到高兴。他们觉得，如果选举结果对‘维持现状’候选人不利，租界赖以支持的外国资本将开始撤出，这将损害包括日本人在内的各方利益。”

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
APR 1 3 1940
Election Results Gratify
Foreign Voters
Japanese to Prepare for Next Election According
To Committee Chairman

RESIDENTS of the International Settlement heaved sighs of relief yesterday morning after it was revealed that voting ratepayers, with the largest vote count ever recorded in a Shanghai municipal election, fought off the threat of Japanese domination of the Council and maintained the status quo for at least one more year by sweeping the five regular British candidates and two American nominees into office with an overwhelming majority of over two thousand votes for each candidate. Biggest flop of the election was the poor showing made by Mr. Ranald G. McDonald, independent British candidate, who polled only 325 votes out of a total of 13,096 ballots cast.

Japanese residents in Shanghai will not abandon their fight to give a greater voice to their ideas on how the administration of the International Settlement should be conducted, Mr. Yukichi Hayashi, chairman of the Japanese Election Committee, said yesterday in a post-election statement.

"We will begin preparations now to obtain a landslide in next year's elections," he declared. "It is not immaterial to command success," he said. "We Japanese shall not complain over the results of the election now that the struggle is over. The importance of an election lies not upon its outcome, but in the righteousness of the platforms at issue."

Mr. Hayashi, however, pointed out that the question of whether or not the election was conducted fairly and justly would require study, together with "the irrationalities of the present system of elections."

"I believe that appropriate steps should be taken separately for their study and reform," he added.

Results Regretted

In discussing the election returns for membership in the S.M.C., Mr. Hayashi remarked: "It is to be regretted that the results of the election fell short of our expectations in spite of our solid unity and I, as the chairman of the Election Committee, lack words to apologize for this to the Japanese residents.

"Our aims towards the International Settlement is to internationalise it on the basis of friendly relations and co-operation among various communities, ousting the monopolization of the Settlement's administration by one national group so as to make Shanghai an ideal international city," the statement said.

In promoting the common welfare of the residents in the Settlement by carrying out gradual reforms in the administration of the Settlement and by re-examining its organization which has not kept pace with this progressive age," the Japanese sought to improve existing conditions, Mr. Hayashi pointed out.

"Our insistence springs from a noble ideal, unlike one based upon egoistic national self-interest. We feel that the results of the election have eloquently shown that our assertions were just and appropriate. In spite of the smaller number of Japanese in the Council against the British and the Americans, we sincerely hope that our opinions will be put into practice before long," the election chairman declared.

Powers Warned

Chungking, Apr. 12.
A warning to foreign Powers that yesterday's elections to the Shanghai Municipal Council should cause them to "realize Japan's intention of dominating China and completely ousting foreign interests, is given by the "Hsin Hua Jih Pao," official organ of the Chinese Communist Party, in an editorial this morning.

The present situation in Shang-
hai, the daily says, is the direct
result of the appeasement policy on the part of the foreign Powers towards Japan. During the past two and a half years, every Japanese demand has been accepted by the Shanghai Municipal Council; but every concession made by the Council has been invariably followed by fresh demands.

"Japan aims at completely ousting the rights and interests of third Powers in China. The election is merely part of the Japanese programme. Though Britain and the United States may be able to maintain the status quo this time, it is almost certain that stronger Japanese pressure is bound to follow.

"To preserve their own interests and rights in China, foreign nationals in this country should urge their Home Governments to change their policy and give China material assistance, in order effectively to check Japanese aggression," the "Hsin Hua Jih Pao" concludes.—Reuter.

Council Thanks Scrutineers

Mr. C. S. Franklin, Chairman of the Municipal Council, yesterday sent the following letter of thanks to Messrs. H. Berents and R. Bringert, the scrutineers in the election:—

On behalf of my colleagues and myself I wish to tender to you our most genuine thanks for undertaking the responsible task of acting as scrutineers in the recent Municipal Election.

We were fortunate in obtaining the help of two Scrutineers who commanded the confidence of the community and whose readiness to devote unremitting attention to details of organisation made possible the smooth conduct of the recent count of votes.

I am sure that all your fellow-rate-payers share in the thanks which I am expressing on behalf of the Council.

The Council has been notified by the Chinese Ratepayers' Association of the election, at a meeting of representatives of Chinese Ratepayers, of Messrs. Yu Ya Ching, L. T. Yuen, W. Gockson, E. Y. B. Kiang and Yuliu Hsi as members of the Shanghai Municipal Council for the year 1940/41.

The Council has also been notified by the Chinese Ratepayers' Association of the election of Messrs. K. T. Ling, K. O. Hsu, F. S. Hsu, Francis Liu, W. J. Lee and D. S. Chen to serve on the Council's Committees for the year 1940/41. Mr. T. S. King has been nominated by the Chinese Ratepayers' Association as a Land Commissioner for the year 1940/41.

《字林西报》
1940年4月13日

选举结果令外籍选民满意
据委员会主席称，日本人将为下一次选举做准备

国际租界的居民昨天早晨如释重负，因为结果显示，拥有投票权的纳税人以创上海市政选举历史最高纪录的票数，击退了日本人对工部局实行控制的威胁，并至少再维持一年现状；五名常规英国候选人和两名美国提名人以每位候选人超过两千票的压倒性多数当选。本次选举最大的失利者是独立英国候选人拉纳德·G·麦克唐纳（Ranald G. McDonald）先生，他在总共投出的13,096张选票中仅获得325票。

日本选举委员会主席林裕吉（Yukichi Hayashi，音译）先生在选后声明中表示，上海的日本居民不会放弃争取让他们关于如何管理国际租界的想法拥有更大发言权的斗争。

“我们将立即开始准备，以便在明年的选举中获得压倒性胜利，”他宣称。“掌握成功之道并非无关紧要，”他说。“既然斗争已经结束，我们日本人不会对现在的选举结果抱怨。选举的重要性不在于其结果，而在于所争论政纲的正义性。”

然而，林先生指出，选举是否公平公正进行的问题，连同“现行选举制度的不合理之处”，都需要加以研究。

“我认为应分别采取适当步骤对其进行研究和改革，”他补充道。

对结果表示遗憾

在讨论工部局董事选举结果时，林先生评论说：“尽管我们团结一致，但选举结果未达到我们的预期，对此我作为选举委员会主席，无言以对日本居民表示歉意。

“我们对国际租界的目标是在各社区友好关系与合作的基础上使其国际化，消除由一个民族群体垄断租界行政管理的局面，从而使上海成为理想的国际城市，”声明称。

林先生指出，日本人试图通过在租界行政管理中实施渐进式改革，并重新审视其未能跟上这个进步时代步伐的组织结构，来促进租界居民的共同福利，从而改善现有状况。

“我们的坚持源于崇高的理想，而非基于自私的民族私利。我们认为，选举结果有力地表明，我们的主张是公正和恰当的。尽管工部局中日本人的数量少于英国人和美国人，但我们真诚希望我们的意见不久后能得到实施，”这位选举主席宣称。

列强受到警告

重庆，4月12日。
中国共产党官方机关报《新华日报》在今早的一篇社论中向外国列强发出警告，称昨天的上海工部局选举应使它们“认识到日本主宰中国并完全排挤外国利益的意图”。

该报称，上海目前的局势是外国列强对日本采取绥靖政策的直接结果。在过去两年半里，上海工部局接受了日本的每一项要求；但工部局的每一次让步 invariably 随之而来的是新的要求。

“日本旨在完全排挤第三国在中国的权利和利益。选举只是日本计划的一部分。虽然英国和美国这次可能能够维持现状，但几乎可以肯定，日本更强的压力必将接踵而至。

“为了保留他们在中国自身的利益和权利，在华外国人应敦促其本国政府改变政策并向中国提供物质援助，以有效遏制日本的侵略，”《新华日报》总结道。——路透社。

工部局感谢监票人

工部局董事会主席C. S. Franklin先生昨天致信选举监票人H. Berents先生和R. Bringert先生，表示感谢：—

我代表我的同事和我本人，就你们承担近期市政选举中担任监票人这一负责任的任务，向你们致以最诚挚的谢意。

我们很幸运得到了两位监票人的帮助，他们赢得了社区的信任，并且愿意对组织细节给予不懈的关注，使得近期的计票工作得以顺利进行。

我相信，所有其他纳税人都会分享我代表工部局表达的谢意。

工部局已收到华人纳税会通知，在该会代表会议上，选举虞洽卿、袁履登（L. T. Yuen，音译）、郭克宣（W. Gockson，音译）、江一平（E. Y. B. Kiang，音译）和席玉楼（Yuliu Hsi，音译）诸先生为1940/41年度上海工部局董事。

工部局还收到华人纳税会通知，选举凌宪扬（K. T. Ling，音译）、许公溥（K. O. Hsu，音译）、徐福煦（F. S. Hsu，音译）、刘湛方（Francis Liu，音译）、李伟士（W. J. Lee，音译）和陈德征（D. S. Chen，音译）诸先生在1940/41年度担任工部局各委员会委员。华人纳税会已提名金廷荪（T. S. King，音译）先生为1940/41年度土地委员。

CHINA PRESS
APR 1 3 1940

Abolish All
Settlements,
Say Japanese

"The final objective of the
Japanese Government is the
abolition of extraterritoriality
itself, and eventually the aboli-
tion of settlements and conces-
sions in China," the Japanese
Embassy spokesman asserted
yesterday in a post-election
statement.
Since this cannot be achieved
immediately, various reforms in the
administration of the International
Settlement, as a half-way measure,
are necessary, he said.
"Of course, an election is con-
ducted on the assumption that
everything is conducted in a fair
and square manner. It must be
investigated how this election
was conducted before any
comment can be made.
"Our object was and still is
fairer representation, and I hope
it is achieved through lawful
means," the spokesman stated.
However, this statement was
later amended, when he said
that this did not imply that
there would be any resort to
unlawful means.
British and American residents
argue that a revision of the Land
Regulations is not suitable now
because of unsettled conditions. The
argument, to the Japanese, is un-
tenable, he declared.
"The Japanese aim is to obtain a
reform of the Land Regulations,
which are archaic—they were drawn
up in 1845. In a world that is mov-
ing forward so rapidly, it is re-
grettable that a statute so old
should govern affairs today," he
continued.
Again attacking the "old-fashion-
ed" laws of the Settlement, he re-
marked that "the tendency in the
world now is to permit suffrage on
a universal basis, not under pro-
perty restrictions. But Shanghai
alone seems to cling to the
anachronistic system whereby a
man must have property to vote.
That this should be true is indeed
surprising."
The results of the election clearly
show the aspects of this anachron-
ism, the spokesman asserted, point-
edly adding that "if one wishes to
go to the extreme, it could be said
that the Council should be run by
nine (if there are nine), mi-
litaires."
Concluding, he declared, "I would
like to congratulate the successful
candidates on their election. An
election is a sort of a game, to be
conducted according to sportsman-
ship rules. The loser should con-
gratulate the winner.
"But as a result of the election,
the feeling is heightened rather
than lessened among the Japanese
community that its platform to
make the Settlement a truly inter-
national place is right."

《大美晚报》
1940年4月13日

日本人说：
废除所有
租界

日本大使馆发言人昨天在选后声明中断言：“日本政府的最终目标是废除治外法权本身，并最终废除在中国的租界和租借地。”

他说，由于这无法立即实现，因此作为中间措施，对国际租界的行政管理进行各种改革是必要的。

“当然，举行选举是基于一切都以公平正直的方式进行的假设。在发表评论之前，必须调查这次选举是如何进行的。

“我们的目标过去是，现在仍然是更公平的代表权，我希望这是通过合法手段实现的，”该发言人陈述道。

然而，这一声明后来得到了修正，他说这并不意味着会诉诸非法手段。

英美居民认为，由于局势动荡，现在不适合修订《土地章程》。他宣称，在日本人看来，这种论点站不住脚。

“日本人的目标是改革《土地章程》，这些章程已经过时——它们制定于1845年。在一个如此迅速向前发展的世界里，如此古老的法规今天仍在管辖事务，令人遗憾，”他继续说道。

他再次攻击租界“老式”的法律，评论说“目前世界的趋势是允许普遍选举权，而不是在财产限制下。但似乎只有上海仍固守这种过时的制度，即一个人必须拥有财产才能投票。这种情况确实令人惊讶。”

发言人断言，选举结果清楚地显示了这种过时性的各个方面，并尖锐地补充说，“如果非要走极端，可以说工部局应该由九名（如果有九名的话）军人来管理。”

最后，他宣称：“我想祝贺当选者当选。选举是一种游戏，应按照体育精神规则进行。失败者应向胜利者祝贺。

“但是，选举的结果加剧了而不是减轻了日本社区中的一种感觉，即他们使租界成为真正国际化地方的政纲是正确的。”

page_data.en:
S.M.C. Election
Shanghai's ten days of excitement concerning
the Municipal Elections are now over, and as
the result of last-minute changes in the voters'
list a considerable difference in the standing of
the various community votes was brought about,
greatly in favour of the occidental nations. The
closeness of the total votes given for the two
American candidates suggests that the British
and American votes were cast solidly for them
and allowing for a certain number of suffrages
given them by ratepayers of other nationalities,
it may safely be considered that these 8,000 was
the greatest number of votes any candidate
could hope to poll without the assistance of the
Japanese. The spread of less than 300 votes
between those cast for Mr. Allman, and the
lowest successful British candidate clearly in-
dicates the solidarity of the occidental voters
on the question of the maintenance of the status
quo, while it is to be noticed that the spread
between the highest and lowest Japanese can-
didate being only 33 demonstrates how thorough-
ly well organized the Japanese voters turned
out to be. There is nothing more significant than
the astonishingly small vote given in favour of
Mr. McDonald. He polled less than three per
cent. of the total votes cast and in the event
proved to be not the menace to the selected
British and American candidates that it was
believed he would be. Nevertheless it has to be
pointed out that had the Japanese voted for
him, as it was thought they would, it would have
resulted in the Japanese only securing one seat
on the Council, a result which would have been
greatly deplored. As a result of this election the
ratepayers are afforded another year in which
the present status quo will be retained. It is to
be hoped that the verdict of the polls will be
accepted without resentment on any side. There
was a grave danger at one time that national
feeling would rise to uncomfortable heights.
Happily good sense prevailed all round and the
election itself was marked by no unfortunate
incident. It is hoped that the good sportsman-
ship for which Shanghai is so noted will pre-
vent any deterioration in the existing situation
and that the results of the election will be ac-
cepted by all. If the coming year is devoted
to a study of the best means of providing the
Japanese with something approaching the degree
of representation, which they demand, it is be-
lieved the time will not be ill-spent. There are
indeed few who do not realize that the Inter-
national Settlement will sooner or later have to
embark on a process of evolution which in fact
has been necessary for several years past, and
if the problems which are now presented and
those which may be expected in the near future
can be dealt with in a purely co-operative spirit,
it will redound to the credit of the leaders of
the various communities, and prove completely
beneficial to the Settlement as a whole.
page_data.zh:
工部局选举

上海围绕市政选举的十天激动时刻现已结束，由于选民名单在最后时刻的变动，各社区选票的地位发生了相当大的变化，极大地有利于西方各国。两名美国候选人获得的总票数非常接近，这表明英国和美国选民坚定地投票支持他们，再加上考虑到其他国籍纳税人投给他们的一定数量的选票，可以稳妥地认为，这8,000票是任何候选人在没有日本人协助的情况下希望获得的最高票数。奥尔曼（Allman，音译）先生与得票最低的当选英国候选人之间的票数差距不到300票，这清楚地表明了西方选民在维持现状问题上的团结，同时值得注意的是，得票最高和最低的日本候选人之间仅有33票的差距，这表明日本选民的组织工作是多么彻底和周密。没有什么比麦克唐纳先生获得的惊人低票更具意义了。他获得的票数不到总投票数的百分之三，事实证明，他并没有像人们认为的那样对选定的英国和美国候选人构成威胁。尽管如此，必须指出的是，如果日本人像人们预期的那样投票给他，结果将是日本人仅在工部局获得一个席位，这将是一个令人深感遗憾的结果。由于这次选举，纳税人又获得了一年时间，在此期间将保持目前的现状。希望各方能毫无怨气地接受投票裁决。有一段时间曾存在严重危险，民族情绪可能上升到令人不安的高度。幸运的是，各方都保持了理智，选举本身也没有发生任何不幸事件。希望上海素以著称的良好体育精神能防止现有局势恶化，并希望选举结果能被所有人接受。如果来年致力于研究最佳途径，为日本人提供某种接近他们所要求的代表权程度，相信这段时间不会白费。确实很少有人不认识到，国际租界迟早必须开始一个演变过程，事实上这个过程在过去几年中一直是必要的，如果现在提出的问题以及不久的将来可能出现的问题能够以纯粹合作的精神加以处理，这将有助于提升各社区领导人的声誉，并对整个租界证明完全有益。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES

S.M.C. ELECTIONS
The result of the ballot for the
Shanghai Municipal Council illustrates to
the full the extraordinary interest taken
by the ratepayers in this year's elections.
It also demonstrates, of course, that the
appeal made to the British and American
communities to vote only for their own
"official" candidates and not for any
Japanese was responded to by the vast
majority of ratepayers. The poll was
headed by the two American candidates
and Mr. Allman, who topped the whole
list, secured the remarkable total of
eight thousand votes. At the same time
none of the British "official" candidates
were far behind their American colleagues.
Mr. Ranald McDonald, the independent
British candidate, was at the bottom of
the poll; he secured only 325 votes and
therefore, it would seem, obtained few,
if any, Japanese votes. Two Japanese
were elected and therefore this year's
representation of the Japanese community
will remain as before in point of number
of Councillors. There is a difference of
personnel, however, as a result of the
ballot; Mr. Y. Hanawa is re-elected but
Mr. O. Okamoto is unseated and his
place taken by Mr. M. Den. Now that the
smoke of battle has rolled away, Shanghai
has, therefore, a Council on the old lines
but that new situations will have to be
faced in the not distant future is certain
and the hope must be expressed that
both Councillors and public will do all
that can be done in the general interest,
and that there will be no harbouring of
jealousies or unpleasant feelings as a
result of the ballot. The actual figures
of the ballot certainly suggest that the
number of Japanese ratepayers entitles
them to a larger representation on the
Council than two seats out of nine and
perhaps at some time in the future the
balance will be redressed. But this
matter may be relegated to the back-
ground for the moment. The business of
the present and the immediate future for
the whole Council is to do its utmost for
the general welfare of the International
Settlement of Shanghai and its people,
regardless of creed and nationality, and
especially, and we say it advisedly, to
have proper regard for the burdens laid
upon the poor. We will not enlarge on
this point, or we may be misunderstood,
but we do feel that all those who live
and work in the Settlement have a duty
to the community as a whole which
transcends mere sectional interests and
that the Council should take a lead in
working for harmonious international
relations, especially in the matter of
recognizing the realities of the present
situation.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》

工部局选举

上海公共租界工部局投票结果充分说明了纳税人对今年选举所表现出的极大关注。当然，这也表明，呼吁英美侨民只投票支持他们自己的“官方”候选人、而不投票给任何日本人的号召，得到了绝大多数纳税人的响应。得票最高的是两名美国候选人，而名列榜首的奥尔曼（Allman）先生获得了惊人的八千票。与此同时，英国“官方”候选人的得票也并未远远落后于他们的美国同僚。独立英国候选人拉纳德·麦克唐纳（Ranald McDonald）先生位居榜尾；他仅获得325票，因此看来，即便有日本人选票，也是寥寥无几。两名日本人当选，因此今年日本侨民在董事人数上的代表权将保持原状。然而，由于投票结果，人员构成有所变化：花轮（Y. Hanawa）先生再次当选，但冈本（O. Okamoto）先生落选，其席位由田（M. Den）先生接替。如今硝烟散尽，上海因此拥有了一个沿袭旧制的董事会，但可以肯定的是，在不久的将来必须面对新的局势，希望董事们和公众都能从整体利益出发，竭尽所能，并且不因投票结果而心存嫉妒或产生不快情绪。投票的实际数据确实表明，日本纳税人的数量使他们有权在九名董事中获得比两个席位更多的代表权，也许在未来某个时候这种不平衡会得到纠正。但此事目前可暂且搁置。当前及近期整个董事会的任务是不分信仰和国籍，为上海国际租界及其居民的普遍福利竭尽全力，特别是——我们慎重地指出——要适当顾及加诸穷人身上的负担。我们不再就此点展开论述，以免被误解，但我们确实感到，所有在租界生活和工作的人对整个社区都负有超越狭隘派系利益的义务，董事会应在致力于和谐的国际关系方面发挥带头作用，特别是在承认当前局势的现实方面。

page_data.en:
APR 1 3 1940

Electoral Verdict Delivered

THE election yesterday of the nine "status quo" candidates of the Shanghai Municipal Council was clearly the electoral verdict of International Settlement ratepayers. With this clear-cut decision, the Japanese community in Shanghai and the Japanese Government in Tokyo must abide in good grace. Any attempt to contest the legally delivered electoral verdict on the part of the Japanese would naturally tend to confirm the widely-held suspicion that their chief objective is to gain control of the International Settlement, regardless of the basis of their claims and the legality of their methods.

In putting forth their five candidates the Japanese had claimed that the number of their residents and the aggregate amount of their business interests have greatly increased during the past year so that there should be a proportionate increase in the number of Japanese Councillors. Evidently these Japanese claims have been refuted by the result of the election yesterday. The returns, which put the "status quo" candidates in office, clearly show that the Occidental residents here still pay a greater amount of rates in the International Settlement. Thus, the voting returns give proof to the fact that the original ratio of Council representation of 5-2-2 is justified.

* * *

IF the Japanese are at all sincere in their pre-election professions that they were ready to achieve their objective by the legal method of the ballot, then the matter of Japanese representation on the Council certainly has been sealed until next April. A year hence, an appeal to the voters of the International Settlement will again be open to the Japanese, and if at that time the Nipponese are able to poll more votes than Occidental ratepayers, they would be clearly entitled to put into effect their planks in the Settlement.

The election of the "status quo" candidates, however, does not mean that the new Council can rest on its laurels. The electoral victory was itself achieved only after the most strenuous struggle and after the various critics of the Council's past policies had agreed to postpone their criticism until the international status of the Settlement was improved. The electoral "united front" among the Occidental ratepayers here does not mean that thinking residents here are blind to the various faults of the Council or that they are ready to give blank support to the future policies of the new Council.

The criticism which has been levelled at the Council for its extravagance, and its administrative inefficiency is both well-founded and legitimate. It is the duty of the new Council to take the opinion of a large section of the local ratepayers into consideration. Reforms and economy should be instituted without delay so that no national group in Shanghai will have reason to hold the Council up as a classic example of "administrative inefficiency."

* * *

IT would be exceedingly unpolitic—and foolhardy—for the new Council to adopt the smug attitude of "let the public be damned," which in the past has largely characterized the unvaried reaction of the Shanghai Municipal Council toward external criticism. The latest Japanese attempt to gain control of the Settlement clearly shows how long the Council can continue—and the Occidental ratepayers can afford to let the Council continue—to operate as a government which refuses to take public opinion seriously.

When the new Council takes office, we repeat, urgent reforms in both administrative and financial affairs must be instituted immediately. Furthermore, malicious rumors which have reflected seriously on the Council must be cleared up at once by the incoming members. No government can continue to operate as a morally and politically solvent body when it allows its prestige and integrity to be undermined and when it plainly refuses to listen to the clamor of public opinion.

* * *

IF the Shanghai Municipal Council, as it is at present constituted, wants to survive as the governing body of this international city, it must have the courage and determination to do its own house-cleaning. Otherwise, the pretext for cleaning house on its behalf will continue to be used by the Japanese as a weapon for gaining control of the Settlement.

Ahead of the new Council is no easy job. It needs a clear head, a staunch heart and a strong spine. But above all it needs the continued support of Shanghai ratepayers, whose civic-mindedness as shown in the elections is a newly acquired asset of this cosmopolitan city.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月13日

选举裁决已出

昨日上海公共租界工部局九名“维持现状”候选人的当选，显然是国际租界纳税人作出的选举裁决。面对这一明确的决定，上海的日本侨民和东京的日本政府必须欣然接受。如果日本人试图质疑依法产生的选举结果，自然只会证实人们普遍的怀疑，即他们的主要目标是控制国际租界，而不管其主张的依据如何，也不管其手段是否合法。

日本人在推出五名候选人时声称，过去一年中，其居民人数和商业利益总额大幅增加，因此日本董事的人数也应相应增加。显然，这些日本人的主张已被昨日的选举结果所驳斥。使“维持现状”候选人当选的计票结果清楚地表明，在此地的西方居民在国际租界缴纳的捐税总额仍然更高。因此，投票结果证明了工部局代表权原有的5-2-2比例是正当的。

* * *

如果日本人在选前声称愿意通过合法的投票方式实现其目标是真诚的，那么关于日本人在董事会中的代表权问题无疑已尘埃落定，直到明年四月之前都不会再变。一年后，日本人将再次有机会向国际租界的选民发出呼吁，如果届时日本人获得的选票多于西方纳税人，他们显然就有资格在租界实施其政策纲领。

然而，“维持现状”候选人的当选并不意味着新董事会可以高枕无忧。这场选举胜利本身是在经过最激烈的斗争之后才取得的，也是在各种批评工部局过去政策的人士同意推迟批评、直至租界的国际地位得到改善之后才取得的。此地西方纳税人之间的选举“统一战线”，并不意味着在此思考的居民们对董事会的各种弊病视而不见，也不意味着他们准备无条件支持新董事会未来的政策。

针对工部局铺张浪费和行政效率低下提出的批评，既有充分依据，也是正当合理的。新董事会有责任考虑当地很大一部分纳税人的意见。应立即实行改革和节约措施，以便上海的任何一个民族群体都没有理由将工部局视为“行政效率低下”的典型例子。

* * *

如果新董事会采取那种“管他公众死活”的自满态度，那是极其不明智且鲁莽的，而这种态度在过去很大程度上构成了上海公共租界工部局对外界批评的一贯反应。日本人最近试图控制租界的举动清楚地表明，作为一个拒绝认真对待舆论的政府，工部局还能继续运作多久——以及西方纳税人还能容忍工部局继续运作多久。

我们要重申，当新董事会就职时，必须立即在行政和财政事务方面进行紧急改革。此外， incoming members（新任成员）必须立即澄清那些严重损害董事会声誉的恶意谣言。如果一个政府允许其声望和正直受到破坏，并且公然拒绝倾听舆论的呼声，它就无法作为一个在道德和政治上健全的机构继续运作。

* * *

如果目前组成的上海公共租界工部局想要作为这座国际城市的治理机构生存下去，它必须有勇气和决心进行内部整顿。否则，日本人将继续以代为整顿为借口，将其作为控制租界的武器。

新董事会面临的任务并不轻松。它需要清醒的头脑、坚定的心和坚强的脊梁。但最重要的是，它需要上海纳税人的持续支持，他们在选举中表现出的公民意识是这座国际化城市新近获得的财富。

page_data.en:
PRESS

APR 1 1940

Election For Chinese Committee

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS
Sir,—The Chinese Ratepayers Association has made its own rule that only members of the Association may vote for the Chinese Councillors in the Shanghai Municipal Council elections, while according to the regulations of Yangkingpang, the election qualification is, as I understand, that any body, residing in the Settlement, and making payment of land tax to Tls. 10 per year or payment of municipal rate on rental of Tls. 41.61 (or $80.00) is entitled to vote. Hundreds of old Chinese residents who have the above qualifications are thus deprived of their voting privilege. Furthermore the Chinese Ratepayers Association does not send voting circulars to anybody except to its members. I wonder who gives the Association such authority. It is the duty of Shanghai Municipal Council to see that the voting for election to be carried out according to the regulations of Yangkingpang or for the interest of the majority of Chinese tax-payers and not according to the wishes of the present executive committee of the above Association.
Will some body propose a remedy?
Yours truly,
TAXATION WITHOUT PROPER REPRESENTATION.
Shanghai, April 6th 1940.
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》

1940年4月1日

华董选举

致《大美晚报》编辑：
先生，——华人纳税人协会自行规定，只有该协会会员才能在上海市公共租界工部局选举中投票选举华董，而据我理解，根据《洋泾浜章程》，选举资格是：任何居住在租界内，并每年缴纳土地税达规银10两，或按租金缴纳市政捐达规银41.61两（或80.00美元）的人，均有权投票。数百名具备上述资格的老中国居民因此被剥夺了投票特权。此外，华人纳税人协会除向其会员外，不向任何人发送投票通告。我想知道是谁赋予了该协会这样的权力。上海公共租界工部局有责任确保选举投票按照《洋泾浜章程》的规定进行，或者为了大多数中国纳税人的利益进行，而不是按照上述协会现任执行委员会的意愿进行。
有人能提出补救办法吗？
此致
敬礼
无代表而纳税者
上海，1940年4月6日。

1940年

华董
正式任命

工部局已收到华人纳税人协会的通知，在中国纳税人代表会议上，选举余亚清（Yu Ya Ching）、袁履登（L. T. Yuan）、郭克生（W. Gockson）、江一平（E. Y. B. Kiang）和席玉麟（Yulin Hsi）诸先生为1940-41年度上海公共租界工部局董事。

page_data.en:
1940
Land Regulations
Reform Wanted
Japanese Spokesman on
Election Result; Aims to
Be Achieved

The final objective of the Japanese
Government is the abolition of ex-
traterritoriality in China and the
return to the Chinese people of all
concessions and settlements, Mr. K.
Tsurumi, Japanese Embassy spokes-
man, revealed at the Japanese press
conference yesterday in a lengthy
comment on the result of the Shang-
hai municipal election held on Wed-
nesday and Thursday. If these aims
could not be achieved at the present
time, he said, the reform of the
administration and constitution of
the International Settlement was
required by the Japanese.

Mr. Tsurumi congratulated the
successful candidates in the election
which, he said, was a sort of game
that should be conducted according
to the rules of sport whereby the
loser should congratulate the win-
ner. As a result of the election,
however, the feeling among the
Japanese people in Shanghai that
the administration of the Settlement
ought to be more international had
only been intensified.

The Japanese community, Mr.
Tsurumi went on, would continue
its efforts to carry out its convic-
tions that the International Settle-
ment of Shanghai should be a place
suitable for everybody to live in.
This could only be accomplished
when the place lived up to its name
of International Settlement.

Japanese Objective

An election always was carried
out on the assumption that it was
conducted justly and fairly, and in
commenting on this, Mr. Tsurumi
stated that facts would have to be
investigated before any comment
could be made as to the fairness of
the election. The object of the
Japanese was to secure fair repre-
sentation in the affairs of the Inter-
national Settlement and this objec-
tive, he hoped, would be achieved by
lawful means. He added that the
Japanese would not resort to unlaw-
ful means to secure this objective.

The tendency in the world today
was to permit suffrage to be carried
out on a universal basis and not
under the restriction of property own-
ed by certain people. In Shanghai,
however, there still be seemed to
be an anachronistic system whereby
a man was allowed to vote if he
possessed sufficient property. That
Shanghai was still allowing this
system to operate only showed how
anachronistic the regulations in the
Settlement were.

Mr. Tsurumi said that if he went
to extremes he could easily say
that the council should be run by
the nine largest landowners in the
Settlement or by the nine richest
millionaires, if there were nine. The
Japanese objective was to obtain a
reform of the Land Regulations and
this matter would have to be settled
by the Council and the Consular
Body.

The Land Regulations, he said,
were archaic. They were introduced
in 1845 and were revised a long
time ago. In a world that was
moving forward, it was a pity that
such a statute governed the ruling
of the Settlement today.
page_data.zh:
1940年
要求改革
《土地章程》
日本发言人谈
选举结果；旨在
实现目标

日本大使馆发言人鹤见（K. Tsurumi）先生昨日在日本记者招待会上，就周三和周四举行的上海市政选举结果发表了长篇评论，透露日本政府的最终目标是废除在华治外法权，并将所有租界和居留地归还给中国人民。他说，如果目前无法实现这些目标，日本方面要求对国际租界的行政管理和组织结构进行改革。

鹤见先生祝贺在选举中获胜的候选人，他说，选举是一种游戏，应该按照体育运动的规则进行，败者应向胜者表示祝贺。然而，选举的结果只是加剧了上海日本民众中认为租界行政管理应当更加国际化的情绪。

鹤见先生接着说，日本侨民将继续努力贯彻其信念，即上海公共租界应当成为一个适合所有人居住的地方。只有当这个地方名副其实地成为“国际”租界时，才能实现这一目标。

日本的目标

选举总是基于公正公平进行的假设而开展的，对此，鹤见先生表示，在对选举的公正性发表评论之前，必须调查事实。日本人的目标是在国际租界的事务中获得公平的代表权，他希望这一目标能通过合法手段实现。他补充说，日本人不会采取非法手段来实现这一目标。

当今世界的趋势是允许在普遍基础上进行选举，而不是受限于某些人拥有的财产。然而，在上海，似乎仍然存在一种过时的制度，即一个人如果拥有足够的财产就被允许投票。上海仍然允许这种制度运行，这只能说明租界的规章是多么过时。

鹤见先生说，如果走极端的话，他可以轻易地说，董事会应该由租界中最大的九位地主来管理，或者如果有九位的话，由最富有的九位百万富翁来管理。日本人的目标是求得《土地章程》的改革，此事必须由工部局和领事团解决。

他说，《土地章程》已经陈旧不堪。它们是在1845年引入的，并在很久以前进行过修订。在一个不断前进的世界里，令人遗憾的是，今天统治租界的仍然是这样一部法规。

April 12, 1940.
Afternoon Translation.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO.

BRITISH RESIDENTS INCREASED VOTES IN AN
UNGENTLEMANLY WAY.

Perturbed by the unfavourable situation
in the Municipal elections on April 10, the British
Election Committee, with the understanding of the Revenue
Office of the S.M.C., which preserved the right to issue
the voting passes, started work to increase the number
of British votes. It is believed that more than 2,000
votes were created during one day.
When Japanese applied for voting passes,
the Revenue Office conducted a thorough investigation
regarding their qualifications. The Revenue Office and
the British Election Committee can be said to be one body
for the former gave every possible facility to the latter
with a view to defeating the Japanese, ignoring the
sacredness of the elections and the principles of democracy.
Furthermore they closed the main entrance of the polling
booth in the S.V.C. drill hall at 3 p.m. as scheduled, but
secretly admitted foreign voters through the back door after
3 p.m. The Japanese residents are paying great attention
to this fact.
The way of voting was advantageous to
British and American residents but inconvenient to Japanese
from start to finish. This matter will be taken up after
the elections this year.

1940年4月12日。
下午译文。

《大陆新报》。

英国居民以不绅士的方式增加票数。

英国选举委员会对4月10日工部局选举中的不利局势感到不安，在拥有签发投票通行证权利的工部局捐务处的谅解下，开始着手增加英国人的票数。据悉，一天之内就制造了2000多张选票。
当日本人申请投票通行证时，捐务处对其资格进行了彻底调查。可以说捐务处与英国选举委员会是一体的，因为前者为了击败日本人，无视选举的神圣性和民主原则，为后者提供了一切可能的便利。此外，他们按计划在下午3点关闭了位于万国商团操厅的投票站正门，但在下午3点后秘密通过后门放外国选民进入。日本居民非常关注这一事实。
从头到尾，投票方式都有利于英美居民，而不利于日本人。此事将在今年选举后提出。
