April 11, 1940
Morning Translation

Central China Daily News (Editorial) :-

RECOVERY OF FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS IN RELATION TO THE
MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS.

We have already told the general public that
what the Chinese people should do is to recover the Foreign
Settlements in China. How should we effect the recovery
of these Settlements? There are many ways and means that
may be adopted to attain this end. For instance, negotiations
may be opened, or steps may be taken to recover the Settlements
by compulsory means, or even the policy of blockade may be
adopted. What steps should be taken depends upon whether
the opposite side is sincere or not.
If the Foreign Settlements cannot be recovered
in entirety immediately, at least the recovery should be
effected by degrees. Which parts of the Settlements should
be taken back immediately? Firstly, the Chinese banking
organizations in the Settlements must be placed under the
direct control of the Chinese Government for these banking
organizations are continuing acts against the Chinese
Government and the Chinese people under the shelter of the
Settlements. For the sake of its existence and of the
welfare of the people, the Chinese Government must have the
power to direct or ban banking organizations throughout the
country, including the banks in the Foreign Settlements.
Secondly, the Chinese propaganda organizations
in the Foreign Settlements must be placed under the direct
control of the Chinese Government. There are many Chinese
newspapers under foreign names, that are publishing
propaganda matter detrimental to the Chinese Government
in the Settlements; this must be thoroughly suppressed.
As to bona fide foreign-managed newspapers which interfere
with the home and foreign affairs of the Chinese Government
in violation of their neutrality, the Chinese Government
should also exercise its authority against these newspapers.
Thirdly, the reason given by foreigners for
the establishment of the Foreign Settlements being to do
business, the Chinese Government has the right to interfere
with any political activities in the Settlements except
the administration of the Settlement authorities, in order
to guard against political intrigues endangering the
existence of China that may be conducted under the cover
of the Settlements.
When the above three things have been carried
out, the Foreign Settlements will return to their original
status, that is to say, places for foreigners to do business.
The best way to obtain the retrocession of the Foreign
Settlements is to open negotiations first, and whether
steps should be taken to recover the Settlements by compulsory
means will be decided in the light of the result of these
negotiations. At first, the political franchise of the
Settlements should be removed and then their commercial
franchise should be eliminated.
We should hereafter make endeavours to recover
the Foreign Settlements according to the abovementioned
formula. Japan has indicated that she will assist China
to effect the retrocession of the Foreign Settlements.

1940年4月11日
上午译文

《华中日报》（社论）：

结合工部局选举谈收回外国租界。

我们已告知公众，中国人民应当做的是收回在中国的外国租界。我们应如何实现这些租界的收回？有许多方法和手段可以采用以达到此目的。例如，可以开启谈判，或者采取强制手段收回租界，甚至可以采取封锁政策。采取何种步骤取决于对方是否真诚。
如果无法立即完全收回外国租界，至少应逐步实现收回。应立即收回租界的哪些部分？首先，租界内的中国银行机构必须置于中国政府的直接控制之下，因为这些银行机构在租界的庇护下继续从事反对中国政府和中国人民的活动。为了自身的存在和人民的福祉，中国政府必须拥有指导或禁止全国银行机构（包括外国租界内的银行）的权力。
其次，外国租界内的中国宣传机构必须置于中国政府的直接控制之下。有许多挂着外国名头的中文报纸，在租界内发布损害中国政府的宣传内容；必须对此进行彻底镇压。至于那些违反中立立场、干涉中国政府内政外交的正牌外人经营的报纸，中国政府也应对这些报纸行使权力。
第三，外国人建立外国租界的理由是经商，因此中国政府有权干涉租界内除租界当局行政管理以外的任何政治活动，以防止借租界为掩护进行危害中国生存的政治阴谋。
当上述三件事得以实施后，外国租界将恢复其原始状态，即成为外国人经商的地方。获得外国租界交还的最佳方式是首先开启谈判，而是否采取强制手段收回租界将根据谈判结果决定。首先应取消租界的政治特权，然后消除其商业特权。
此后，我们将按照上述公式努力收回外国租界。日本已表示将协助中国实现外国租界的交还。

page_data.en:
April 11, 1940. Morning Translation.

As to the present Municipal elections of the
S.M.C., there is no reason why we Chinese people should
help the British and American candidates to win the
competition, because to help the British and American
candidates to win means helping the Settlements to preserve
their present status. The existence of the Settlements
has led to China's present plight. Therefore, we Chinese
rather wish that the Japanese candidates will win in the
Municipal elections on the following grounds :-
(1) The International Settlement with its existing status
is under the control of the British and Americans.
This is a great hindrance to the movement for the
recovery of all Foreign Settlements. This state of
affairs can be removed should the status of the Japanese
in the Settlement be raised. This will prove helpful
to the movement for the recovery of the Foreign
Settlements.
(2) We are entirely convinced that the desire of Japan to
help China to recover the Foreign Settlements is
sincere. When we help the Japanese to improve their
position in the Settlement, it means that we help
ourselves.
The attitude of the Chinese towards the
competition in the Municipal elections of the S.M.C. is as
above and we would like to ask foreigners of other
nationalities to realize that their welfare in the
Settlements in future cannot be assured by the British
and Americans but only by China. These foreigners,
therefore, should attach importance to the attitude of the
Chinese towards the competition in the Municipal elections.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月11日。上午译文。

关于目前工部局的市政选举，我们中国人没有理由帮助英美候选人赢得竞争，因为帮助英美候选人获胜意味着帮助租界维持其现状。租界的存在导致了中国目前的困境。因此，基于以下理由，我们中国人更希望日本候选人在市政选举中获胜：
(1) 国际租界目前的状况处于英美控制之下。这对收回所有外国租界的运动是一个巨大障碍。如果提高日本人在租界的地位，这种状况就可以消除。这将证明有助于收回外国租界的运动。
(2) 我们完全相信日本帮助中国收回外国租界的愿望是真诚的。当我们帮助日本人改善其在租界的地位时，这意味着我们在帮助自己。
中国人对工部局市政选举竞争的态度如上所述，我们要请其他国籍的外国人认识到，他们在租界未来的福利不能由英美保证，而只能由中国保证。因此，这些外国人应重视中国人对市政选举竞争的态度。

Warum alle Emigranten Shanghais fuer die amerikanischen und englischen
Repraesentanten stimmen:

1. Weil wir den beiden grossen republikanischen Nationen dankbar sind, dass sie uns
und unseren Glaubensgenossen in ihren Laendern Aufnahme und Existenz gewaehren.
2. Weil wir unser Dasein hier ihrer finanziellen Unterstuetzung und Hilfe verdanken.
3. Weil wir hier nur in Gemeinschaft mit Englaendern und Amerikanern eine Existenz
werden gruenden und erhalten koennen.
4. Weil die Japaner unseren Angehoerigen die Reise durch Sibirien erneut unmoeglich
machen.
5. Weil die Japaner den gesamten Handel Shanghais fuer sich monopolisieren wollen.
6. Weil die Japaner Hongkew gesperrt haben, dass ihnen nicht einmal gehoert.
7. Weil die Japaner nur Japanern Arbeit und Verdienst geben.
8. Weil die Japaner uns fuer eine Autobusfahrt 20 cents abnehmen, die im Settlement
5 cents kostet.
9. Weil die Japaner uns noch keine 50 Einreisepermits gegeben haben, waehrend die von
dem Englaender Pits gefuehrte Stelle des Settlements bereits ueber 1000 gewaehrt hat.
10. Weil die Japaner unsere Meinung durch Erpressung kaufen wollen und wir uns nicht
erpressen lassen.
11. Weil wir uns in Shanghai eine Heimat gruenden wollen und muessen, und unsere
Interessen darum auf Seiten der Englaender und Amerikaner sind.
12. Weil, wenn die Japaner den groesseren Einfluss gewinnen, die Steuern sprunghaft in
die Hoehe schnellen werden.

Wenn Sie Ihrem Schicksal nicht asiatische Gleichgueltigkeit und Interessenlosigkeit
gegenueberstellen wollen, dann wissen Sie, was Sie, zu tun haben!

Sie muessen sicher sein, nur fuer die 5 Englischen und Amerikanischen Kandidaten
zu waehlen,

WAEHLEN SIE NICHT FUER
RANALD Mc DONALD
page_data.zh:
为什么所有上海移民都投票给美国和英国代表：

1. 因为我们感谢这两个伟大的共和制国家，因为它们允许我们和我们的教友在其国土上居住和生存。
2. 因为我们的生计得益于他们的财政支持和帮助。
3. 因为只有与英国人和美国人在一起，我们才能在此建立并维持生计。
4. 因为日本人再次使我们的亲属无法经由西伯利亚旅行。
5. 因为日本人想要垄断上海的所有贸易。
6. 因为日本人封锁了虹口，而那里甚至不属于他们。
7. 因为日本人只给日本人提供工作和收入。
8. 因为日本人收取我们20分钱的公交车费，而在租界内只需5分钱。
9. 因为日本人尚未给我们发放50份入境许可证，而由英国人皮茨（Pits）负责的租界机构已经发放了超过1000份。
10. 因为日本人想通过勒索收买我们的意见，而我们不接受勒索。
11. 因为我们想要且必须在上海建立一个家园，因此我们的利益站在英国人和美国人一边。
12. 因为如果日本人获得更大的影响力，税收将会急剧飙升。

如果您不想以亚洲式的冷漠和无动于衷来面对您的命运，那么您就知道该做什么了！

您必须确保只投票给那5位英国和美国候选人，

不要投票给
拉纳德·麦克唐纳（RANALD Mc DONALD）

page_data.en:
TRANSLATION FROM GERMAN

Why all Shanghai emigrants are voting for the American
and British candidates:

1. Because we are thankful to the two great democracies since
they allow our co-religionists to exist in their lands.
2. Because we owe our livelihood to their financial aid.
3. Because we will be able to live and create an existence
only with the English and Americans.
4. Because the Japanese are again preventing our relatives from
travelling via Liberia.
5. Because the Japanese desire to monopolize all Shanghai trade.
6. Because the Japanese have closed Hongkew which does not even
belong to them.
7. Because the Japanese are giving employment and work to Japanese
only.
8. Because the Japanese charge 20 cents for a bus-fare which
costs 5 cents in the Settlement.
9. Because the Japanese have not yet given us 50 landing permits
whereas the Settlement office in charge of the Englishman Pitts
has given us over a 1000.
10. Because the Japanese want to secure our opinion by blackmail,
but we do not wish to be intimidated.
11. Because we want to and have to found a home in Shanghai and
our interests consequently are the same as the English and
American.
12. Because if the Japanese gain bigger influence taxes will
rapidly increase.

If you do not wish to view the future with Asiatic stoicism
and disinterestedness, then you know what you have to do.
You must be sure to vote for the 5 English and American
candidates.

DO NOT VOTE FOR RONALD McDONALD.

“Anglo-Saxon” Front
Candidates Triumph
By Substantial Margin

The attempted Japanese “blitzkrieg” through the local polls floundered yesterday without reaching its objective, namely the election of five Japanese to the Shanghai Municipal Council.

The “Anglo-Saxon” front turned out to the polls en bloc and elected the seven approved British and American candidates by majorities ranging from 2,800 to more than 2,000. In other words, the Japanese were “snowed” under, gaining only the usual traditional two seats on the S.M.C.

Defeated Candidates
I. Okamoto . . . . . . 4,903.
K. Kuroda . . . . . . 5,198.
O. Okamoto . . . . . . 5,187.
Ronald G. McDonald . . 285.
Largest In History
The total vote polled during the elections was the largest in the history of this city, vivid evidence of the concerted efforts displayed by the British and American election committees to get their ratepayers to the polls. The total ballot was 13,008 and of this number, 98 votes were declared invalid for the final valid count of 13,000.

The scrutineers, Mr. Hans Berents and Mr. A. Bringert, did not complete the job of counting the votes until 3.30 a.m. today.

As minutes dragged by towards the hour when the future of the International Settlement administration would be decided, Shanghai was quiet but it was not asleep.

Unceasing Telephone Calls
Telephone calls poured into newspaper offices, all asking the same excited questions: “Who won the elections?” “Has the status quo been preserved?” More than 150 calls were received in the offices of THE CHINA PRESS alone after midnight, definite indication that a large section of the city was remaining awake to hear the final results of the balloting.

Apparently suspecting that the Japanese cause was lost before the voting came to an end yesterday afternoon, the local Japanese press yesterday started to hint that it was displeased with the balloting system.

The Shanghai Mainichi charged that “the action of British residents in trying to suppress Japanese rate-payers at the elections by taking advantage of the authority of the Municipal Council has given rise to much indignation in various circles.”

The Mainichi and the Tairiku Shimpo alleged insufficient accommodations were provided by the Council for the Japanese voters. Incidentally, this was the same allegation made by many foreign voters in regard to the accommodations they received.

Officials Miscalculate
The fact that the voting was light both at Hongkew and at the S.V.C. Drill Hall yesterday indicates that the Council officials in charge of arrangements had miscalculated on the size of the crowds that would turn out on the first day of the elections. They had expected less congestion on the opening day and more voting on the second.

What actually happened is that a jam occurred on Wednesday while the voting slumped off yesterday, less than 3,000 votes being cast while some 11,000 votes were cast on the day previous.

However, the Japanese press maintains it was all a trick intended to slow up the Japanese voters. Said the Mainichi:
“The British residents evidently thought that busy Japanese rate-payers would not be able to wait a long time to change their voting passes for ballot papers. They believed the Japanese would eventually abandon their desire to vote and that was why they adopted such measures to suppress the Japanese rate-payers.

“This cunning trick,” continued the same paper, “constitutes a violation of the secrecy of the elections and has given rise to high indignation among Japanese rate-payers. It is said that Japanese residents may lodge a strong protest in this connection.”

S.M.C. officials denied these allegations last night and maintained that they had expected to handle about 1,200 votes hourly on both days of the election at the two polling places. They had not anticipated such a heavy jam on Wednesday and were required to handle more than 2,000 votes an hour while on Thursday, the voting was comparatively quiet.

1940年11月19日

“盎格鲁-撒克逊”阵线
候选人以压倒性优势获胜

日本方面试图通过本地投票发动的“闪电战”昨日受挫，未能实现其目标，即选举五名日本人进入上海工部局董事会。

“盎格鲁-撒克逊”阵线的选民集体前往投票站，使七名获认可的英、美候选人以2,800票至2,000多票不等的多数票当选。换言之，日本人被彻底击败，仅获得在上海工部局董事会中通常传统的两个席位。

以下是截至今日凌晨3时30分统计的最终选举结果：
N. F. Allman . . . . . . 8,000票。
J. W. Carney . . . . . . 7,908票。

落选候选人

创历史最高纪录
本次选举的总投票数是本市历史上最高的，这生动地证明了英美选举委员会为动员纳税人投票所做出的协同努力。总票数为13,008票，其中98票被宣布无效，最终有效计票数为13,000票。

监票员Hans Berents先生和A. Bringert先生直到今天凌晨3时30分才完成计票工作。

随着决定国际租界行政未来命运的时刻一分一秒地临近，上海虽然安静，但并未沉睡。

电话铃声不断
各报社的电话铃声此起彼伏，询问的都是同样令人激动的问题：“谁赢得了选举？”“现状是否得以保持？”仅《字林西报》社在午夜后就接到了150多个电话，这明确表明，本市很大一部分居民一直未眠，等待听取投票的最终结果。

日本媒体显然怀疑在昨天下午投票结束前，日本的竞选事业已告失败，因此当地日本报纸昨天开始暗示其对投票制度表示不满。

《上海每日新闻》指责称，“英国居民利用工部局的权威，试图在选举中压制日本纳税人，此举在各阶层引起了极大愤慨。”

《上海每日新闻》和《大陆新报》指控工部局为日本选民提供的设施不足。顺便提一下，许多外国选民也就他们受到的接待提出了同样的指控。

官员误判
昨天在虹口和上海志愿者公司（S.V.C.）操厅的投票人数均较少，这一事实表明，负责安排工作的工部局官员误判了选举第一天会出现的人群规模。他们原以为开幕当天拥挤程度会较轻，而第二天的投票人数会更多。

实际情况是，周三出现了拥堵，而昨天的投票人数骤减，昨天投票数不到3,000票，而前一天约为11,000票。

然而，日本媒体坚持认为这全是为了延缓日本选民投票而设下的圈套。《上海每日新闻》称：
“英国居民显然认为，忙碌的日本纳税人无法长时间等待将投票证换成选票。他们认为日本人最终会放弃投票意愿，因此采取了此类措施来压制日本纳税人。

“这种狡猾的手段，”该报继续说道，“构成了对选举保密性的违反，并在日本纳税人中引起了高度愤慨。据悉，日本居民可能会就此提出强烈抗议。”

工部局官员昨晚否认了这些指控，并坚称他们预计两天内在两个投票点每小时处理约1,200张选票。他们未预料到周三会出现如此严重的拥堵，当时不得不每小时处理超过2,000张选票，而周四的投票情况则相对平静。

归档

CHINA PRESS.
APR 1, 1940

Review Hits Out
Frank Comment
On Elections
In Weekly Here

The Municipal elections which ended yesterday are called "farcical and probably illegal" by a hard-hitting editorial in the current issue of the China Weekly Review, which will be on the news-stands to-morrow.

The Japanese "debauched the democratic machinery with methods reminiscent of the worst periods of corrupt municipal administration in western lands....by padding their lists with hundreds or even thousands of names of persons who had no legitimate right to vote," the editorial states, adding that the money supplied for the payment of taxes, probably came from the Japanese Army's secret fund.

Charging that the consent of foreign leaders to hold the election under these circumstances "reflected little credit on either their intelligence or courage," the editorial said that "apparently the foreigners were committed to an agreement made by the chairman, whereby they were compelled to accept lists of voters supplied by the Japanese Residents' Corporation."

Delving into greater detail on the election methods employed by the Japanese, the editorial says: "Six months ago the Japanese had approximately 800 votes. By utilizing their carpet-baggers, ronin and other hangers-on of the Army, they artificially expanded their list to more than 3,000.

"Up to a few weeks ago it was practically impossible for the Municipal Treasury to collect taxes from Japanese property owners. But when they realized that it was necessary to pay their taxes in order to obtain the right to vote, they almost overwhelmed the tax office with the amount of overdue revenues they dumped on the counter."

The article concludes by saying that "the foreigners themselves should do some house-cleaning after the election smoke has blown away." In particular, it says that, "something should be done to clear up scandals, rumors which have circulated in Shanghai for many years, alleging the receipt of bribes by high officials of the Settlement."

坦率评论
选举
见于本周本地周刊

昨天结束的市政选举被《密勒氏评论报》本期一篇措辞严厉的社论称为“滑稽且可能非法”，该刊将于明天上架发售。

社论指出，日本人“用让人想起西方土地上市政管理最腐败时期的方法败坏了民主机制……通过在其名单中填充数百甚至数千个没有合法投票权的人名”，并补充说，用于缴纳税款的资金可能来自日本陆军的秘密基金。

社论指责外国领袖同意在这种情况下举行选举，“既不能彰显他们的智慧，也不能彰显他们的勇气”，并称“显然，外国人已受制于主席达成的一项协议，据此他们被迫接受由日本居留民团提供的选民名单”。

在更详细地探究日本人所采用的选举手段时，社论称：“六个月前，日本人仅有约800张选票。通过利用其投机分子、浪人以及军队的其他依附者，他们人为地将名单扩充至3,000多人。

CHINA PRESS
APR 1 2 1940

We, The People

THE CHINA PRESS welcomes the views of its readers on subjects of the day, but publication in the correspondence column does not mean necessarily that the views expressed by correspondents are those of THE CHINA PRESS.

A Chinese View On S.M.C.

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.
Sir,—I fully realize that a Chinese taxpayer has no voice whatever in the municipal affairs of the International Settlement of Shanghai. But that does not mean that he cannot express his views and opinions on problems that affect the daily life of several million Chinese residents in this international community.
For the last few days the S.M.C. elections have been the center of interest in the local press. Foreign residents are making a big fuss over the nomination of candidates and election of councilmen. Since the Japanese recently came out in the open to demand 5 seats on the S.M.C., the Americans and Britons are now in an uproar for the maintenance of the so-called status quo of international representation, meaning the proportion of Council seats on a 5-2-2 basis among British, American and Japanese representatives.
While the Japanese are agitating for increased representation on the S.M.C. with plausible reasons, the British and Americans are highly apprehensive of the consequences of Japanese domination over the municipal administration of the Shanghai International Settlement. In fairness to all nationalities the number and proportion of seats on the S.M.C. should be readjusted and adapted to changed conditions. There is no reason under the sun why the S.M.C. should be dominated and controlled by any single nationality. In an international community everything should be done in a co-operative spirit and on a democratic basis. And isn't the International Settlement of Shanghai a "democracy"—and not a "bureaucracy"?
Yet it is painful to admit that the S.M.C. has been traditionally dominated by British nationals and inefficiently administered by the so-called "pivot boys" with their salaries partly or entirely on sterling basis. For years the S.M.C. authorities have played the part of "rubber stamps" with no brain power to devise and adopt proper measures of financial retrenchment and municipal economy. In their secure and powerful position they have pretended to be blind and deaf to popular protest against their autocratic method of running the International Settlement. The concrete proof of their incompetency may be found in the tyrannical imposition of municipal taxes beginning from July this year. The dogmatic attitude of the S.M.C. authorities in the financial administration of the Settlement is too much colored by an air of British colonialism. The S.M.C. authorities have been incurably addicted to the habits of a spendthrift. Why shouldn't they spend freely and carelessly, if they could always call upon the taxpayers (mostly Chinese) to foot the bill through the instrumentality of higher taxes and more loans?
The recent announcement of the S.M.C. to effect a "tax hike" by 50 per cent and secure a $10,000,000 (Chinese currency) loan from the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation in order to cover a deficit of some $6,000,000 is an elementary trick to shield a state of inefficiency in municipal administration. In contrast to the financial conditions in the French Concession life is happier in a "bureaucracy" than in a "democracy." This is at least true so far as the living conditions of the Chinese residents in both areas are concerned. It is most amazing to note that the editorial comments of local periodicals published by British subjects are still taking an apologetic and condolent attitude toward every move of the S.M.C. authorities.
Much ink has been spilled on the salary question of the high officials of the Council. As the cat is now out of the bag, we might just as well discuss the matter openly. In the first place, there is no question that the No. 1 official and Class "A" employees (now better known as "pivot boys" in local parlance) are over-paid. Frankly speaking, if they cannot live in China on a salary commensurate with Chinese living conditions, why can't they immediately return to the land of their nativity and live comfortably on a fat income in sterling? It is obviously unfair and even ridiculous to earn a good living in China on sterling basis and pay one's expenses in "fapi" according to commodity prices prevailing in the Chinese market. Honestly, I don't believe that every Briton or American buys and uses nothing but imported articles from his homeland. No wonder, adventurous foreigners like to come and stay in Shanghai with the hope of making a fortune in the shortest possible time. And do I need to add that many did? Thus the over-paid S.M.C. officials have ceased to be public servants in the proper sense of the term, because they are earning a big salary at the expense of the ratepayers and even in competition with fellow employees of lower ranks.
In a word, the ratepayers, especially the Chinese ratepayers, are just "fed up with" such heavy SMC and salary basis. We are perfectly willing to pay honest workers of whatever nationality for the competent management of municipal affairs in Shanghai; but we absolutely refuse to support any S.M.C. employee, Chinese or foreign, of the parasitical type. Likewise, we demand the drastic reduction, if not the outright abolition, of the so-called "retirement benefits" of former S.M.C. employees in British or Chinese currency, for they are downright parasites of colonial exploitation on Chinese soil.
Now the municipal elections of the International Settlement are already on. The contest between the Anglo-American group and the Japanese group is bound to be keen and bitter. It is difficult to predict the result of this election, but it is easy to tell that the election results will have far-reaching consequences. Whether or not the status quo of Council seats on a 5-2-2 basis will be maintained, the fate of the S.M.C. hangs in the balance. One thing is sure: the Japanese will ask for a louder voice in the municipal administration of the Shanghai International Settlement—and they are going to get it even if the 5-2-2 ratio is kept intact. For the British are ever ready to take a realistic policy to appease the Japanese by making all sorts of adjustments, compromises and concessions to keep them quiet. But I am afraid the days of British domination in the International Settlement are numbered and the tottering position of British "rulers" is ready to crumble before long.
The current elections will decide whether the International Settlement will henceforth be dominated and controlled by the British or by the Japanese. To the Chinese ratepayers the S.M.C. under British or Japanese domination is a concrete case of relativity. For there is not much choice between the greater or lesser evil. The Chinese ratepayers were, are, and will probably remain "the forgotten men"—the scapegoats of municipal maladministration and victims of colonial exploitation. It may be argued that this is no time to "change horses in mid-stream," especially when China is at war with Japan with Shanghai temporarily under Japanese military influence. But the International Settlement of Shanghai is "international" in character and its municipal affairs

《字林西报》
1940年4月12日

我们，人民

《字林西报》欢迎读者就当前时事发表观点，但来信栏刊登这些观点并不必然意味着撰稿人所表达的观点代表《字林西报》的立场。

一位华人对工部局的看法

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——我充分认识到，中国纳税人在上海公共租界的市政事务中没有任何发言权。但这并不意味着他不能就影响这个国际社区中数百万中国居民日常生活的问题表达自己的观点和意见。
过去几天，工部局（S.M.C.）选举一直是当地媒体关注的中心。外籍居民在候选人提名和董事选举问题上大做文章。自从日本人最近公开要求在工部局中占据5个席位以来，美国人和英国人现在为了维护所谓的国际代表权现状而一片哗然，即英、美、日三方代表按5-2-2的比例分配董事会席位。
虽然日本人以看似合理的理由鼓动增加在工部局中的代表权，但英国人和美国人非常担心日本主宰上海公共租界市政管理的后果。为了对所有国籍公平起见，工部局席位的数量和比例应当重新调整，以适应变化了的形势。天下没有理由让工部局被任何单一国籍所主导和控制。在一个国际社区中，一切事务都应以合作精神和民主基础来进行。难道上海公共租界不是一个“民主”政体，而是一个“官僚”政体吗？
然而，令人痛心的是，工部局传统上一直由英国国民主导，并由所谓的“关键人物”（pivot boys，其薪水部分或全部以英镑计发）进行低效管理。多年来，工部局当局扮演着“橡皮图章”的角色，缺乏制定和采取适当财政紧缩及市政节约措施的脑力。凭借其稳固且强大的地位，他们对民众抗议其专制管理公共租界的方式装作视而不见、听而不闻。他们无能的铁证可以从今年七月开始强行征收市政税中找到。工部局当局在租界财务管理上的教条态度带有浓厚的英国殖民主义色彩。工部局当局已经无可救药地染上了挥霍的习惯。如果他们总是可以通过提高税收和增加贷款的手段让纳税人（主要是中国人）来买单，他们为什么不随意且漫不经心地花钱呢？
工部局最近宣布将“增税”50%，并向汇丰银行（Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation）争取一笔1000万元（中国货币）的贷款，以弥补约600万元的赤字，这是掩盖市政管理低效状态的一种初级伎俩。与法租界的财务状况相比，在“官僚”体制下的生活比在“民主”体制下更幸福。至少就这两个区域中国居民的生活条件而言，这是事实。令人惊讶的是，由英国臣民出版的当地期刊的社论评论仍然对工部局当局的每一项举措采取道歉和同情的态度。
关于董事会高级官员的薪水问题，人们已连篇累牍地讨论。既然秘密已经泄露，我们不妨公开讨论此事。首先，毫无疑问，一号官员和“A类”雇员（在当地用语中现在更被称为“关键人物”）薪水过高。坦率地说，如果他们无法依靠与中国生活水平相称的薪水在中国生活，为什么他们不立即返回他们的出生地，靠着丰厚的英镑收入舒适地生活呢？在中国依靠英镑基准赚取优厚生活费用，却按照中国市场 prevailing 的商品价格用“法币”支付开销，这显然是不公平甚至荒谬的。老实说，我不相信每个英国人或美国人只购买和使用来自他们祖国的进口商品。难怪那些爱冒险的外国人喜欢来上海并停留下来，希望在尽可能短的时间内发财致富。而且我需要补充说，许多人确实做到了吗？因此，高薪的工部局官员已不再具有真正意义上的公仆性质，因为他们是以牺牲纳税人利益为代价赚取高薪，甚至与较低层级的同事竞争。
总之，纳税人，尤其是中国纳税人，已经“受够了”如此高昂的工部局薪水和薪资基准。我们完全愿意为任何国籍的诚实工作者支付报酬，以胜任地管理上海的市政事务；但我们绝对拒绝供养任何寄生类型的工部局雇员，无论是中国人还是外国人。同样，我们要求大幅削减，如果不是彻底废除，前工部局雇员以英镑或中国货币支付的所谓“退休福利”，因为他们是在中国土地上进行的殖民剥削的彻头彻尾的寄生虫。
现在，公共租界的市政选举已经开始。英美集团与日本集团之间的竞争注定是激烈且痛苦的。很难预测这次选举的结果，但很容易看出选举结果将产生深远的影响。无论是否维持董事会席位5-2-2比例的现状，工部局的命运都悬而未决。有一件事是肯定的：日本人将要求在上海市公共租界的市政管理中拥有更大的话语权——即使保持5-2-2的比例不变，他们也将得到它。因为英国人随时准备采取现实政策，通过做出各种调整、妥协和让步来安抚日本人，让他们保持安静。但我恐怕英国人在公共租界的主导地位时日无多，英国“统治者”摇摇欲坠的地位不久就会崩溃。
目前的选举将决定公共租界今后是由英国人还是由日本人主导和控制。对中国纳税人来说，处于英国或日本主导下的工部局是一个具体的相对性案例。因为在两害相权取其轻之间没有太多选择。中国纳税人过去是、现在是、并且可能仍然是“被遗忘的人”——市政管理不善的替罪羊和殖民剥削的受害者。有人可能会争辩说，现在不是“临阵换马”的时候，尤其是当中国正与日本交战，而上海暂时处于日本军事影响之下时。但是，上海公共租界具有“国际”性质，其市政事务

ternational" basis. According to the

应当基于“国际”基础进行管理。根据门户开放政策和机会均等原则，不应有任何国籍（无论是英国、日本还是美国）的主导地位。工部局中的民众代表应以上述标准为基础，并经共同同意产生。应当决定是以各国籍的投资总额还是居民总数作为市政代表权的基础。因此，争论英国人应该永远拥有最多的董事会席位，并以可疑的便利条件永远主导和控制市政事务，似乎是徒劳的。

在这次选举之际，让我们既考虑遥远的未来，也考虑眼前的现状。工部局运行不当已是定局。整个市政机器需要彻底检修。不应延误进行必要的调整，以使租界真正成为“国际性”的。必须强调，所有民族群体都有权在上述建议的标准基础上获得平等代表权。当然，作为合法主人的中国人不应再扮演“被遗忘的人”的角色，即在市政事务中几乎没有或完全没有代表权却要缴纳税款。
我再怎么强烈强调也不为过：所有中国纳税人现在必须团结一致，为我们在上海公共租界的公民权利和共同福利而战。对中国人来说，这就是当前市政选举的隐藏含义。其他一切都是表面且不重要的。但是，中国纳税人应当要求在上海工部局中获得平等代表权。

平等代表权。
上海，1940年4月9日。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS

APR 1 2 1940

“Aspersions” Hit
British Straw
Vote Said
Democratic

The secrecy of the British Straw Vote is completely foolproof, and methods employed by the British Election Committee are purely democratic, Mr. H. G. W. Woodhead said at the annual general meeting of the China Association, held in 27 The Bund at 5.15 p.m. yesterday.

Mr. Woodhead made a detailed explanation of workings of the Committee to correct “misunderstanding, genuine or otherwise, which has led to all kinds of aspersions on the methods of nomination and balloting.” “It has been alleged, for instance,” he stated, “that it is a self-constituted committee.”

Ballot slips which are not signed, are numbered solely for the purpose of avoiding duplication or fraud, Mr. Woodhead stated. “The Scrutineers do not have access to the numbered list, and they would only be interested in seeing that no numbers were duplicated, or, where an allegedly invalid ballot slip had been replaced by another, that an illicit vote was not secured by this means,” he added.

Check By Numbers

“If, for instance, Mr. Brown reported that he had never received his ballot slip, the original number of which was 771, he would be given another, but the Scrutineers would be requested to treat slip No. 771 if it appeared in the ballot box as invalid,” Mr. Woodhead explained.

“It is scarcely necessary to add that one of the objects of enlisting the honorary services of prominent Chartered Accountants was to ensure that the secrecy of the ballot should be maintained.”

Tracing the history of the British Election Committee, Mr. Woodhead recalled that in 1936 it became evident that if the balance of power in the Settlement administration was to be maintained it was imperative to organize and mobilize the British vote.

“Ticket” Nominated

Accordingly, Mr. Woodhead continued, the three local British Committees decided to nominate a British “ticket” of five candidates: Messrs. H. E. Arnold, V. St. J. Killery, W. P. Lambe, J. H. Liddell, and H. Porter.

“This action was criticised in some quarters,” the speaker continued. “Two independent candidates, one a Briton and the other of another foreign nationality, were nominated. But the official ticket was adopted.”

Attendance at the polls that year was said to be “deplorable,” and as a result the two Japanese candidates headed the list by several hundred votes. “It was evident that different tactics would have to be adopted if the British voting strength was to make itself felt,” said Mr. Woodhead.

Vote Mobilized

At a second joint meeting of the three Committees held in October, 1938, it was decided to appoint an Executive sub-Committee with power to employ a paid organiser to mobilise the British vote, it was continued. Lt. Colonel Hayley Bell was then appointed as paid Election Agent. The name of the Committee was changed to “British Election Committee.”

“This Committee felt that the practice of nominating its own ticket was open to serious criticism, and that it would be more in accordance with democratic principles to call for nominations, and if they exceeded five in number, to select the British candidates by Straw Vote,” the speaker went on.

“The Committee approached 19 qualified ratepayers, to stand for this poll, and also invited outside nominations. Eventually ten candidates were duly proposed and seconded. It was recognized that some precautions must be taken to prevent duplication or forgery of ballot slips, so each slip was countersigned by the Election Agent.

Japanese Defeated

“The result of this step was to increase the votes polled at the 1938 election to 3,166, of which all British and American candidates received over 1,800, and the Japanese fell to the bottom of the list with under 900.

“It will be recalled that an unfortunate contretemps, due to the overlooking of ballot papers, invalidated this election. But the Japanese then withdrew their third candidate so that a second election became unnecessary,” Mr. Woodhead said.

The meeting concluded with the election of the new Committee as follows: Mr. J. R. Jones, M. C., Mr. P. W. Massey, Mr. M. Mellor, Mr. W. P. Rial, and Mr. H. G. W. Woodhead, C. B. E.

《字林西报》

1940年4月12日

“诽谤”击中
英国模拟投票
据称投票
具有民主性

H. G. W. 伍德黑德（Woodhead）先生昨日午后5时15分在外滩27号举行的英人协会（China Association）年度大会上表示，英国模拟投票（Straw Vote）的保密性完全无懈可击，且英国选举委员会所采用的方法纯粹是民主的。

伍德黑德先生详细解释了委员会的运作情况，以纠正“导致对提名和投票方法产生各种诽谤的误解，无论这些误解是出于真诚还是其他原因”。他陈述道：“例如，有人指控该委员会是自封的。”

伍德黑德先生指出，未签名的选票仅编有号码，目的是为了避免重复或舞弊。他补充说：“监票人无法接触编号名单，他们只关心确保没有号码重复，或者在据称无效的选票被另一张替换的情况下，确保没有通过这种手段获取非法选票。”

按号码核查

伍德黑德先生解释道：“例如，如果布朗（Brown）先生报告说他从未收到其原始编号为771的选票，他将获得另一张选票，但会要求监票人将出现在票箱中的第771号选票视为无效。”

“几乎无需补充说明，聘请知名特许会计师提供荣誉服务的目的之一，就是确保投票的保密性得以维持。”

在追溯英国选举委员会的历史时，伍德黑德先生回忆说，1936年情况已变得明显，如果要维持租界行政中的权力平衡，就必须组织和动员英国人的选票。

提名“名单”

因此，伍德黑德先生继续说道，三个当地英国人委员会决定提名一份由五名候选人组成的英国“名单”：H. E. 阿诺德（Arnold）、V. St. J. 基勒里（Killery）、W. P. 兰贝（Lambe）、J. H. 利德尔（Liddell）和 H. 波特（Porter）诸位先生。

发言人继续说道：“这一行动受到了一些方面的批评。两名独立候选人获得提名，一名是英国人，另一名是其他外籍人士。但最终采用了官方名单。”

据说当年的投票出席率“令人惋惜”，结果两名日本候选人以数百票的优势位居榜首。伍德黑德先生说：“显然，如果要让英国的投票力量发挥作用，就必须采取不同的策略。”

动员投票

他接着说，在1938年10月举行的三个委员会的第二次联席会议上，决定任命一个执行小组委员会，有权雇用一名受薪组织者来动员英国人的选票。随后，海利·贝尔（Hayley Bell）中校被任命为受薪选举代理人。委员会的名称改为“英国选举委员会”。

发言人继续说道：“本委员会认为，提名自家名单的做法容易受到严厉批评，而呼吁提名，如果提名人数超过五人，则通过模拟投票选出英国候选人，更符合民主原则。”

“委员会接洽了19位有资格的纳税人参与此次民意测验，并邀请外部提名。最终，十名候选人被正式提议和附议。人们认识到必须采取一些预防措施以防止选票重复或伪造，因此每张选票均由选举代理人副署。”

日本人落败

“这一步骤的结果是，1938年选举的投票数增加到3,166票，其中所有英国和美国候选人都获得了超过1,800票，而日本人则以不足900票跌至榜尾。

“值得一提的是，由于疏忽遗漏了选票，发生了一次不幸的意外事件，导致这次选举无效。但随后日本人撤回了他们的第三名候选人，因此无需进行第二次选举，”伍德黑德先生说。

会议最后选举产生了新委员会，成员如下：J. R. 琼斯（Jones）先生（获军事十字勋章），P. W. 马西（Massey）先生，M. 梅勒（Mellor）先生，W. P. 里亚尔（Rial）先生，以及 H. G. W. 伍德黑德（Woodhead）先生（获大英帝国司令勋章）。

CHINA PRESS.

APR 1 2 1940

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL Q. ALCOTT

Election Sidelights
DESPITE the apathy of the Shanghai ratepayer in years past, the fellow has just given vivid evidence of his ability to rise to an occasion when the political situation in the International Settlement becomes a bit serious. The so-called units "Anglo-Saxon" front was more solid than the opposition north of Soochow Creek apparently envisaged when it attempted to obtain domination of the Shanghai Municipal Council by standing five candidates for the elections that closed yesterday.

What the public did not know was the fact that Japanese were counting on more than 5,000 votes when they trooped to the polls on Wednesday morning. This figure included most of the European refugee vote and a 100 per cent "Aryan" German vote. A majority of the latter did not cast their ballots but nevertheless, the Japanese were fairly certain of being able to poll in the neighborhood of the 5,000 mark, come hell or high water.

But what the Japanese were not aware of and the general public as well is the fact that while the Japanese Residents' Corporation were busy drumming up votes by any method that came handy, the British assured themselves of a majority by the subdivision of three of the biggest properties in the city.

Despite this mighty effort, it took a united front of all American and British ratepayers, small and big, to pass the Japanese and show a substantial majority. Evidence that the united front was working almost to a man was to be seen at the end of the first day of the elections. More than 11,000 votes were polled during that period. Early reports placed the minimum at 5,500, but this figure, it was revealed yesterday morning, was about half of the real size of the ballot.

Mr. Ranald O. McDonald, the independent British candidate who jumped the traces after being defeated in the primaries held by his nationals, made a bid for every stray vote. He was the only candidate who had election campaign circulars printed and distributed at the entrances of the voting places. Some of these were in Jewish and made an appeal for the European refugee vote.

Members of the American Election Committee took no chances on having a single vote go astray. Wednesday morning, every American ratepayer received a telegram reminding him of his duty to Shanghai and urging him to exercise his right to vote. And just to make sure that the Americans were turning out, members of the election committee took up posts outside the polls, checked off the name of each American ratepayer as he left the building. Those who failed to vote on the first day were given a reminder by telephone early yesterday. Seven telephones in the American Club were kept busy handling this routine.

The Japanese had a much bigger task on their hands in getting their ratepayers to turn out primarily because they had more ratepayers to handle than did the Americans. The Japanese solved that problem by bringing them to the polls in car and truck load lots. More than 1,500 Japanese were lined up outside the voting booths at the Hongkew Market on the first day of the election long before the polls opened.

Handling the crowds was quite a problem for the election officials. A battery of tellers checked off the names of voters as they lined up and entered the polls and they had their hands full. One of the common complaints was that the number of tellers was not sufficient to take care of the crowd. However, his complaint seemed more or less unjustified when it became known that 11,000 votes had been cast on the first day of the election. Election officials had originally calculated that if they could move fast enough to take care of 3,000 votes an hour, they would be doing well. They did slightly better than this and I presume they should feel satisfied

《字林西报》

1940年4月12日

我常常在想 作者：卡罗尔·Q·奥尔科特（Carroll Q. Alcott）

选举侧记
尽管上海纳税人在过去几年中表现冷漠，但当国际租界的政治局势变得有点严峻时，这家伙刚刚生动地证明了他有能力应对局面。所谓的“盎格鲁-撒克逊”阵线比苏州河北岸的反对派在试图通过参加昨天结束的选举并推出五名候选人来控制上海工部局时所预想的要团结得多。

公众不知道的事实是，日本人在周三上午成群结队前往投票站时，指望获得5,000多张选票。这个数字包括了大多数欧洲难民选票和100%的“雅利安”德国人选票。后者中的大多数人并未投票，但尽管如此，日本人相当确信无论如何都能投出接近5,000票的数字。

但是，日本人和普通公众都不知道的是，当日本居留民团忙于用任何顺手的方法拉票时，英国人通过对市内三处最大产业的分户来确保多数票。

尽管付出了巨大的努力，但仍需所有美国人和英国纳税人，无论大小，组成统一战线，才能超越日本人并显示出实质性的多数优势。在选举第一天结束时，可以看到统一战线几乎全员运作的证据。在此期间投出了超过11,000张选票。早期报告将最低票数定为5,500票，但昨天早上透露，这一数字大约是实际投票规模的一半。

独立英国候选人拉纳德·O·麦克唐纳（Ranald O. McDonald）先生在其同胞举行的初选中落败后脱缰而出，争取每一张散票。他是唯一印制并在投票站入口分发竞选传单的候选人。其中一些传单是用犹太语写的，旨在争取欧洲难民的选票。

美国选举委员会成员不冒任何让一张选票流失的风险。周三早上，每位美国纳税人都收到一封电报，提醒他对上海的义务，并敦促他行使投票权。为了确保美国人出来投票，选举委员会成员在投票站外占据位置，每当一名美国纳税人离开大楼时，就核对他的名字。那些在第一天未投票的人在昨天一早收到了电话提醒。美国俱乐部里的七部电话一直忙于处理这一常规工作。

日本人在让其纳税人出面投票方面面临的任务要大得多，主要是因为他们的纳税人比美国人多。日本人通过将纳税人成车成卡车地拉到投票站来解决这个问题。在选举第一天，投票站开放前很久，就有超过1,500名日本人在虹口市场外的投票亭外排起了长队。

管理人群对选举官员来说是个大问题。一排计票员在选民排队和进入投票站时核对他们的名字，他们忙得不可开交。常见的抱怨之一是计票员数量不足以应付人群。然而，当得知选举第一天投出了11,000张选票时，这种抱怨似乎多少有些不合理。选举官员最初计算，如果他们能足够快地处理每小时3,000张选票，就算做得很好了。他们的表现略好于这个水平，我想他们应该感到满意。

7831
" H O

SHANGHAI NAZIS AND MUNICIPAL
ELECTIONS.

We are informed that in connection with the municipal
elections which will take place to-day and to-morrow a "Ger-
man Election Committee" has been formed consisting of members
of The National Socialist Labour Party. The Committee has ap-
proached separately every member of the German Community resid-
ing in the Settlement and entitled to vote. The Committee has
also advised all German ratepayers entitled to vote,who have
not received voting tickets,to obtain such tickets without delay
"VOTE FOR THE FIVE JAPANESE CANDIDATES" is the slogan of the Na-
tional-Socialist Election Committee.

It is of interest to note that the German Consulate-
General does not come forward openly in connection with this
election campaign. It has been suggested to the German Consu-
late-General that/ it can issue a slogan for German nationals in con-
nection with the municipal elections in the same way as other
foreign consulates do. However, it appears that the Consulate
has not followed this suggestion. According to well informed
circles, the German Consulate-General understands the mentality
and feelings of the Chinese population better than certain of-
ficers of the National-Socialist Party,who have been in Shanghai
for a short time only and evidently underestimate the ability of
the Chinese to form an opinion on political affairs and not to
forget what have learned. This is the reason why the abovementi-
oned slogan was not issued by the German Consulate-General. The
question is open as to whether or not all "Aryan" voters of the
German community will follow the advice of the Nazis.

(10)
A. Perkins
D. S. I.

译自1940年4月10日刊登在德国日报《黄色邮报》（GELBE POST）上的一篇文章。由广东路17号的A.J.斯托弗（Storfer）先生出版和编辑。

7831
" H O

上海纳粹与市政选举。

据悉，针对今天和明天举行的市政选举，成立了一个由民族社会主义劳工党成员组成的“德国选举委员会”。该委员会分别接触了居住在租界并有投票权的德国社区的每一位成员。该委员会还建议所有有投票权但未收到选票的德国纳税人立即获取选票。“投票给五名日本候选人”是民族社会主义选举委员会的口号。

值得注意的是，德国总领事馆并未在此次竞选活动中公开露面。有人向德国总领事馆建议，它可以像其他外国领事馆一样，就市政选举向德国国民发布口号。然而，领事馆似乎并未采纳这一建议。据消息灵通人士称，德国总领事馆比某些仅在沪短期停留、显然低估了中国人对政治事务形成意见能力且不忘所学知识的民族社会主义党军官，更了解中国民众的心态和感受。这就是上述口号未由德国总领事馆发布的原因。德国社区的所有“雅利安”选民是否会听从纳粹的建议，这个问题尚无定论。

(10)
A. 珀金斯（Perkins）
副警务处长

Translation from Russian

APPEALS ADDRESSED TO US

An "initiative group of Russian ratepayers" from the area
North of Creek appeal to us with a request to vote for the
candidates who intend to establish a new order in Shanghai.

From the experience gained in Manchuria, Peking, Tientsin,
Tsingtao and other places we, Russians, know what this order is.
Owing to the establishment of the new order, Russian employees
of the Chinese Eastern Railway were deprived of the hard earned
monies due to them from the superannuation fund; owing to this
new order thousands of Russian employees of that railway were
dismissed or offered a miserable pay; owing to this new order
Russians are arrested and deported from Manchuria without any
trial at court and many people endeavour to escape from the new
order to other cities.

Many thousands of these people are in Shanghai at present.
Ask them about the new order in the places, from which they have
escaped leaving their homes, and you will know whether or not
you want the establishment of the new order in Shanghai.

We are assured by the people from the area North of Creek
that our life is difficult, that we have not equal rights, that
we are treated as inferiors, that we are paid miserable wages
for our work etc.

We cannot boast of living in very good conditions.
However, we would like to ask the agitators in favour of the
establishment of the new order: why their representatives, who
have been members of the Municipal Council for many years, have
never said a word regarding any improvement in the material and
legal position of the Russian community? On the contrary, they
have advocated the disbandment of the Russian Regiment. Their
candidates have no Russians in their employ.

At the same time the candidates standing for the status
quo, namely :
page_data.zh:
译自俄文

致我们的呼吁书

来自苏州河北岸地区的一个“俄罗斯纳税人倡议小组”向我们提出请求，要求投票给那些打算在上海建立新秩序的候选人。

根据我们在满洲、北京、天津、青岛和其他地方获得的经验，我们俄罗斯人知道这种秩序是什么。由于建立了新秩序，中东铁路的俄罗斯雇员被剥夺了他们从养老基金中应得的辛苦钱；由于这种新秩序，该铁路的数千名俄罗斯雇员被解雇或只能接受微薄的薪水；由于这种新秩序，俄罗斯人在未经法庭审判的情况下在满洲被捕并被驱逐出境，许多人试图逃离新秩序前往其他城市。

目前有成千上万这样的人在上海。询问那些逃离家园的人关于他们离开地方的新秩序，你就会知道你是否希望在上海建立新秩序。

苏州河北岸地区的人士向我们保证，我们的生活艰难，我们没有平等的权利，我们被视为下等人，我们的工作报酬微薄等等。

我们不能夸耀生活在非常好的条件下。
然而，我们想问那些鼓吹建立新秩序的宣传者：为什么他们的代表，那些担任工部局董事多年的人，从未就改善俄罗斯社区的物质和法律地位说过一句话？相反，他们主张解散俄罗斯团。他们的候选人中没有雇佣任何俄罗斯人。

与此同时，支持现状的候选人，即：

page_data.en:
- 2 -
N.F. ALMAN
J.W. CARNEY
G.A. HALEY
W.J. KESWICK
RODERICK G. MACDONALD
G.E. MITCHELL
T.S. POWELL

are heads of British and American firms in which thousands of
Russians are employed.

We will keep the above in mind when going to the polling
booths on April 10 and 11. Everyone should go to the polling
booths on those days.

Vote in accordance with the attached form.

On your participation in the elections depends the
question - whether or not the new order will be established in
Shanghai. In other words : whether we can live in Shanghai as
we have been living until the present time or whether we shall
have to flee from Shanghai in the same way as Russians have fled
from the areas where the "new order" has been established.

But where can we go ? Think over this question !

For God's sake do not follow the example of the ignorant
peasant who refused to help to extinguish a fire in his village
because he thought that his own house was out of danger. Let
us join the common effort to extinguish this fire.

Do not forget the destruction of the Memorial Church
at Tientsin which was erected on the common grave of Russian
heroes who gave their lives for our Great Motherland.

Following the establishment of the "new order" in
Shanghai, local Russian churches may expect the same fate.

Oppose the establishment of the "new order".

Everyone to the polling booths !

The secrecy of voting is fully guaranteed.

Russian ratepayers.
April, 1940.

是雇用数千名俄国人的英美商行的负责人。

我们在4月10日和11日前往投票站时，将牢记上述情况。在这两天，每个人都应前往投票站。

请按照附上的表格进行投票。

我们是否参与选举，决定了这样一个问题——上海是否会建立“新秩序”。换句话说：我们是能够像迄今为止那样继续在上海生活，还是不得不像俄国人从那些已建立“新秩序”的地区逃离一样，逃离上海。

但是我们能去哪里呢？请深思这个问题！

看在上帝的份上，不要效仿那个无知的农民，他因为认为自己的房子没有危险而拒绝帮助扑灭村里的火灾。让我们共同努力扑灭这场火灾。

不要忘记天津纪念教堂被毁一事，该教堂是建在为我们的伟大祖国献出生命的俄罗斯英雄们的集体墓地之上的。

随着“新秩序”在上海的建立，当地的俄罗斯教堂可能会面临同样的命运。

page_data.en:
Къ намъ обращаются.

«Иніціативная группа Русскихъ налогоплательщиковъ» изъ за моста
обращается къ намъ и проситъ насъ голосовать за кандидатовъ, стремящих-
ся установить новый порядокъ здѣсь въ Шанхаѣ.
Какой этотъ порядокъ, намъ Русскимъ извѣстно по опыту въ Маньч-
журіи, въ Пекин, Тяньзинѣ, Циндао и др. мѣстахъ. Благодаря нового поряд-
ка на КВжд. русскіе желѣзнодорожные служащіе лишились своихъ защит-
ныхъ денегъ, трудомъ и потомъ заработанныхъ, благодаря новаго порядка
тысячи желѣзнодорожниковъ были уволены или переведены на нищенскіе ок-
лады содержанія, благодаря новаго порядка Русскіе люди безъ суда и слѣд-
ствія арестовываются и въ лучшемъ случаѣ высылаются изъ Маньчжуріи, а
остальные стараются бѣжать отъ новаго порядка кто куда можетъ.
Многіе тысячи изъ нихъ теперь въ Шанхаѣ. Распросите ихъ о сущно-
сти новаго порядка тамъ, откуда они бѣжали, бросивъ насиженные и род-
ные мѣста и Вамъ ясно станетъ: нужно ли этотъ порядокъ возста-
навливать здѣсь.
Изъ за моста насъ увѣряютъ, что намъ живется плохо, что мы не
пользуемся равноправіемъ, что насъ держать въ черномъ тлѣ, что намъ
платятъ гроши и т. д. и тому подобное.
Хвастаться намъ не приходится, что намъ живется хорошо. Но мы
честно спрашиваемъ агитаторовъ новаго порядка, почему ихъ представители,
находясь въ Муниципалитетѣ многіе годы ни однимъ словомъ не обмолвились
объ матеріальномъ и правовомъ улучшеніи положенія Русскихъ, а наоборотъ
добивались расформированія Русскаго волонтерскаго полка и почему ихъ кан-
дидаты не имѣютъ ни одного Русскаго служащаго въ своихъ предпріятіяхъ.
Въ то же время, выставляемые кандидаты стараго порядка, какъ то:

N. F. Alman
J. W. Carney
G. A. Haley
W. J. Keswick
Roderick G. Macdonald
G. E. Mitchell
T. S. Powell

являются руководителями Англіискихъ и Американскихъ фирмъ, гдѣ рабо-
таютъ и имѣютъ кусокъ хлба тысячи Русскихъ людей.
А посему, идя къ Урнамъ 10 и 11 сего апрѣля, будемъ помнить о
вышеизложенномъ.
10 и 11 всѣ къ Урнамъ.
Подавайте свои голоса по прилагаемой формѣ.
Отъ нашего участія въ выборахъ зависитъ: быть или не быть новому
порядку въ Шанхаѣ, а это значитъ: продолжать жить намъ, какъ мы жили въ
Шанхаѣ до сихъ поръ или бѣжать отсюда, какъ разбѣгаются Русскіе люди
изъ тѣхъ мѣстъ, гдѣ водворенъ «новый порядокъ».
Но тогда возникаетъ вопросъ: куда? Подумайте надъ этимъ.
Бога ради не уподобляйтесь Рязанскимъ и Вятскимъ. Помните: наша
Русская хата съ краю и на нее нацливается пожаръ. Погасимъ этотъ пожаръ
нашимъ дружнымъ всполохомъ.
Не забывайте о взорванномъ въ Тяньцзинѣ Храмѣ — Памятникѣ, со-
оруженномъ на Братской могилѣ нашихъ героевъ — воиновъ, погибшихъ за
счастье Родины — Нашей великой Россіи.
Не могутъ ли и здѣсь Святые Храмы подвергнуться при новомъ по-
рядкѣ той же участи.
Не допустимъ возстановленія «Новаго порядка».
Всѣ къ урнамъ какъ одинъ!
Секретъ голосованія гарантированъ на 100%.

Русскіе налогоплательщики.

Апрѣль 1940 года.
page_data.zh:
有人向我们呼吁。

桥那边的“俄罗斯纳税人倡议小组”向我们发出呼吁，请求我们投票支持那些致力于在上海建立新秩序的候选人。
这种秩序是什么样子的，我们俄罗斯人通过在中东铁路、北京、天津、青岛及其他地方的经验已经知晓。由于新秩序，成千上万的中东铁路俄国雇员失去了他们靠辛勤劳动和汗水挣来的退休金；由于新秩序，成千上万的铁路员工被解雇或降至微薄的薪水；由于新秩序，俄罗斯人在未经审判和调查的情况下被捕，最好的情况是被驱逐出满洲，其余的人则尽力逃离新秩序，各奔东西。
现在有成千上万这样的人在上海。向他们询问他们逃离之地的新秩序的实质，他们抛弃了世代居住和熟悉的地方，您就会清楚：是否应该在这里恢复这种秩序。
桥那边的人向我们保证，我们生活困苦，我们没有享有平等权利，我们被置于黑暗之中，我们只得到微薄的报酬等等诸如此类的话。
我们并不夸耀自己生活得很好。但我们诚实地质问新秩序的宣传者，为什么他们的代表在工部局任职多年，却从未提及改善俄罗斯人的物质和法律地位，反而力求解散俄罗斯志愿团，以及为什么他们的候选人在其企业中没有任何俄罗斯雇员。
与此同时，旧秩序推出的候选人，如：

N. F. Alman
J. W. Carney
G. A. Haley
W. J. Keswick
Roderick G. Macdonald
G. E. Mitchell
T. S. Powell

是英国和美国公司的负责人，成千上万的俄罗斯人在那里工作并以此谋生。
因此，在今年4月10日和11日前往投票箱时，我们将铭记上述内容。
10日和11日，所有人都去投票箱。
请按照附带的格式投票。
我们参与选举决定了：上海的新秩序是否存在，这意味着：我们是继续像迄今为止那样在上海生活，还是像俄罗斯人从那些实行“新秩序”的地方四散逃离那样，从这里逃走。
但随之而来的问题是：去哪里？请思考这一点。
看在上帝的份上，不要像梁赞人和维亚特卡人那样。请记住：我们的俄罗斯小屋在边缘，火灾正朝它蔓延。让我们用团结的行动扑灭这场火灾。
不要忘记在天津被炸毁的纪念教堂，它是建在我们的英雄——为祖国的幸福——我们伟大的俄罗斯而牺牲的战士们的集体墓地之上的。
在新秩序下，这里的神圣教堂难道不会遭受同样的命运吗？
我们不允许恢复“新秩序”。
所有人一致前往投票箱！
投票保密性100%得到保证。

俄罗斯纳税人。

1940年4月。

page_data.en:
Die Shanghaier Nazis
und die S.M.C.-Wahl

Wie wir erfahren, hat sich zu
der heute und morgen stattfin
denden Wahl der Councilmit
glieder im Settlement auch ein
"Deutscher Wahlausschuss" ge-
bildet, der aus Mitgliedern der
Nationalsozialistischen Deut-
schen Arbeiterpartei besteht.
Dieser Wahlausschuss wandte
sich einzeln an jedes Mitglied
der "Deutschen Gemeinde",
soweit der Betreffende im Ge-
biete des Settlements wohnt
und das Wahlrecht besitzt. Der
Ausschuss machte sich auch
erboetig, allen denjenigen, die
keine Wahlkarte haben, aber
Anspruch auf eine solche, sie
zu besorgen. Die Parole dieses
nationalsozialistischen Wahl-
ausschusses ist: Stimmt fuer
die fuer... japsischen Kan-
didaten!

Es ist interessant, dass das
deutsche Generalkonsulat bei
dieser Wahlpropaganda nicht
in die Erscheinung tritt. Es ist
dem deutschen Generalkonsulat
wohl nahegelegt worden, es

moechte, wie andere aus-
laendische Vertretungen in
Shanghai, eine Wahlparole fuer
seine Konnationalen ausgeben,
doch ist, wie sich zeigt, das
Generalkonsulat auf diese An-
regungen nicht eingegangen.
Gut informierte Kreise meinen,
das Deutsche Generalkonsulat
habe viel mehr Verstaendnis
fuer Denkart und Gefuehlsein-
stellung der chinesischen Be-
voelkerung als gewisse natio-
nalsozialistische Parteifunktio-
naere, die erst seit kurzem in
Shanghai sind, und die Faehig-
keit der Chinesen, politische
Handlungen zu beurteilen, und
das, was sie einmal wahr-
genommen haben, auch niemals
zu vergessen, offenbar unter-
schaetzen. Darum ist denn
auch die oben erwaehnte
Wahlparole nicht vom General-
konsulat ausgegangen und es
bleibt auch fraglich, ob alle der
deutschen Gemeinde an-
gehoerenden "arischen" Waehler
die nationalsozialistische Parole
befolgen werden.
page_data.zh:
上海的纳粹分子
与工部局选举

据悉，为今日及明日举行的租界董事选举，一个由德意志民族社会主义工人党（纳粹党）成员组成的“德国选举委员会”也已成立。该选举委员会逐一联系了居住在租界区域内并拥有选举权的每一位“德国侨民团”成员。该委员会还主动提出，将为那些虽有权领取但未持有选票的人代为办理选票。这个纳粹选举委员会的口号是：投票支持……日本候选人！

有趣的是，德国总领事馆并未在此次选举宣传中露面。显然曾有人建议德国总领事馆像上海其他外国代表机构一样，向其本国国民发布选举口号，但事实证明，总领事馆并未采纳这些建议。消息灵通人士认为，相比某些近期才抵达上海的纳粹党党务官员，德国总领事馆更能理解中国民众的思维方式和情感倾向；而这些纳粹官员显然低估了中国人评判政治行为的能力，以及中国人一旦察觉某事便永不忘怀的特质。因此，上述选举口号并非出自总领事馆，且属于德国侨民团的“雅利安”选民是否都会遵循这一纳粹口号，也尚存疑问。

REPORT
Date April 8, 1940.

Subject. Attitude of the "Novosti Dnia" towards the forthcoming elections of
the Municipal Council.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason.

Russian daily newspaper "NOVOSTI DNIA" published and edited by Mr. V.A. CHILIKIN, 620 Avenue Foch, in its issue dated 8-4-40 carries the following headlines in connection with the forthcoming municipal elections:-

1. IF YOU WISH TO KEEP THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE INTERNATIONAL SETTLEMENT IN EUROPEAN HANDS; IF YOU WISH A GUARANTY OF PEACEFUL LIFE AND WORK FOR YOURSELF; IF YOU WISH SAFETY AND ORDER IN THE CITY - VOTE FOR THE SEVEN BRITISH AND AMERICAN CANDIDATES ONLY.

2. HARBIN, MUKDEN AND TIENTSIN CAN BEST TELL TO EVERY RESIDENT OF THE SETTLEMENT TO WHOM HE SHOULD GIVE HIS VOTE.

3. IF YOU WISH FURTHER PROSPERITY OF THE RUSSIAN COMMUNITY IN SHANGHAI - VOTE FOR THE EUROPEAN CANDIDATES!

4. EUROPEANS SHOULD VOTE FOR EUROPEANS ONLY.

5. DO NOT ALLOW YOURSELVES TO BE INFLUENCED BY ANY PROMISES-PERSUASION: GIVE YOUR VOTES TO THE EUROPEANS!

6. RUSSIAN RESIDENTS KNOW WELL ALL THE CHARMS OF THE HARBIN MUNICIPAL COUNCIL AND THEREFORE THEY WILL VOTE FOR EUROPEAN CANDIDATES.

7. IF YOU WISH TO KEEP RUSSIAN REGIMENT AND SIMPHONIC ORCHESTRA IN WHICH MANY RUSSIANS ARE EMPLOYED - VOTE FOR EUROPEAN CANDIDATES!

8. ALL RUSSIAN RESIDENTS HAVING THE RIGHT OF VOTE SHOULD CARRY OUT THEIR SOCIAL DUTY.

9. DEFEATISTS FROM THE AREA NORTH OF CREEK. THE GROUP OF ZAITSEFF AND METZLER ATTEMPT TO PERSUADE RUSSIAN RESIDENTS NOT TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FORTHCOMING ELECTIONS. OPEN ANTI-MUNICIPAL COUNCIL PROPAGANDA OF MACHINATORS FROM THE AREA NORTH OF CREEK.

日期：1940年4月8日。

主题：“Novosti Dnia”（《每日新闻》）对即将举行的工部局董事会选举的态度。

制作人：D.S.I. Prokofiev。呈报人：督察长 J. Mason。

由 V.A. CHILIKIN 先生出版并编辑、地址为霞飞路 (Avenue Foch) 620号的俄文日报《NOVOSTI DNIA》（《每日新闻》），在其1940年4月8日的刊物中，就即将举行的市政选举刊登了以下标题：-

1. 如果你希望将国际租界的行政管理权保留在欧洲人手中；如果你希望为自己保障和平的生活与工作；如果你希望城市的安全与秩序——请只投票给七位英美候选人。

2. 哈尔滨、沈阳和天津最能告诉每一位租界居民他应该把票投给谁。

3. 如果你希望上海的俄国侨民社区进一步繁荣——请投票给欧洲候选人！

4. 欧洲人应只投票给欧洲人。

5. 不要让自己受任何承诺或劝说的影响——确信无疑：将你们的票投给欧洲人！

6. 俄国居民深知哈尔滨市政委员会的一切“魅力”，因此他们将投票给欧洲候选人。

7. 如果你希望保留雇佣了许多俄国人的俄罗斯团和交响乐团——请投票给欧洲候选人！

8. 所有拥有选举权的俄国居民都应履行其社会义务。

9. 来自苏州河以北地区的失败主义者。ZAITSEFF 和 METZLER 集团试图劝说俄国居民不参加即将举行的选举。揭露来自苏州河以北地区的阴谋家进行的反工部局公开宣传。

MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS.

The forthcoming municipal elections attract general
attention in view of the fact that the main force in these
elections will be the Japanese community - the largest and best
organized community. The five candidates nominated by this
community will be supported not only by the Japanese voters, but
probably by a considerable number of ratepayers of other natio-
nalities. This,perhaps,would be the correct action to take in
view of the fact that the time is ripe for a revision of the Mu-
nicipal administration.

Follows a sympathetic review of the declarations out-
lining the respective views of Messrs Ronald McDonald,V.Den and
Hayashi on the municipal affairs.

It is important to note in the above statements that
it is intended to invite residents of all nationalities in Shang-
hai,including Russian emigrants, to participate in the municipal
administration.

We,of course, should welcome these statements,for they
fully correspond to the interests of the Russian community. There
are a number of very important problems in the life of the Rus-
sian community which are waiting for a solution and which can
be solved only when persons have been included in the Municipal
Council who regard Russian emigrants not as inferiors,but as mem-
bers of one international family governed by a Municipal Council
not separated from them by a wall of archaic traditions of the
"colonial rulers".

We have been in Shanghai for about twenty years,during
which period we have paid millions of dollars in taxes. What have
we received? Have we schools maintained by the Council? We are
ashamed to say that Russian schools in Shanghai are in a worse
financial position than were village schools in old Russia.

Have we hospitals for the poorer and middle classes of

市政选举。

鉴于日本侨民社区将是此次选举中的主要力量——这是规模最大且组织最完善的社区——即将到来的市政选举引起了普遍关注。该社区提名的五位候选人不仅将获得日本选民的支持，还可能获得相当数量的其他国籍纳税人的支持。鉴于修改市政管理的时机已经成熟，这或许将是正确的行动方针。

随后是对 Ronald McDonald 先生、V.Den 先生和林 (Hayashi) 先生关于市政事务各自观点声明的同情性评论。

在上述声明中，值得注意的是，其意图是邀请上海所有国籍的居民，包括俄国移民，参与市政管理。

当然，我们应该欢迎这些声明，因为它们完全符合俄国侨民社区的利益。俄国侨民社区的生活中存在许多亟待解决的重要问题，而这些问题只有当那些不将俄国移民视为低人一等，而是将其视为一个国际大家庭成员的人进入工部局董事会后才能得到解决，这个大家庭由一个不与俄国移民隔着“殖民统治者”陈旧传统高墙的市政委员会治理。

我们在上海已生活约二十年，在此期间我们缴纳了数百万美元的税款。我们得到了什么？我们有由工部局维持的学校吗？我们羞于提及，上海的俄国学校的财务状况比旧俄国的乡村学校还要糟糕。

我们有供贫困和中产阶级使用的医院吗

the Russian community or a free municipal clinic for Russian pa-
tients? Is there as much as a shade of gentlemanly attitude to-
wards the question of equal status of Russians in the employ of
the Council? Are our homeless,unemployed,children and aged people
cared for?

WE,RUSSIAN RATEPAYERS,WELCOME THE INTENTION OF JAPANESE
RATEPAYERS TO CARRY OUT A REORGANIZATION OF THE MUNICIPAL ADMINI-
STRATION. WE WELCOME THEIR INTENTION OF TAKING ADVANTAGE OF THE
POSSIBILITIES OF REVISING THE PRESENT SYSTEM OF NATIONAL REPRE-
SENTATION IN THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL,which will enable us,Russians,
to have our representative in the Council who will defend our
rights and interests.

We are of the opinion that the inclusion of five Japa-
nese members in the Council will strengthen the position of this
institution. In order to bring about this situation it would be
advisable to have more Japanese members in the Council.

We advise Russian ratepayers,who will be called to vote
at the forthcoming elections, to give their votes to the Japanese

俄罗斯社群，还是为俄罗斯贫困患者设立的免费市立诊所？在对待受雇于工部局的俄罗斯人享有平等地位的问题上，是否有一丝一毫的绅士风度？我们的无家可归者、失业者、儿童和老年人是否得到了照顾？

我们，俄罗斯纳税人，欢迎日本纳税人对市政行政进行重组的意图。我们欢迎他们打算利用修订工部局董事会中各国代表名额现行制度的可能性，这将使我们俄罗斯人能够在董事会中拥有自己的代表，以捍卫我们的权利和利益。

我们认为，在董事会中加入五名日本成员将加强该机构的地位。为了实现这一局面，宜在董事会中安排更多的日本成员。

我们建议将在即将到来的选举中被召集投票的俄罗斯纳税人，将票投给日本候选人。常识要求采取这一行动。这提供了绝对的保证，即包含更多日本成员的新工部局董事会将考虑到俄罗斯移民的需求，并将尽其所能满足这些需求。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 1 1940
No. S. L. 7834
Date 9 4 40

Japanese Have Not Yet
Named Representatives
For S.M. Council Seats

Closed Session Of Nippon Residents Held Yesterday
For Purpose Of Selecting Candidates; Nothing Is
Said As To Number, Names Of Nominees

POSSIBILITY OF EXCITING ELECTION
STILL INTRIGUING RATEPAYERS

Mystery still shrouds the intentions of Japanese ratepayers in the International Settlement regarding the names and number of candidates to stand for election to the Shanghai Municipal Council this year. It was believed that, following a meeting of the Japanese Election Committee yesterday afternoon, a statement would be made regarding the prospective Japanese Councillors, but the committee met in closed session. The exact intentions, therefore, of the Japanese community regarding representation on the Council this year are still obscure.

It is the veil of secrecy which has been cast over the Japanese intentions which has given additional zest to the forthcoming poll for Councillors, which is set for April 10 and 11. Should the Japanese Election Committee decide to nominate more than their allotted quota of two candidates, and select three or even more nominees, a ballot will be necessary and national sections of the community will marshal voters for a determined municipal contest.

As the position stands the Japanese have until noon to-morrow in which to name their candidates. Nominations must be in the hands of the Municipal Secretariat before that hour. Announcement of candidates will be made shortly after the closing hour.

Another Possibility

Another aspect which is not to be overlooked regarding the coming election is the possibility of one or more independent candidates offering themselves for selection. Although the straw votes conducted by the British and American communities have resulted in decisions to nominate the customary quotas for these nationalities, unsuccessful candidates in these primary ballots have not definitely intimated that they will not seek election, irrespective of the adverse national ballots.

The British community has selected as nominees five candidates, which constitutes the usual British quota under the "gentlemen's agreement" for proportional representation on the S. M. C. The American community has elected their two candidates. In accordance with time-honoured procedure the Japanese are entitled to two representatives, bringing the foreign quota to nine.

Japanese Desires

However, owing to steadily increasing numbers of Japanese in the areas under S. M. C. jurisdiction, there has been an ardent desire on the part of the local Japanese community for increased representation. One question which has apparently given the Japanese election Committee some concern is whether among the Japanese community in Shanghai there are sufficient ratepayers to swing a vote in their favour. It has been admitted that there is an increased Japanese population in the city, but just how many of these are entitled to vote at the forthcoming election has been a subject of considerable investigation by the Japanese Residents' Corporation.

The fact that the Japanese community, through their officials, applied for and received permission to appoint their own scrutineers at the various polling booths, were permitted to have "coaches" for the guidance of Japanese voters at the booths, and that the names of Japanese candidates be printed in Japanese, as well as English on ballot papers, has given rise to the belief that more than two Japanese candidates will be named this year, thereby necessitating an election.

The names of the British candidates are: Messrs. George A. Haley, W. J. Keswick, G. E. Mitchell, R. G. MacDonald and T. S. Powell. The two American candidates are: Messrs. N. F. Allman and J. W. Carney.

The names of the Japanese candidates are awaited with interest.

日本人尚未提名
工部局董事会席位的代表

昨日举行日本居民闭门会议
旨在挑选候选人；未透露
提名人数及姓名

激动人心的选举可能性
仍令纳税人兴致盎然

关于今年竞选上海公共租界工部局董事会的日本纳税人的候选人姓名和人数，其意图仍笼罩在神秘之中。人们原以为，在日本选举委员会昨日下午开会后，会就预期的日本董事发表声明，但该委员会举行了闭门会议。因此，日本社群今年关于董事会代表权的确切意图仍然模糊不清。

正是笼罩在日本人意图之上的秘密面纱，给定于4月10日和11日举行的即将到来的董事投票增添了额外的刺激。如果日本选举委员会决定提名超过其分配配额的两名候选人，并选出三名甚至更多提名人，则必须进行投票，而各界别的选民将为激烈的市政竞选动员起来。

就目前情况而言，日本人直到明天中午之前都有时间提名他们的候选人。提名必须在该时间之前送达市政秘书处。候选人名单将在截止后不久公布。

另一种可能性

关于即将到来的选举，另一个不容忽视的方面是，可能有一名或多名独立候选人自荐参选。虽然英国和美国社群进行的意向性投票已导致决定提名这些国籍的常规配额，但在这些初选中落选的候选人并未明确表示，尽管全国性的投票结果不利，他们将不再寻求当选。

英国社群已选出五名候选人作为提名人，这构成了根据“绅士协定”在工部局董事会中按比例代表制的通常英国配额。美国社群已选出他们的两名候选人。按照历史悠久的惯例，日本人有权拥有两名代表，使外籍人士配额总数达到九名。

日本的愿望

然而，由于在工部局管辖区域内日本人的数量稳步增加，当地日本社群强烈渴望增加代表权。显然让日本选举委员会有些担忧的一个问题是，在上海的日本社群中是否有足够的纳税人能扭转投票结果有利于他们。有人承认城市中的日本人口有所增加，但其中有多少人有权在即将到来的选举中投票，一直是日本居留民团深入调查的主题。

事实上，日本社群通过其官员申请并获准在各投票站任命自己的监票员，获准在投票站配备“指导员”以指导日本选民，并且日本候选人的名字在选票上除英文外还印有日文，这些事实使人相信，今年将提名两名以上的日本候选人，从而使得进行选举成为必要。

英国候选人的名单是：乔治·A·哈利（George A. Haley）、W. J. 凯斯威克（W. J. Keswick）、G. E. 米切尔（G. E. Mitchell）、R. G. 麦克唐纳（R. G. MacDonald）和 T. S. 鲍威尔（T. S. Powell）先生。两名美国候选人是：N. F. 奥尔曼（N. F. Allman）和 J. W. 卡尼（J. W. Carney）先生。

人们正饶有兴致地等待日本候选人的名单。

由特别调查员普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev）制作。由警司 J. Leson 转呈。

现随函附上数份俄文印刷的匿名传单样本及其译文，据报道，这些传单的副本于两天前通过邮件分发给俄罗斯居民。该传单声称出自“俄罗斯纳税人发起小组”，敦促俄罗斯纳税人不要将票投给工部局董事会中的英国候选人，而是支持日本候选人，或将选票留白以示对现行市政管理制度的抗议。

RUSSIAN VOTERS

The time of the election of the Shanghai
Municipal Council is approaching.
The "city fathers" are already agitated and
worried by the question of whether or not they will
remain at the helm for another year and keep their
comfortable and lucrative positions. The new British
candidates are worried by the question of whether or
not they will receive a sufficient number of votes
to enable them to take seats next to those of the
"city fathers" and to participate in the present
inefficient administration and uncontrolled management
of the affairs of this populous and rich town.
They will need you at the time of elections
or, rather, your voting papers with "their names"
written on them will be needed.
As was the case in past years, you will be
promised tha t should they be elected they will pay
attention to your Russian interests and will see that
the Municipal Council takes into account your needs.
Do not believe them. Things will remain as
before, if they do not get worse. Once they are
elected by the duped "second rate citizens" they
will have neither wish nor time to think about them.
You want proof? Here are a few facts both
from the recent past and from the present time, to
recall which would not be out of place :-
Following the conclusion of the civil war in
Russia, White Russians sought refuge in Shanghai.
The Municipal authorities did not allow them to land
here. Those who succeeded in landing were received
page_data.zh:
俄文译文

俄罗斯选民

上海公共租界工部局选举的时间即将来临。
“城市父老”们已经因一个问题而感到不安和担忧，即他们是否能再掌舵一年，并保持其舒适且有利可图的职位。新的英国候选人也在担心，他们是否能获得足够的票数，使他们能够坐在“城市父老”们的旁边，并参与这个人口众多且富裕城镇的当前低效行政和无序管理事务。
他们在选举时需要你，或者更确切地说，他们需要写有“他们名字”的你的选票。
如同往年一样，他们会向你承诺，如果他们当选，他们将关注你们的俄罗斯利益，并确保工部局董事会考虑到你们的需求。
不要相信他们。事情将保持原样，甚至可能变得更糟。一旦他们被受骗的“二等公民”选出，他们既没有愿望也没有时间去考虑这些人。
你想要证据吗？这里有一些来自近期和当前的事实，回顾一下并不为过：
在俄国内战结束后，白俄难民寻求在上海避难。市政当局不允许他们在此登陆。那些成功登陆的人受到了

page_data.en:
- 2 -

coldly, treated in an off-hand manner and called
parasites on the body of old Russia. Neither work
nor any positions were given to them and they were
refused temporary shelter in the vacant Municipal
buildings. From necessity, however, certain minor
concessions had to be made later.

Employers began to engage Russians to do certain
low paid work and the city fathers authorised the
recruiting of Russian policemen and the formation of
Russian Volunteer Regiment. On the face of it one
would think that they did so solely in the interests
of Russians and not in their own interests. However,
this was not the case.

Russians were engaged to work in factories and
offices because reliable and efficient workers were
required, to whom it was necessary to pay only a little
more than one had to pay Chinese. In the Police,
Russians were required to deal with Russian affairs,
which the guardians of law, being unfamiliar with the
Russian language, were unable to handle. However,
having engaged Russians to fill the lower positions,
representatives of perfidious Albion did not promote
them above the rank of Sergeant or, at the most, above
the rank of Sub-Inspector.

Where, then, is the equal treatment to which
all residents of Shanghai are supposed to be entitled
in the Municipal Administration?

Do you think that the formation of the Russian
Regiment was an act of consideration to Russians -
just to give them some employment? Nothing of that
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

冷遇，受到漫不经心的对待，并被称为旧俄罗斯身上的寄生虫。既没有工作也没有任何职位提供给他们，并且拒绝让他们在空置的市政建筑中临时栖身。然而，出于必要，后来不得不做出某些微小的让步。

雇主开始雇佣俄罗斯人从事某些低薪工作，城市父老们授权招募俄罗斯警察并组建俄罗斯志愿团。乍一看，人们会认为他们这样做完全是为了俄罗斯人的利益，而不是为了他们自己的利益。然而，事实并非如此。

雇佣俄罗斯人在工厂和办公室工作，是因为需要可靠且高效的工人，支付给他们的薪水只需比支付给中国人的稍多一点即可。在警察部门，需要俄罗斯人来处理俄罗斯事务，因为法律守护者不熟悉俄语，无法处理这些事务。然而，在雇佣俄罗斯人填补低级职位后，背信弃义的阿尔比恩（指英国）的代表并没有将他们晋升至警长以上，或者最多晋升至副巡官以上。

那么，所有上海居民在市政管理中理应享有的平等待遇在哪里呢？

你认为组建俄罗斯团是对俄罗斯人的体贴之举——只是为了给他们提供一些就业机会吗？绝非

page_data.en:
- 3 -

sort. Russian volunteers were engaged on the
understanding that they should shed their blood for
the sake of the commercial interests of the "enlightened
sea-farers". Indeed, the selfish Britons neither like
nor wish to shed their own blood.

And what about Russian schools? We recall that
an application from a Russian school to the Municipal
Council for permission to take over, on easy terms, the
vacant building of a Municipal School for Chinese, in
Wayside District, was turned down. However, shortly
afterwards, this building and many others, were given
free of charge, to Jewish refugees and all necessary
repairs etc. were carried out at the Council's expense.

How can Russian schools educate Russian children
if the financial position of these schools is miserable?
In the past they were refused any assistance and the
Municipal Authorities even sent their officials in order
to have the premises of a Russian school sealed for non-
payment of Municipal taxes. Later, however, crumbs
from the master's table were given to Russian schools
in the shape of subsidies, which could not materially
improve their position.

What are the taxes we, Russian ratepayers, pay
out of our scanty and hard earned means, and why is it
that European refugees are exempted from the payment
of taxes on their shops, bars, cafes, etc.?

It would seem that the Municipal Authorities
do not treat all in the same manner.

Now, let us see what is the attitude of the city
rulers towards the present profiteering which so
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

如此。招募俄罗斯志愿者是基于这样的理解：他们应当为“开明的航海者”的商业利益流血。的确，自私的英国人既不喜欢也不愿意流自己的血。

那么俄罗斯学校呢？我们要指出，一所俄罗斯学校向工部局董事会提出申请，请求以优惠条件接管位于越界筑路区（Wayside District）的一处空置的中国市立校舍，但该申请被驳回。然而，不久之后，该建筑以及许多其他建筑被免费提供给犹太难民，所有必要的维修等费用均由董事会承担。

如果这些学校的财务状况糟糕，俄罗斯学校如何教育俄罗斯儿童？过去，它们被拒绝提供任何援助，市政当局甚至派遣官员去查封一所俄罗斯学校的房产，理由是未缴纳市政税。然而，后来以补贴的形式给了俄罗斯学校一些主人餐桌上的残羹剩饭，但这并不能实质性地改善它们的处境。

我们，俄罗斯纳税人，从微薄且辛苦赚来的收入中支付的税款是什么？为什么欧洲难民可以免除其商店、酒吧、咖啡馆等的税款？

看来市政当局并没有以同样的方式对待所有人。

现在，让我们看看城市统治者对目前如此

page_data.en:
- 4 -

badly affects the poorer residents? What are they
doing in order to put an end to this evil? They merely
discuss this matter and will do nothing else.
As long as there is no one to represent in the
Municipal Council the interests of the second largest
foreign community in Shanghai. -
DO NOT GIVE THEM YOUR VOTES.
Do not support those from whom you get nothing
but promises. Struggle for equal rights in this
international city, in which all nationalities should
have certain rights.
Help others to establish a new order under
which you will be granted equal rights.
It is better to give your votes to those who
regard you as friends - you know who they are - than
to those who always regarded you as pariahs, who in
reply to all your appeals for justice, haughtily
said "do not forget that you are Russians".
Are you not grieved when you hear these words
which are repeated only too often?
Then do not creep before the "privileged" nation
and do not follow the example of small hungry dogs
which lick the hands of those who mercilessly beat them.
If, for some reason, you refrain from voting for
those who are really struggling for your interests,
then at least do not humiliate yourselves, maintain
your selfrespect and struggle in a passive way.
Return your papers blank. By doing so you will
demonstrate your protest against your being deprived
of legal rights, against the predominance and
unfairness
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

严重影响了较贫困的居民？他们正在采取什么措施来终结这一弊病？他们仅仅是在讨论此事，而不会采取其他任何行动。
只要工部局董事会中没有代表上海第二大外籍社群利益的人选。——
切勿将选票投给他们。
不要支持那些除了空头承诺外给不了你任何东西的人。在这座国际都市中争取平等权利，在这里所有国籍的人都应享有某些权利。
帮助他人建立一种新秩序，在这种秩序下你将获得平等权利。
最好将选票投给那些视你为朋友的人——你知道他们是谁——而不是投给那些始终视你为贱民的人，对于你所有关于正义的呼吁，他们总是傲慢地回答：“别忘了你是俄国人”。
当你听到这些被过于频繁重复的话语时，难道你不感到悲痛吗？
那么，不要在“特权”民族面前卑躬屈膝，也不要效仿那些饥饿的小狗，去舔舐那些无情殴打它们的人的手。
如果出于某种原因，你 refrain from（克制/避免）投票给那些真正为你利益而斗争的人，那么至少不要羞辱自己，保持自尊，以被动的方式进行斗争。
交回空白选票。通过这样做，你将表明你对被剥夺合法权利、对某种“骄傲民族”的霸权和不公

arbitrariness of a certain "proud nation", against the
connivance at profiteering and against the deafness of
the municipal authorities to the needs of the less
fortunate section of the foreign population of Shanghai.

Initiative group of Russian
Ratepayers.

March 23, 1940, Shanghai.

page_data.en:
Русскіе Избиратели.

Наступает время выборов въ Муниципальный Совѣтъ Международнаго Сеттель-
мента Шанхая.
Уже «отцы города» волнуются и безпокоятся — останутся ли они еще на
год у кормила власти на насиженныхъ хлѣбныхъ мѣстахъ, а новые англійскіе кандидаты
тревожатся мыслью, соберутъ ли они достаточное количество голосовъ, чтобы сѣсть
рядомъ съ «отцами» и принять участіе въ бездарномъ управленіи и безконтрольномъ
хозяйничаньѣ во многолюдномъ, богатомъ городѣ.
На время выборовъ вы будете нужны им или вѣрнѣе понадобятся ваши изби-
рательныя карточки, на которыхъ будут написаны «их имена».
Какъ и прежде ежегодно, такъ и теперь Вамъ будут обѣщать, что въ случа
избранія, они будут принимать во вниманіе Ваши русскіе интересы и заставят го-
родской совѣтъ считаться съ вашими насущными нуждами.
Не вѣрьте им. Все останется попрежнему, если не хуже. Послѣ выборовъ съ
обманутыми надеждами «гражданами второго сорта», думать о которыхъ им будет
некогда, да и не захочется.
Нужны доказательства ?
Извольте, вот факты недавняго прошлаго и настоящаго, о которыхъ весьма кстати
вспомнить:
Когда по окончаніи гражданской войны въ Россіи бѣлые русскіе стали искать
убѣжище въ Шанхаѣ, муниципальныя власти не позволяли им высаживаться съ кора-
блей на берегъ, а высадившихся встрѣчали съ ледяным холодком на устахъ, третировали
и называли «ихъ» паразитами на тѣлѣ былой Россіи. Не принимали на службу, не
давали работы, отказывали во временном пріютѣ въ свободных муниципальныхъ
помѣщеніяхъ.
Необходимость, однако, заставила их пойти немного на уступки.
Работодатели стали предоставлять русским черную работу, а отцы города
разрѣшили принимать ихъ въ полицію и сформировать из добровольцевъ русскій полкъ.
Со стороны казалось, что они дѣлали это только въ интересах русскихъ, а не
из своих расчетовъ, но это было не такъ.
На фабрики и конторы стали принимать русских только потому, что им были нужны
полезные и надежные работники, которым можно было дешево платить, немного
больше оплаты китайскаго труда.
Полиціи русскіе понадобились по русским дѣламъ, въ которых блюстители
порядка без знанія языка не могли разобраться сами. Но допуская къ себѣ на службу
на низшія должности, представители коварнаго Альбіона не дают русским служеб-
наго продвиженія дальше сержанта и лишь въ крайнем случаѣ суб — инспектора.
Гдѣ же тут равенство въ городском учрежденіи, въ котором права всѣх шанхай-
ских резидентов объявлены равными.
Вы думаете сформированіе русскаго полка было актом расположенія къ рус-
скимъ, — оторых надо было как то устроить ?
Ничего подобнаго. Русскіе волонтеры были наняты съ обязательством проливать свою
кровь за торговые интересы «просвященных мореплавателей». Вѣдь свою кровь эгои-
стичные бритты проливать не любят и не желают.
А русская школа? Мы помнимъ, как русское реальное училище, не имя средствъ,
обратилось къ Муниципальному Совѣту съ просьбой о предоставленіи на льготныхъ
условіях пустующаго муниципальнаго зданія китайской школы на Вейсайд, но эта
просьба была отказана, а спустя немного времени это же зданіе, как и многіе другіе,
были переданы бесплатно еврейским бѣженцамъ, при чем сам муниципалитет произво-
дил ремонт и нужныя перестройки этих зданій.
Развѣ русская школа имѣет возможность воспитывать русских дѣтей, когда
она влачит жалкое матеріальное существованіе. Вѣдь сначала ей отказывали во всемъ
и даже муниципальныя власти приходили опечатывать ее за невзнос муниципальнаго
налога, потом стали давать крохи съ господскаго стола въ видѣ субсидіи, на которыя
ничего существеннаго сдѣлать нельзя.
Какой налог платим мы русскіе налогоплательщики из своих скудных грошей,
зарабатываемых кровью и почему европейскіе бженцы освобождены от уплаты
муниципальнаго налога въ своих магазинахъ, барахъ, кафе и т. д.
Как видно отношеніе муниципальных властей не совсѣм одинаковое.
Теперь посмотрите, как городскіе заправилы относятся къ развившейся
спекуляціи, которая самым чувствительным образом отражается на неимущих и мало-
обезпеченных гражданах города.
Что они дѣлают для пресѣченія этого зла ?
Только обсуждают и дальше обсужденія не пойдут.
Нѣтъ. Пока въ муниципальном совѣтѣ не будет русскаго представителя от
второй по численности иностранной колоніи Шанхая, до тѣх пор НЕ НЕСИТЕ ИМ
СВОИ ИЗБИРАТЕЛЬНЫЯ КАРТОЧКИ.
Не лейте воды на чужую мельницу, от которой вам ничего, кромѣ посулов, не
дают.
Боритесь за свое равноправіе въ международном городѣ, гдѣ у всѣх націо-
нальностей должны быть какіе то права.
Помогите создать новый порядок другим, при котором вы получите одина-
ковые права.
Лучше отдайте свои голоса тѣмъ, кто считает вас друзьями, а их вы знаете, нежели
тѣмъ, кто всегда считал вас паріями, кто на ваши просьбы объ оказаніи справедливо-
сти надменно отвѣчалъ: — «не забывайте, вы русскіе».
Развѣ вам не больно слышать подобныя, ставшія обычными, заявленія.
Так не раболепствуйте же перед «привилегированной» націей и не изобра-
жайте из себя маленькую голодную собачку, которая лижет руку того, кто безжа-
лостно и долго ее бьет.
Если почему либо вы воздержитесь подать голос за тѣхъ, кто действительно
борется и за ваши права, то не унижайтесь и имѣйте чувства собственнаго достоинства
и боритесь, хотя бы пассивно.
ОПУСКАЙТЕ В ИЗБИРАТЕЛЬНЫЯ УРНЫ ПУСТЫЯ ЗАПИСКИ.
Этим вы подчеркнете свой протест против своего безправія, против засилія и
своеволія нѣкоей «гордой націи», против потворства спекуляціи и бездушнаго отноше-
нія муниципальных властей къ нуждам обездоленной части иностраннаго Шанхая.

Иніціативная группа русских
page_data.zh:
俄国选民。

上海公共租界工部局选举的时刻即将来临。
“城市父老”们已经焦虑不安——他们是否还能在那些坐惯了的肥缺上掌权一年；而新的英国候选人则担心是否能收集到足够的票数，以便与“父老”们并肩而坐，参与对这个人口众多、富裕城市的无能管理和不受监督的营私舞弊。
在选举期间，他们需要你们，或者更准确地说，需要你们的选票卡，上面将写上“他们的名字”。
和往年一样，现在他们也会向你们许诺，一旦当选，他们将考虑你们的俄国利益，并迫使市议会重视你们的迫切需求。
不要相信他们。一切都将维持原状，甚至可能更糟。选举结束后，他们既没时间也不愿去想那些希望落空的“二等公民”。
需要证据吗？
好吧，以下是近期过去和现在的事实，此时回想起来非常恰当：
当俄国内战结束后，白俄开始在上海寻求庇护时，市政当局不允许他们从船上登陆，而对那些已经登陆的人则冷眼相待，虐待他们，并称他们为前俄罗斯身上的“寄生虫”。不录用他们任职，不提供工作，拒绝在空闲的市政房屋中提供临时住所。
然而，必要性迫使他们做出了一些让步。
雇主开始向俄国人提供苦力工作，而“城市父老”们允许招募他们进入警队，并由志愿者组建了一个俄国团。
表面上看，他们这样做似乎只是为了俄国的利益，而非出于自身算计，但事实并非如此。
工厂和事务所开始雇佣俄国人，仅仅是因为他们需要有用且可靠的工人，支付给他们的薪水很低，仅比中国劳工的工资稍高一点。
警队需要俄国人处理涉及俄国人的案件，在这些案件中，不懂语言的执法者无法自行理清头绪。但是，尽管允许俄国人担任低级职务，狡诈的阿尔比恩（指英国）的代表却不给予俄国人超过警长的晋升机会，仅在极个别情况下升至副督察。
在这个宣称所有上海居民权利平等的市政机构中，平等何在？
你们认为组建俄国团是对俄国人表示好感的举动——毕竟总得想办法安置他们？
完全不是这样。俄国志愿者是被雇佣来的，负有为“文明航海者”的商业利益流血的义务。毕竟，自私的英国人不喜欢也不愿意流淌自己的鲜血。
还有俄国学校呢？我们记得，俄国实科中学因缺乏资金，曾向工部局董事会请求以优惠条件提供位于韦斯特盖特（Wayside，音译）的一所闲置的中国学校校舍，但这一请求遭到拒绝。不久之后，同一栋建筑以及许多其他建筑被免费移交给了犹太难民，且市政当局还出资对这些建筑进行了维修和必要的改建。
当俄国学校在悲惨的物质条件下挣扎求生时，它怎么可能有机会教育俄国儿童？起初，当局拒绝提供一切援助，甚至市政官员前来查封学校，理由是未缴纳市政税；后来才以补贴的形式施舍一点残羹剩饭，这点钱根本做不成什么实质性的事情。
我们这些俄国纳税人用血汗挣来的微薄收入缴纳了多少税款？为什么欧洲难民在他们的商店、酒吧、咖啡馆等场所却免缴市政税？
显然，市政当局的态度并不完全一致。
现在看看城市当权者是如何对待日益发展的投机行为的，这种行为对城市中无产和低收入公民的影响最为严重。
他们为遏制这一弊病做了什么？
只是讨论，而且仅限于讨论。
不。只要工部局董事会中没有来自上海第二大外籍社群的俄国代表，就绝对不要将你们的选票投给他们。
不要为他人做嫁衣，除了空头许诺，他们什么也不会给你们。
在这座国际都市中为你们的平等权利而斗争，在这里所有民族都应拥有某些权利。
帮助他人建立一种新秩序，使你们在其中获得平等的权利。
最好将选票投给那些视你们为朋友的人——你们知道他们是谁——而不是投给那些始终视你们为贱民的人，对于你们关于正义的请求，他们傲慢地回答：“别忘了，你们是俄国人”。
听到这些已成为常态的言论，难道你们不感到痛心吗？
因此，不要在“特权”民族面前奴颜婢膝，也不要像那只饥饿的小狗一样，去舔舐那个无情且长期殴打它的人的手。
如果出于某种原因，你们 abstain from（克制/避免）投票给那些真正为你们权利而斗争的人，那么不要自轻自贱，保持尊严，即使是以被动的方式进行斗争。
向投票箱投入空白选票。
以此强调你们对自己无权状态的抗议，反对某种“骄傲民族”的专横和肆意妄为，反对对投机行为的纵容，以及市政当局对上海不幸的那部分外籍人口需求的冷漠态度。

俄国发起人小组

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 7834
Date 8 / 4 / 40

APR 3 1940

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED by CARROLL

On The Inside
GOSSIP going the rounds of local White Russian circles is that Ataman Semionoff was imported to Shanghai from Manchuria to do some electioneering work among his own countrymen hereabouts. This may be the case but the Ataman is not working very hard at it. According to all accounts, he is paying more attention to the beautiful blonde in his party than to the business of helping the Japanese gain control of the Shanghai Municipal Council. When the Ataman walks into a certain swanky hotel on the south side of Soochow Creek, he puts on quite a show. Close behind comes the blonde and directly back of the pair trail a brace of Russian bodyguards.

Speaking of the Russian vote, a circular letter sent out by a certain local White Russian organisation of importance two days ago advised Russians to vote for the "Russian candidate." Since no candidate of that nationality is standing for election to the Shanghai Municipal Council the letter is generally interpreted as leaving the choice of candidates up to the ratepayer.

Soviet Russian forces in Shanghai, however, are urging Soviet sympathisers to vote among the Russians

here solidly against the Japanese and Reginald MacDonald. This might be accepted as fair indication that the Russian vote will probably wind itself out with about an even division.

One of the big reasons that the British and Americans stand a chance of losing the European refugee vote is because these people are under the impression that the ballot is not altogether secret. They are afraid that the ballot papers might fall into the hands of the Japanese.

I believe it is quite generally recognised that the signing of the ballot papers is one of the faults of the present electoral system in the International Settlement. However, the ballot is much more secret than generally supposed. The ballot papers are seen only by two scrutineers who, immediately after they have completed their count, take the papers out and burn them. It is doubtful if the scrutineers, even if they had the time, could take note of the several thousand names that will be signed to ballot papers in the forthcoming elections. In view of these circumstances, it would seem most doubtful that the names of voters and how they vote will fall into the hands of people who could use such information for purposes retaliation.

5/100

Liu
Ch

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处
编号 S. B. D. 7834
日期 1940年4月8日

1940年4月3日

卡罗尔（Carroll）著《我常纳闷》

内幕消息
在当地白俄圈子中流传的小道消息称，阿塔曼·谢苗诺夫（Ataman Semionoff）是从满洲被引入上海的，目的是在他周围的同胞中进行拉票活动。情况或许如此，但这位阿塔曼对此并未十分卖力。据各方说法，他关注其随行那位金发美女的程度，远胜于帮助日本人控制上海工部局董事会的事务。当这位阿塔曼走进苏州河南岸某家豪华酒店时，场面颇为招摇。那位金发美女紧随其后，两人身后直接跟着一对俄国保镖。

说到俄国人的选票，两天前由当地某个重要的白俄组织发出的一封通函建议俄国人投票给“俄国候选人”。由于没有该国籍的候选人参加上海工部局董事会的选举，这封信通常被解读为将候选人的选择权留给纳税人自行决定。

然而，上海的苏维埃俄国势力正在敦促同情苏维埃的俄国人

在此团结一心，投票反对日本人和雷金纳德·麦克唐纳（Reginald MacDonald）。这可以被视为一个合理的迹象，表明俄国人的选票最终可能会大致平分。

英国人和美国人有可能失去欧洲难民选票的一个重要原因是，这些人认为投票并非完全秘密。他们担心选票可能会落入日本人手中。

我相信人们普遍认识到，在选票上签名是当前公共租界选举制度的缺陷之一。然而，投票的秘密性远比一般人想象的要高。选票仅由两名监票员查看，他们在完成计票后立即取出选票并将其烧毁。即使有时间，监票员能否注意到即将在选举中签署在选票上的数千个名字，也令人怀疑。鉴于这些情况，选民姓名及其投票方式落入可能利用此类信息进行报复的人手中的可能性似乎微乎其微。

5/100

刘
查
