Mr. Ranald McDonald
Tells How He Means To
Vote In S.M.C. Election

Selects Himself, Three British “Straw Vote” Men
Both American Candidates, And Three Japanese
Candidates To Constitute New Council

EMPHASIZES MAKING OCCASION KIND OF
“DOG FIGHT” IS CONTEMPTIBLE

The letter given below has been addressed to “The Shang-
hai Times” by Mr. Ranald McDonald, the independent British
candidate for election to the Shanghai Municipal Council at the
Annual Elections this week. It will be noted that Mr. McDonald
states that he intends to vote for himself, for three of the
British “straw vote” candidates, for both the American
candidates, and for three of the Japanese candidates, and sets
forth reasons.

He urges ratepayers to follow his example in this selection
of Councillors and says that if everyone were to take his advice
in this matter there would be no trouble in Shanghai, “no
humiliation, no bitter resentment, no friction, no lasting racial
antagonism” and it would mean the inauguration of an era of
goodwill, of genuine co-operation, of honest give-and-take, and
mark the commencement of an era of unparalleled prosperity
and progress” for this city.

S. M. C. ELECTION
To The Editor.
THE SHANGHAI TIMES

Sir,—1.—I should like to be given
the opportunity of stating publicly
how immensely I appreciate the
scrupulously fair treatment and
valuable assistance which I have re-
ceived at your hands, at the hands
of the American community at
large, and also at the hands of the
“Shanghai Evening Post” in what
has been to me one of the bitterest
and most unpleasant tasks which I
have ever felt called upon to dis-
charge. The vilest slurs and
insults have been hurled at my head
and covert and even semi-open
threats of varying kinds have been
made against me on numerous
occasions ever since the publication
of the fact that I, a free Scotsman,
had dared to put my name forward
for election. On an occasion such
as this one has to expect the hardest
of knocks, however convinced one
may be that one’s motives and
actions are beyond reproach, and I
am accustomed to expect every type
of blow both above and below the
belt and to take them without
serious complaint, unless they
actually amount to an outrage.

Appeal To Americans

2.—I feel an irresistible urge to
address the American community on
my own behalf and at the risk of
being accused of blatant propagan-
dism, if not effrontery, to defend
them, for the purpose of supporting
some of my points, in certain out-
standing facts in their own glorious
history.

3.—Americans—let me refer first
to your “Independence Day” in
connection with which it has been
said:—

“The Fourth of July marks an
epoch in the world’s history. It
marks the birth of a free nation,
with all that implies—a nation in
the guidance of which, the
supremacy of all land rights, and
of which every true American is
justly proud” and again:—

“In the course of ages no
event is to be paralleled in the
annals of glory and renown.”

4.—Let me remind you also of
that great American soldier and
statesman, Alexander Hamilton,
who was one of the foremost figures
in establishing American nation-
alism, who was born on January
11, 1757, on the island of Nevis in
the West Indies, and whose father
was a Scottish merchant. He also
was a captain of artillery, a private
secretary and a lawyer in earlier
days, and wrote a series of papers
in defence of the rights of the
Colonies against Great Britain
when the latter was govern-
ed by a mad King and an even
madder Foreign Office who
between them were responsible for
one of the greatest blunders or
tragedies in British history. How
do you think that he would have
voted at this Election if he had
been alive to-day? Can you im-
agine him being swayed by the
views or advice of the “British
nameless nine,” alias “The British
Election Committee”? Never. His
first two votes would have been
for the two American candidates
and his third for the free and
independent candidate, myself.

“How I Intend To Vote”

5.—And now, in order that there
may be no shadow of ambiguity or
uncertainty about my views or my
proposed actions, I will state how
I intend to vote. In spite of the
fact that some of my more ardent
supporters have announced that
they intend to vote for me alone,
I firmly intend to vote and to urge
others to vote as follows:—

(a) For both American Can-
didates:
1.—ALLMAN. N. P.
2.—CARRY. J. W.

(b) For myself, the British
Independent Candidate:
3.—McDONALD, RANALD G.

(c) For 3 of the British Straw
Vote Candidates:
9.—KIRWAN, W. J.
10.—SMALL, G. E.
13.—POWER, T. S.

(d) For 3 of the Japanese
Candidates:
12.—ONODERA, OSAMU

（印：OFFICIAL POLICE REGISTRY S. M. D. 7834 Date 5 / 1 / 40）
SHANGHAI TIMES
APRIL 1940

拉纳尔德·麦克唐纳先生
阐述其在上海工部局选举中的投票意向

选定自己、三名英国“试探性投票”候选人、
两名美国候选人以及三名日本候选人组成新董事会

强调将选举变成某种“狗咬狗”式的争斗是可鄙的

下文所示信件由独立英国候选人拉纳尔德·麦克唐纳先生致《字林西报》，他正参加本周举行的上海工部局年度选举。值得注意的是，麦克唐纳先生表示，他打算投票给自己、三名英国“试探性投票”候选人、两名美国候选人以及三名日本候选人，并阐述了理由。

他敦促纳税人在选择董事时效仿他的做法，并称如果每个人都在这方面听从他的建议，上海就不会有麻烦，“没有屈辱，没有痛苦的怨恨，没有摩擦，没有持久的种族敌意”，这将意味着开启一个善意、真诚合作、诚实互谅的时代，并标志着这座城市前所未有的繁荣与进步时代的开始”。

上海工部局选举
致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——1. 我希望有机会公开陈述，我是多么感激您、广大美国社区以及《上海晚邮报》给予我的极其公正的对待和宝贵的帮助，这对我而言是我所感到不得不履行的最痛苦和最不愉快的任务之一。自从我，一个自由的苏格兰人，敢于提名自己参加选举的事实公布以来，各种最恶毒的诽谤和侮辱劈头盖脸地向我袭来，针对我的隐蔽甚至半公开的各类威胁也多次发生。在这样的场合，人们必须预料到会受到最沉重的打击，无论一个人多么确信自己的动机和行为无可指责，而且我习惯于预期受到来自上下各方面的各种攻击，并在不造成实际暴行的情况下默默承受，不予严重抱怨。

呼吁美国人

2. 我感到一种不可抗拒的冲动，要代表我自己向美国社区发表讲话，即使冒着被指责为公然宣传甚至厚颜无耻的风险，也要为他们辩护，目的是通过他们光辉历史中的一些突出事实来支持我的一些观点。

3. 美国人——让我首先提及你们的“独立日”，对此曾有如下说法：

“七月四日标志着世界历史上的一个纪元。它标志着一个自由国家的诞生，及其所蕴含的一切——在这个国家的指引下，所有土地权利至高无上，每个真正的美国人都为此感到正当的自豪”；此外还有：

“在岁月的长河中，没有任何事件能在荣耀与名声的史册中与之媲美。”

4. 让我也提醒你们那位伟大的美国士兵和政治家亚历山大·汉密尔顿，他是建立美国民族主义的首要人物之一，于1757年1月11日出生在西印度群岛的尼维斯岛，其父亲是一位苏格兰商人。他在早期也曾担任炮兵上尉、私人秘书和律师，并撰写了一系列文章，捍卫殖民地对抗英国的权利，当时英国由一位疯狂的国王和一个更加疯狂的外交部统治，他们共同造成了英国历史上最大的失误或悲剧之一。你认为如果他今天还活着，他会在这次选举中如何投票？你能想象他会受“英国无名九人”（即“英国选举委员会”）的观点或建议的影响吗？绝不会。他的前两票会投给两位美国候选人，第三票会投给自由独立的候选人，也就是我自己。

“我打算如何投票”

5. 现在，为了使我的观点或拟议行动没有任何含糊或不确定的余地，我将声明我打算如何投票。尽管我的一些更热情的支持者宣布他们打算只投票给我，但我坚定地打算投票，并敦促其他人按以下方式投票：—

(a) 投给两名美国候选人：
1. 奥尔曼 (ALLMAN), N. P.
2. 卡里 (CARRY), J. W.

(b) 投给我自己，英国独立候选人：
3. 麦克唐纳 (McDONALD), 拉纳尔德 G.

(c) 投给三名英国“试探性投票”候选人：
9. 柯万 (KIRWAN), W. J.
10. 斯莫尔 (SMALL), G. E.
13. 鲍尔 (POWER), T. S.

(d) 投给三名日本候选人：
12. 小野寺 (ONODERA), 修 (OSAMU)

（印：官方警务登记处 S. M. D. 7834 日期 40年1月5日）
《字林西报》
1940年4月

the manner suggested above are as follows:—
(a) "For both American Candidates":—
This is your first and foremost duty and is fundamental in the interests of the whole community, not only on account of the large American interests in Shanghai and China, but, inter alia, on account of the splendid record of service of American members of the Council, of their ability and impartiality and not least of all on account of their democratic, their free and independent outlook.
(b) "For myself, the British Independent Candidate":—
I have expressed my views in my "Brief Preliminary Election Address" and in my numerous and lengthy letters to the Press, and a summary of possibly rather egotistical information concerning myself has also appeared in the press.
(c) "For 3 of the British Straw Vote Candidates:"—
The British are clearly entitled in my view on every ground to 4 members —Myself and the three elected Straw Vote Candidates. If I appear to have been invidious in their selection, it is due to the accepted methods of secrecy which prevail. We can only speculate as to the respective merits of each of the five from such information as the Council chooses to peddle out to us and from what we can glean from other sources.
(d) "For 3 of the Japanese Candidates:"—
The Japanese are in my opinion clearly entitled upon every ground to at least 3 members this year, and it seems to me downright lunacy to suggest anything else—a lunacy not unlike that which led Britain to the loss of America.
Even as long ago, I think, as about 1908, I was urged by the then British Consul-General to support him and to speak in a campaign against the suggested increase of the Japanese members from 2 to 3; but I had considered the whole matter with great care and serious thought and could not do so. In fact I stated that I might even feel impelled openly to fight against it, if I thought that evil consequences to British interests and to the interests of the Settlement as a whole, might ensue. All that has happened since that date has only increased the validity and strength of the Japanese claim. I cannot imagine anything more fatuous and more calculated to lead to a major disaster to British interests and the general interests of the Settlement than the adoption of an arrogant and wholly unreasonable attitude of blank obstruction to legitimate Japanese aspirations. The senseless and almost criminal suggestion that the election is a kind of dog fight to the death between Occidental and Oriental factions is so contemptible and so fraught with future and lasting dangers than I cannot imagine how any calm and balanced mind can for one moment entertain it. For God's sake, remember the Council's motto, Omnia juncta in uno, and let Sanity prevail.

Era Of Goodwill
7.—If everyone were to follow this year my advice with regard to voting as set out in paragraph 5 above, there would be no trouble in Shanghai, there would be no humiliation, no bitter resentment, no friction, no lasting racial antagonism. It would mean the inauguration of an era of goodwill, of genuine co-operation, of honest give-and-take, and mark the commencement of an era of unparalleled prosperity and progress for this great, this unique city of Shanghai. Immediate steps could then be taken, in conjunction with the Chinese, for drastic and fundamental changes in the whole machinery and methods of Government not only of the Settlement but of the surrounding districts, and it would not then be long before Shanghai became one of the greatest, if not the greatest of the Cities in the World.
8.—Voters of every nationality, let us all co-operate—let us work for harmony—I therefore urge you to give my advice at least a trial this year. It can do no possible harm and might prove to be an undercurrent of success.
RANDAL MACDONALD.
Shanghai, April 4, 1930.
P.S.—Since writing the above, the names of the other two Japanese for whom to vote which have been suggested to me are:—
6.—HARAWA, Y.
and
7.—KIMURA, K.,
but there may still be some further alteration in this connection.

上述建议的方式如下：—
(a) “投给两名美国候选人”：—
这是你们首要的职责，符合整个社区的根本利益，这不仅是因为美国在上海和中国拥有巨大的利益，而且还因为工部局美国成员出色的服务记录、他们的能力和公正性，尤其是因为他们民主、自由和独立的视野。
(b) “投给我自己，英国独立候选人”：—
我已在我的《简短初步竞选演说》以及写给新闻界的众多长篇信件中表达了我的观点，报纸上也刊登了关于我自己的一些可能略显自负的信息摘要。
(c) “投给三名英国‘试探性投票’候选人”：—
在我看来，英国人显然有理由获得四个席位——我自己和三名当选的“试探性投票”候选人。如果在他们的选择上我显得有所偏颇，那是由于普遍存在的保密惯例所致。我们只能根据工部局选择向我们兜售的信息以及我们从其他来源搜集到的情况，推测这五个人各自的优点。
(d) “投给三名日本候选人”：—
在我看来，日本人今年显然有理由获得至少三个席位，提出其他建议简直是彻头彻尾的疯狂——这种疯狂类似于导致英国失去美洲的那种疯狂。
早在大约1908年，当时的英国总领事就敦促我支持他，并在反对将日本成员从两名增加到三名的运动中发言；但我经过仔细考虑和深思熟虑，无法这样做。事实上，我当时表示，如果我认为这会对英国利益和整个租界的利益产生不良后果，我甚至可能会感到被迫公开反对。自那以来发生的一切只增加了日本诉求的有效性和力度。我无法想象还有什么比采取傲慢且完全不合理的态度，盲目阻挠日本人的合法愿望，更愚蠢、更可能导致英国利益和租界整体利益遭受重大灾难的了。那种认为选举是西方和东方派系之间殊死搏斗般的“狗咬狗”的无稽且近乎犯罪的建议是如此可鄙，充满了未来和持久的危险，以至于我无法想象任何冷静和平衡的头脑怎么会片刻接受它。看在上帝的份上，请记住工部局的格言“Omnia juncta in uno”（万物合一），让理智占上风。

善意时代
7. 如果今年每个人都遵循我在上述第5段中提出的投票建议，上海就不会有麻烦，不会有屈辱，不会有痛苦的怨恨，不会有摩擦，不会有持久的种族敌意。这将意味着开启一个善意、真诚合作、诚实互谅的时代，并标志着这座伟大、独特的上海城市前所未有的繁荣与进步时代的开始。届时，可以与中国人一起立即采取步骤，对不仅限于租界而且包括周边地区的整个政府机器和方法进行剧烈和根本性的变革，不久之后，上海将成为世界上最大、如果不是最大的城市之一。
8. 各国籍的选民们，让我们合作吧——让我们为和谐而努力——因此，我敦促你们今年至少尝试一下我的建议。这不会造成任何可能的伤害，并且可能会证明是成功的潜流。
兰德尔·麦克唐纳 (RANDAL MACDONALD)。
上海，1930年4月4日。

6. 原 (HARAWA), Y.
和
7. 木村 (KIMURA), K.,
但在这方面可能还会有进一步的变动。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 1940

Election Fever Sweeping
Over Settlement As Days
For Polling Draw Nearer

Excitement Over Selection Of Nine Candidates
Has Never Been Higher In Municipal History;
National Groups Canvassing For Every Vote

CANDIDATES HAVE ANNOUNCED POLICIES;
NATIONAL RATIO MAY BE ALTERED

Never in Shanghai's history has there been so much comment and excitement over a Municipal Election as that which is scheduled at the ballot of Settlement ratepayers Wednesday and Thursday. Qualified voters of all foreign nationalities will cast their votes for one or more of the 13 candidates who have offered themselves for selection as Councillors during the forthcoming Municipal year. Nine only can be selected—four will go into the discard.

This year, more than ever before, the nationality question has been injected into the poll. There are two American, five British and five Japanese candidates and each national group since the announcement of nominations has been conducting a vigorous campaign for election of their respective nominees.

For the first time in the Municipal history of the Settlement, the Japanese are seeking to secure the election of five candidates. Hitherto the Japanese quota has been two members, with five British and two Americans occupying the other seven seats allotted to the foreign community. Five Chinese members are elected by the Chinese community, bringing the total to 14 Chinese and foreign Councillors. Only on one previous occasion did the Japanese community seek to increase their number of candidates. Two only were elected following a miscount of the ballot, and the subsequent withdrawal of the additional Japanese candidate.

National Viewpoint

The issue this year is regarded among the various national factions as of extreme importance. The British and American communities have been advised to vote solidly for the five British and two American nominees. The Japanese have been instructed to plump equally strongly for the five Japanese candidates to the exclusion of the American and British candidates from the ballot papers. One independent British candidate is seeking election and his presence has further complicated the outcome, according to well-informed circles.

This year there are no clearly defined issues for the ratepayers to decide in casting their votes, apart from the purely national viewpoint. In other years there have been certain definite questions upon which election campaigns have been based, such as the abolition or retention of the Municipal Orchestra, the purchase of a site for a new town hall, the admission of Chinese to the public parks, the admission of Chinese to the Municipal Council and other questions which have lent a certain amount of colour to the campaign.

Voters at the poll to be conducted Wednesday and Thursday will apparently have to decide their candidates on a purely national basis, although the election platforms of candidates have indicated to some extent policies which may be adopted by nominees, if elected.

A record poll is expected as every Settlement resident with a vote is being urged to the ballot boxes. Voting commences each day at 10 a.m. and concludes at 8 p.m.

随着投票日临近，选举热席卷租界

对九名候选人选择的兴奋程度创下市政历史新高；
各国籍群体争取每一张选票

候选人已宣布政策；
国籍比例可能改变

上海历史上从未有过像定于本周三和周四举行的租界纳税人投票那样的市政选举引发如此多的评论和兴奋。所有外籍国籍的合格选民将从13名自荐参选下一市政年度董事的候选人中，投票选出一名或多名。只能选出九名——四人将被淘汰。

今年，国籍问题比以往任何时候都更多地被注入到投票中。有两名美国、五名英国和五名日本候选人，自提名公布以来，每个国籍群体都在为其各自的提名人进行激烈的竞选活动。

在租界市政历史上，日本人首次试图确保五名候选人当选。此前，日本人的名额一直是两名，其余七个分配给外侨社区的席位由五名英国人和两名美国人占据。五名中国董事由中国社区选举产生，使中外董事总数达到14名。日本社区此前只有一次试图增加其候选人数量。在计票错误及随后额外的一名日本候选人退出后，仅当选了两名。

国家视角

今年，这一议题在各国籍派系中被视为极其重要。英国和美国社区被告知要团结一致投票支持五名英国和两名美国提名人。日本人接到指令，同样强烈地投票支持五名日本候选人，而在选票上排除美国和英国候选人。据消息灵通人士称，一名独立的英国候选人正在寻求当选，他的出现使结果变得更加复杂。

今年，除了纯粹的国家视角外，纳税人在投票时没有明确的问题需要决定。在其他年份，曾有一些基于竞选活动的具体问题，例如废除或保留工部局乐队、购买新市政厅用地、允许华人进入公共公园、允许华人进入工部局董事会以及其他为竞选增添一定色彩的问题。

周三和周四进行的投票选民显然必须纯粹基于国籍基础来决定他们的候选人，尽管候选人的竞选纲领在一定程度上表明了如果当选，提名人可能采取的政策。

预计投票率将创纪录，因为每一位有投票权的租界居民都被敦促前往投票站。每天上午10点开始投票，晚上8点结束。

1940
0 1 2

Fateful Week Dawns For Settlement

One of the most vital weeks in the history of the International Settlement began this morning, with one clear-cut issue rising starkly from the welter of Municipal election politics.

This week will decide whether the Japanese obtain virtual control of the Shanghai Municipal Council, or whether the status quo (or a slightly changed ratio) is maintained.

As the campaigns enter the last lap before the fateful Wednesday and Thursday, feverish activity was noted in all camps. The Japanese bid for domination will be hotly contested on all sides in the next few days.

Two main forces face each other in the battle, and they are almost equal in strength. The Japanese vote is now estimated at about 3,700, while the "Anglo-Saxon" vote, which was estimated yesterday at about 3,500, was reported growing in strength, as more British and American ratepayers are being registered on the eligible list.

The minority vote also seemed to be splitting into two distinct camps. The Latin community—Portuguese, Spanish and Italian,—have been reported solidly on the side of the Japanese, while it was expected that part of the German and Russian communities would also vote for the five Japanese candidates.

Minority Group

Totaling about 500 votes, (excluding Germans and Russians), the minority group is split up as follows: French, 100; Portuguese, 60; Italians, 84; Poles, 40; Danes, 39; Norwegians, 36; Dutch, 34; Greeks, 18; Jews, 14; Lithuanians, 13; Spaniards, 13; Swedes, 12; Finns, 3 and other nationalities about 30.

The German vote, totaling about 700, seems to be divided into two parts: one "pro-Aryan", and the other composed mainly of refugees. One refugee pointed out yesterday that the methods of the Japanese in this respect are much like those used by Hitler in his early rise to power.

"The activities of the Japanese are said to be perfectly legal," he said, "but so were these of Hitler. It is a question of what happens after power is once achieved."

Third Power Relations

Informed quarters also pointed out yesterday that the Japanese, if they win control of the Settlement, will be in an enviable position as regards relations with Third Powers. Heretofore, it was noted, most protests to Japan by Third Powers, especially England and America, were based on charges that the activities had been "illegal," or contrary to international law.

However, if the forthcoming elections prove a victory for the Japanese, Third Powers will have nothing on which to base a protest. "It is a case of a semi-totalitarian power using so-called democratic methods in an attempt to defeat the Democracies," the situation was summed up.

An American resident who said that he was "disgusted with the Council's methods," declared yesterday that the Japanese threat of domination will have at least one good effect on the S.M.C. and Settlement residents, if the threat does not succeed. "The big boys are so scared now, that they'll be forced to institute drastic reform measures. The ratepayers are aroused, and they'll demand action after this," he asserted.

S.M.P. Deny Charges

Charges that the Shanghai Municipal Police had intimidated Jewish refugees on Friday, so that they would not vote for the Japanese candidates were emphatically denied yesterday by Police officers at the Wayside Station, in whose district the intimidation was alleged to have occurred.

The Shanghai Mainichi carried a story, which was picked up and circulated by Domei news agency, that at about 3 p.m. seven British and 20 Chinese police officers in uniform surrounded the vicinity of No. 800 Tongshan Road. The British officers were alleged to have made house-to-house visits to Jewish refugees and questioned them, asking whom they were supporting in the elections and what were their relations with the Japanese. "All this information was recorded by the Police officers," the Japanese paper charged. "The police officers are acting beyond their authority; it constitutes interference with the elections."

Said Propaganda

"Propaganda and rubbish," S.M.P. officers told THE CHINA PRESS yesterday. "It's a fairy tale that smacks of the ridiculous." A formal protest may be entered with the Japanese Consulate-General, it was reported yesterday, although informed circles declared that the Police would probably ignore it, as being "too silly to deserve any serious attention."

The Chinese press carried lengthy editorials on the issue, asking that all foreign ratepayers follow the advice of the British Election Committee and the American Association, and vote for the seven "authorised" candidates: the five British and two Americans selected by straw votes, of their respective communities. "Vote for no one else," they said. "Take no chance of jeopardising the results."

Advice to the German community to abstain from voting for the Japanese nominees was also given in the Chinese press. The National Herald declared, "Even the German residents in Shanghai should not support the Japanese candidates, because they should understand that they are likewise liable to expulsion under the slogan of 'a new order in East Asia.' Moreover, it would be unwise for them to lose the friendship of the Chinese by befriending the enemy of China."

Other papers pointed out the implications of such a move. German trade interests in China would inevitably be irreparably hurt, they said.

1940年
0 1 2

租界迎来命运攸关的一周

随着市政选举政治的混乱局面中浮现出一个清晰明确的问题，国际租界历史上最为关键的一周于今晨拉开帷幕。

本周将决定日本人是获得上海工部局的实际控制权，还是维持现状（或仅对比例稍作调整）。

随着竞选活动进入命运攸关的周三和周四前的最后冲刺阶段，各方阵营均表现出狂热的活动迹象。在未来几天内，日本谋求主导地位的企图将在各方面受到激烈 contest。

在这场较量中，两股主要力量针锋相对，且实力几乎相当。目前估计日本方面的选票约为3,700张，而昨日估计约为3,500张的“盎格鲁-撒克逊”选票据报道正在增强，因为越来越多的英美纳税人被登记在合格选民名单上。

少数族裔选票似乎也分裂为两个截然不同的阵营。据报道，拉丁裔群体——葡萄牙人、西班牙人和意大利人——坚定地站在日本一边，同时预计德国和俄国社区的部分人员也将投票支持五名日本候选人。

少数族裔群体

少数族裔群体总计约500张选票（不包括德国人和俄国人），其构成如下：法国人100票；葡萄牙人60票；意大利人84票；波兰人40票；丹麦人39票；挪威人36票；荷兰人34票；希腊人18票；犹太人14票；立陶宛人13票；西班牙人13票；瑞典人12票；芬兰人3票；其他国籍约30票。

德国人的选票总计约700张，似乎分为两部分：一部分是“亲雅利安人”，另一部分主要由难民组成。一名难民昨天指出，日本人在此方面的做法与希特勒早期掌权时使用的手段非常相似。

他说：“据说日本人的活动是完全合法的，但希特勒的活动也是如此。问题在于一旦掌握权力后会发生什么。”

第三国关系

知情人士昨天还指出，如果日本人赢得租界的控制权，他们在与第三国的关系上将处于令人羡慕的地位。此前值得注意的是，第三国（尤其是英国和美国）对日本提出的大多数抗议，都是基于指控其行为“非法”或违反国际法。

然而，如果即将到来的选举证明是日本人的胜利，第三国将没有任何理由提出抗议。有人总结这一局势称：“这是一个半极权国家利用所谓民主手段试图击败民主国家的案例。”

一位自称对工部局做法感到“厌恶”的美国居民昨天宣称，如果日本的统治威胁未能得逞，至少会对工部局和租界居民产生一个良好的效果。“那些大人物现在非常害怕，将被迫采取激烈的改革措施。纳税人已被唤醒，此后他们将要求采取行动，”他断言。

工部局警务处否认指控

针对上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）在周五恐吓犹太难民以使其不投票给日本候选人的指控，据称发生恐吓事件的辖区——路边巡捕房（Wayside Station）的警官们昨天予以坚决否认。

《上海每日新闻》刊登了一则故事，该故事被同盟通讯社（Domei news agency）转载并传播，称下午3点左右，7名英籍巡捕和20名华籍巡捕身着制服包围了同山路800号附近区域。据报道，英籍巡捕挨家挨户拜访犹太难民并进行盘问，询问他们在选举中支持谁以及他们与日本人的关系如何。该日文报纸指控称：“所有这些信息均由巡捕记录在案。巡捕的行为超越了其职权范围；这构成了对选举的干涉。”

称为宣传

工部局警务处官员昨天对《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）表示：“这是宣传和垃圾。这是一个荒谬可笑的神话。”据报道，可能会向日本总领事馆提出正式抗议，尽管知情圈子声称，警方可能会对此置之不理，认为其“过于愚蠢，不值得认真对待”。

中文报刊就此事发表了长篇社论，呼吁所有外籍纳税人遵循英国选举委员会和美国协会的建议，投票支持七位“获授权”的候选人：即由各自社区通过模拟投票选出的五名英国人和两名美国人。社论称：“不要投票给其他人。不要冒损害选举结果的风险。”

中文报刊还建议德国社区不要投票支持日本提名人。《国民新闻》（National Herald）宣称：“即使是在上海的德国居民也不应支持日本候选人，因为他们应该明白，在‘东亚新秩序’的口号下，他们同样面临被驱逐的风险。此外，通过与中国的敌人为友而失去中国人的友谊，对他们来说是不明智的。”

其他报纸指出了此举的含义。它们表示，德国在华贸易利益将不可避免地受到无法弥补的伤害。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

S.M.C. Elections:
What Do Candidates Say?

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
Sir,—Rightly or wrongly, I believe
that many of the major problems con-
fronting the Council are the direct
and indirect consequence of the
efforts which have been made during
the past three years or so to establish
a new order in East Asia.
I refer particularly to such matters
as:—
(a) The absence of Council control
and sanitation in the areas north of
the Creek.
(b). The appalling congestion in
the Settlement arising in the main out
of the destruction of Nantao and
Chapel.
(c). The uncontrolled development
of inferior factories and squatter
settlements in the Western areas.
(d) The breakdown of the Settle-
ment and Concession drainage system
brought about largely by (c) and
resulting in serious floodings even
when rainfall cannot be considered
abnormal.
(e) The fantastic figures to which
the price of rice and locally-produced
foodstuffs have soared.
(f) The spread of gambling, burg-
laries, hold-ups, etc., etc.
One could go on ad infinitum.
I am of the opinion that the present
Council is as well able as any other
to administer ordinary civic affairs,
and I also believe that the new can-
didates offering themselves for elec-
tion will be as impotent as the pre-
sent Council to remedy matters which
are affected by considerations outside
the realm of ordinary civic affairs.
In regard to the latter I may be
wrong, and it would assist me, and
I hope the electorate generally, to
obtain a better appreciation of the
qualifications of the new candidates
if, instead of fulminating upon the
ethics of the "straw vote," or of
oozing platitudes about "national do-
mination" and "economic feudalism,"
or of making sinister and meaning-
less references to evils lurking in
crannies, they would inform us how
they propose to solve the major pro-
blems I have referred to above. What
are the ways and means open to them
which are not available to the present
Council?
B.
Shanghai, Apr. 6.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。

工部局选举：
候选人怎么说？

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

无论对错，我认为工部局面临的许多主要问题，都是过去三年左右为在东亚建立新秩序所作努力的直接和间接后果。

我特别指以下事项：—
(a) 苏州河以北地区缺乏工部局的控制和卫生管理。
(b). 由于南市和闸北的破坏，导致租界内出现可怕的拥挤状况。
(c). 西部地区劣质工厂和贫民窟定居点的无序发展。
(d) 租界和法租界排水系统的崩溃，这在很大程度上是由(c)引起的，导致即使在降雨量不能被视为异常的情况下也发生严重洪涝。
(e) 大米和本地生产的食品价格飙升至惊人的数字。
(f) 赌博、入室盗窃、抢劫等行为的蔓延，等等。

此类问题不胜枚举。

我认为，现任工部局在管理普通市政事务方面与其他任何机构一样有能力，我也相信，参加竞选的新候选人将与现任工部局一样，无力补救受普通市政事务范畴之外的因素影响的问题。

关于后者，我可能是错的。如果新候选人不是大肆抨击“模拟投票”的道德问题，或滔滔不绝地发表关于“民族主导”和“经济封建主义”的陈词滥调，或对潜伏在角落里的邪恶进行阴险且毫无意义的暗示，而是告知我们他们打算如何解决我上述提到的主要问题，那将有助于我，也希望有助于广大选民，更好地了解新候选人的资格。有哪些途径和方法是他们拥有而现任工部局所不具备的？

B.
上海，4月6日。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
April 1940. S. B. (D) 7834
Date 8 / 4 / 40

Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

The printed matter attached, relative to the
forthcoming Municipal Election, was delivered to this office
at 10.30 a.m. April 6. At 10.35 a.m. Mr. W.M. Macoustra
called and asked if any objection existed to the distribution
of this printed matter on public thoroughfares. The voting
paper and the election address will, I understand, be printed
in the English, German, Russian and Italian languages.
Mr. Macoustra proposes to station Chinese distributors at
Central Road and Kiangse Road corner, Nanking Road and The
Bund and at the South end of the Garden Bridge. Distributors
will be in possession of printed matter in one language only
and will distribute under the personal guidance of Mr.
Macoustra. It has not yet been definitely decided on which
dates or during which hours the distributions will be made.

There is nothing in the address which might
violate the Council's proclamation relative to printed
matter, and I have reminded Mr. Macoustra that no obstruction
or nuisance must be committed by the distributors on public
thoroughfares. I suggested it would be preferable for
the printed matter to be delivered to individuals through
the post or by messenger.

Mr. Macoustra also requested permission to station
distributors outside the Drill Hall in the Municipal Compound,
and in respect of this request he was referred to the
Secretary-General.

R. W. YORKE
D. C. (Special Branch)

特别处档案室
1940年4月。 S. B. (D) 7834
日期 1940年4月8日

警务处处长。

先生，

随附的关于即将举行的市政选举的印刷品，于4月6日上午10:30送达本办公室。上午10:35，W.M. Macoustra先生来访，询问在公共道路上分发此印刷品是否存在任何异议。据我了解，选票和竞选宣言将以英文、德文、俄文和意大利文印刷。Macoustra先生提议在中路与江西路路口、南京路与外滩以及外白渡桥南端安排中方分发人员。分发人员将仅持有一种语言的印刷品，并在Macoustra先生的亲自指导下进行分发。具体在哪几天或哪几个小时进行分发尚未最终确定。

该宣言中没有任何内容可能违反工部局关于印刷品的公告，我已提醒Macoustra先生，分发人员不得在公共道路上造成阻碍或滋扰。我建议最好通过邮政或信使将印刷品递送给个人。

Macoustra先生还请求允许在工部局大院内的操练厅外安排分发人员，关于此项请求，他被指引去联系总办。

R. W. YORKE
特别处副督察

April 2, 1940.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO :-

DEMAND FOR MORE JAPANESE REPRESENTATIVES ON
THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL.

At the outset, we wish to point out
that the areas surrounding the district of Shanghai have
been occupied by the Japanese forces and the foreign area
in Shanghai forms a part of the districts under the
influence of the Japanese Army. Secondly, the number of
Japanese residents is rapidly increasing and the
population has reached 70,000. As a result the number
of Japanese ratepayers has reached over 3,000 against
2,800 British ratepayers.

It is natural that such a change in
the local situation should be reflected in the Municipal
Council and the Japanese demand for more representatives
is reasonable and in accordance with the changed situation.
The fact that the British themselves have recommended five
candidates this year would seem to indicate that they
are ignoring the changed situation and are regarding
the International Settlement as their own concession.

It should be noted that the Japanese
are not attempting to monopolise the Settlement or to
replace the British by means of increasing the number of
Japanese representatives on the Council. Mr. Hayashi
stressed this in a statement issued on April 1. The
Japanese desire is to remove monopolization by any Power
in the Settlement; they intend to establish a system so
that the various Japanese nationals can impartially take
part in the administration of the Settlement as befits
its title the "International Settlement". At present,
there are many questions pending such as the reorganization
of the Municipal Council and reconsideration of its
financial policy. These questions should be settled
only by a revision of the Land Regulations. Before the
revision of the Land Regulations is taken in hand, the
number of members of the Municipal Council must be
changed impartially in accordance with the prevailing
situation in the Settlement. The Japanese desire to
increase their representatives arises from this
consideration.

We would like to draw the attention of
the public to the following two points:-

Firstly, the Japanese have independently
decided to recommend five candidates without negotiating
with the British and American residents. We attempted to
increase the number of Japanese representatives to three
in 1936, but owing to the unreasonable election law, we
were defeated. As the British will not dare to abolish
their monopolization of the Settlement, this is the
reason why Japanese have avoided negotiations and have
independently recommended five candidates. This is an
indication of the determination of the Japanese.

Secondly, the Japanese are attempting
to increase their representatives by lawful means. When
disputes over the status of the Settlement arose last year,
it was strongly advocated that the question of the
Settlement, which is a base of anti-Japanese movement, should
be settled by force as it forms part of the Japanese military
operations. But the desire for a lawful settlement of the
dispute prevailed and as a result an agreement was reached
over the Western Area and Hongkew District was reopened.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月2日。

《大陆新报》：

要求增加日本人在工部局董事会中的代表名额。

首先，我们要指出，上海周边地区已被日军占领，上海的外国区域构成了受日本陆军影响地区的一部分。其次，日本侨民人数迅速增加，人口已达70,000人。因此，日本纳税人人数已超过3,000人，而英国纳税人为2,800人。

地方局势的这种变化自然应反映在工部局董事会中，日本人要求增加代表名额是合理的，也符合变化后的局势。英国人今年自行推荐了五名候选人，这一事实似乎表明他们无视局势的变化，并将公共租界视为其专属的租界。

需要注意的是，日本人并非试图通过增加董事会中的日本代表人数来垄断租界或取代英国人。林先生（Mr. Hayashi）在4月1日发表的声明中强调了这一点。日本人的愿望是消除任何强国对租界的垄断；他们打算建立一种制度，使各位日本国民能够与其“国际”租界的称号相称地公正参与租界的管理。目前，有许多悬而未决的问题，如工部局董事会的改组及其财政政策的重新审议。这些问题只有通过修订《土地章程》才能解决。在着手修订《土地章程》之前，必须根据租界当前的局势，公正地改变工部局董事会的成员人数。日本人希望增加其代表人数正是出于这一考虑。

我们愿提请公众注意以下两点：

第一，日本人未与英美侨民协商，便独立决定推荐五名候选人。我们曾于1936年试图将日本代表人数增加至三名，但由于不合理的选举法而失败。既然英国人不敢废除其对租界的垄断，这就是日本人避免谈判并独立推荐五名候选人的原因。这表明了日本人的决心。

第二，日本人正试图通过合法手段增加其代表人数。去年当出现关于租界地位的争端时，有人强烈主张，作为反日运动基地的租界问题，因其构成日本军事行动的一部分，应以武力解决。但依法解决争端的愿望占了上风，结果就西区达成了协议，虹口区也重新开放。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

1 1940

Japanese Give Order
For Vote Of Emigres

While Japanese canvassers are reported ordering Jewish emigres,
who are qualified ratepayers north of the creek, to vote for the
Nipponese candidates, all Spanish ratepayers have been summoned
to visit their Consul-General to confer on the elections.
"We are not doing this to tell our citizens for whom to vote"
said a Spanish Consulate official to the Shanghai Evening Post to-
day. "We are only trying to find out how many Spanish voters
there are."
There were some 300 Spanish citizens in Shanghai he said, and
although most lived in the French Concession, there were only 12
names on the SMC voting list published Saturday. "I think there
should be quite a few more. That is why we have asked our citizens
to call at their consulate, for us to make inquiries."
North of the creek the Japanese have started a campaign to try
to round up minority votes, going round with translators who speak
either German or Yiddish. Last minute efforts of the Japanese to
add more voters to the list are envisaged, despite warning by the
SMC that this should be carried out early.
No announcement as to how many candidates the Japanese are
putting up has been made, and it is expected that they will follow
their normal custom of sending in the names five minutes before
noon tomorrow, closing time.

1 1940

日本人下令
流亡者投票

据报道，当日本拉票人员命令苏州河以北具备纳税人资格的犹太流亡者投票给日本候选人时，所有西班牙纳税人均被召见其总领事以商讨选举事宜。
“我们这样做并不是为了告诉我们的公民该投给谁，”一位西班牙领事馆官员今日对《上海晚邮报》表示。“我们只是试图查明有多少西班牙选民。”
他说，上海约有300名西班牙公民，虽然大多数人住在法租界，但周六公布的工部局选民名单上只有12个名字。“我认为应该还有更多。这就是为什么我们要求我们的公民前往领事馆，以便我们进行查询。”
在苏州河以北，日本人已开始一场运动，试图收拢少数族裔的选票，他们带着会说德语或意第绪语的翻译四处活动。尽管工部局警告此类工作应尽早完成，但仍预计日本人会在最后时刻努力将更多选民加入名单。
关于日本人将提名多少名候选人，尚未发布公告，预计他们将遵循惯例，在明天中午截止时间的最后五分钟提交名单。

Translation

China Evening News of April 5 published the following editorial:

ADVICE TO BRITISH AND AMERICAN RATEPAYERS

The result of the coming Municipal elections on April 10 and 11 will decide the fate of the International Settlement as to whether it will be able to maintain its status quo or whether it will come under the domination of the Japanese. The whole manoeuvre is nothing but an attempt of the Japanese to oust, by political means, the British and American interests from the International Settlement. As the outcome of the elections will not only affect the future of the Settlement but the interests of all the residents as well, we would like to offer a word of advice to the local foreign ratepayers.

There are two ways to counter the Japanese attack on the International Settlement. It is of utmost importance that the British and American ratepayers should collaborate in a united front against the Japanese and vote unanimously for the five British and two American candidates. They should not do anything that is liable to undermine their own strength or to benefit the Japanese. As their interests in Shanghai are considerable and furthermore as they belong to the Anglo-Saxon race, the British and American residents should work in close collaboration and this will be of great benefit to them, but a split in their ranks would lead disaster for both. At ordinary times there may be some discord between the British and American ratepayers, but at this time of crisis they should bury their private grudges and not create any loophole for others. We learn with pleasure that the British and American ratepayers, in the course of their meetings held last night, have resolved to stand shoulder to shoulder in the present Municipal elections. The significance of their move is clear; this concerted action by the British and American residents is an indication, a reflection of the unanimous stand that has been adopted by their respective governments towards the Far Eastern problem.

Secondly, the British and American residents should endeavour to win over the foreign ratepayers except, of course, the Japanese, lest they should be made use of by the Japanese. It is possible that with the war going on in Europe local German residents, who come next in population after the British, Americans and Japanese, may boycott the British and take the side of the Japanese. In this connection, we wish to advise the German residents that if they jeopardise the status quo of the Settlement by such a move, they would be destroying their own relations with China. At this time when the trade between Germany and Japan is fast dwindling and when Germany is endeavouring to restore her vast trade with China, we are convinced that the intelligent German residents in Shanghai will desist from making any move that will favour the Japanese. On this account, it will be wise for the local German community to turn out in support of the British and American candidates.

译文

4月5日的《大美晚报》刊登了以下社论：

致英美纳税人的建议

即将于4月10日和11日举行的工部局选举结果，将决定国际租界的命运，即它能否维持现状，还是将落入日本的统治之下。整个阴谋不过是日本试图通过政治手段将英美利益逐出国际租界的一次尝试。由于选举结果不仅影响租界的未来，也关系到所有居民的利益，我们谨向当地外籍纳税人进一言。

 counter 日本对国际租界的进攻有两种途径。至关重要的是，英美纳税人应结成统一战线对抗日本，并一致投票支持五位英国候选人和两位美国候选人。他们不应做任何可能削弱自身力量或使日本受益的事情。鉴于他们在上海拥有相当大的利益，而且同属盎格鲁-撒克逊种族，英美居民应当密切合作，这将对他们大有裨益；但若内部发生分裂，则会导致双方灾难。平时英美纳税人之间或许存在一些不和，但在这一危机时刻，他们应当摒弃私怨，不给他人留下可乘之机。我们欣慰地获悉，英美纳税人在昨晚举行的会议中已决议在本次工部局选举中并肩作战。此举意义明确；英美居民的这一协同行动，表明并反映了各自政府在远东问题上所采取的一致立场。

其次，英美居民应努力争取除日本人以外的其他外籍纳税人的支持，以免这些人被日本利用。随着欧洲战事的进行，当地德国居民（其人口数量仅次于英、美、日三国居民）可能会抵制英国人而站在日本一边。就此，我们要劝告德国居民，如果通过此类举动危及租界的现状，他们将破坏自己与中国的关系。当前德日贸易迅速萎缩，而德国正努力恢复与中国的庞大贸易，我们相信上海的明智德国居民不会采取任何有利于日本的行动。因此，当地德裔社群出面支持英美候选人是明智之举。

Morning Translation

National Herald publishes the following editorial :-

The Contest For The Election Of Foreign Councillors
In International Settlement

The question of election of councillors in the
Shanghai Municipal Council has now reached a serious stage
because of the Japanese violation of the original ratio of
candidates by increasing the number of their candidates to
five for participation in the forthcoming election. According
to regulations governing the organization of the S.M.C., the
Council has the right to decide upon important administrative
affairs as well as the right to offer suggestions regarding
the enforcement of certain important decisions. Consequently,
it is very powerful and is the supreme administrative organ
of the International Settlement. In former times the
councillors of the S.M.C. were elected by the Foreign
Ratepayers Meeting. It was only during 1928/1930 that the
Chinese began to be represented in the Council by five members.
In the election of councillors this year, a
dispute of an international character has taken place; it is
not so simple as it seems; it is evidently a kind of plot on
the part of the Japanese authorities who are intending to
make use of the present contest as a means to seize the
administrative powers of the S.M.C., thereby enabling them
to bring the whole of the International Settlement under their
virtual control.
The Japanese have made known to the public again
and again their determination in connection with the present
contest for election of councillors in the S.M.C. and are
known to have already made all preparations towards the
attainment of this end. This suffices to prove that the
Japanese have long had an envious eye upon the Settlement;
they now consider it a very rare opportunity for them to
attain their desired object. That Japan has become so
envious towards the foreign controlled areas in Shanghai
is a fact that requires no explanation and is known to all.
The Japanese forces have been engaged in their campaign of
aggression against China for almost three years and they now
realize that they have gone deep into the mire. Consequently,
they find it necessary to intensify their attacks politically
and for this reason they consider the seizure of the Foreign
Settlements an important urgent programme to be carried out
in their political attacks. The Japanese authorities are
doing this because they consider the existence of the European
War a rare opportunity for them to take the place of the

《国民新闻报》刊登以下社论：

国际租界外籍董事选举之争

上海公共租界工部局董事选举问题现已进入严重阶段，原因是日本违反原有的候选人比例，将其参与即将到来的选举的候选人人数增加至五名。根据管理工部局组织的规章，工部局有权决定重要的行政事务，并就某些重要决定的执行提出建议。因此，工部局权力很大，是国际租界的最高行政机关。过去，工部局的董事由外籍纳税人会议选举产生。直到1928/1930年间，中国人才开始有五名代表进入工部局。在今年的董事选举中，发生了一场具有国际性质的争端；这并不像表面看起来那么简单；这显然是日本当局的一种阴谋，他们意图利用当前的竞争作为夺取工部局行政权力的手段，从而使他们能够将整个国际租界置于其实际控制之下。
日本方面已一再向公众表明其在当前工部局董事选举竞争中的决心，并且据悉已为实现这一目标做好了所有准备。这足以证明日本觊觎租界已久；他们现在认为这是实现其 desired object（期望目标）的难得机会。日本对上海的外国控制区如此垂涎，这是一个无需解释且众所周知的事实。日军从事侵华战争已近三年，他们现在意识到自己已深陷泥潭。因此，他们认为有必要在政治上加强攻击，出于这个原因，他们将夺取外国租界视为其政治攻击中要执行的一项重要紧急计划。日本当局之所以这样做，是因为他们认为欧洲战争的存在是他们取代

page_data.en:
April 6, 1940.
Morning Translation

British people in the leading role in the International
Settlement. They are demanding an increase of the number
of their candidates under the pretext that the number of
their ratepayers in Shanghai has increased, but such an
increase is recognized by nobody in view of their forcible
occupation of Hongkew and the Western District. It is said
that the Japanese authorities possess some means to fill up
the empty ranks among their ratepayers. This evidently
proves that they have had the plot under preparation for
some time.
The present contest for election of
councillors in the S.M.C. not only affects the future status
of the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai but also the
international situation in the Far East. The Japanese
not only aim at the occupation of the International
Settlement but they are also intending to bring about the
realization of their idealism for the establishment of a
new order in East Asia as well as the fundamental expulsion
from the Far East of the influence of the third party nations
by means of their control of this Far Eastern metropolis.
Moreover, in case the Japanese succeeded in the seizure of the
administrative power of the International Settlement, they
will naturally make use of the Council in their conspiracy
with the puppet organizations in activities detrimental to
the sovereign rights of China. It is for this reason that
the present attempt of the Japanese should not be looked upon
lightly. It is a plot that impairs the rights of all
parties and should therefore be opposed by all foreign
residents in Shanghai other than the Japanese themselves.
The opposition to this plot by the Chinese residents should
be all the more vigorous. Even the German residents in
Shanghai should not support the Japanese candidates, because
they should understand that they are likewise liable to
expulsion under the slogan of a new order in East Asia.
Moreover, it would be unwise for them to lose the friendship
of the Chinese by befriending the enemy of China.
Though the contest has entered a serious
stage, yet there are still four or five days before the
official election takes place, sufficient for the various
parties concerned to arrive at adequate measures to deal
with the matter. At present it is most important for
the American and British authorities in Shanghai to
co-operate with each other concertedly; at the same time
they should also seek the co-operation of foreign residents
of other neutral parties. They should understand that
Japan has had an envious eye upon the foreign controlled
areas of Shanghai for quite a long time. It was due to
the attitude of compromise and submission on the part of
the Settlement authorities that the Japanese have become
more aggressive. Now they are attempting to seize complete
control of the International Settlement. It is time for
the nations concerned to take positive action to deal with
the matter. The Chinese residents, though they are not in
a position to participate in the election of foreign
councillors, should likewise exert their utmost to co-operate
with the nations concerned, so as to avert an unfavourable
change of the local situation. We should understand that even
after failure this time, the Japanese will make further attempts
next time. However, time is the most remarkable factor in all
things; it may be that the Japanese militarists will not be so
truculent at the election next year as they are at present.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月6日。
晨间译文

英国人在国际租界中主导地位的难得机会。他们以上海日本纳税人数量增加为借口，要求增加其候选人名额，但鉴于他们强行占领虹口和西区，这种增加并未得到任何人的认可。据说日本当局有一些手段来填补其纳税人中的空缺名额。这显然证明他们策划此阴谋已有一段时间。
当前工部局董事选举之争不仅影响上海外国租界的未来地位，也影响远东的国际局势。日本不仅旨在占领国际租界，还意图通过控制这座远东大都市，实现其建立东亚新秩序的理想，并从根本上将第三方国家的影响力驱逐出远东。此外，如果日本成功夺取国际租界的行政权力，他们自然会利用工部局与傀儡组织勾结，进行损害中国主权的活动。正是出于这个原因，不应轻视日本目前的企图。这是一个损害各方权益的阴谋，因此应受到上海除日本人以外的所有外籍居民的反对。中国居民对此阴谋的反对更应 vigorous（激烈）。甚至上海的德国居民也不应支持日本候选人，因为他们应该明白，在“东亚新秩序”的口号下，他们同样面临被驱逐的风险。此外，通过与中国的敌人为友而失去中国人的友谊，对他们来说是不明智的。
尽管竞争已进入严重阶段，但在正式选举举行前仍有四五天时间，足够有关各方采取适当措施来处理此事。目前最重要的是上海的美国和英国当局相互协调合作；同时，他们还应寻求其他中立方面外籍居民的合作。他们应该明白，日本觊觎上海的外国控制区已有很长一段时间。正是由于租界当局的妥协与屈服态度，日本才变得更具侵略性。现在他们正试图完全控制国际租界。有关各国现在是采取积极行动处理此事的时候了。中国居民虽然无法参与外籍董事的选举，但也应尽最大努力与有关各国合作，以避免当地局势发生不利变化。我们应该明白，即使这次失败，日本下次还会再次尝试。然而，时间是万事万物中最显著的因素；也许日本军国主义者在明年的选举中不会像现在这样嚣张。

S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. R. 7834
Date 8 4 40

April 8, 1940. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News (Editorial) dated April 7 :-

The S.M.C. Elections : Advice to German and Jewish
Residents in Shanghai

The creation of a New Order in East Asia is
but another term for the subjugation of China and the
expulsion of third party interests and rights from this
country. In the hope of attaining this object, Japan has
made all kinds of attempts, both forcible and political.
Now she is demanding an increase in the number of Japanese
Councillors on the S.M.C. as a means to seize control of
the International Settlement and to convert it into a
Japanese Concession. If she succeeds in this attempt, not
only will this last stronghold for third party interests
and rights in China disappear but the residents of Shanghai
will have no assurance for their safety and welfare.

The foreign residents in Shanghai have always
been represented by nine seats on the S.M.C., of which
five are occupied by British members, two by Americans
and the rest by Japanese, all of whom are elected by
ratepayers. Ostensibly, the contest seems to be one among
individuals; in reality, the contest has actually become
an international affair. The Japanese desire to increase
the number of their representatives on the Council from
two to five. Should all five Japanese be elected, the
Japanese would have five out of the nine seats on the S.M.C.
and they will therefore be placed in a favourable situation.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处
编号 S. B. R. 7834
日期 1940年4月8日

1940年4月8日。晨间译文。

4月7日的《中美日报》（社论）：

工部局选举：致上海德国和犹太居民的建议

建立“东亚新秩序”不过是征服中国并将第三方利益和权利从这个国家驱逐出去的另一种说法。为了实现这一目标，日本进行了各种尝试，包括武力和政治手段。现在，她要求增加工部局中日本董事的人数，以此作为控制国际租界并将其转变为日本租界的手段。如果她在此尝试中成功，不仅中国境内第三方利益和权利的最后一个堡垒将消失，上海居民的安全和福利也将毫无保障。

上海的外籍居民在工部局中一直由九个席位代表，其中五个由英国成员占据，两个由美国成员占据，其余由日本成员占据，所有这些人都由纳税人选举产生。表面上看，这场竞争似乎是个人之间的竞争；实际上，这场竞争实际上已成为一件国际事务。日本希望将其在工部局中的代表人数从两名增加到五名。如果五名日本候选人全部当选，日本人将在工部局的九个席位中占据五席，从而处于有利地位。

page_data.en:
April 8, 1940. Morning Translation.

The Council meeting issues orders in the administration of the Council. It is not the Secretary and Commissioner-General or the Deputy Secretaries who decide the administrative policy of the S.M.C.; it is the Council which holds meetings once every two weeks. All decisions reached at these meetings are handed to the Secretary for enforcement by his subordinates. Thus, if the Japanese have five seats on the Council, they will have supreme control over the Council meetings and they can vote for all decisions that are favourable to themselves and veto those that are unfavourable. For instance, they can vote for a decision to order the Council to enter into negotiations over all kinds of matters with the puppet organizations, thereby enhancing the legal status of such regimes. Similarly, they will be able to order a change in the administrative system of the S.M.C., or increase the number of Japanese officials, thereby enabling them to seize the entire control of the S.M.C. Should the Japanese succeed in the present elections, they will have full control over the administration of the International Settlement. In that event, not only will the neutrality of the Settlement be violated but the interests of all residents in the Settlement will be seriously affected. Therefore, it is only natural that the Japanese should intensify their activities to bring about the expulsion of foreign interests from China and for domination of the Orient if they are given an opportunity.

The local British and American ratepayers are said to have made preparations to deal with the Japanese campaign. According to statistics, the joint British-American group can pool 3,574 votes, while the Japanese have only 3,600 votes. These figures do not include the votes held by German ratepayers or Jewish refugees in Shanghai. The former have 300 votes, while the latter hold 500 votes. If all these 800 votes are cast in favour of the British and American candidates, the latter will be sure to get more votes than the Japanese. Consequently, these 800 votes will decide the future of the International Settlement.

Germany is now engaged in an armed conflict with Britain; therefore it is only natural that the German ratepayers will refuse to vote for the British candidates. But this does not mean that they will vote in favour of the Japanese. They can vote for the two American candidates and withhold voting for either the British or the Japanese. We believe that the wise German ratepayers must have already considered the matter and realized from the lessons they received at Tientsin, Tsingtao and other ports in North China that they will not be able to develop their commerce in Shanghai if this city is to be under the control of the Japanese. They have already suffered much at the hands of the Japanese; consequently they can place no trust in the verbal assurances of the Japanese. Therefore, we are of the opinion that in their own interests, to say nothing of their concern over the future of the International Settlement, the German ratepayers should refrain from voting for the Japanese.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月8日。晨间译件。

工部局董事会会议发布工部局行政管理命令。决定上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）行政政策的并非总办兼总监务或副总办，而是每两周召开一次会议的董事会。这些会议上作出的所有决定均交由总办，由其下属执行。因此，如果日本人在董事会中拥有五个席位，他们将对董事会会议拥有最高控制权，他们可以投票赞成所有对其有利的决定，并否决那些不利的决定。例如，他们可以投票决定责令工部局就各种事务与伪组织进行谈判，从而增强此类政权的法律地位。同样，他们将能够责令改变工部局的行政体制，或增加日本官员的数量，从而使他们得以夺取对工部局的全面控制。如果日本人在目前的选举中成功，他们将完全控制公共租界的行政。在那种情况下，不仅租界的中立地位将受到侵犯，而且租界内所有居民的利益也将受到严重影响。因此，如果日本人获得机会，他们加紧活动以将外国利益逐出中国并主宰东方，也是顺理成章之事。

据称，当地的英美纳税人已做好准备以应对日本的竞选活动。据统计，英美联合集团可汇集3,574票，而日本人仅有3,600票。这些数字不包括德国纳税人或上海犹太难民持有的选票。前者拥有300票，后者持有500票。如果这800票全部投给英美候选人，后者的得票数肯定将超过日本人。因此，这800票将决定公共租界的未来。

德国目前正与英国处于武装冲突之中；因此，德国纳税人拒绝投票给英国候选人也是顺理成章之事。但这并不意味着他们会投票支持日本人。他们可以投票给两名美国候选人，而不投票给英国人或日本人。我们相信，明智的德国纳税人一定已经考虑过此事，并从他们在天津、青岛和华北其他港口吸取的教训中认识到，如果上海这座城市处于日本人的控制之下，他们将无法在上海发展其商业。他们已经在日本人手中吃尽了苦头；因此，他们不能信任日本人的口头保证。因此，我们认为，出于自身利益考虑，更不用说对公共租界未来的关切，德国纳税人应避免投票给日本人。

page_data.en:
April 8, 1940. Morning Translation.

Now take, for instance, the Jewish rate-payers who are mostly refugees who recently arrived in Shanghai. They want to take up residence in Shanghai rather than in Tientsin, Tsingtao, Canton and other ports in China because following the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from Shanghai, the International Settlement has remained neutral. Consequently, they must have enjoyed a certain amount of benefit from the neutrality of the Settlement. The Jewish refugees should remember that at one time they were refused entry into Hongkew by the Japanese---a fact that goes to show that the Japanese have no sympathy towards the Jewish people. Therefore, we may surmise whom the Jewish refugees will support in the present elections. Moreover, being immigrants in China, they should naturally seek the friendship of the Chinese so as to secure more room for the development of their commerce. Though the Chinese Government is now away from Shanghai, it has never given up its sovereign rights over this port. The Chinese Government does not like to see any change in the present status of the Foreign Settlements in Shanghai nor does it like to see the Jewish refugees vote for the Japanese, thereby indirectly affecting the neutrality of the foreign controlled areas.

We believe that if the Jewish residents will carefully consider all the circumstances, they will not go so far as to create opportunities for the Japanese, thereby impairing the neutrality of the International Settlement resulting in the prevention of the development of their legitimate trade under Japanese domination of the Orient and indirectly losing the friendship of the world because of this blunder---a blunder that will never be pardoned by future generations of Jews.
page_data.zh:
1940年4月8日。晨间译件。

再以犹太纳税人为例，他们大多是最近抵达上海的难民。他们希望定居上海，而不是天津、青岛、广州和中国其他港口，因为在中国军队撤离上海后，公共租界保持了中立。因此，他们一定从租界的中立地位中获得了一定的利益。犹太难民应该记得，日本人曾一度拒绝他们进入虹口——这一事实表明日本人对犹太民族毫无同情心。因此，我们可以推测犹太难民在本次选举中将支持谁。此外，作为在中国的移民，他们自然应寻求与中国人的友谊，以便为其商业发展争取更多空间。虽然中国政府目前已不在上海，但它从未放弃对该口岸的主权权利。中国政府不愿看到上海外国租界的现状发生任何变化，也不愿看到犹太难民投票给日本人，从而间接影响外国控制区的中立地位。

我们相信，如果犹太居民仔细考虑所有情况，他们不会走到为日本人创造机会的地步，从而损害公共租界的中立地位，导致他们在日本人主宰东方的情况下无法发展其合法贸易，并因这一失误而间接失去世界的友谊——这一失误将永远得不到后世犹太人的原谅。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
APR 5 1940
Emigres
Deciding S'hai
Fate
British-American Bloc
Votes Equal Japanese;
Jewish Holding Balance
NIPPONESE RESCIND VETO
ON RELATIVES ENTERING
CITY, WOO WAYSIDE AID
Exchange Drop Enlarges Electorate
Leaving their homelands within only the past year or so, German and Austrian Jewish refugees today hold the destiny of the International Settlement of Shanghai in their hands.
The emigre vote in the Municipal Elections to be held next week, eagerly wooed by the Japanese with specious promises, and innuendo threats, are seen as the decisive factor as to whether the Japanese may acquire five members of the SMC. at the expense of the British and Americans, and thus gain a position from which they may eventually control the Settlement.
German Paradox
Actually a paradoxical situation seems to have arisen as regards the German (and Austrian) vote. The Japanese are asking both Nazis and Jews to vote for them.
Allotting the minority votes either to the British-American bloc or to the Japanese, the position appears to be that the Japanese plus Italian and Spanish vote roughly totals the British-American vote plus French, Portuguese and Dutch. Leaving the Russian vote to cancel itself out, the balance of power rests with the Germans, of whom the bulk are emigres.
Balance Sheet
Taking estimates of the total number of votes, the balance sheet, as it were, is as follows:
British 2000 Japanese 2000
American 800 Italian 80
French 100 Spanish 20
Portuguese 100
Dutch 94
2074 2000
The Russian vote totals 304, of which approximately 100 live north of the creek and will probably be entitled to vote for the against the remainder this leaves the German vote as that which will swing the election one way or another.
Increase Seen
Of the 800 German and Austrian ratepayers qualified to vote, 800 are emigres. Many of these live north of the Soochow Creek, where the Japanese have been canvassing them assiduously. Next year it is estimated that there will be an additional 800 emigre ratepayers, as more and more of them find their feet, lease houses and open shops.
The Japanese authorities have been particularly active over gaining the friendship of the German emigres, and thus their votes, in the past two or three months. Whereas a month ago they had refused the application of many emigres for landing permits for relatives whom they were bringing to Shanghai, the authorities have now intimated that they are willing to apply once more for such permits.
Japanese Votes
Japanese voters last year totalled a little over 1600. This number has been trebled in the past year by many immigrants during that period, who knew nothing of the history of Shanghai and its large foreign investments, and who will vote exactly as they are told by their authorities.
The increase of 3000 is largely due to the fall in exchange.
Some former residents and many new arrivals find that they are qualified ratepayers because the rentals they pay total but Yen 22, taking the Taels 50 stipulation as equalling $70 and converting at the official exchange rate in force in Japan. With former rates of exchange a large number of these would never have been ratepayers.
Chinese Stand Pat
The Chinese Ratepayers' Association has formally notified the Shanghai Municipal Council that the five Chinese members of the Council and members of the various committee will serve for another term.
The re-elected five Chinese councillors are: Messrs. Yu Yaching, shipping magnate and the doyen of Chinese community leaders; L. T. Yuan, prominent Chinese merchant of varied interests; William Gockson, managing director of the Wing On Company; Eugene Y. B. Kiang, prominent legal practitioner; and Yulin Hsi, prominent chartered accountant.
（批：YODA S. 3 No. S. B. D. 7831 Date 6 / 10）
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》
1940年4月5日
流亡者
决定上海
命运
英美集团
票数与日本持平；
犹太人掌握平衡
日本人撤销亲属
入城禁令，拉拢
中间派援助
汇率下跌扩大选民范围
德国和奥地利犹太难民在仅仅过去一年左右的时间里离开家园，如今掌握着上海公共租界的命运。
在下周举行的工部局选举中，流亡者的选票受到日本人以虚伪承诺和含蓄威胁的热切拉拢，被视为决定性因素，决定着日本人是否可能以牺牲英美利益为代价获得工部局（SMC）的五个席位，从而获得最终控制租界的地位。
德国悖论
实际上，在德国（和奥地利）选票方面似乎出现了一种矛盾的局面。日本人要求纳粹分子和犹太人都投票给他们。
将少数族裔选票要么分配给英美集团，要么分配给日本人，局势似乎是：日本人加上意大利人和西班牙人的选票大致等于英美选票加上法国人、葡萄牙人和荷兰人的选票。让俄罗斯选票相互抵消，平衡权力掌握在德国人手中，其中大部分是流亡者。
资产负债表
如果对选票总数进行估算，所谓的资产负债表如下：
英国人 2000 日本人 2000
美国人 800 意大利人 80
法国人 100 西班牙人 20
葡萄牙人 100
荷兰人 94
2074 2000
俄罗斯选票总数为304票，其中约100人居住在苏州河以北，可能有资格投票反对其余部分，这使得德国选票成为左右选举结果的关键。
预计增长
在800名有资格投票的德国和奥地利纳税人中，800人是流亡者。其中许多人居住在苏州河以北，日本人一直在该地积极向他们拉票。据估计，明年还将增加800名流亡者纳税人，因为越来越多的人站稳脚跟，租赁房屋并开设商店。
在过去两三个月里，日本当局特别积极地争取德国流亡者的友谊，从而争取他们的选票。一个月前，他们还拒绝了许多流亡者为其带往上海的亲属申请登陆许可证，但现在当局暗示愿意再次为此类许可证提出申请。
日本选票
去年日本选民总数略超过1600人。在过去一年里，由于期间许多移民的到来，这一数字增加了两倍，这些人对上海的历史及其巨大的外国投资一无所知，并将完全按照当局的指示投票。
3000人的增长很大程度上是由于汇率下跌所致。
一些前居民和许多新来者发现他们有资格成为纳税人，因为他们支付的租金总额仅为22日元，按照50两相当于70美元的规定，并按日本现行的官方汇率换算。按照以前的汇率，这些人中的大多数永远不会有纳税人资格。
中国人维持现状
中国纳税人协会已正式通知上海公共租界工部局，工部局的五名中国董事及各委员会成员将继续任职一届。
重新当选的五名中国董事是：航运巨头、华人社区领袖元老虞洽庆先生；拥有多种利益的著名华商袁履登（L. T. Yuan）先生；永安公司总经理郭顺（William Gockson）先生；著名法律从业者江一平（Eugene Y. B. Kiang）先生；以及著名注册会计师席玉麟（Yulin Hsi）先生。
（批注：YODA S. 3 No. S. B. D. 7831 日期 6 / 10）

SM ELECTION
DRIVE OPENED
BY AMERICANS

Committee Seeks Vote
Holders Not Yet
Registered

POLL PLANS SET

Under the chairmanship
of Mr. Wilber Judd, a
special "get-out-the-vote"
committee of the American
Association held its initial
meeting in the American Club
at 10 o'clock this morning and
laid out a comprehensive cam-
paign of activity for the
period before and during the
municipal election on April 10 and
11 next week.

Work of various sorts which has
already been instituted will be
continued and accelerated, with
special emphasis at this phase on
seeing to it that all Americans
residing in the International Set-
tlement and entitled to vote are
put on the list of registered voters.

Next week the work will enter
the phase of getting the register-
ed voters to the polls.

Circular Letter

A circular letter is being pre-
pared, to go out to American
voters urging them among other
things to vote early on the first
day, Wednesday. That evening
a check-over will be made, in
order to put special pressure on
voters who have not gone to the
polls, and it will greatly facilitate
the task of the committee as
well as saving the more energetic
ratepayers from needless remin-
ders of their duty if they will
vote the first day so that their
names can be eliminated.

The letter will also request
American ratepayers to vote for
the seven official foreign can-
didates, pointing out that the
committee does not assess the
merits of any individual can-
didate but that a vote cast for
others than the official candidates
will help destroy the chances that
one or more of the American
candidates will be elected.

Arrangements are to be made
whereby American ratepayers
who have no way of getting to
the polls will be provided with
transportation.

Unregistered Votes

With reference to the problem
of unregistered potential voters,
the committee is following up
work which started with an Am-
erican Association circular letter

sent out March 8. It is under-
stood that as result of this letter,
a number of people telephoned to
the office of the secretary, Mr.
James M. Howes, at the Ameri-
can Chamber of Commerce, and
obtained the necessary informa-
tion but took no further steps
when they found that some ad-
ditional show of energy was re-
quired. Efforts to stir these
laggards into qualifying as rate-
payers constitute one of the im-
mediate jobs being undertaken
by an augmented office staff
including a number of volun-
teers.

It is pointed out that anyone
paying rates on housekeeping
quarters of $31.60 a quarter or
over in the Settlement (slightly
more for other categories) which
means payment of approximate-
ly $90 a month rent inclusive of
taxes (providing that this does
not apply to people living in
lodging places and specially con-
tracted as a lodger, even
temporary of a single room, who
this sub-let or otherwise, gives
this right providing there are
housekeeping facilities putting
one into a ratepayer status.

Certificates

Such persons may fill out a
"Certificate of Occupancy" to be
had from the Deputy Treasurer
Revenue, Revenue Office, Ad-
ministration Building, 209 Kiangse
Road, telephone 12810 extension
27. The certificate must be
signed by the landlord or person
from whom sublet. Americans
may obtain any further or special
information by calling the Am-
erican Association, telephone
14742, its headquarters being at
the American Club, 223 Foochow
Road.

An official statement specially
furnished the Shanghai Evening
Post on the subject of voters'
qualifications gives the entire
technical position in detail, as
follows:

Regulation Quoted

Land Regulation XIX sets out
that:—"Every foreigner, either in-
dividually or as a member of a
firm, residing in the Settlement,
having paid all taxes due, and
being an owner of land of not
less than five hundred taels in
value, whose annual payment of
assessment on land or houses or
both, exclusive of all payments
in respect of licenses, shall amount
to the sum of ten taels and up-
wards, or who shall be a house-
holder paying on an assessed
rental of not less than five hun-
dred taels per annum and up-
wards, shall be entitled to vote
in the election of the said Mem-
bers of the Council and at the
public meetings. Provided always
that the proxies of Ratepayers
only who are absent from the
Consular District of Shang-
hai, or are prevented by
illness from attending shall be
admitted to vote at such meet-
ings."

Thus it will be seen that a
vote can be claimed only by
virtue of the ownership of land
of the requisite value or of being
a householder (or renter of an
office shop or flat) on a certain
minimum assessed rental. In
cases where landlords are letting
premises for a sum inclusive of
rates (such as apartment build-
ings) the landlords are required
to furnish the Revenue Office
quarterly with a list of tenants
showing the gross rental paid
in each case. They are also re-
quired to sign a declaration that
such rates are paid for and on
behalf of such tenants. Those
tenants named who pay the re-
quisite rental under Land Regula-
tion XIX are given votes.

Living Quarters

Also in cases where living
quarters are provided by the em-
ployer he makes an annual re-
turn to the Revenue Office of
the premises occupied by each
individual employee and showing
the rateable value on which
General Municipal Rate is paid
by him on the employee's behalf.
Similar conditions prevail in
regard to the occupation of office
premises where the rental paid
includes the General Municipal
Rate. Forms are supplied by
the Revenue Office and upon
these must be stated the amount
of the General Municipal Rate
included in the rental.

Apartments

Occupation of furnished apart-
ments when the occupier depends
upon the landlord for essential
services in connection with these
apartments precludes the oc-
cupier from being considered a
householder within the meaning
of Land Regulation XIX; he is
a lodger. The general principle
may be set out as follows:—

"To entitle a person to a fran-
chise as a householder he must
show that he occupies a house or
a part of a house separately. If
another person is really in con-
trol of that part of the house the
person living in it has not a
separate occupation, he is a
lodger. On the other hand, if
he has an independent occupa-
tion which the landlord cannot
control his occupation is that of
a tenant and entitles him to a
franchise as an inhabitant oc-
cupier."

340

工部局选举
美国人发起
动员活动

委员会寻求尚未
登记的选民
投票

投票计划已定

在威尔伯·贾德（Wilber Judd）先生的主持下，美国协会的一个特别“动员投票”委员会于今天上午10时在美国总会举行了首次会议，并制定了在下周4月10日和11日市政选举前后期间开展全面活动的计划。

已经启动的各种工作将继续并加速进行，这一阶段的重点是确保所有居住在公共租界并有资格投票的美国人都被列入登记选民名单。

下周，工作将进入引导登记选民前往投票站的阶段。

通函

目前正在准备一封通函，发给美国选民，敦促他们除其他事项外，在第一天（星期三）尽早投票。当晚将进行核查，以便对尚未去投票的选民施加特别压力；如果选民能在第一天投票，从而将其名字从待催办名单中剔除，这将大大 облегчить委员会的工作，并使那些较为积极的纳税人免于收到不必要的职责提醒。

该信函还将请求美国纳税人投票支持七名正式外籍候选人，指出委员会并不评估任何个别候选人的优劣，但投票给非正式候选人将会破坏一名或多名美国候选人当选的机会。

将作出安排，为无法自行前往投票站的美国纳税人提供交通工具。

未登记选民

关于潜在未登记选民的问题，委员会正在跟进始于3月8日发出的一封美国协会通函的工作。据悉，由于这封信，许多人致电美国商会秘书詹姆斯·M·豪斯（James M. Howes）先生的办公室，获得了必要信息，但当发现需要再付出一些努力时，便未采取进一步行动。促使这些拖延者取得纳税人资格的努力，构成了由包括多名志愿者在内的增补办公室职员正在承担的即时任务之一。

有人指出，凡在租界内缴纳每季度31.60美元或以上住宅税捐的人士（其他类别略高），即相当于每月支付约90美元含税费的租金（只要此规定不适用于居住在寄宿处所并特别以寄宿者身份签约的人，即使是临时单人间，若通过转租或其他方式，且具备居家生活设施，从而使人具备纳税人地位，则享有此权利）。

证明书

此类人士可填写一份“居住证明书”，该表格可向江西路209号行政大楼税务局副局长办公室索取，电话12810转27。证明书必须由房东或转租人签署。美国人如需获取更多或特别信息，可致电美国协会，电话14742，其总部设在福州路223号美国总会。

就选民资格问题专门提供给《上海晚邮报》的一份官方声明，详细阐述了全部技术细节，如下：

引用章程

《土地章程》第十九条规定：“凡居住于租界之内之外人，无论个人或商号成员，已缴清一切应付税捐，且为价值不少于五百两之土地所有者，其每年缴纳之地税或房捐或两者合计（不包括一切执照费）达十两及以上者，或为年纳评估租金不少于五百两及以上之住户者，均有权在选举上述董事会董事及出席公众大会时投票。惟须注意，仅当纳税人因不在上海领事管区或因病无法出席时，其代理人方获准在此类会议上投票。”

由此可见，只有凭借拥有 requisite 价值的土地，或作为按最低评估租金计算的住户（或办公室、店铺、公寓的承租人），方可主张投票权。在房东出租房屋收取包含税捐的租金（如公寓大楼）的情况下，房东须每季度向税务局提交一份租户名单，列明每种情况下支付的总租金。他们还须签署声明，证实此类税捐系代表此类租户支付。根据《土地章程》第十九条缴纳规定租金的上述具名租户，将被授予投票权。

居住用房

此外，在雇主提供居住用房的情况下，雇主须每年向税务局申报每位员工所占用的房屋，并显示由其代表员工缴纳一般市政捐的应税价值。在办公用房的占用方面，若支付的租金包含一般市政捐，则适用类似条件。表格由税务局提供，上面必须注明租金中包含的一般市政捐金额。

公寓

当居住者依赖房东提供与公寓相关的基本服务时，占用带家具公寓的情况排除了占用者被视为《土地章程》第十九条意义上的“住户”的可能性；他是一名寄宿者。一般原则可表述如下：

“要使一个人以住户身份获得选举权，他必须证明他单独占用一所房屋或房屋的一部分。如果另一人实际上控制着该部分房屋，则居住其中的人并非独立占用，而是寄宿者。另一方面，如果他拥有房东无法控制的独立占用权，则其身份为租户，并使其作为居住占用者享有选举权。”

Japanese Seek To Halt Probe
Of Ratepayers' Qualifications

Complaining against the activities of officers of the Revenue Department of the Shanghai Municipal Council in investigating the qualifications of Japanese "indirect" ratepayers, the Japanese Residents Corporation yesterday urged high officials of the S.M.C. to curb the inquiry, according to Japanese reports.

A spokesman for the Japanese Residents Corporation is stated to have told Japanese pressmen yesterday that the action of these "lower grade" Council officials constitutes a violation of an understanding between the S.M.C. and the Corporation based upon a recent exchange of letters.

The spokesman also was quoted as saying that "these minor officials, apparently prejudiced against the increase in Japanese ratepayers, are acting in disregard of the wishes of higher officials of the Council."

Residences Visited By Officers

Revenue officers, accompanied by policemen, the Japanese spokesman continued, had started to visit the residences, godowns and other properties of Japanese who were paying their rates indirectly to the Council and were therefore entitled to vote in the coming elections.

This action, the spokesman deplored, had been taken without any notice of it being given to the Corporation. Certificates of occupancy, for persons paying their rates "indirectly," were forwarded to the Council by the Corporation under written agreement.

日本人试图阻止
对纳税人资格的调查

据日文报道，日本居留民团昨日投诉上海公共租界工部局税务局官员调查日本“间接”纳税人资格的活动，并敦促工部局高级官员遏制此项调查。

据称，日本居留民团发言人昨日告诉日本记者，这些工部局“下级”官员的行为违反了工部局与该团基于近期换文达成的谅解。

该发言人还被引述称，“这些低级官员显然对日本纳税人的增加抱有偏见，其行为无视工部局高级官员的意愿。”

官员走访住所

该日本发言人继续称，税务官员在警察陪同下，已开始走访那些间接向工部局缴纳税捐、因而有权在即将举行的选举中投票的日本人的住所、仓库及其他产业。

该发言人对此表示遗憾，称采取此行动前未通知居留民团。根据书面协议，居留民团已将“间接”纳税人的居住证明书转交工部局。

CHINA PRESS.

1940

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED
BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

Thoughts On The Election
THERE are some foreigners in Shanghai who have been guilty of saying: "Let the Japanese run the blooming Council. They can't do any worse than the crowd that is already in office. But perhaps these people have never been to Harbin. Perhaps they have closed their eyes to the corruption, vice and violent crime that has been rampant in the "badlands" on the western fringe of the International Settlement for the past two years or more.

It is quite possible that these individuals have ignored the state of condition in Hsinkew; just how completely the Japanese have taken over control in the northern and eastern districts.

I should also calculate that it is more than likely that these people do not know that the municipal rate in the International Settlement, even with the proposed 50 per cent increase, is lower than it is in any other city of any size in China, or Japan, or the whole of the Far East for that matter, and certainly it is much lower than the rate in any city of the western world.

Or perhaps these same people have never stopped to consider the fact that were they residing in their home countries, the United States or Britain for instance, or any other western nation for that matter, they would pay a high income tax and a dozen and one other taxes from which they are freed in Shanghai.

And a lot of their women folks would be doing their own house work. I raise this point because, if the Japanese gain control of the International Settlement, as they are now striving to do, there will be a lot of lads and their families leaving this town for other parts because their new masters don't want them around. This should be no secret to anyone who has lived here for any length of time. The precedent was established at Harbin and Mukden and perpetuated at Tientsin and Peiping and is now extending into Central China. And when these people get back home or wherever else they may go, they'll discover just how foolish they were to do so much kicking about things here in Shanghai.

Please understand that I am talking about the case of the average ratepayer in Shanghai and not

from the viewpoint of the Chinese. I know many will raise the question: "What about the high rents, sometimes excessive rents we are paying? What about Municipal Council waste? What about the orchestra? What about the pivot boys? And how about this, that and the other thing? What about the surcharges on power and gas and other utilities?"

I admit that these would be issues of importance under more normal conditions but they fade away into obscurity when compared with the much greater issue involved in this election—whether or not a Japanese dictatorial administration shall be imposed on the Settlement. Actually, the entire situation boils to the fact that there is only one issue involved in this election, namely the boys from north of Soochow Creek against the people who built Shanghai and made it a great city.

Although this is the only issue that the ratepayer should expect to solve in this election, it is possible to answer, in a single paragraph, all the other minor questions that Ranald G. MacDonald and his supporters have raised. And in this connection, let me ask a question of the average foreign ratepayer in Shanghai who is entitled to vote. How is your standard of living? Do you have a cook or a house-boy to look after your apartment? Do you make the beds yourself or does a boy do it? Does your wife slave over a washtub doing her own laundry? Certainly she doesn't. Do you have enough to eat everyday? Do you have enough to go to cinema? I know the answer to that. Box office receipts show that both foreigners and Chinese are spending far more money on pictures than they ever did before and that attendance is much greater? Do you still manage to go to a night club once in a while? I also know the answer to that. Seventy per cent of you do. And when you do, you spend more money in a single night than you do on your surcharges.

The point is that the standard of living of the average Shanghai foreign ratepayer today is better than he would find in his home country. Hence, when it comes to deciding between his minor complaints against the administration of the Settlement and the greater issue at stake, he has only one choice and that is to vote solid for the status quo candidates in the forthcoming election.
