1940年

我常常在想
卡罗尔·D·奥尔科特（Carroll D. Alcott）著

关于选举的思考
在上海，有些外国人曾不负责任地说：“让日本人去管那个该死的工部局吧。他们不会比现在在任的那帮人干得更糟。”但也许这些人从未去过哈尔滨。也许他们对过去两年或更长时间里，在国际租界西部边缘的“不良地带”猖獗的腐败、罪恶和暴力犯罪视而不见。

这些个人很可能忽视了虹口（Hsinkew，音译）的状况；即日本人在北部和东部地区接管控制的程度之深。

我也应该想到，这些人极有可能不知道，即使加上拟议中的50%增幅，国际租界的市政税率仍低于中国、日本乃至整个远东任何同等规模城市的税率，当然也远低于西方世界任何城市的税率。

或者，也许同样是这些人，从未停下来考虑过这样一个事实：如果他们居住在自己的祖国，例如美国或英国，或其他任何西方国家，他们将缴纳高额的所得税以及十几种其他税项，而在上海他们却免除了这些税负。

而且他们的许多女性家属将不得不亲自做家务。我提出这一点是因为，如果日本人像现在正努力做的那样取得了国际租界的控制权，将会有许多年轻人及其家庭离开这座城市前往其他地方，因为他们的新主子不希望他们留在这里。对于任何在此居住过一段时间的人来说，这都不应是什么秘密。这一先例已在哈尔滨和沈阳确立，并在天津和北平得以延续，现在正扩展到华中地区。而当这些人回到家乡或去往其他任何地方时，他们会发现自己在上海如此牢骚满腹是多么愚蠢。

请理解，我谈论的是上海普通纳税人的情况，而并非

从中国人的角度出发。我知道许多人会提出这样的问题：“我们支付的高昂租金，有时甚至是过高的租金，该怎么办？工部局的浪费怎么办？乐队怎么办？门童（pivot boys，原文用词，指代特定服务人员）怎么办？还有这个、那个以及其他事情怎么办？电力、煤气和其他公用事业的附加费又怎么办？”

我承认，在更正常的条件下，这些问题都很重要，但与本次选举所涉及的更大问题——即是否要在租界强加一个日本独裁行政机构——相比，它们便显得微不足道了。实际上，整个局势归结为一点，即本次选举只涉及一个问题：苏州河以北的那些人对抗建设上海并使其成为伟大城市的人们。

虽然这是纳税人期望在本次选举中解决的唯一问题，但仍可以用一段话来回答兰纳德·G·麦克唐纳（Ranald G. MacDonald）及其支持者提出的所有其他次要问题。就此而言，让我向上海有资格投票的普通外国纳税人问一个问题。你的生活水平如何？你有厨师或男仆来打理你的公寓吗？床铺是你自己整理还是由男仆整理？你的妻子是否在洗衣盆前辛苦劳作，亲自洗衣服？当然不是。你每天有足够的食物吗？你有足够的钱去看电影吗？我知道答案。票房收入显示，外国人和中国在电影上的花费比以往任何时候都多，而且观影人数也大大增加？你还能偶尔去夜总会吗？我也知道答案。你们中有70%的人能去。而且当你去的时候，你一个晚上花的钱比你的附加费还多。

关键在于，如今上海普通外国纳税人的生活水平比他在本国所能找到的要好。因此，当他在对租界行政管理的微小不满与面临的重大问题之间做出抉择时，他只有一个选择，那就是在即将到来的选举中坚定地投票支持维持现状的候选人。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI PRESS
APR 4 1940
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. G. 7834
You, The Ratepayers

THIS is no time for recrimination; rather it is the time for urgent, but calm consideration of an acute crisis in Shanghai's civic affairs, but at the outset it must be admitted that the dilemma in which voters find themselves today as the result of the Japanese election bombshell is largely the outcome of ratepayers' lack of interest in their Council matters.

Briefly, the situation is this: The Japanese with a certain 3,000 or so votes are nominating five candidates for the Council; eight other foreign candidates (including Mr. R. McDonald's last-minute entry) will share the support of approximately 4,000 rate-payers. Both groups will compete for the minority votes (foreign ratepayers other than Japanese, British and American) which number about 1,000 and which are as yet the unknown quantity in the mathematical problem set out above. The nomination of Mr. McDonald has further involved the problem.

If the forthcoming elections are voted on a national ticket, and if the foreign community is finally shocked out of its customary apathy, as it should have been by the Japanese action, then conjecture may be simplified on the basis of the figures given above. There are eight foreign candidates, who, if elected, would leave only one seat for a Japanese candidate; by this token, if two Japanese candidates are elected then there appears to be no reason why the whole five should not be chosen for seats on the Council, as a majority for two on the national ticket would mean a majority for all.

THERE are, however, considerations other than national prejudice and preference which may vitally affect the returns next week, and they cannot be ignored. The Council's record from a strictly financial view is written in red, and its political history is not much happier. The imposition of a 50 per cent increase in taxation is going to hit many pockets, and in times such as these a man's pocket is his most vulnerable point, while politically there is a small group of ardently pro-Japanese foreigners who will support the Nippon cause.

Thus there arises a distinct possibility that all five Japanese candidates for the Council will be elected, with eventual results that are utterly impossible to forecast in the existing circumstances, but with the immediate result that the Japanese would be given virtual control of the Settlement.

To use a phrase popular with the Japanese publicists, "it goes without saying" that Japanese Councillors would take their orders direct from the Army Headquarters in Tokyo, and those who have suffered from the Japanese Army's conception of the "new order in East Asia" will understand what that means. It means the rapid and as complete as possible exclusion of all foreign participation in what the Japanese Army deems to be its particular sphere, in short the Nipponization of the Settlement.

However, all other considerations apart, the elections next week are certain to be spectacular, with preceding campaigns unequalled in the history of the Settlement. It was understood yesterday that the Japanese ratepayers had already received their instructions on how to vote and for whom, while yesterday afternoon both the British and American election committees held urgent meetings to discuss the situation arising out of the Japanese move. Doubtless both groups decided on measures to ensure as great a representation of nationals at the polls as humanly possible in order to maintain the status quo of five Britons, two Americans and two Japanese on the Council, and if the elections of 1936 set any precedent, then ratepayers during the coming week may expect to receive a flood of "propaganda."

The lines along which the Japanese will justify their nomination of five candidates, obviously will be numerical and possibly political necessity, while the British and American groups will base their claims on economic interests, of which they undoubtedly can claim the greater proportion in Shanghai.

The national appeal, it is expected, will beg the discontents and rebels among the British and American communities to bury whatever axes they may have had in the communal interests, while the Japanese will probably do their utmost to grind those axes as sharply as possible.

Meanwhile, whatever the outcome, Shanghai will look forward confidently to only one thing, that the elections will be bitterly contested with the betting even money to the final count.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》
1940年4月4日
上海公共租界工部局
S. G. 7834
致各位纳税人

现在不是相互指责的时候；而是需要对上海市政事务中的严峻危机进行紧急但冷静的思考的时候，但在开始时必须承认，选民今天因日本人的选举炸弹而陷入的困境，很大程度上是纳税人对工部局事务缺乏兴趣的结果。

简而言之，局势如下：日本人拥有大约3,000张确定的选票，正在提名五名工部局候选人；另外八名外国候选人（包括R·麦克唐纳先生在最后一刻的加入）将获得大约4,000名纳税人的支持。双方都将争夺少数族裔选票（除日本人、英国人和美国人以外的外国纳税人），这部分选票约有1,000张，在上述数学问题中仍是未知数。麦克唐纳先生的提名使问题更加复杂。

如果即将到来的选举按国籍阵营投票，并且如果外国社群最终像本应因日本人的行动那样，从其惯常的冷漠中震惊醒悟，那么基于上述数字的推测可以简化。有八名外国候选人，如果当选，将只留给日本候选人一个席位；据此，如果有两名日本候选人当选，那么似乎没有理由不选出全部五人进入工部局，因为在国籍阵营中获得两席的多数票意味着所有人都会获得多数票。

然而，除了民族偏见和偏好之外，还有一些其他考虑因素可能会严重影响下周的投票结果，这些因素不容忽视。从严格的财务角度来看，工部局的记录是一片赤字，其政治历史也不怎么令人愉快。征收50%的增税将打击许多人的钱包，而在这样的时代，一个人的钱包是他最脆弱的弱点，同时在政治上，有一小群狂热亲日的外国人将支持日本的事业。

因此，出现了一种明显的可能性，即五名日本工部局候选人将全部当选，其最终结果在目前情况下完全无法预测，但其直接结果是日本人将获得对租界的实际控制权。

借用日本宣传家流行的一句话，“不言而喻”，日本董事将直接听命于东京的陆军总部，而那些遭受过日本陆军“东亚新秩序”观念之苦的人将明白这意味着什么。这意味着迅速并尽可能彻底地排除所有外国人参与日本陆军视为其特定势力范围的事务，简而言之，就是租界的“日本化”。

然而，撇开所有其他考虑因素不谈，下周的选举注定将是引人注目的，此前的竞选活动在租界历史上也是空前的。据悉，日本纳税人昨天已经收到了关于如何投票以及投给谁的指示，而昨天下午，英国和美国选举委员会均举行了紧急会议，讨论因日本人的举动而产生的局势。毫无疑问，双方都决定了采取措施，以确保尽可能多的本国国民参与投票，以维持工部局中五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人的现状，如果1936年的选举有任何先例可循，那么纳税人在接下来的一周可能会收到大量的“宣传材料”。

日本人为其提名五名候选人辩护的理由，显然将是数量上的，也可能是政治上的必要性，而英国和美国团体则将基于经济利益提出主张，他们无疑可以声称在上海拥有更大比例的经济利益。

预计民族诉求的呼吁将使英国和美国社群中的不满者和反叛者埋葬他们在社区利益中可能存在的任何成见，而日本人可能会竭尽全力将这些成见磨得更加尖锐。

与此同时，无论结果如何，上海都自信地期待着一件事，即选举将进行激烈的竞争，直到最后计票时胜负几率各半。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
APR 4 1940

Platform Of Independent
British Candidate

Ranald G. McDonald Offers To Be A Servant Of
Ratepayers At Large, Not Nominee Of Any
Corporation, Clique, Vested Interests

In a brief, preliminary election address issued yesterday, Mr. Ranald G. McDonald, prominent lawyer, and independent British candidate for the Shanghai Municipal Council, offered to consider himself a servant of the community at large, if elected, and not a candidate for or the nominee of any corporation or vested interest.
Mr. McDonald's address follows:
1.—I am a British Candidate; but I am not one of "the favoured five," although I am as British as any one of them in every single respect, and considerably more British than some of the "British" Election Committee. However, although by descent I am a Highlander, of which I am intensely proud, just as the Japanese are of their great and virile race and of its phenomenal advance in every direction during the last 70 odd years, yet, for the purposes of this election I am, and, if elected, I shall be first and foremost, a Shanglander, so far as Shanghai is concerned.
Independent
2.—I am Independent in that I am not a candidate for or the nominee of any corporation, caucus, clique or sectional or vested interest. If I am elected, I shall be subservient to none, but consider myself the servant of the community at large, and shall strive to be a fearless and impartial guardian of the interests of all regardless of race or creed.
3.—I am a democrat of the democrats and believe in a much more democratic form of Government than has ever been seen in Shanghai, and in a larger and more representative council. I stand for government of the people, by the people, for the people.
Publicity Wanted
4.—I believe in much greater publicity as regards Municipal affairs than has ever been granted by the grudging plutocrats and oligarchs of the past to their Lords and Masters, the Ratepayers of the Settlement. Clean fresh healthy daylight must be allowed to permeate all the evil and secret nooks and crannies of the Council system.
5.—I am in favour of an immediate and a drastic revision of the present anachronistic, inequitable and generally ludicrous Land Regulations.
6.—If am elected, I shall fight for rigid and ruthless economy, wherever it is necessary, until the finances of the Settlement are firmly and securely placed upon a solid and unassailable basis, but I shall not hesitate to vote for capital expenditure wherever or whenever I consider it essential or even desirable. Squandermania must never be allowed to raise its ugly head again.
Wants Town Hall
7.—I am bitterly and relentlessly opposed to the present farcical iniquitous and semi-fraudulent system of voting qualifications under which the quick may be outvoted by the dead and factitious entities. It reeks of lowdown chicanery and manipulation. In short I stand for Public Decency and honest dealing in the Administration.
8.—I am in favour of a Town Hall worthy of the Settlement.
9.—I am in favour of the retention of the Russian Volunteer Regiment, at any rate for the present.
Favours Municipal Lottery
10.—I am in favour of a Municipal Lottery, after a careful study has been made of the question.
11.—I believe in advertising Shanghai to the fullest possible extent.
12.—I strenuously maintain that the "British" Straw Vote should be utterly disregarded and treated as an evil, un-British, undemocratic and unrepresentative farce. A fuller statement of my views will, I hope, be made at a later date.

《字林西报》。
1940年4月4日

英国独立候选人的政纲

兰纳德·G·麦克唐纳（Ranald G. McDonald）表示愿做全体纳税人的公仆，而非任何公司、派系或既得利益集团的提名人

在昨日发布的一份简短的初步竞选演说中，著名律师、上海工部局董事会英国独立候选人兰纳德·G·麦克唐纳先生表示，如果当选，他将视自己为整个社区的公仆，而不是任何公司或既得利益集团的候选人或提名人。
麦克唐纳先生的演说全文如下：
1.—我是一名英国候选人；但我并非“受宠的五人”之一，尽管我在各方面都和他们一样是地道的英国人，甚至比某些“英国”选举委员会成员更具英国特质。然而，虽然我的血统是高地人（Highlander），并为此深感自豪，正如日本人为其伟大而充满活力的民族及其在过去70多年里在各方向取得的惊人进步感到自豪一样，但就本次选举而言，我是，且如果当选，我将首先是上海人（Shanglander），就上海事务而言。
独立
2.—我是独立的，因为我不是任何公司、核心集团、小圈子或局部或既得利益的候选人或提名人。如果我当选，我不受制于任何人，而是视自己为整个社区的公仆，并将努力成为所有种族或信仰人士利益的无畏且公正的守护者。
3.—我是民主主义者中的民主派，相信一种比上海以往所见更为民主的政府形式，以及一个规模更大、更具代表性的董事会。我主张民有、民治、民享的政府。
要求公开透明
4.—我相信，关于工部局事务的公开程度应远超过去那些吝啬的富豪和寡头对其主子——租界纳税人——所允许的程度。必须让清洁、新鲜、健康的阳光穿透董事会体系中所有邪恶和隐秘的角落。
5.—我主张立即对现行过时、不公且普遍荒谬的土地章程进行彻底修订。
6.—如果我当选，我将在必要时争取严格且无情的节约，直到租界的财政稳固地建立在坚实且不可动摇的基础之上；但在我认为必要甚至可取的任何地方或任何时候，我都将毫不犹豫地投票支持资本支出。绝不允许挥霍无度的恶习再次抬头。
希望建造市政厅
7.—我坚决且毫不留情地反对目前这种滑稽、不义且半欺诈性的选民资格制度，在该制度下，活人可能被死人及人为实体以票数压倒。这散发着卑鄙的诡计和操纵的气息。简言之，我主张行政上的公共体面和诚实交易。
8.—我主张建造一座配得上租界的市政厅。
9.—我主张保留俄国志愿队，至少目前如此。
赞成市政彩票
10.—在对问题进行仔细研究后，我赞成发行市政彩票。
11.—我相信应尽可能充分地宣传上海。
12.—我强烈主张，“英国人”的非正式投票（Straw Vote）应被完全无视，并被视为一种邪恶、非英国式、不民主且缺乏代表性的闹剧。我希望日后能更充分地阐述我的观点。

The Gentlemen's Agreement
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—On reading the remarks made by Mr. Makoto Den it seems to me necessary to raise a question and not to allow such statements to pass unchallenged.
Everyone is aware of the extreme sensitiveness of the Japanese breast to criticism, which is invariably construed as anti-Japanese sentiment. It is regrettable that no allowance is made for British sensibilities and anti-British feelings under attack. It is pertinent to remind Mr. Makoto Den, who alleges "autocratic control and an abnormal dictatorial system" by British administration, that the International Settlement was built up by British and American effort, in co-operation with Chinese, and until recently, when a marked deterioration can be observed on all sides, without Japanese aid.
It will be necessary for Mr. Den to elaborate his statement, and prove where autocracy and a dictatorial attitude has been practised. A bare statement of such a sweeping character is not enough.
A word may be added here as to the action of Mr. Ranald McDonald in reference to a "dictatorial" attitude. One wonders whether Japanese authority would tolerate a Japanese citizen flying in the face of Japanese interests and national pride and policy. It seems that here we have a case where dictatorial methods would be justified, with all that is implied thereby.
The breaking of a gentleman's agreement, which means what it says, namely an agreement between gentlemen (and being such, seldom a written agreement), shocks British opinion, the more so coming from a gentleman of Mr. McDonald's past attainments, his brilliance as a member of the learned profession (and who can forget, who heard it, his speech at a Ratepayer's Meeting in 1934), and his former position in the community which he has now forfeited.
CHARLES R. SHAW.
Shanghai, Apr. 3.

What to Do?
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—With the date for the Elections only a week ahead, and with this election the most important in many years, we are without any real lead which may guide the voter who has not seriously considered the problem.
There is real doubt in the minds of many as to what they should do. I spoke to one Briton yesterday and jocularly asked him whether he was ready to "plump" for the five Japanese candidates. To my surprise he said he might.
It is a definite fact that recently the Council has lost the sympathy of many of the ratepayers. Complete indifference to public opinion, resentment to suggestions from outsiders, injustices in pay (both too much and too little), extravagance, etc., have lost for the Council the support that they now need desperately if the Settlement is not to be turned over to Japanese control.

兰纳德·麦克唐纳。

绅士协定
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，—在阅读了丹诚（Makoto Den）先生的言论后，我认为有必要提出一个问题，不能让此类陈述不受质疑地通过。
众所周知，日本人对于批评极其敏感，这种批评 invariably 被解读为反日情绪。令人遗憾的是，人们并未考虑到英国人的感受以及反英情绪正受到攻击这一事实。有必要提醒丹诚先生，他指控英国行政当局实行“专制控制和异常的独裁制度”，但国际租界是由英美两国在华人合作下建立的，且在最近各方出现明显恶化之前，并未得到日本的援助。
丹先生有必要详细阐述其陈述，并证明何处实行了专制和独裁态度。仅凭如此笼统的陈述是不够的。
在此不妨补充一句关于兰纳德·麦克唐纳先生在所谓“独裁”态度方面所作所为的话。人们不禁要问，日本当局是否会容忍一名日本公民公然违背日本利益、民族自豪感和政策。看来在这里，我们有理由采取独裁手段，以及由此隐含的一切。
违反绅士协定——顾名思义，即君子之间的协定（因此很少是书面协定）——令英国舆论震惊，尤其是出自像麦克唐纳先生这样过去成就斐然、作为法律界杰出成员才华横溢（听过他1934年在纳税人会议上发言的人谁能忘记呢）、并在社区中曾拥有现已丧失的地位的人士之口。
查尔斯·R·肖（CHARLES R. SHAW）。
上海，4月3日。

该怎么办？
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，—距离选举日期仅剩一周，而这次选举是多年来最重要的一次，我们却没有任何真正的指引来引导那些尚未认真考虑此问题的选民。
许多人心存疑虑，不知该如何是好。昨天我与一位英国人交谈，开玩笑地问他是否准备“集中投票”（plump）给五位日本候选人。令我惊讶的是，他说他可能会。
一个确切的事实是，工部局最近失去了许多纳税人的同情。对公众舆论的完全漠视、对外界建议的抵触、薪酬方面的不公（既有过高也有过低）、铺张浪费等，已使工部局失去了如果不想让租界落入日本控制之下而现在迫切需要的支持。
有人应该为各国籍选民的利益起草一份

comparison of the status of this place
under a Council constituted as at
present and what its status may be
if five Japanese members should be
elected. As at present constituted we
have and shall probably have again
under the same Council:—

1. Excess of expenditure, over in-
come.
2. Unduly high pay for some ranks
and insufficient for the lower grades.
3. An autocratic attitude from the
Council and the Pivot-Boys towards
the general public.
4. A genuine attempt to keep the
Settlement a decent place to live in
with the minimum of immorality,
gun-men, gambling, noxious drugs,
etc., etc.
5. Reasonable liberty of the in-
dividual in person and in speech
(even if no notice is ever taken).
If the five Japanese come in we do
not know what will happen and have
as a guide only what goes on in the
Western District, Hongkew, etc., to
give an indication, of what we may
expect are:—

1. A reduction of expenditure,
drastic and general.
2. Axing of High-Ups.
3. Police and other department re-
inforced by Japanese in large
numbers.
4. Possibly an even more autocratic
attitude than before.
5. An increase in drugs, gambling
dens and gun-men (see what goes on
in Jessfield Road).
6. Muzzling of the press, depriva-
tion of the right to express opinion
freely (remember Young in Tokyo
and what already goes on here.)
7. Probably a system of taxation
giving Japanese a special favoured
position.

So, though this Election may give
discontented people an opportunity
of getting their own back on the
existing authorities, it is highly prob-
able that the new Council so ob-
tained would be very much worse—
from the frying pen to the fire.
So the remedy is, plump all your
eight votes for the six British and
two Americans and try to get them in,
then at the Annual Meeting give the
Council "the works," throw out the
Budget, the proposed new rules of
procedure and demand another post-
poned Meeting at which a new Bud-
get designed to meet conditions as
they really exist shall be presented.
All voters should be told again and
again that their voting papers are
secret, they can vote as they wish
without any fear of retaliation from
anyone, and that this may be the
last opportunity for retaining the
existing status.

VOTER.
Shanghai, Apr. 3.

Another Point of View
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—I, for one, do not agree with
your strictures on Mr. Ranald Mc-
Donald. For my part, I only regret
that one other independent has not
come forward as a candidate.

The Japanese have thrown over-
board the "gentlemen's agreement,"
and it is not up to the rest of us to
abide thereby. In other words, why
try to maintain the status quo of five
British, two American and two Japan-
ese councillors, which the Japanese
do not want? For my part, I think
we should accept Mr. Ranald Mc-
Donald's candidature as a Heaven-
sent opportunity to reply unmis-
takably to the Japanese threat, and
elect Mr. Ranald McDonald, the five
official British candidates, the two
official American candidates, and one
Japanese.

We can do it, too! It is not at all
necessary for ratepayers to vote for
the full quota of nine councillors.
They can delete from their voting
papers as many names as they wish.
In my case, the names to be deleted
will be all five Japanese candidates;
and if all or most other non-Japanese
ratepayers will follow suit, the com-
position of the 1940 Council will con-
sist of Mr. Ranald McDonald, the
five official British candidates, the
two official American candidates, and
one Japanese.

I do hope Mr. Ranald McDonald
will get elected. A truly independent
spirit and outlook are required, and
this cannot be said of the other
British, American or Japanese can-
didates.

NORTH OF THE CREEK.
Shanghai, Apr. 3.

A Straight Tip
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Referring to BRITISH RATE-
PAYERS letter regarding voting of
Jewish refugees in your today's issue
I beg to draw the attention of the
foreign community to the fact that
as a matter of fact nearly none of
the refugees entitled to vote have
any idea as to the question at issue.
I am convinced that if properly
informed all of them would vote for
the British respectively American
representatives. I, therefore, beg to
suggest that your esteemed paper
publish if possible in the German
language the main points and a very
specified instruction as to the tech-
nical procedure of voting. Besides
that you might publish the regula-
tions concerning the ability to vote,
as a considerable number of rate-
payers amongst the refugees have
not been registered so far.
All refugees living in Shanghai
know how much they owe to this
city, its generous communities and
especially the British, who helped
them in many instances to a very
considerable extent. Here the re-
fugees have a chance to prove their
gratitude, and I hope that none of
them will miss this chance.

H. A. LEIBERER.
Shanghai, Apr. 3.

比较此地目前在按现有方式组成的工部局治理下的地位，以及如果选出五名日本籍董事后其地位可能如何。按目前的组成，我们拥有并且可能在同一届工部局下再次拥有：—

1. 支出超过收入。
2. 某些职级的薪酬过高，而较低职级的薪酬不足。
3. 工部局及“核心人物”（Pivot-Boys）对公众采取专制态度。
4. 真诚地努力使租界成为一个体面的居住地，将不道德行为、枪手、赌博、毒品等危害降至最低，等等。
5. 个人在人身和言论方面享有合理的自由（即使从未受到重视）。

如果五名日本人进入工部局，我们不知道会发生什么，仅能以西区和虹口等地正在发生的情况作为指引，以此预示我们可能预期的情况是：—

1. 大幅且普遍地削减开支。
2. 裁撤高层人员。
3. 警务处及其他部门大量增补日本人。
4. 态度可能比以往更加专制。
5. 毒品、赌窟和枪手增加（参见极司菲尔路 Jessfield Road 的情况）。
6. 钳制新闻界，剥夺自由表达意见的权利（回想一下东京的杨格 Young 事件以及此处已经发生的情况。）
7. 可能会建立一种给予日本人特殊优待地位的税收制度。

因此，虽然这次选举可能给不满现状的人提供一个向现有当局报复的机会，但极有可能通过这种方式产生的新工部局会糟糕得多——可谓刚出油锅又入火坑。

因此，补救办法是，将您所有的八张选票全部投给六名英国人和两名美国人，尽力让他们当选，然后在年度纳税人会议上对工部局予以严厉抨击，否决预算案和拟议的新议事规则，并要求另期召开会议，届时提交一份旨在切合实际状况的新预算案。

应反复告知所有选民，他们的选票是秘密的，他们可以随心所欲地投票，无需担心任何人的报复，而且这可能是保留现有地位的最后机会。

选民。
上海，4月3日。

另一种观点
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，—我本人不同意您对拉纳德·麦克唐纳先生（Mr. Ranald McDonald）的严厉批评。就我而言，我只遗憾没有另一位独立候选人站出来参选。

日本人已抛弃了“君子协定”，我们其他人没有义务继续遵守。换句话说，既然日本人不想要，为何还要试图维持五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人的董事现状？就我而言，我认为我们应该接受拉纳德·麦克唐纳先生的候选资格，将其视为一个天赐良机，以明确无误地回应日本的威胁，并选举拉纳德·麦克唐纳先生、五名官方英国候选人、两名官方美国候选人以及一名日本人。

我们也做得到！纳税人完全没有必要投票选出全部九名董事的名额。他们可以从选票上删去任意数量的名字。在我的情况下，将被删去的名字是所有五名日本候选人；如果所有或大多数其他非日本籍纳税人都效仿此举，那么1940年工部局的组成将是拉纳德·麦克唐纳先生、五名官方英国候选人、两名官方美国候选人以及一名日本人。

我衷心希望拉纳德·麦克唐纳先生能够当选。真正需要的是独立的精神和视野，而这在其他英国、美国或日本候选人身上是看不到的。

溪北人。
上海，4月3日。

一条直率建议
致《字林西报》编辑
先生，—关于贵报今日刊登的“英国纳税人”来信中提及犹太难民投票一事，我谨提请外侨社区注意这样一个事实：实际上，几乎所有有资格投票的难民都对争议问题一无所知。我深信，如果得到适当的信息告知，他们所有人都会分别投票支持英国或美国代表。因此，我恳请贵报尽可能用德语刊登主要要点以及关于投票技术程序的非常具体的说明。此外，贵报还可以刊登有关投票资格的规定，因为难民中有相当数量的纳税人至今尚未登记。

所有居住在上海的难民都知道他们欠这座城市、其慷慨的社区，尤其是英国人多少情义，英国人在许多情况下给予了他们极大的帮助。在这里，难民们有机会证明他们的感激之情，我希望他们中没有人会错过这个机会。

H. A. LEIBERER。
上海，4月3日。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. B. REGISTER
No. S. B. D. 783 H
Date H H 40

CHINA PRESS

APR 4 1940

Japan Daily Warns
Action Hinted
If Elections
Attempt Fails

An indication of the Japanese determination to grasp more control over Settlement affairs was given in the warning recently issued by the Tairiku Shimpo, semi-official Japanese Army organ here.

Unless the demands for greater representation were heeded, it was declared, a possible move to gain control of the Settlement by force might eventuate.

Should the "reasonable" demand of the Japanese be "unfairly ignored" and the "monopolisation" of the Settlement by the British be continued, the Japanese may have to give up their "efforts to re-organize" the Settlement by "means of lawful measures." If this happens, the Settlement will be "again thrown into confusion."

The party which intends to check the advance of the Japanese should be prepared to accept responsibility for the consequences, the paper grimly warned.

This announcement was made in the face of repeated statements by Japanese authorities that it was not the Japanese intention to dominate the Council.

The Tairiku Shimpo asserted that "when disputes over the status of the Settlement arose last year, it was strongly advocated that the question of the Settlement, which is a base of the anti-Japanese movement, should be settled by force as it forms part of the Japanese military operations."

However, "the desire for a lawful settlement of the dispute prevailed," and as a result, the Outside Roads and Hongkew roads were opened.

Japanese conditions already have been laid down regarding the Council which must be settled at the Municipal Meeting on April 17.

《大美晚报》

1940年4月4日

日本日报发出警告
暗示若选举尝试失败将采取行动

驻沪半官方日本陆军机关报《大陆新报》最近发出的警告，表明了日本决心攫取更多租界事务控制权的意图。

该报宣称，除非对增加代表权的要求予以重视，否则可能会导致通过武力夺取租界控制权的行动。

如果日本的“合理”要求被“不公平地忽视”，并且英国人对租界的“垄断”继续下去，日本可能不得不放弃通过“合法手段”“重组”租界的“努力”。如果发生这种情况，租界将“再次陷入混乱”。

该报严厉警告，意图遏制日本推进的一方应准备好承担后果的责任。

这一声明是在日本当局反复声明日本无意主导工部局的背景下发表的。

《大陆新报》断言，“去年当关于租界地位的争端出现时，有人强烈主张，作为反日运动基地的租界问题应通过武力解决，因为它构成日本军事行动的一部分。”

然而，“依法解决争端的愿望占了上风”，结果，越界筑路地区和虹口道路得以开放。

关于工部局的日本条件已经提出，必须在4月17日的纳税人会议上解决。

March 24, 1940.                                                                                     7834

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

JAPANESE DEMANDS RELATING TO THE ELECTION OF THE
COUNCILLORS ACCEPTED BY THE S.M.C.

The procedure regarding the election of members
of the Municipal Council is not helpful to Japanese ratepayers.
In view of this Mr. Hayashi Chairman of the Federation of the
local Japanese street unions, representing the Japanese
ratepayers, visited Mr. Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner
General of the S.M.C. on March 16 and presented the following
7 demands :-
        1) That owing to the increase in Japanese
ratepayers one of the two election committee members be
Japanese.
        2) That for the same reason one of the two observers
of the election be Japanese.
        3) That as the Japanese are not accustomed to election
regulations, they should be given a separate polling place.
        4) This year a certificate authorising the vote will
be sent to ratepayers by S.M.C. by post. The ratepayers must
take the certificate to the polling place to vote. Some
Japanese operate warehouses in the Settlement and have a right to
vote, despite the fact that they do not live in the Settlement.
In these cases certificates should be handed over to the Japanese
Residents Corporation by the S.M.C.
        5) That in view of the increase in the number of
ratepayers the period for voting should be extended.
        6) That the names of the Japanese candidates on the
voting sheets should be in Japanese as well as in English.
        7) That signature in Japanese on the voting sheets
should be recognised by the S.M.C.
        After some negotiations items No. 3, 6 and 7 were
accepted by the Municipal authorities. Regarding item No. 1
the Municipal authorities stressed that two members of the
election committee will be British, but that Japanese may be
appointed as their assistants. Regarding items No. 4 and 5
the Municipal authorities refused to accept them because of the
Land Regulations.
        On March 21, Mr. Miura, Japanese Consul-General,
visited Mr. Franklin, Chairman of the S.M.C. and Mr. Phillips
and negotiated the unsettled portions of the foregoing demands.
        Regarding item No.4, it was decided that Japanese
ratepayers who desire their certificates sent to the Japanese
Residents' Corporation should refer the matter to the Japanese
Residents' Corporation. The Japanese Residents' Corporation
will make a list of Japanese ratepayers who desire their
certificates be sent to that body. The list will be forwarded
by the Japanese Residents' Corporation to the S.M.C. and will
secure the certificates on behalf of the ratepayers. Regarding
item No.2, the two observers of the election have already been
appointed by the Municipal Council, therefore the authorities
promised that appointment of two Japanese assistant observers be
proposed.
        As mentioned above, the Japanese demands with the
exception of item 5 were accepted by the Municipal authorities.

《大陆新报》

工部局接受与董事选举有关的日本要求

市政局成员的选举程序对日本纳税人不利。鉴于此，代表日本纳税人的当地日本街道联合会主席林先生（Mr. Hayashi）于3月16日拜访了工部局总办兼秘书长菲利普斯先生（Mr. Phillips），并提出了以下7项要求：

1) 由于日本纳税人增加，两名选举委员会成员中应有一名日本人。
2) 出于同样原因，两名选举观察员中应有一名日本人。
3) 由于日本人不熟悉选举规定，应为他们设立单独的投票站。
4) 今年，工部局将通过邮政向纳税人寄送授权投票的证明。纳税人必须携带该证明前往投票站投票。一些日本人在租界内经营仓库，尽管他们不住在租界内，但仍拥有投票权。在这些情况下，工部局应将证明移交给日本居留民团。
5) 鉴于纳税人数量增加，应延长投票时间。
6) 选票上的日本候选人姓名应同时使用日文和英文。
7) 工部局应认可选票上的日文签名。

经过一些谈判，市政当局接受了第3、6和7项。关于第1项，市政当局强调两名选举委员会成员将是英国人，但可以任命日本人为其助理。关于第4和5项，市政当局以《土地章程》为由拒绝接受。

3月21日，日本总领事三浦先生（Mr. Miura）拜访了工部局主席富兰克林先生（Mr. Franklin）和菲利普斯先生，并就上述要求中未决部分进行了谈判。

关于第4项，决定希望将证明寄送至日本居留民团的日本纳税人应向日本居留民团提出申请。日本居留民团将编制一份希望将证明寄送至该机构的日本纳税人名单。该名单将由日本居留民团转交工部局，并代表纳税人领取证明。关于第2项，两名选举观察员已由工部局任命，因此当局承诺将提议任命两名日本助理观察员。

如上所述，除第5项外，日本的要求均被市政当局接受。

& MERCURY
APR 3 1940
Japanese Bribing Emigres
For Votes
Relatives Getting
Landing Permit
Canvassers In Council
Election Woo
Minorities
Japanese canvassers for
votes in the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council elections are
holding out tempting bait
to European emigres living
north of the creek in their
latest move. "Vote for the
five Japanese candidates" they
say "And we'll give permis-
sion for your relatives to enter
Shanghai."
The Nipponese have established
a canvassing office in Chacufcoong
Road, where two Japanese work,
aided by four emigres from Ger-
many. They are doing all they
can to secure minority votes, in
their drive to put five Japanese
on the SMC, instead of the two
accepted for years under a gen-
tlemen's agreement.
It is believed, however, that
most of the German Jewish
qualified voters live south of the
creek, where they are not subject
to Japanese pressure or blandish-
ments. It is also believed that
only half of the German voters
in Shanghai are Nazis.
Japanese voters are expected
to follow their usual tactics this
year in plumping for their re-
presentatives, and not voting for
anyone else, and for once the
American and British voters are
expected to follow their example.
In past years the majority of
British and American voters have
voted for the two Japanese can-
didates as well as their own
with the result that the Nippon-
ese have been top of the poll.
This year Britons and Americans
are not likely to vote for the
Nipponese.
Extra reason for this is the in-
dependent candidacy of Mr.
Ronald G. McDonald. With five
Britons nominated by their com-
munity primary ballot, the extra
candidate, Mr. Ronald McDonald,
might otherwise split the British
vote, in that some voters might
prefer him to one of the five.
By ignoring the Japanese can-
didates, British and American
ratepayers can vote for the five
and two nominated in their res-
pective straw ballots, and for Mr.
Ronald McDonald as well, if
they feel like it. It might even
be possible by this, it is held to
reduce the Japanese councillors
to one.
The poll commences a week
from today, to be held at the
Drill Hall and Hongkew market
between the hours of 10 a.m. and
3 p.m. on two days, following the
usual system.
Intense activity is in full swing
among Japanese, British and
American circles to obtain votes
from the smaller representations,
and to make sure that the rates
and taxes of their own voters
have been paid up. A ratepayer
who hasn't paid doesn't get a
voting pass, which has to be pro-
duced at the polling booths.
The official scrutineers who
open the ballot box and count
and tabulate the votes may have
as many assistants as they like,
the Shanghai Evening Post was
informed today. Votes are not
counted by Council officials.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

选举中争取
少数族裔
在上海公共租界工部局选举中，日本拉票者在其最新行动中，正向居住在苏州河以北的欧洲侨民抛出诱人的诱饵。“投票给五位日本候选人，”他们说，“我们就允许你们的亲属进入上海。”
日本人在乍浦路（Chacufcoong Road，音译）设立了一个拉票办事处，由两名日本人工作，并有四名来自德国的侨民协助。他们正竭尽全力争取少数族裔的选票，致力于将五名日本人送入上海公共租界工部局（SMC），而不是按照多年来的一项君子协定仅接受两名。
然而，据信大多数具备资格的德籍犹太选民居住在苏州河以南，在那里他们不受日本人的压力或甜言蜜语的影响。另据信，在上海的德国选民中只有一半是纳粹分子。
预计今年日本选民将沿用其惯常策略，集中投票支持其代表，而不投票给其他人；而英美选民预计也将效仿这一做法。在过去几年中，大多数英国和美国选民在投票给自己国家候选人的同时，也投票给了两名日本候选人，结果导致日本人得票居首。今年，英国人和美国人不太可能投票给日本人。
造成这种情况的一个额外原因是罗纳德·G·麦克唐纳先生（Mr. Ronald G. McDonald）作为独立候选人参选。由于英国社区通过初选提名了五名候选人，这位额外的候选人罗纳德·麦克唐纳先生可能会分散英国的选票，因为部分选民可能更喜欢他而非那五人中的某一位。
通过忽略日本候选人，英国和美国的纳税人可以投票给他们各自非正式民意测验中提名的五人和两人，如果愿意的话，也可以投票给罗纳德·麦克唐纳先生。据认为，甚至有可能借此将日本籍董事减少至一名。
投票将于从今天起的一周后开始，按照惯例，在两天内的上午10时至下午3时之间，在操厅（Drill Hall）和虹口市场举行。
在日本、英国和美国的圈子中，激烈的活动正在全面展开，以争取较小群体代表的选票，并确保其自身选民的捐税已缴清。未缴纳税款的纳税人无法获得投票通行证，而在投票站必须出示该证件。
据今日获悉，《上海晚邮报》得知，负责开启票箱、计票并统计选票的官方监票员可以根据需要雇佣任意数量的助手。选票不由工部局官员清点。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
1940
7834
+ H 40

RATEPAYERS AND S. M. C.
The forthcoming election of foreign Councillors for the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Annual Meeting of Rate-payers which is to follow on April 17 continue to be the chief topic of conversation in the town and never before have Municipal affairs awakened such interest as they are doing to-day. Many and varied are the views being aired upon all sorts of issues connected with our City Government but on one matter there is complete agreement—and that is that greater economy must be practised and that a less expensive personnel will have to be recruited in the future. The prospect of a fifty per cent. surcharge on rates and on all licence and other fees charged by the Council from July 1 is causing the most serious misgiving among the poorer classes of residents as it is believed that the cost of living, already so high, will rise further as an immediate consequence. Some people are openly advocating that the ratepayers should go en masse to the meeting on April 17 and refuse to sanction the increase. This, however, is not very likely to happen for commonsense tells us that the bill which has been incurred has got to be paid and the only proper way in which it can be paid is by raising the rates. We have no doubt that the great majority of the rate-payers will come to this conclusion but it will be with a stern sense of duty rather than lightheartedly that they will put their hands in their pockets. But what the ratepayers will insist upon in return is that the affairs of the Council shall be conducted with greater economy in the future, especially in regard to the salaries paid to the “higher ups” among the staff. While there is every desire to maintain the standards set in the past in Municipal administration the demand that the work shall be done by men who are willing to accept salaries which are less of a burden on the ratepayers is wholly justified by all the circumstances of the case. In the jokes and sneers which have been hurled against “pivot boys” this journal has never joined and has no intention of joining; nevertheless there has been failure to understand that the large salaries paid so carelessly to some of the Council’s employees have all got to be found by the public of Shanghai, many of whom are desperately poor. That the Council’s employ should be more in the nature of a training ground and that promising youths should be recruited locally for departmental service whenever possible is a widely held view.
For far too long it has been tacitly assumed that the control of Municipal affairs belongs by right to a small number of men in this town; this idea is largely due to past apathy of the ratepayers but it has been to some extent deliberately cultivated by those who want to keep the control of things in their own hands as much as possible. This is the wrong spirit and it is up to the public to see that the general welfare is put first before sectional interests. We observe with regret appeals being made for “plump voting” on national lines at the forthcoming election. Although under the circumstances this is understandable, it is unfortunate that at the very time when Municipal reform needs the most careful attention that can be given No. 3, other considerations should be permitted to govern the choice of Councillors. Shanghai to-day wants men on its governing authority who are prepared to promote the general welfare, including that of the poor, and not merely to seek to help forward special interests with which they may be connected. With thirteen candidates in the field for the nine foreign seats on the Council, the ratepayers have plenty of room for exercising their discretion. No doubt many ratepayers will elect to vote for the whole list officially sponsored by their own national community but some will have the courage and good sense to use their own judgment. The ballot, it may be emphasized, is absolutely secret and there is no question of any person being liable to persecution if he votes differently to the way in which it is being politely suggested he should. If nationality is to be the test, there is undoubtedly a great deal to be said for the view that the Japanese are entitled to a larger representation on the Council. There is no reason why five out of nine foreign seats on the Council should be looked upon as the right of the British community and many would like to see other sections of the population represented from time to time. Had only one of the seats been offered to the Japanese community the Japanese ratepayers might have been satisfied, a new “gentleman’s agreement” on the basis of four British, two American and three Japanese Councillors might have been concluded, and an election avoided but apparently the heads of the British community did not feel so generously disposed. As it is to be an election on “national” lines with “plump voting,” whatever its result, it will leave a rather unpleasant taste behind, we fear, at the very time when it is least desirable. It is not fair to say that the challenge comes from the Japanese. The challenge really comes from those who want to keep the latter from getting a larger representation and who are now urging the other foreign ratepayers to get busy and vote them down. The supposition that British interests in Shanghai demand a lion’s share in the representation on the Council may be well-founded or it may not, but what we feel chiefly concerned about is the welfare of Shanghai generally. The very large Japanese population at present in Shanghai and the number of their ratepayers give Japanese views a right to be adequately heard. Moreover, we feel that the Japanese Councillors, like the Chinese, are more likely to favour economy than some of the foreign Councillors who have served us in the past. We have no complaint to make about the present membership of the Council but we do feel that there has been far too much careless spending of the rate-payers’ money in the past. The manner in which the Taels 81,000,000 received for the sale of the Electricity Department to an American company has vanished into thin air during the last decade would seem to be witness to this. Whether we are to have four Britons or five Japanese on the Council is perhaps less important than the spirit in which all the gentlemen who wish to serve the ratepayers in this capacity are prepared to face the future.

纳税人与上海公共租界工部局
即将举行的上海公共租界工部局外籍董事选举以及随后于4月17日召开的纳税人年会，继续成为本市谈论的主要话题，市政事务从未像今天这样引起如此大的兴趣。关于我们市政府的各种问题，人们发表了多种多样、各不相同的观点，但在一个问题上大家完全一致——那就是必须实行更严格的经济节约，未来必须招募薪资要求较低的人员。从7月1日起，工部局征收的捐税及所有执照费和其他费用将加收百分之五十的附加费，这一前景在较贫困的居民阶层中引起了最严重的担忧，因为人们相信，本已高昂的生活成本将因此立即进一步上升。有些人公开主张，纳税人应集体参加4月17日的会议，拒绝批准这项增加。然而，这不太可能发生，因为常识告诉我们，已经产生的账单必须支付，而支付这笔款项的唯一适当方式就是提高捐税。我们毫不怀疑，绝大多数纳税人会得出这一结论，但他们掏腰包时将带着一种严肃的责任感，而非轻松愉快的心情。但是，纳税人坚持要求作为回报的是，工部局的事务在未来必须以更大的经济性来运作，特别是在支付给职员中“高层”人员的薪水方面。虽然人们普遍希望保持过去在市政管理中设定的标准，但鉴于本案的所有情况，要求由那些愿意接受对纳税人负担较轻的薪水的人士来完成工作是完全合理的。
针对“关键岗位人员”（pivot boys）所投去的玩笑和冷嘲热讽，本报从未参与，也无意参与；尽管如此，人们未能理解的是，支付给工部局某些雇员的那些漫不经心的高额薪水，都必须由上海公众来承担，其中许多人极度贫困。一种广泛持有的观点是，工部局的雇佣性质应更像是一个训练场，并且应尽可能在当地招募有前途的青年为各部门服务。
长期以来，人们 tacitly（默许地）假设市政事务的控制权理所当然地属于本市的一小部分人；这种想法很大程度上是由于过去纳税人的冷漠，但在某种程度上也是由那些希望尽可能将控制权掌握在自己手中的人刻意培养的。这是一种错误的精神，公众有责任确保整体福利置于局部利益之前。我们遗憾地观察到，在即将到来的选举中，有人呼吁按国籍路线进行“集中投票”（plump voting）。虽然在这种情况下这是可以理解的，但不幸的是，正值市政改革最需要给予三号大楼（No. 3，指工部局大厦）最仔细关注的时候，其他考量却被允许主导董事的选择。今天的上海需要在其管理机构中有这样的人才：他们准备促进包括穷人在内的整体福利，而不仅仅是寻求推动与他们可能有关的特殊利益。鉴于有十三名候选人竞争工部局九个外籍席位，纳税人有充分的空间行使他们的判断力。毫无疑问，许多纳税人会选择投票给他们本国社区正式支持的整个名单，但有些人会有勇气和理智运用自己的判断。需要强调的是，投票是绝对秘密的，任何人如果投票方式与被人礼貌建议的方式不同，不存在受到迫害的问题。
如果以国籍作为测试标准，毫无疑问，有很多理由支持日本人有权在工部局中获得更大代表权的观点。没有理由认为工部局九个外籍席位中的五个应被视为英国社区的权利，许多人希望看到人口的其他部分不时得到代表。如果只向日本社区提供一个席位，日本纳税人可能就会满意，或许可以达成一项新的“君子协定”，即四名英国董事、两名美国董事和三名日本董事，从而避免选举，但显然英国社区的领袖们并没有感到如此慷慨。既然这将是一场按“国籍”路线进行“集中投票”的选举，无论结果如何，我们担心它都会留下相当不愉快的余味，而这正是在最不希望出现这种情况的时候。说挑战来自日本人是不公平的。挑战实际上来自那些想要阻止日本人获得更大代表权，并现在敦促其他外籍纳税人行动起来将他们投票击败的人。假设上海的利益要求在工部局代表权中占据最大份额，这可能是有根据的，也可能没有，但我们主要关心的是上海的整体福利。目前在上海庞大的日本人口及其纳税人数量，赋予了日本观点被充分听取的权利。此外，我们认为，与过去为我们服务的一些外籍董事相比，日本董事和中国董事更有可能倾向于经济节约。我们对现任董事会成员没有任何抱怨，但我们确实感到过去在花费纳税人的钱方面过于漫不经心。出售电力部门给一家美国公司所获得的8,100万两白银，在过去十年中消失得无影无踪，这一事实似乎就是见证。工部局中是有四名英国人还是五名日本人，或许不如所有希望以此身份为纳税人服务的绅士们准备面对未来的精神态度重要。

1940
Election Postponement
Discussed
Present Conditions
Justify Move, Say
Leading Americans

The possibility of postponing the forthcoming Shanghai Municipal Council elections because of the current abnormal conditions prevailing in this city was being discussed in a serious way by leading American ratepayers of Shanghai last night.

The argument has been advanced that since the Council is not in complete control of the entire Settlement, especially the northern and eastern districts and other disturbed conditions brought about because of the hostilities, there is ample ground to petition the Consular Body of Shanghai for a postponement of the elections, scheduled to be held on April 10 and 11.

Move Planned

Although no action has yet been taken in this direction, it understood that such a move is contemplated. Meanwhile an atmosphere of expectancy prevailed in British and American circles and some minority quarters last night over the possible outcome of the elections if the ballot is held as scheduled. There was still some hope, however, that the Japanese will not walk away completely with the vote.

This depends entirely, according to authoritative American and British sources, on the ability of the opposition to the Japanese to form a united front against the candidates from north of Soochow Creek. A check yesterday revealed that the Japanese can produce about 3,700 votes while the other ratepayers of the city entitled to vote number more than 5,000. Of the minorities, the German vote, including the German and Austrian refugees, is about 600.

Four hundred of the German votes are European refugees, the majority of whom live north of Soochow Creek. Japanese election canvassers, according to reports current yesterday, are making a determined effort to swing the emigres into line with promises of permitting their relatives to enter in Shanghai.

Solidarity Needed

Assuming that the Japanese are able to muster 70 per cent of the European emigre vote and a part of the regular German, or all of it, they will still have a battle on their hands, provided the other ratepayers of the city turn out en mass and vote solidly for their candidates and cast no votes for even two Japanese candidates, these same quarters declared.

Meanwhile, British and American authoritative quarters last night refuted the claim of the Japanese that the latter are entitled to greater representation on the Shanghai Municipal Council because they have 70,000 residents in this city, 98 per cent living in the northern and eastern districts.

This refutation is based on the fact that in these areas, although a part of the International Settlement, the Shanghai Municipal Council has little or no control. Hence, it is argued, that since the S.M.C. has practically no jurisdiction over the areas populated by the Japanese, it is unfair for the Japanese to expect that they should have jurisdiction in the Settlement area south of Soochow Creek. In this connection, British and American quarters point out, the situation tantamount to allowing the ratepayers of the French Concession to come over into the Settlement and vote in candidates residing in Frenchtown onto the Shanghai Municipal Council.

Apathy A Problem

Although the opposition to the Japanese, in theory stands a chance of winning, American and British quarters admit that the apathy of their ratepayers must be taken into consideration. Of this apathy can be overcome, all well and good, but it is generally realized that many voters, if they turn out, will need constant reminding to get them to the booths.

While the Japanese strength is about even or a little less than the total of other ratepayers in the Settlement, including the Germans and 82 Italian and Spanish voters, the Japanese can and probably will turn 97 or 98 per cent strong.

The "Anglo-Saxon" vote has never, even in times of greatest election stress, rallied more than 80 per cent of its strength to the polls. In 1936, when the Japanese tried to upset the prevailing status quo by running a third candidate, a bare 80 per cent of the British and American qualified ratepayers were dragged to the voting booths.

One American authority, in forecasting a Japanese victory yesterday, pointed out that even if 2,900, or 85 per cent of the Americans and British registered their vote, a fair number would pick whom they chose and would not be influenced by any

1940年
选举延期
经讨论
现状
证明此举合理，
主要美籍人士称

昨晚，上海的主要美籍纳税人正严肃地讨论因本市当前异常局势而推迟即将举行的上海工部局董事会选举的可能性。

有人提出论点称，由于董事会无法完全控制整个租界，特别是北部和东部地区，且敌对行动导致了其他动荡局势，因此有充分理由向上海领事团请愿，推迟原定于4月10日和11日举行的选举。

计划采取行动

尽管目前尚未就此方向采取任何行动，但据悉正在考虑此类举措。与此同时，昨晚英美圈子及部分少数族裔群体中弥漫着一种期待的氛围，关注如果按预定时间进行投票，选举可能产生的结果。不过，仍存有一丝希望，即日本人不会完全掌控选票。

据英美权威消息来源称，这完全取决于反日势力能否结成统一战线，以对抗苏州河以北的候选人。昨日的核查显示，日本人能动员约3,700张选票，而本市其他有资格投票的纳税人超过5,000人。在少数族裔中，包括德国和奥地利难民在内的德籍选票约为600张。

其中400张德籍选票来自欧洲难民，他们大多居住在苏州河以北。据昨日流传的消息，日本选举拉票人员正竭力通过承诺允许难民的亲属进入上海，来说服这些移民与其保持一致。

需要团结

上述圈子宣称，假设日本人能够集结70%的欧洲移民选票，以及部分或全部常规德籍选票，他们仍将面临一场苦战，前提是本市其他纳税人大规模 turnout（出席投票），并坚定地为其候选人投票，且不投给哪怕两名日本候选人中的任何一人。

与此同时，昨晚英美权威人士驳斥了日本人的说法，即后者因在本市拥有70,000名居民（其中98%居住在北部和东部地区）而有权在上海工部局董事会中获得更多代表席位。

这一驳斥基于这样的事实：在这些虽属公共租界一部分的地区，上海工部局几乎没有任何控制权。因此，论点认为，既然工部局对日本人聚居区实际上没有管辖权，那么日本人期望在苏州河以南的租界区域拥有管辖权是不公平的。对此，英美方面指出，这种情况等同于允许法租界的纳税人进入公共租界，投票选举居住在法租界的人士进入上海工部局董事会。

冷漠是个问题

尽管从理论上讲，反日势力有获胜的机会，但英美方面承认必须考虑到其纳税人的冷漠态度。如果能克服这种冷漠，那自然最好，但人们普遍认识到，许多选民如果出来投票，需要不断的提醒才能促使他们前往投票站。

虽然日本人的力量与公共租界内其他纳税人（包括德国人以及82名意大利和西班牙选民）的总数大致持平或略少，但日本人能够且可能会以97%或98%的高投票率出动。

“盎格鲁-撒克逊”选民的投票率即使在选举压力最大的时候，也从未超过其总力量的80%前往投票站。1936年，当日本人试图通过推出第三名候选人来打破 prevailing status quo（ prevailing 现状）时，仅有勉强80%的符合资格的英美纳税人被拖到了投票箱前。

一位美国权威人士昨天预测日本人将获胜，他指出，即使有2,900名（即85%）注册的美英人士登记投票，相当一部分人会根据自己的选择投票，而不会受任何

The representatives of the Com-
mittees had stated that in their
view exercise of franchise in the
S.M.C. elections constituted a
"political activity" in the sense of
the form referred to. They also
stated that in their view, emi-
grants owed gratitude equally to
the Japanese authorities for their
sympathetic treatment in Hong-
kew and to the peoples of Europe
and America for the financial sup-
port received. Thus it would be
inadvisable for emigrants to jeo-
pardise their good relations with
either party by the exercise of
a franchise, the significance of
which they probably had scarcely
had time to realize since their re-
latively recent arrival in Shang-
hai, Mr. Komor concluded.

Mr. Ranald G. MacDonald, well-
known local British attorney and an
independent candidate for election
issued an election statement yester-
day. He called himself a "demo-
crat of democrats," advocated eco-
nomies in the Settlement adminis-
tration, a Town Hall, retention of
the Russian Regiment, a properly
regulated municipal lottery and full
publicity of the activities of the
municipal council.

来自本族群的压力影响，
而日本人则可以指望他们
不顾个人意见，按照指示
投票。

两位主要的少数族裔选民
群体——德国人和俄罗斯人
——将在选举中大致相互抵
消，因为双方各有一半人站
在对立面，同一消息人士宣
称。

德国人分裂

德国人群体人数略超600
人，分裂为“雅利安”德国人
和难民，后者大多居住在苏
州河以北的日本控制区。无
论“雅利安”人是投票支持维
持“现状”的英美候选人，还
是完全弃权，近400名德国
难民 bloc（集团）都将把赌注
押在日本人身上，无论是出
于恐吓、贿赂还是对更好境
遇的承诺。

同样，租界内的480名俄罗
斯选民也将分散他们的选票，
住在河以南的大多数人可能
会登记支持英美候选人，而
居住在虹口的人则会投票支
持日本人。

其余少数族裔中，约有160
名法国人和100名葡萄牙人。
两者很可能都会投“盎格鲁-
撒克逊”阵营。70名意大利选
民可能会与租界内的13名西
班牙选民一起，站在其“反共
产国际”的日本盟友一边。预
计24名荷兰选民以及其他各
种少数族裔剩余的300多名选
民将主要把票投给英美候选
人。

少数族裔的平衡

如果除德国人和俄罗斯人
外的所有少数族裔，在选举
中与达到最佳水平85%的“盎
格鲁-撒克逊”选民一起投票，
总数将大致与日本选票持平。
受访的消息人士称，如果认
为有必要，日本人已制定计
划，通过在选举前夕为苏州
河以北的数十名日本居民缴
纳欠税，来进一步增加选票。

科莫尔评论

针对犹太难民报刊最近报
道称国际难民委员会的保罗·
科莫尔（Paul Komor）先生曾
向日本当局保证，不会劝阻
欧洲难民投票支持日本籍工
部局董事候选人一事，科莫
尔先生昨天发表声明，称该
报道仅半真半假。

科莫尔先生宣称，虽然支
持哪个政党（如果有）由每位
移民个人决定，但他认为，
国际委员会和上海援助欧洲
犹太难民委员会均认为，移
民应保持中立，并完全避免
投票。

科莫尔先生说，这一观点
得到了委员会成员埃利斯·哈
伊姆（Ellis Hayim）先生和M.
斯佩尔曼（M. Speelman）先生
的支持，并且已提请日本当
局注意每位移民抵达上海时
获发的黄色表格。该表格建
议避免参与一切政治活动。

委员会代表表示，在他们
看来，行使工部局选举中的
选举权构成了上述表格意义
上的“政治活动”。他们还表
示，在他们看来，移民既应
感激日本当局在虹口给予的
同情待遇，也应感激欧美人
民提供的财政支持。因此，
移民通过行使选举权来危及
与任何一方的良好关系是不
明智的，因为他们相对近期
才抵达上海，可能几乎没有
时间意识到选举权的意义，
科莫尔最后总结道。

当地知名英国律师、独立
候选人拉纳德·G·麦克唐纳
（Ranald G. MacDonald）先生
昨天发表了一份选举声明。他
自称是“民主中的民主派”，主
张在租界行政中实行节约，建
造市政厅，保留俄国军团，实
行适当监管的市政彩票，并充
分公开工部局的活动。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

APR 1 1940

Anachronisms Of Council
Government Should Give
Way To Modern Reforms

Japanese Newspaper Claims That Idea Of British
Holding Majority Of Seats, Despite Number Of
Ratepayers, Should Be Altered By Votes

RIGHT TO VOTE FOR COUNCILLORS MUST
NOT DEPEND ON TAX PAYMENTS ONLY

Contentions that, because British interests predominate in
the International Settlement the British should have a majority
on the Municipal Council, regardless of the number of British
ratepayers, were vigorously assailed in an editorial published
by the Shanghai "Mainichi" yesterday.
"With the same logic," the Japanese daily said, "we may
propose that it would be far better to make nine millionaires,
residing in the Settlement, municipal councillors. Such a line
of argument is absurd."
The newspaper declared it was
"Even anachronistic that the right
to vote should be dependent upon
the payment of a certain municipal
rate."
"The British have boasted that
they are democratic people and
still seem to be proud of that.
Democracy means government for
the welfare of the majority by the
majority. It is usual in democra-
cies to turn from limited suffrage
to universal suffrage," it continu-
ed.
Shanghai Britons, the "Mainichi"
said, were disregarding democratic
principles by opposing a change of
the status quo, using this pretext
as a reason to attack the nomina-
tion of the five Japanese candidates.
"The International Settlement of
Shanghai," the journal declared,
"should not be a British monopoly.
The interests of all nationalities
In carrying out these reforms, we
represented in its population should
be equally and equitably respected
and their free developments
guaranteed. The forthcoming elec-
tions, therefore, may be said to
constitute a struggle between the
principles of the maintenance of
the status quo and of reform. They
will be epoch-making if the Bri-
tish agree to make the International
Settlement an international city
where the various national groups
will work together in harmony for
the development of the city after
having discarded the tradition of
autocratic control," the "Mainichi"
declared.
The Japanese did not intend to
monopolize the administration of
the Settlement by taking the place
of the British, the newspaper de-
clared. "What we desire is to
achieve a reform of the administra-
tion of the Settlement so that it
will be adapted to a new situation.
must endeavour to endow the
Settlement with the character of a
truly international city by accord-
ing various communities living
in it a just and fair right to parti-
cipate in its administration," the
"Mainichi" stated.
The "many current evils" pre-
vailing in the Settlement were the
result of British arbitrary action in
disregard of the true character of
the International Settlement and
achieved by suppressing the voices
of various other communities, the
"Mainichi" contended.
The Japanese nomination of five
candidates for councillors was
justified by the increase in Japan-
ese ratepayers, the newspaper de-
clared.
In conclusion, the "Mainichi"
invited the Shanghai British to
"return to the right mind of
Anglo-Saxons by sweeping away
the prevailing perverse anachron-
ism." Have not Anglo-Saxons
always tided over a revolutionary
crisis to proceed along the path of
evolution?" it asked.

《上海泰晤士报》

1940年4月1日

董事会政府
的陈旧观念
应让位于现
代改革

日本报纸声称，尽管纳税人数量如此，英国人占据多数席位的想法应通过投票予以改变

选举董事的权利
绝不能仅取决于纳税

上海《每日新闻》昨天发表的一篇社论猛烈抨击了这样一种论调：由于英国利益在公共租界占主导地位，无论英国纳税人数量多少，英国人都应在工部局董事会中占据多数席位。

该日本日报称：“按照同样的逻辑，我们可以提议，最好让居住在租界的九位百万富翁担任市政董事。这种论证路线是荒谬的。”

该报宣称，“选举权依赖于缴纳一定市政捐”的观念“甚至是过时的”。

该报继续说道：“英国人一直 boast（吹嘘）他们是民主民族，并且似乎仍以此为荣。民主意味着由多数人为多数人的福利而治理。在民主国家，从有限选举权转向普选权是惯例。”

《每日新闻》称，上海英国人反对改变现状，以此作为攻击提名五名日本候选人的借口，这是在无视民主原则。

该刊物宣称：“上海公共租界不应成为英国的垄断物。其人口中所代表的各国利益应得到平等和公正的尊重，并保障其自由发展。因此，即将到来的选举可以说是一场维持现状原则与改革原则之间的斗争。如果英国人同意使公共租界成为一个国际城市，摒弃专制控制的传统，让各个民族群体和谐合作以促进城市发展，那么这次选举将具有划时代的意义，《每日新闻》宣称。”

该报宣称，日本人并不打算通过取代英国人来垄断租界的行政管理。“我们希望通过改革租界行政管理，使其适应新形势。我们必须努力赋予租界真正国际城市的特征，给予居住其中的各个社区公正公平的参与行政管理的权利，”《每日新闻》 stated（陈述）。

《每日新闻》辩称，租界中盛行的“许多现行弊病”是英国人无视公共租界的真正性质、压制其他各个社区的声音而采取的任意行动的结果。

该报宣称，日本人提名五名董事候选人是基于日本纳税人数量的增加而正当化的。

最后，《每日新闻》邀请上海英国人“扫除盛行的乖张陈旧观念，回归盎格鲁-撒克逊人的理智”。它问道：“盎格鲁-撒克逊人不总是渡过革命危机，沿着进化的道路前进吗？”

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. C. RECORDS
No. S. B. 1) 7834
Date 3 4 c/c

MAR 3 1940

Thirteen Candidates Are
Nominated For S.M.C.

One Independent Nominee
Will Contest Elections To
Commence On April 10

Five British, Five Japanese, Two Americans And
One Independent Briton Standing For Selection
By Local Foreign Ratepayers

SPIRITED CAMPAIGN IS ASSURED WITH
ISSUE IN CONSIDERABLE DOUBT

Adding another hazard to the 1940 elections for the Shanghai Municipal Council was the entry of a thirteenth candidate for the nine available seats for foreign representatives, as announced officially by the S.M.C. Secretariat yesterday noon. The thirteenth candidate whose name appeared among the official nominees was Mr. Ranald G. McDonald, one of the unsuccessful candidates in the British straw ballot conducted by the British Residents' Association.

Mr. Ranald McDonald's nomination yesterday brought the total of candidates to a "baker's dozen," there being five British, five Japanese and two American nominees, in addition.

From the ratepayers' point of view there has never been a poll with such important and interesting possibilities as that which will be posed for electors on April 10 and 11. National aspirations and susceptibilities are held to be at stake, and the outcome will be awaited with more than usual interest.

The candidates who have submitted their names for election are:—
British:—Messrs. G. A. Hoyer, W. J. Broun, Roderick G. Macdonald, G. H. Streat and T. S. Power.
Japanese:—Mr. Masaji G. Matsumoto.
Japanese:—Messrs. M. Ito, Y. Nakamura, E. Kuroda, Isao Ohmura, and Seiichi Okamoto.
American:—Messrs. N. F. Allman and F. W. Carney.

No Late Changes

As was indicated in these columns yesterday, the possibility of one or more additional candidates seeking election after the closing of the ordinary nomination period was remote. There was also the possibility in the minds of some keen followers of municipal affairs that there would be an adjustment of various nominations to the original 5-3-2 ratio, with a view to forestalling an election. Last-minute decisions of such a character have just been unknown in the past. But each national group adhered to its preliminary announcement, the British nominating their customary five candidates, the American community standing by their two nominees and the Japanese presenting five candidates instead of their customary three under the so-called proportional representation idea.

There are today 12 candidates for election by foreign rate-payers and only nine S.M.C. seats available. Four of these candidates have no chance of selection. The Chinese, who are entitled to five seats on the Council, will make their own selection of representatives subsequent to the foreign election. It is understood that the five Chinese who are now sitting members will be returned.

The election is still about one week away. The poll will open at 10 a.m. on April 10 and close at 3 p.m. the same day. Polling hours will be the same the following day, after which votes will be counted and the names of successful candidates announced.

Several Changes

The Japanese community this year, in view of the additional number of candidates selected, are taking unusual steps to see that a full vote is registered by that national group. Permission to station "coaches" at the various polling booths for the guidance of Japanese ratepayers has been approved by the Council. There will also be a Japanese scrutineer appointed to each booth. Furthermore, the names of Japanese candidates, for the first time, will be printed on ballot papers in the Japanese language. These concessions were made by the S.M.C. prior to the announcement of the nominations.

From yesterday until the day of the poll, energetic campaigns by political groups are to be conducted to see that every person entitled to a vote makes his appearance at one of the numerous polling booths throughout the city.

A second poll is suggested this year.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
工部局档案
编号 S. B. 1) 7834
日期 3 4 c/c

1940年3月3日

十三名候选人获提名
竞选工部局董事

一名独立候选人将参加
4月10日开始的选举

五名英国人、五名日本人、两名美国人及
一名独立英国人参选，由当地外籍纳税人遴选

鉴于结果存在相当大的不确定性，
激烈的竞选活动已在所难免

工部局秘书处于昨日中午正式宣布，又有一名第十三号候选人加入争夺九个外籍代表席位的行列，这给1940年的上海公共租界工部局选举增添了另一个变数。出现在官方提名人名单中的这位第十三号候选人是拉纳尔德·G·麦克唐纳先生（Mr. Ranald G. McDonald），他是在英国居民协会举行的英国人非正式投票中落选的候选人之一。

随着拉纳尔德·麦克唐纳先生昨日的提名，候选人总数达到了“一打加一个”（即十三人），其中包括五名英国人、五名日本人和两名美国人的提名。

从纳税人的角度来看，从未有哪次投票像4月10日和11日即将面临的这次选举那样，具有如此重要且充满趣味的可能性。民族愿望和敏感神经被认为正处于紧要关头，人们将以比往常更浓厚的兴趣等待选举结果。

提交姓名参加选举的候选人如下：—
英国籍：—G. A. Hoyer 先生、W. J. Broun 先生、罗德里克·G·麦克唐纳（Roderick G. Macdonald）先生、G. H. Streat 先生和 T. S. Power 先生。
日本籍：—松本正二（Masaji G. Matsumoto）先生。
日本籍：—M. Ito 先生、Y. Nakamura 先生、E. Kuroda 先生、大村功（Isao Ohmura）先生和冈本诚一（Seiichi Okamoto）先生。
美国籍：—N. F. Allman 先生和 F. W. Carney 先生。

无后期变动

正如本报专栏昨日所指出的，在常规提名期结束后，再有一名或多名候选人寻求参选的可能性微乎其微。在一些密切关注市政事务的人士心中，也曾存在另一种可能性，即对各项提名进行调整，以恢复原有的5-3-2比例，从而避免举行选举。过去从未出现过此类最后一刻的决定。但每个国籍群体都坚持了其初步公告，英国人提名了惯常的五名候选人，美国人社群坚守其两名提名人，而日本人则根据所谓的比例代表制理念，提出了五名候选人，而非惯常的三名。

今天共有12名候选人参加外籍纳税人的选举，而工部局仅有九个席位可供分配。这些候选人中有四人没有当选机会。有权在董事会中占据五个席位的华人，将在外籍选举之后自行推选代表。据悉，目前在任的五名华籍董事将获得连任。

选举仍有一周左右的时间。投票将于4月10日上午10时开始，并于当日下午3时结束。次日投票时间相同，随后将进行计票并公布当选者名单。

几项变更

日本人社群今年鉴于候选人数量的增加，正采取不同寻常的措施，以确保该国籍群体的投票率。工部局已批准允许在各投票站派驻“指导员”，以指导日本纳税人投票。此外，每个投票站还将任命一名日本监票员。再者，日本候选人的姓名将首次以日文印在选票上。这些让步是工部局在公布提名之前作出的。

从昨天直到投票日，各政治团体将开展积极的竞选活动，以确保每一位有投票权的人都能前往遍布全市的众多投票站之一进行投票。

今年有人提议进行第二轮投票。

page_data.en:
13 In Race
For Berths
On Council

One of the most vital and hard-fought elections in the history of the International Settlement will be held next week, with thirteen candidates battling for the nine foreign seats on the Municipal Council.

Shortly after noon yesterday, the deadline for all nominations, an official statement was issued with the list of authorized candidates. Five have been proposed by Japanese committees, five by British, two by Americans, and one is backed by an independent group.

The full authorized list as follows:
British candidates: Messrs. G. A. Haley, W. J. Keswick, Roderick G. MacDonald, G. E. Mitchell, and T. S. Powell
American candidates: Messrs. N. F. Allman and J. W. Carney.
Japanese candidates: Messrs. M. Den, Y. Hanawa, K. Kuroda, Issaku Okamoto, and Otoichi Okamoto.
Independent candidate: Mr. Ranald G. McDonald.

Election Hours
The elections will take place next Wednesday and Thursday, and it was announced yesterday that the poll will remain open from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on both days.

Notice was also given yesterday by the Council that Mr. R.D.K. Skey having been proposed by Mr. A. W. Buck and seconded by Mr. W. Mellor, is considered to be elected Land Commissioner for the Municipal year 1940, in accordance with Article VI-A of the Land Regulations.

Predictions Upset
All predictions as to the outcome of the race for seats on the Council were dramatically upset on Monday, with the announcement by the Japanese election committee that five Japanese candidates, instead of the expected two or three, had been entered.

The "gentlemen's agreement" ratio which has been in effect for almost a decade had provided for five British, two American, and two Japanese members of the Council.

A bitterly-fought election was prophesied yesterday by many competent observers, who noted that, almost certainly, the existing ratio is on its way out. The 5-2-2 ratio, they said, will, beginning next week, be almost unalterably changed.

Informed sources declared that the Japanese are almost certain not to win five seats on the Council, but the exact number they will get depends directly on the strength of the other nationalities' vote.

They coupled this statement with the plea that all nationalities must go to the polls next week, and vote. Some groups, including the British Election Committee, have adopted the slogan, "Maintain the status quo!"

Possible Majority Seen
If all five Japanese candidates are elected, this will mean an almost certain majority on the Council. Although Japanese officials denied that the Japanese community in Shanghai sought to "control" the Council, it was pointed out that a large number or a near-majority would obviously signify a very greatly increased direction of S.M.C. affairs.

Reason why the three extra Japanese nominees were put forward, it was announced Monday, is that since the Japanese ratepayers in the Settlement now exceed the 3,000 mark, and thus outnumber even the 2,800 Britons, they are entitled to increased representation. This move, they said, was "a transitory measure required to destroy the existing abnormal state of affairs, so that the Japanese ideal of a truly international administration of the Settlement may be attained."

Another indication of the unique characteristics of this year's election is the fact that an independent candidate, Mr. Ranald McDonald, has broken the ties of tradition by allowing his name to be put on the list.

The British Election Committee met yesterday afternoon, putting finishing touches to its campaign, and planning to rally all the British voters in the city around its platform asking for the maintenance of the existing ratio of councillors. The American election groups, including the American Association, are also expected to meet shortly.
page_data.zh:
十三人竞逐
工部局席位

下周将举行国际租界历史上最关键、竞争最激烈的选举之一，十三名候选人将争夺工部局的九个外籍席位。

昨日中午，即所有提名的截止时间过后不久，一份包含经授权候选人名单的官方声明发布。其中五人由日本委员会提名，五人由英国方面提名，两人由美国人提名，还有一人得到独立团体的支持。

完整的经授权名单如下：
英国候选人：G. A. Haley 先生、W. J. Keswick 先生、罗德里克·G·麦克唐纳（Roderick G. MacDonald）先生、G. E. Mitchell 先生和 T. S. Powell 先生
美国候选人：N. F. Allman 先生和 J. W. Carney 先生。
日本候选人：M. Den 先生、Y. Hanawa 先生、K. Kuroda 先生、Issaku Okamoto 先生和 Otoichi Okamoto 先生。
独立候选人：拉纳尔德·G·麦克唐纳（Ranald G. McDonald）先生。

选举时间

选举将于下周三和周四举行，昨日宣布投票在这两天均将从上午10时持续至下午3时。

工部局昨日还发布公告，称 R.D.K. Skey 先生由 A. W. Buck 先生提名，W. Mellor 先生附议，根据《土地章程》第六条A款，被视为当选为1940市政年度的土地委员。

预测落空

周一，随着日本选举委员会宣布有五名日本候选人参选，而非预期的两到三名，关于董事会席位争夺战结果的所有预测都被戏剧性地推翻。

生效近十年的“君子协定”比例规定，工部局成员由五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人组成。

昨日，许多有能力的观察家预言这将是一场苦战，他们指出，现有的比例几乎肯定正在走向终结。他们说，从下周开始，5-2-2的比例将发生几乎不可逆转的改变。

消息灵通人士宣称，日本人几乎肯定无法赢得工部局的五个席位，但他们确切能获得的席位数直接取决于其他国籍选民的投票力度。

他们在发表这一声明的同时，呼吁所有国籍的人下周都要去投票站投票。包括英国选举委员会在内的一些团体已采用“维持现状！”作为口号。

可能出现多数派

如果五名日本候选人全部当选，这意味着他们在工部局中将几乎肯定占据多数。尽管日本官员否认在上海的日本人社群试图“控制”工部局，但有人指出，大量席位或接近多数显然意味着工部局事务的主导权将大大增强。

周一宣布，提出额外三名日本提名人的原因是，既然租界内的日本纳税人现在已超过3,000人大关，从而甚至超过了2,800名英国人，他们有权获得增加的代表权。他们说，此举是“为打破现有不正常状态所必需的过渡性措施，以便实现日本人对租界真正国际化管理的理想。”

今年选举独特性质的另一个迹象是，独立候选人拉纳尔德·麦克唐纳先生打破了传统束缚，允许将自己的名字列入名单。

英国选举委员会于昨日下午召开会议，对其竞选活动进行最后的润色，并计划围绕其要求维持现有董事比例的纲领，动员全市所有英国选民。包括美国协会在内的美国选举团体预计也将很快开会。

13 Candidates
Nominated for
Council Seats
Mr. Ranald G. McDonald
Standing for Election

Elements of further competition in
the forthcoming Shanghai Municipal
Council election were introduced
yesterday when the nomination list of
candidates, which closed at the Ad-
ministration Building at noon, in-
cluded the name of Mr. Ranald G.
McDonald. On Monday, with the
addition of five Japanese candidates,
the number nominated for the nine
vacant foreign seats on the Council
was 12, but Mr. McDonald's candida-
ture increases this to 13.
The nomination list issued by Mr.
G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and
Commissioner-General, yesterday was
as follows:
N. F. Allman: Proposed by G. F.
Richardson and seconded by J. M.
Hykes.
J. W. Carney: Proposed by J.
Fistere and seconded by J. T. S. Reed.
M. Den: Proposed by Y. Hayashi
and seconded by C. Fukuda.
G. A. Hayley: Proposed by E.
Calder Marshall and seconded by J.
H. Liddell.
Y. Hamawa: Proposed by Y. Hayashi
and seconded by C. Fukuda.
W. J. Keswick: Proposed by A. S.
Henchman and seconded by F. A.
Pollock.
K. Kuroda: Proposed by Y. Hayashi
and seconded by C. Fukuda.
Roderick G. MacDonald: Proposed
by A. S. Henchman and seconded by
G. H. Wright.
Ranald G. McDonald: Proposed by
W. M. Macostra and seconded by
G. T. Lloyd.
G. E. Mitchell: Proposed by E.
Calder Marshall and seconded by L.
J. Davies.
Isaku Okamoto: Proposed by Y.
Hayashi and seconded by C. Fukuda.
Oteishi Okamoto: Proposed by Y.
Hayashi and seconded by C. Fukuda.
T. S. Powell: Proposed by J. H.
Liddell and seconded by T. G.
Drakeford.

The election will be held on
Wednesday and Thursday, April 10
and 11, between the hours of 10 a.m.,
and 3 p.m.

Land Commissioner Chosen

On the proposal of Mr. A. W. Buck,
seconded by Mr. W. Mellor, Mr. R.
D. K. Silby is elected Land Commis-
sioner for the municipal year 1940 in
accordance with Article VIA of the
Land Regulations.
Meanwhile the British and Ameri-
can election committees are taking
steps to counteract the situation
caused by the nomination of five
Japanese candidates. The American
committee met yesterday to discuss
the matter but no plans were re-
leased for publication.
A meeting of the British Election
Committee was held yesterday eve-
ning when the electoral situation,
created by the announcement of five
Japanese candidates and the nomina-
tion of Mr. Ranald G. McDonald,
was discussed. It is understood that
it was decided to make no changes
in the existing plans and to support
the 5-5-3 basis of representation on
the Council and the straw vote
candidates.

Passes Being Sent Out

Notice is hereby given that voting
passes are being forwarded by post
to ratepayers entitled to vote at the
election.
Voters who have not received their
voting pass by the first post on
Thursday morning, April 4, should
apply immediately to the Deputy
Treasurer-Revenue, No. 309 Kiangse
Road (Telephone 13819—Ext. 27) for
a duplicate pass. Application may
also be made in person at Hongkew
Police Station.
The poll will be opened on Wednes-
day and Thursday mornings, April
10 and 11 at 10 a.m. precisely, and
will remain open continuously until
3 p.m. each day.
Polling will take place at the S.V.C.
Drill Hall, Foochow Road, and at the
Hongkew Market, 2nd Floor.
Attention is drawn to the rule that
voters must present their pass at the
polling place in exchange for a
voting paper.
The officials can not be responsible
for any inconvenience to voters aris-
ing from the voters' failure to obtain
the requisite voting pass prior to the
date of the election.

Chinese Press Concerned

A review of Chinese press reports
published yesterday reveal that al-
though no editorial comments have
been published, prominence is given
to the news about the nomination of
five instead of two Japanese candi-
dates for the election of members of
the Shanghai Municipal Council, ex-
pressing alarm in news articles and
headlines and asserting that the "out-
look of the Settlement is a matter
of great concern," since the Japanese
are trying to become the controlling
factor in the Settlement adminis-
tration.
The headline of the news published
by the "Shun Pao" reads "Japanese
Violate Gentlemen's Agreement," and
"Number of Candidates Increased
Without Authority." It is alleged
that the Japanese want to cancel the
gentlemen's agreement in regard to
the ratio of candidates reached by
representatives of the four Powers,
China, Great Britain, the United
States and Japan, many years ago.
The Japanese announcement of the
names of their candidates is publish-
ed. More or less identical reports
appear in other leading Chinese
newspapers.
It is stated that foreigners are
much surprised by the Japanese an-
nouncement, but it is asserted that
it may be a strong feeler put out by
the Japanese so that owing to their
insistence, foreigners may give in a
little. Quoting foreign sources and
observers, the reports state that the
British have many more interests
here than the Japanese and that it
has been forecast that Japanese can-
didates may not all be elected.
Although the reports state that
British circles believe that the num-
ber of British ratepayers is at least
equal to Japanese ratepayers, it is
said that the latter may make use of
Jewish refugees living north of the
creek. It is also pointed out that
qualifications of Japanese ratepayers
may be questionable. It is not known
whether or not all Japanese residing
here have been paying taxes to the
Shanghai Municipal Council, it is
stated.

Japanese Nominee
Issues Statement

"Dictatorial" Regime in
Shanghai Opposed

Fundamental reforms in the ad-
ministration of the International
Settlement, now faced with "an un-
precedented financial crisis," were
seen as necessary by Mr. Makoto
Den, one of the five Japanese can-
didates for membership in the
Shanghai Municipal Council. Mr.
Den is vice-president of the Central
China Railways Company, a Sino-
Japanese joint enterprise.
All residents of the Settlement, he
said in a statement issued here last
night, demanded a reform of "the
confusion and the traditional abuses"
brought about by the "autocratic
control of the Settlement's administra-
tion by a specific nation for almost a
century."
In announcing his candidacy for
municipal councillor, Mr. Den pledged
his efforts to break down the exist-
ing "abnormal dictatorial system in
the Settlement so as to make the
International Settlement one that
really belongs to those residing
there."

APR 3 1940

13名候选人
被提名角逐
工部局董事席位

昨日，随着候选人提名名单在中午于行政大楼截止，其中包括了麦克唐纳（Ranald G. McDonald）先生的名字，即将举行的上海公共租界工部局选举中进一步竞争的因素随之显现。周一，随着五名日本候选人的加入，角逐工部局九个空缺外籍董事席位的提名人数为12人，但麦克唐纳先生的参选使这一数字增至13人。

秘书兼总办戈弗雷·菲利普斯（G. Godfrey Phillips）先生昨日发布的提名名单如下：

K. Kuroda：由 Y. Hayashi 提名，C. Fukuda 附议。

选举将于4月10日（星期三）和11日（星期四）举行，时间为上午10时至下午3时。

地产委员人选确定

经 A. W. Buck 先生提议，W. Mellor 先生附议，R. D. K. Silby 先生当选为1940市政年度地产委员，此系依据《土地章程》第六条甲款之规定。

与此同时，英美选举委员会正采取措施，以抵消因五名日本候选人提名所造成的局面。美国委员会昨日开会讨论此事，但未公布任何计划。

英国选举委员会于昨晚召开会议，讨论了因宣布五名日本候选人及拉纳德·G·麦克唐纳（Ranald G. McDonald）先生参选而形成的选举局势。据悉，会议决定不对现有计划进行任何变更，并支持工部局代表权的5-5-3比例基础以及意向投票（straw vote）候选人。

正在发送通行证

特此通知，投票通行证正通过邮政寄送给有资格在选举中投票的纳税人。

若在4月4日（星期四）上午第一次邮递时仍未收到投票通行证的选民，应立即向江西路309号副财务长-税务处（电话13819—分机27）申请补发通行证。也可亲自前往虹口巡捕房提出申请。

投票站将于4月10日（星期三）和11日（星期四）上午10时整开放，并持续开放至每日下午3时。

投票将在福州路万国商团操厅及虹口市场二楼进行。

提请注意一项规定：选民必须在投票站出示其通行证以换取选票。

若选民未能在选举日前取得所需的投票通行证，由此产生的任何不便，官员概不负责。

中文报刊表示关切

对昨日发表的中文报刊报道的综述显示，虽然尚未发表社论评论，但关于五名而非两名日本候选人被提名为上海公共租界工部局董事的新闻占据了显著位置，新闻文章和标题表达了惊恐，并断言“租界的前途令人极为担忧”，因为日本人正试图成为租界行政中的控制因素。

《申报》刊登的新闻标题为“日人违背君子协定”，及“擅自增加候选人数”。据称，日本人希望取消多年前由中国、英国、美国和日本四国代表达成的关于候选人比例的君子协定。

日本方面公布的候选人名单已见报。其他主要中文报纸也刊登了大致相同的报道。

报道称，外侨对日本的公告感到非常惊讶，但有人断言，这可能是日本人放出的一种强有力的试探性气球，以便凭借其坚持，使外侨稍作让步。引用外侨来源和观察家的说法，报道指出英国人在这里的利益远多于日本人，并且据预测，日本候选人可能不会全部当选。

虽然报道指出英国界人士认为英国纳税人数量至少与日本纳税人相当，但据说后者可能会利用居住在苏州河以北的犹太难民。此外还指出，日本纳税人的资格可能值得怀疑。据报道，目前尚不清楚所有居住在此的日本人是否一直向上海公共租界工部局缴纳税款。

日本候选人
发表声明

反对上海的
“独裁”统治

丹诚（Makoto Den）先生是角逐上海公共租界工部局董事席位的五名日本候选人之一，他认为，面对“前所未有的财政危机”，国际租界的行政管理需要进行根本性改革。丹先生是中日合资企业华中铁道公司的副总裁。

他在昨晚于此间发表的一份声明中表示，所有租界居民都要求改革“近一个世纪以来由特定国家对租界行政实行专制控制”所带来的“混乱和传统弊政”。

在宣布参选工部局董事时，丹先生承诺将努力打破现有的“租界内不正常的独裁制度”，使国际租界真正成为属于居住在那里的人们的租界。

1940年4月3日

CHINA PRESS
APR 3 1940

Status Of The Settlement

THE action of the Japanese election committee in putting forward five candidates for the municipal election has crystalized the issue at this year's polls. The single question to be decided at the election on April 10 and April 11 is: Shall the political status and the international character of the International Settlement be changed at this time?

Since August 1937, the Japanese have brought all manner of pressure on the International Settlement. They have threatened the neutrality and the security of the foreign areas by their military actions. They have continuously used the spearhead of pressure diplomacy to undermine the authority and international character of the Settlement. By the encouragement of lawlessness and extra-legal actions, they have repeatedly challenged the ability of the Shanghai Municipal Council to rule the areas under its jurisdiction.

The latest Japanese challenge is one at the polls, which must be met and repulsed by the ratepayers of the International Settlement alone. Unlike previous Japanese attempts to gain control of the Settlement, the present election maneuvers by the Japanese cannot be sidetracked by the diplomatic action of the Third Powers. The foreign ratepayers in the Settlement must fight their forthcoming election battle without relying upon any outside aid.

* * *

IF the international Settlement and the non-Japanese foreign community in Shanghai should succumb to the Japanese election challenge, it would not be because the British and American Governments were unwilling to support the Shanghai Municipal Council. Neither would such a defeat be the result of the much-criticized weak-kneed policy of the S.M.C. officials. The responsibility—if the Japanese should have their way—would rest entirely on the civic lethargy of the Shanghai foreign ratepayers.

In the past, the residents here have always relied too much on the actions of third powers having an interest in the International Settlement to fight their battles. When the Japanese sought to gain control of the Settlement by threat, diplomatic pressure and force, the ratepayers calmly turned their hopeful eyes toward Washington and London, with the confident belief that the British and American Governments would pull the Shanghai chestnut out of the Nipponese fire.

But this time the situation will be different. No amount of American and British willingness to protect the International Settlement could help to reverse the verdict of the polls on April 10 and April 11. If by default or by internal disharmony, the non-Japanese foreign community should fail to deliver enough votes to beat the Nipponese, then the Japanese in Shanghai would be legally entitled to rule the International Settlement with their bloc of Council members.

The election platform as announced by Mr. Yukichi Hayashi, chairman of the Japanese election committee, perhaps deserves the attention of the local ratepayers. "The Japanese aim," he said, "lies in discarding the dictatorship of any specific national group in municipal affairs so that the administration of the International Settlement may be carried out in a truly international manner."

* * *

IT does not need an extraordinary amount of intelligence to see the real meaning of this diplomatically phrased election platform. It merely means that the Japanese aim lies in the discarding of the present dictatorship and substituting for it a Japanese dictatorship. It also means that the Japanese aim lies in changing the present international set-up of the Settlement into a purely Nipponese administration.

From the point of view of Shanghai's future the importance of the municipal election on April 10 and April 11 can hardly be over-exaggerated. Upon the outcome of the voting will depend the question of whether the International Settlement will become a suburb of Tokyo. Upon the ability of the non-Japanese foreign community to deliver votes will depend the question of whether the foreigners here will continue to be governed by themselves or be governed by their Japanese municipal overlords.

The decision on these important questions rests, as we pointed out, not with Washington or London. It rests with the voters in the International Settlement, whose ballots or whose failure to cast a ballot may mean the difference between the maintenance of the international status of the Settlement and the Japanization of Shanghai.

《字林西报》
1940年4月3日

租界的地位

日本选举委员会在五名候选人参加工部局选举一事上的行动，使今年投票中的问题具体化。4月10日和11日选举中需要决定的唯一问题是：国际租界的政治地位和国际性质是否应在此时改变？

自1937年8月以来，日本人对国际租界施加了各种压力。他们以军事行动威胁外侨区域的中立与安全。他们不断使用压力外交的先锋手段，削弱租界的权威和国际性质。通过鼓励非法行为和法外行动，他们多次挑战上海公共租界工部局管辖其辖区的能力。

日本最新的挑战是在投票箱前，这必须且只能由国际租界的纳税人予以迎击和挫败。与以往日本人试图控制租界的企图不同，日本人目前的选举策略无法通过第三国的外交行动来规避。租界内的外籍纳税人必须在不依赖任何外部援助的情况下，打好即将到来的选举战。

* * *

如果国际租界和上海的非日籍外侨社群屈服于日本的选举挑战，那并不是因为英国和美国政府不愿意支持上海公共租界工部局。这样的失败也不会归咎于备受批评的工部局官员的软弱政策。如果日本人得逞，责任将完全在于上海外籍纳税人的公民惰性。

过去，这里的居民总是过于依赖在国际租界拥有利益的第三国的行动来为他们战斗。当日本人试图通过威胁、外交压力和武力来控制租界时，纳税人平静地将充满希望的目光投向华盛顿和伦敦，坚信英美政府会将上海从日本的火坑中拯救出来。

但这次情况将有所不同。无论美国和英国保护国际租界的意愿多么强烈，都无法扭转4月10日和11日投票的结果。如果由于疏忽或内部不和，非日籍外侨社群未能投出足够的票数以击败日本人，那么上海的日本人将在法律上有权凭借其工部局董事集团统治国际租界。

日本选举委员会主席林康侯（Yukichi Hayashi）先生宣布的选举纲领，或许值得本地纳税人关注。他说：“日本人的目标在于摒弃任何特定民族群体在市政事务中的独裁统治，以便使国际租界的行政管理能够以真正的国际方式进行。”

* * *

无需非凡的智慧即可看出这一措辞外交化的选举纲领的真实含义。它仅仅意味着日本人的目标在于摒弃目前的独裁统治，代之以日本的独裁统治。这也意味着日本人的目标在于将租界目前的国际架构转变为纯粹的日本行政管理。

从上海未来的角度来看，4月10日和11日的工部局选举的重要性无论如何强调都不为过。投票结果将决定国际租界是否会成为东京的郊区。非日籍外侨社群能否投出足够的票数，将决定这里的外国人将继续由自己治理，还是受其日本市政上司的统治。

正如我们指出的那样，对这些重要问题的决定权不在华盛顿或伦敦手中。它掌握在国际租界的选民手中，他们的选票或不投票，可能意味着维持租界的国际地位与上海日本化之间的区别。

Association stated yesterday that
the Association would meet to-
morrow afternoon and that plans
were being prepared to get as many
Americans as possible to the poll-
ing stations next Wednesday and
Thursday. He added that the cam-
paign effort of the Association
would be the maintenance of the
status quo.

Japanese Campaign

The Japanese Election Committee
was reported yesterday to be work-
ing hard, organizing all the Japan-
ese ratepayers for the polls. The
Japanese ratepayers will be called
upon to turn out en masse to sup-
port their five candidates at the
elections.

Two Polling Stations

The Council has arranged for
two polling stations, one at the
S.V.C. Drill Hall and the other
on the Second Floor of the Hong-
kew Market. The poll will be open-
ed on Wednesday and Thursday
mornings, April 10 and 11, at 10
a.m. precisely, and will remain
open continuously until 3 p.m. each
day.

Attention has been drawn by the
Council to the rule that voters
must present their pass at the poll-
ing place in exchange for a voting
paper. The officials cannot be re-
sponsible for any inconvenience to
voters arising from the voters’
failure to obtain the requisite vot-
ing pass prior to the date of the
election.

SHANGHAI TIMES
1946
page_data.zh:
投票通行证
已寄往
纳税人

英籍人士全员出动
美籍、日籍人士
力争参与投票

向选民提出
明确议题

当各全国委员会正在召开会议并制定计划，以动员尽可能多的纳税人参加将于4月10日和11日举行的即将举行的工部局选举时，上海公共租界工部局昨日宣布，投票通行证正通过邮政寄送给有资格投票的纳税人。

工部局公告称，若选民在明早第一班邮件送达后仍未收到其投票通行证，应立即向江西路269号副司库——收入处（电话12810转27）申请补发通行证。也可亲自前往虹口巡捕房提出申请。

继宣布除独立英籍候选人拉纳德·G·麦克唐纳（Ranald G. McDonald）先生外，另有五名日籍候选人被提名为工部局议员候选人之后，英籍选举委员会于昨日下午召开会议。该委员会制定了一系列计划，旨在为选举争取具有代表性的英籍选票。

秘书指出：“将请求所有英籍纳税人支持英籍候选人，”并补充说，“英籍选举委员会将为维持现状而努力。”他接着表示，将尽一切努力使所有英籍纳税人前往投票站投票。

明确议题

英籍选举委员会秘书总结道：“议题如此明确，毫无疑问，大多数英籍纳税人会亲自出来投票。”

美国协会的一名代表昨日表示，该协会将于明日下午开会，并正在制定计划，以便在下周三和周四让尽可能多的美国人前往投票站。他补充说，该协会的竞选工作重点将是维持现状。

日方竞选活动

据报，日籍选举委员会昨日正在努力工作，组织所有日籍纳税人参与投票。日籍纳税人将被号召大规模出动，在选举中支持他们的五名候选人。

两个投票站

工部局已安排两个投票站，一个位于上海义勇队（S.V.C.）操练厅，另一个位于虹口市场二楼。投票将于4月10日和11日（星期三和星期四）上午10时整开始，并每天持续开放至下午3时。

工部局提请注意一项规定：选民必须在投票站出示其通行证以换取选票。官员不对因选民未能在选举日前获得所需投票通行证而给选民带来的任何不便负责。

《字林西报》
1946年
