APR 3 1940

Japanese To
Seek Reform
In Council

Unprecedented Crisis In
Financial Affairs Has
Been Disclosed

JAPANESE CANDIDATE
EXPRESSES VIEWS

Fundamental reforms in the
administration of the Interna-
tional Settlement, now faced
with "an unprecedented
financial crisis," were seen as
necessary by Mr. Makoto Den,
one of the five Japanese can-
didates for membership in the
Shanghai Municipal Council.
Mr. Den is vice-president of
the Central China Railways
Company, a Sino-Japanese
joint enterprise.
All residents of the Settlement,
he said in a statement issued here
last night, demanded a reform of
"the confusion and the traditional
abuses" brought about by the auto-
cratic control of the Settlement's
administration by a specific nation
for almost a century.
In announcing his candidacy for
municipal councillor, Mr. Den pledg-
ed his efforts to break down the
existing" abnormal dictatorial sys-
tem in the Settlement so as to
make the International Settlement
one that really belongs to those
residing there."
"Swift Revision"
"Japanese residents," Mr. Den said
in his statement," have consistent-
ly maintained their just opinion on
the need of such a reform. The
situation in the International Settle-
ment has now reached a stage
where a swift revision of existing
conditions is required. The admin-
istrative organs of the Settlement
require a thorough, not a temporary,
reform.
"As a member of the Finance
Committee of the Council, I have
done whatever I could to restore
the Settlement's finances to a sound
basis However, the minority, in
the right, has always been defeated
by the majority, which was in the
wrong.
"I opposed the recent proposal for
an increase in rates and licence fees
and advocated a thorough re-
appraisal of the Council's finances
to restore their foundation. I am
confident that the Japanese are not
alone in realizing the need for a
re-examination of the Council's
financial structure but of its other
departments as well.
"There are to-day 70,000 Japan-
ese sharing in Shanghai the task of
establishing a new order in East
Asia. Japanese ratepayers, qualified
to vote, number more than 3,000,
constituting the largest single
national group of such voters. They
have the largest voice in the con-
duct or municipal affairs and are
in a position to reorganize and
clear up the atmosphere in the In-
ternational Settlement.
"The Japanese candidates in the
coming elections have entered the
contest to break down the abnorm-
al dictatorial system existing in the
Settlement so as to make the Inter-
national Settlement one that really
belongs to those residing there."
page_data.zh:
1940年4月3日

日方寻求
工部局改革

前所未有的
财政危机已被揭露

日籍候选人
发表观点

田中诚（Makoto Den，音译）先生是上海公共租界工部局董事的五名日籍候选人之一，他认为，面对“前所未有的财政危机”，对国际租界的行政进行根本性改革是必要的。田中先生是中日合资企业华中铁路公司的副总裁。

他在昨晚于此间发表的一份声明中表示，所有租界居民都要求改革由某一特定国家近一个世纪以来对租界行政实行专制控制所造成的“混乱和传统弊病”。

在宣布参选工部局董事时，田中先生承诺将努力打破租界现有的“异常独裁制度”，使国际租界成为真正属于居住在那里的人们的租界。

“迅速修订”

田中先生在声明中说：“日籍居民一贯坚持认为有必要进行此类改革。国际租界的局势现已达到需要迅速修订现有状况的阶段。租界的行政机构需要进行彻底的、而非暂时的改革。

“作为工部局财务委员会的成员，我已竭尽所能使租界财政恢复到健全的基础。然而，有理的少数派总是被无理的多數派所击败。

“我反对最近增加捐税和执照费的提议，并主张对工部局的财政进行彻底重新评估，以恢复其基础。我相信，不仅日本人意识到需要重新审查工部局的财政结构，其他部门也是如此。

“如今有7万日本人在上海分担建立东亚新秩序的任务。有资格投票的日籍纳税人超过3000人，构成了此类选民中最大的单一国籍群体。他们在市政事务的管理中拥有最大的发言权，并有能力重组和澄清国际租界的氛围。

“即将到来的选举中的日籍候选人参加竞选，是为了打破租界中存在的异常独裁制度，从而使国际租界成为真正属于居住在那里的人们的租界。”

page_data.en:
1940

S. M. Elections:
Plea for Compromise

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—There can be few that realize
the tremendous value of the Foreign
Settlement who will not deplore the
fact that the Municipal Elections this
year will be fought between com-
munity and community in what you
describe as a "trial of strength." One
fully realizes that the nomination of
five Japanese candidates, disguise the
motive how they will, is a challenge
on the part of the Japanese com-
munity against the old-time balance
of power here and that if British and
American ratepayers desire to retain
seven out of the nine foreign seats
they will have to muster all their
voting strength to do so. If they do
manage to retain those seven seats on
this occasion there is no guarantee
that they will be able to do so in the
future. The Japanese community is
likely to grow in strength and the
other foreign communities to decline,
in consequence of international trends
and current happenings in other parts
of the world.

It is a pity that in the evolutionary
changes which have come, and must
continue to come, over this city, no
machinery for negotiation, consulta-
tion and decision upon such a matter
as proportionate international repre-
sentation upon the S.M.C. has ever
been set up. The British, American
and Japanese communities are not the
only ones concerned, though they may
be numerically the strongest. All
foreign residents go to make up this
international community and they are
all entitled to a sense of participation
in the Administration towards which
they individually and severally con-
tribute. If the Municipal Elections
are going to be left to develop into
an annual "dog fight" between com-
munities instead of being a contest
between individuals as to their fitness
to govern, then Shanghai will inevit-
ably lose that corporate international
harmony which has been one of its
most valuable characteristics.

One wonders whether the leaders
of the important communities have
given that aspect of the matter the
deep and constructive consideration it
deserves. This city is not the exclu-
sive affair of the big communities,
neither should it be made an arena
for their political contentions. It
needs a co-operative pooling of the
best of all communities, and the
British, American . . . Japanese lead-
ers ought not to be blind to the fact
that in such a co-operative pooling
their own best interests will un-
doubtedly lie.

Perhaps it is not yet too late for
a get-together on this point in the
search for a formula—for this year
at least—by which an inter-com-
munal contest might be avoided. The
result of such a contest must inesca-
pably leave victors and vanquished
with a psychological aftermath of an
extremely unfortunate character.

CONCERNED.
Shanghai, Apr. 2.

The Jewish Refugees

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—In view of the Japanese an-
nouncement of the desired increase
of representation on the Council, and
the threat to the "Occidental" vote,
I would like to make the following
observations for consideration by our
councillors.

The Jewish Community, who have
approximately 400 votes, and who
might thereby become "a decisive
factor" in determining our position in
the Municipal administration, are
new to the procedure of the voting.
I have been approached by one or
two Jews who have asked whether
the ballot is "secret" or not. Several
of this community have apparently
been "canvassed" by Japanese civil-
ians, accompanied by a German inter-
preter, and have been given a paper
in the form of a "questionnaire," which
I am given to understand is a veiled
threat that should they not vote for
the Japanese, they will be the suffer-
ers. One must understand that these
peoples are "oppressed" and know no
liberty. Their position here is very
precarious, for they are residing in
a military occupied zone, with the
favour bestowed upon them by that
military force.

In my opinion, the propaganda sec-
tion of the Council should get to work
and allay the worry of those who
desire to cast their vote in favour of
the British or American representa-
tives but fear repercussions. After all,
financial support of the Jewish Re-
fugee Committee emanates in the
main from Europe and America, and
this should be impressed on them to
obtain either their support, or absolute
neutrality.

They have done nothing to build up
this port, and it is known that their
only desire is to live in peace in a
newly found haven.

A BRITISH RATEPAYER.
Shanghai, Apr. 2.
page_data.zh:
1940年

上海工部局选举：
呼吁妥协

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——凡是认识到外国租界巨大价值的人，几乎都会对今年工部局选举将在各社群之间以贵报所称的“实力较量”形式展开这一事实感到惋惜。人们充分认识到，五名日籍候选人的提名，无论其动机如何掩饰，都是日籍社群对此地旧有权力平衡的挑战；如果英籍和美籍纳税人希望保留九个外籍席位中的七个，他们将不得不集结所有的投票力量来做到这一点。即使他们此次设法保住了这七个席位，也不能保证未来仍能如此。由于国际趋势和世界其他地区的当前事态，日籍社群的力量可能会增长，而其他外籍社群的力量可能会衰退。

令人遗憾的是，在这座城市已经发生且必将继续发生的演变变化中，从未建立起就工部局按比例进行国际代表权等事项进行谈判、协商和决策的机制。虽然英籍、美籍和日籍社群在人数上可能最强，但并非只有它们与此相关。所有外籍居民共同构成了这个国际社群，他们都有权参与行政管理，因为他们各自都为该管理做出了贡献。如果工部局选举任由其发展为各社群之间每年的“恶斗”，而不是个人之间关于其治理能力的竞争，那么上海将不可避免地失去那种集体性的国际和谐，而这一直是其最有价值的特征之一。

人们不禁怀疑，重要社群的领导人是否对问题的这一方面给予了应有的深刻和建设性考虑。这座城市并非大社群的专属事务，也不应成为它们政治争斗的舞台。它需要各社群最佳力量的合作汇聚，而英籍、美籍……日籍领导人不应忽视这样一个事实：在这种合作汇聚中，无疑符合他们自身的最大利益。

也许现在寻求一种公式——至少在今年——以避免社群间竞争还为时不晚。这种竞争的结果不可避免地会产生胜者和败者，并留下性质极其不幸的心理后果。

关切者
上海，4月2日。

犹太难民

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——鉴于日方宣布希望增加在工部局的代表权，并对“西方”选票构成威胁，我想提出以下意见，供我们的董事考虑。

犹太社群拥有大约400张选票，因此可能成为决定我们在市政管理中地位的“决定性因素”，他们对投票程序尚不熟悉。曾有一两名犹太人向我询问，投票是否是“秘密”的。该社群中的几个人显然已被日籍平民（由一名德语翻译陪同）进行了“游说”，并向他们提供了一份“问卷”形式的文件，据我了解，这是一种含蓄的威胁，即如果他们不投票给日籍候选人，他们将遭受苦难。必须理解，这些人受到“压迫”，不知自由为何物。他们在此地的处境非常 precarious（不稳定/危险），因为他们居住在一个军事占领区，依靠该军事力量给予的恩惠生存。

在我看来，工部局的宣传部门应当开展工作，消除那些希望投票支持英籍或美籍代表但又害怕遭到报复的人的担忧。毕竟，犹太难民委员会的财政支持主要来自欧洲和美国，应当向他们强调这一点，以争取他们的支持或绝对中立。

他们并未为建设此港口做出任何贡献，众所周知，他们唯一的愿望是在新找到的避风港中和平生活。

一名英籍纳税人
上海，4月2日。

page_data.en:
MAR 1 2 1940
US Association Rules
Hold No Tricks
Three Contest
For SMC Seats
S'hai Americans Using
Plan Similar
To British

Ratepaying members of
the American Association,
qualified to vote at Shang-
hai Municipal Council elec-
tions, will take part in the
primary ballot of the Associa-
tion to select two SMC can-
didates out of the three pro-
posed, Messrs. J. W. Carney,
R. T. McDonnell and N. F. All-
man.
This follows the practise of the
similar "straw vote" taken by
local British organisations to
select the British candidates, who
this year number seven for five
seats.
Numbers Unknown
At present the American As-
sociation has not checked up to
see how many of its 1000 or so
members are qualified ratepayers.
American voters in Shanghai
total somewhere around the 500
mark, and it is believed, however,
that the great majority of these
are members of the Association.
No details have been fixed re-
garding the primary ballot, and
it is expected that a committee
meeting will be held in the next
couple of days to fix all arrange-
ments.
Membership Open
Allegations that primary voting
by ratepayer members of the As-
sociation only formed a "trick
clause" in the constitution
were denied to the Shanghai
Evening Post today, when an
official was questioned. "The
trouble is" he said "that not
enough people read the constitu-
tion. I've told quite a few people
that they should apply for a copy
and study it."
"As regards membership of the
Association, it is open. Any
American can join it. I've never
heard of anyone refusing to join
it. Some people who are not on
the register today are people who
have just neglected to send a sub-
scription along. The officials will
be only too glad to get as many
members as possible." There is no
fixed subscription to the Associa-
tion. Any contribution can be
made.
Other Proposers
Other officials pointed out that
there was nothing to prevent
Americans from proposing other
candidates directly to the SMC.
apart from those of the Associa-
tion. "The Association was only
formed five years ago. Candidates
were proposed directly before
then, and can be proposed direct-
ly now."
It was pointed out, however,
that the idea of the Association,
whose membership was greatly
inclusive, in proposing American
candidates was to simplify mat-
ters and prevent any conflict of
interests.
page_data.zh:
1940年3月12日
美国协会规则
不搞花招
三选二
竞选工部局席位
上海美国人采用
与英国人类似的
计划

有资格在上海公共租界工部局选举中投票的美国协会纳税会员，将参加协会的初选投票，从提名的三位候选人——J. W. Carney 先生、R. T. McDonnell 先生和 N. F. Allman 先生——中选出两位工部局候选人。

此举效仿了当地英国组织为选出英国候选人而进行的类似“意向投票”的做法，今年英国候选人为七人，争夺五个席位。

人数不详

目前，美国协会尚未核查其约一千名会员中有多少人是具备资格的纳税人。上海的美国选民总数大约在500人左右，不过据信，其中绝大多数都是该协会会员。

关于初选投票的细节尚未确定，预计将在未来几天内召开委员会会议，以确定所有安排。

会员资格开放

今日，当一名官员接受《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）询问时，否认了有关仅由协会纳税会员进行初选投票构成章程中“花招条款”的指控。他说：“问题在于，没有足够的人去阅读章程。我已经告诉不少人，他们应该申请一份副本并加以研读。”

“至于协会会员资格，它是开放的。任何美国人都可以加入。我从未听说过有人拒绝加入。今天有些不在名册上的人，只是疏忽了未缴纳会费。官员们非常乐意吸纳尽可能多的会员。”协会没有固定的会费标准。任何金额的捐款均可接受。

其他提名人

其他官员指出，除了协会提名的候选人外，美国人可以直接向工部局提名其他候选人，对此没有任何阻碍。“该协会成立于五年前。在此之前，候选人是直接提名的，现在也可以直接提名。”

不过也有人指出，该协会成员具有广泛的包容性，由其提名美国候选人的初衷是为了简化事务，防止任何利益冲突。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 7834
Date 14 3 40

MAR 7 1940

Americans Pick
Extra Candidate

N. F. Allman Chosen;
Primary Election
Needed For SMC

Local Americans will have to
hold a primary ballot to choose
their candidates for the Shanghai
Municipal Council this year, for
an additional name is being pro-
posed to the American Association
today, that of Mr. N. F. Allman.
Two candidates already picked
for the two SMC seats by the
American Association committee
are Mr. J. W. Carney, former
councillor, and Mr. R. T. McDon-
nell, present councillor.

Many Sponsors

Under the association's byelaws,
candidates for the SMC must be
proposed by ten American rate-
payers, but this morning it ap-
peared that the response to the
proposal of Mr. Allman was so
enthusiastic that the form may
be signed by from 50 to 100 peo-
ple.

There is no indication yet as to
whether any other names will be
forwarded for the primary ballot,
but there are only four days to go.
Nominations must be in the hands
of Mr. James M. Howes, secretary
of the American Association, on
or before next Monday.

Persuasion

The whole committee of the as-
sociation acted as the Municipal
Elections sub-committee in pick-
ing the first two candidates, Messrs.
Carney and McDonnell. Mr. Car-
ney, assistant manager of the
Standard-Vacuum Oil Company,
resigned from the Council last
year without giving any reasons.
On this occasion he did not want
to stand as a candidate but "they
persuaded me" he told the Shang-
hai Evening Post.

Mr. McDonnell general manager
of William Hirst and Company,
was coopted to the Council on Mr.
Carney's resignation. The Amer-
ican Association will now have to
nominate one from the trio formed
by these two and Mr. Allman, the
Shanghai lawyer, rider and WWI
officer, provided still more names
do not come forward.

Lil
C 7/3

1940年3月7日

美国人增选
额外候选人

N. F. Allman 获选；
需举行初选
以定工部局人选

今年，上海本地美国人必须举行初选投票来选出他们的上海公共租界工部局候选人，因为今天向美国协会提名了一位额外的人选，即 N. F. Allman 先生。

美国协会委员会此前已为两个工部局席位选出的两位候选人是：前董事 J. W. Carney 先生，以及现任董事 R. T. McDonnell 先生。

众多附议人

根据协会附则，工部局候选人必须由十名美国纳税人附议提名，但今天上午看来，对 Allman 先生提名的响应如此热烈，以至于附议签名的人数可能达到50至100人。

目前尚无迹象表明是否会有其他名字被提交参加初选投票，但只剩下四天时间。提名必须在下周一或之前送达美国协会秘书 James M. Howes 先生手中。

游说

协会全体委员会在挑选最初两位候选人 Carney 先生和 McDonnell 先生时，充当了市政选举小组委员会的角色。Carney 先生系美孚真空石油公司（Standard-Vacuum Oil Company）副经理，去年无理由辞去董事职务。此次他本不想作为候选人参选，但他告诉《上海晚邮报》：“是他们说服了我”。

McDonnell 先生系 William Hirst and Company 总经理，在 Carney 先生辞职后被增补进董事会。如果不再有更多名字出现，美国协会现在将不得不从这三人——这两位以及上海律师、骑手兼第一次世界大战军官 Allman 先生——组成的三人组合中提名一人。

Lil

March 13, 1940. Morning Translation

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-
FORTHCOMING ELECTION OF S.M.C. MEMBERS : BRITISH UNLAWFULLY
INTERFERING WITH JAPANESE RIGHT OF ELECTION

The monopolization of the S.M.C. by the British
has been exposed, while the administration of the Council
has given rise to much criticism.
The election of members of the Council for
the ensuing year is approaching. The Japanese hope to
remove this unreasonable monopolization of the S.M.C. by
the British; on the other hand, the British authorities
desire to maintain their policy of dictatorship and to
interfere with the right of the Japanese to elect more
representatives on the Council.

At present, the Council has five British members,
two Americans, two Japanese and five Chinese. Such a
proportion is improper either on the basis of population,
or political or economic influence. Since the outbreak
of local hostilities, the Japanese population has registered
a large increase. The Japanese should have more members
on the Council than even the British.
The British authorities, who are greatly
embarrassed over the increase in the number of Japanese voters,
are devising counter-measures by resorting to mean acts.
In December last year, the S.M.C. made public a list of
persons qualified to vote, in which the Japanese are shown
to possess more than 2,000 persons. The increase in the
political and economic influence of the Japanese in Shanghai
and vicinity is an undeniable fact.
Britain must not be allowed to maintain the
existing status of the S.M.C. The following should be
remembered when dealing with the matter :-
1) The S.M.C. should be neutral in the elections and the
office of elections should be established in the Council
building.
2) Formerly, the ratepayers were entitled to vote in the
elections if they had paid the municipal tax for six
months prior to the elections, but this condition was
cancelled in order to provide facilities to British
ratepayers.
3) Japanese have appealed for a right to vote for "indirect"
taxpayers, but this was refused. While this system
was secretly instituted on behalf of British residents,
the municipal authorities did not inform the Japanese
of this until it was referred to by the Japanese.
4) The land owned by the British real estate companies is
permitted to be split up in order to increase the number
of persons entitled to vote.

1940年3月13日。晨间译稿

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：
工部局董事即将选举：英国非法干涉日本选举权

英国垄断工部局的行径已被揭露，且工部局的行政管理引发了诸多批评。
下一年度工部局董事选举即将来临。日本人希望消除英国对工部局这种不合理的垄断；另一方面，英国当局则希望维持其独裁政策，并干涉日本人选举更多代表进入工部局的权利。

目前，工部局有五名英国董事、两名美国董事、两名日本董事和五名中国董事。无论是基于人口比例，还是政治或经济影响力，这样的比例都是不恰当的。自本地战事爆发以来，日本人口大幅增加。日本人在工部局中的董事人数甚至应多于英国人。
英国当局因日本选民人数的增加而深感尴尬，正诉诸卑劣手段 devising counter-measures。去年十二月，工部局公布了一份合格选民名单，其中显示日本人拥有超过2,000人。日本人在上海及周边地区政治和经济影响力的增长是一个不可否认的事实。
决不允许英国维持工部局的现状。在处理此事时应记住以下几点：
1) 工部局在选举中应保持中立，选举办公室应设在工部局大楼内。
2) 以前，纳税人若在选举前六个月缴纳了市政税，即有权在选举中投票，但为了给英国纳税人提供便利，这一条件被取消。
3) 日本人曾呼吁给予“间接”纳税人投票权，但遭到拒绝。虽然这一制度是秘密为英国居民设立的，但市政当局直到日本人提及此事后才告知日本人。
4) 英国房地产公司拥有的土地被允许分割，以增加有资格投票的人数。

March 13, 1940.
Morning Translation.
Sin Shan Pao (Japanese owned Chinese Language newspaper):-
Japanese Decide to Increase the Number of Their Councillors

Fearing a possible change in the status of the
International Settlement, the British authorities have
been attempting since the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities to check the advance of Japanese influence and
had adopted certain steps to check this influence. In
view of the increase in the Japanese population in Shanghai
and the existing conditions in the Settlement, the Japanese
residents, supported by various bodies and the Japanese
army, navy and foreign authorities, are doing their best to
expand their power in the Settlement.
The Japanese population in Shanghai is increasing,
while the number of Japanese voters is also increasing.
It is, therefore, natural for the Japanese to demand an
increase in the number of Japanese members on the Council.
Worried over the attitude of the Japanese, the British
authorities have mobilized in an endeavour to check the
Japanese influence. The residents are dissatisfied with
the poor administration of the S.M.C. in the past. Even
the Chinese are hoping that the Japanese influence will
expand in the Settlement.
It is to be hoped that Japanese bodies will
do their utmost to oppose the arbitrary exercise of power
by the Settlement authorities.

1940年3月13日。
晨间译稿。
《新山报》（日资中文报纸）：
日本人决定增加其董事人数

出于对国际租界地位可能发生变化的担忧，英国当局自中日战事爆发以来一直试图遏制日本影响力的扩张，并采取了一些措施来抑制这种影响力。鉴于上海日本人口的增加以及租界内的现有状况，日本居民在各团体以及日本陆、海军和外国当局的支持下，正尽力扩大其在租界内的权力。
上海的日本人口正在增加，日本选民的人数也在增加。因此，日本人要求增加工部局中日本董事的人数是自然的。
英国当局对日本人的态度感到担忧，已动员起来试图遏制日本的影响力。居民们对工部局过去的糟糕管理感到不满。甚至连中国人都希望日本人在租界内的影响力能够扩大。
希望日本各团体竭尽全力反对租界当局任意行使权力。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
JAN 2 . 1940
7834
25 / 40

Japanese Voter
Total Recording
Surprise Decline

Nipponese Held Likely
To Make Efforts
For Control

MANY HONGKEW
RATES UNPAID

Campaign For Election
Problem Provided
For Settlement

Opening gun in this year's municipal election and ratepayers' meeting has been fired in the reminder sent by Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner General of the SMC, to the Senior Consul Commander L. Neyrone, to fix the date of the meeting, while a surprise has been occasioned in the discovery that Japanese voters have declined in numbers.

The number of Japanese voters in the International Settlement of Shanghai eligible to cast their ballots at the Annual Ratepayers' Meeting this year has decreased from 2256 to 2024 votes, while the total number of qualified voters in the Settlement has increased from 4772 to 5054 votes, according to comparisons which have been compiled by the Shanghai Evening Post from the SMC's final voting list for the 1939 meeting issued on March 31, last year, and the provisional voting list for the 1940 meeting which was issued by the SMC last month.

Unusual Situation

The figures just indicated lend further surprise to the unusual situation which had been anticipated in several local quarters with regard to the coming SMC election for 1940, which this year is again scheduled to take place early in April, before the rate payers' meeting.

Belief and opinions have already been expressed in local circles that this year would see a concerted effort on the part of Japanese voters to obtain a maximum or majority of Japanese councillors elected to the SMC, although there were indications a few weeks ago that the Japanese would "let sleeping dogs lie." The expected attempt of the Japanese voters to do so at last year's elections was apparently cancelled almost at the last moment.

Majority Control

Several local observers, appraised of the decline shown in the number of Japanese voters, continue to share the feeling, however, that the Japanese would renew their efforts to obtain at least a majority control of the SMC at the coming annual meeting.

Moreover, it was pointed out by one well-known official when questioned by the Shanghai Evening Post on the situation, the comparisons shown to exist between last year's voting list and the provisional list for this year could not be considered altogether as representing a "final picture," he pointed out. Strong possibilities remain that the number of Japanese voters would be increased prior to the elections "if a fairly large percentage of residents in the northern areas catch up with their obligations on Municipal rates."

USA And Japan

A similar opinion is shared by a prominent local businessman, who adds his belief that in view of the present world situation and a possible "dark period" in US.-Japan trade relationships, Japan would concentrate upon improving her position in China as an alternative, and at the same making it almost a necessity on her part to strengthen her control over Shanghai.

The Land Regulations which bind the legal powers of the Shanghai Municipal Council also determine rights and eligibility which are conformed with at the Annual Ratepayers' Meeting and the election of the Council.

Voting Qualifications

Sufficiently clear, Article 19 of the Land Regulations describes the qualifications which is required of voters as follows:

"Every foreigner, either individually or as a member of a firm, residing in the (International) Settlement, having paid all taxes due, and being an owner of land of not less than five hundred taels ($700) in value, whose annual payment of assessment on land or houses or both, exclusive of all payments in respect of licences, shall amount to the sum of ten taels ($14) and upwards, or who shall be a householder paying on an assessed rental of not less than five hundred taels per annum and upwards, shall be entitled to vote in the election of the (said) Members of the Council and at the public meetings. Provided always that the proxies of Ratepayers only who are absent from the Consular District of Shanghai, or are prevented by illness from attending shall be admitted to vote at such meetings. And no one shall be qualified to be a member of the (said) Council unless he shall pay an annual assessment, exclusive of licences, of fifty taels ($70), or shall be a householder paying on an assessed rental of one thousand two hundred taels ($1680) per annum, Provided always that this clause shall not entitle any firm to more than one vote.

List Publication

"A list of persons duly qualified to vote according to the Regulations to which these Bye-laws are appended shall be kept at the office of the Council, and such list shall be revised and corrected by the Secretary of the Council on the first day of December in each year, or so soon after as may be convenient, and published for the information of the public in such manner as the Council for the time being shall think proper."

In a broad way, it can be inferred that the manner in which the election of the Council and the Annual Ratepayers' Meeting are held, shows similarity to procedure which takes place at the annual meeting of stockholders of a business corporation.

Date Of Meeting

It is a standing custom about the middle of January in every year, for the Secretary of the SMC to issue a formal reminder to the Consular Body to fix a date for the Annual Ratepayers' Meeting. This has already been done this year.

Customary day for the ratepayers' meeting is the Wednesday nearest the middle of April, while the election of councillors for the ensuing year takes place a week before the meeting.

Nominations

With regard to the election of members of the Council, the ruling of the Land Regulations is fixed and clear that such nominations must be forwarded in writing at least seven days prior to the day appointed for the election.

In the case of foreign nominees for the Council, each nomination must be accompanied by the signature of two persons, proposer and seconder, who are duly qualified voters.

Altogether only nine foreign seats are available for foreign Councillors. Five Chinese Councillors also participate in the membership of the Council, but are elected to office separately by members of the Chinese Ratepayers' Association. The foreign representation, by "gentlemen's agreement" for several years past, has consisted of five Britons, two Americans and two Japanese.

（批：G. C. S. M）

1940年1月2日
7834
25 / 40

日本选民
总登记人数
意外下降

日本人被认为
可能努力争取
控制权

许多虹口纳税人
未缴纳税款

选举运动
为解决问题
提供了契机

工部局秘书兼总办 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生致函资深领事指挥官 L. Neyrone，要求确定纳税人大会日期，由此打响了今年市政选举和纳税人大会的开场枪；与此同时，人们惊讶地发现日本选民人数有所下降。

根据《上海晚邮报》对工部局去年3月31日发布的1939年大会最终投票名单，以及工部局上月发布的1940年大会临时投票名单所作的比较统计，上海公共租界内有资格在今年年度纳税人大会上投票的日本选民人数已从2256人减少至2024人，而租界内合格选民总数则从4772人增加至5054人。

不寻常的情况

上述数据进一步加剧了本地各界对即将到来的1940年工部局选举所预期的不寻常局势的惊讶，今年的选举仍定于4月初、纳税人大会之前举行。

本地各界已表达了一种看法和意见，认为今年日本选民将 concerted effort（协同努力），力求使当选工部局董事的日本人达到最大数量或占多数，尽管几周前有迹象表明日本人将“按兵不动”（let sleeping dogs lie）。去年选举中日本选民预期的此类举动显然在最后一刻被取消。

多数控制

然而，几位了解日本选民人数下降情况的本地观察家继续认为，日本人将在即将到来的年度大会上重新努力，以至少获得对工部局的多数控制权。

此外，一位知名官员在接受《上海晚邮报》就此事询问时指出，去年的投票名单与今年的临时名单之间存在的比较结果，不能完全被视为代表了“最终图景”。他指出，如果北部地区相当大比例的居民补缴了市政税欠款，日本选民的人数仍很有可能在选举前增加。

美国与日本

一位本地著名商人也持有类似观点，他补充认为，鉴于当前的世界局势以及美日贸易关系可能出现的“黑暗时期”，日本将转而集中力量改善其在中国的地位，同时也使得加强其对上海的控制几乎成为其必要之举。

约束上海工部局法律权力的《土地章程》也确定了在年度纳税人大会和董事会选举中所遵循的权利和资格。

投票资格

《土地章程》第19条对选民所需资格作了足够清晰的描述，如下：

“凡居住于（国际）租界内的外国人，无论是个人还是作为商号成员，已缴清所有应付税款，且拥有价值不少于五百两（700美元）的土地，其每年缴纳的土地或房屋或两者之评估税（不包括所有执照费用）总额达到十两（14美元）及以上，或者是年评估租金不少于五百两及以上的住户，均有权在（所述）董事选举及公众会议上投票。但规定只有那些不在上海领事管辖区或因病无法出席的纳税人的代理人才被允许在此类会议上投票。除非某人每年缴纳的评估税（不包括执照费）达到五十两（70美元），或者是年评估租金为一千二百两（1680美元）的住户，否则无资格成为（所述）董事会成员。但规定任何商号不得因此条款获得超过一票的权利。”

名单公布

“一份根据附有此等附例的章程 duly qualified（具备正式资格）的投票人名单应保存在董事会办公室，该名单应由董事会秘书于每年12月1日或此后方便时尽快进行修订和更正，并以当时董事会认为适当的方式公布，以供公众知晓。”

大体而言，可以推断，董事会选举和年度纳税人大会的举行方式，显示出与商业公司年度股东大会程序相似之处。

会议日期

每年1月中旬，由工部局秘书向领事团发出正式提醒，以确定年度纳税人大会的日期，这是一项惯例。今年此项工作已经完成。

纳税人大会的习惯日期是4月中旬最近的星期三，而下一年度董事的选举则在大会前一周举行。

提名

关于董事会成员的选举，《土地章程》的规定固定且明确，即此类提名必须在指定的选举日前至少七天以书面形式提交。

对于外籍董事候选人，每份提名必须附有两名具备正式资格的选民（即提议人和附议人）的签名。

外籍董事席位总共只有九个供外籍人士竞选。五名中国董事也参与董事会成员构成，但由中国纳税人协会成员单独选举产生。根据过去几年的“君子协定”，外籍代表由五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人组成。

《上海泰晤士报》

1939年9月16日

据上海《每日新闻》昨日报道，三井物产株式会社上海支店经理、上海日本商工会议所会长花轮裕太郎先生，预计将被推荐为上海工部局董事，以取代大阪商船株式会社上海支店经理杉坂富之助先生。杉坂先生已被任命为新成立的东亚海运株式会社大阪支店经理，他将于昨日向工部局递交辞呈，并于今日乘坐日本邮船会社的“镰仓丸”号邮轮离开上海。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
03578
APR 4 1939

1939 Councillors
Elected En Bloc
At Noon Today

No Extra Nominations
Made By Japanese
Residents Of City

FIVE-TWO-TWO
RATIO UNCHANGED

British Ranks Follow
Recent Selections
Of Straw Vote

There will be no municipal
election this year. The Shanghai
Municipal Council will continue
to consist of five Britons, two
Americans and two Japanese, to-
gether with five Chinese, despite
rumors circulating for past months
that the Japanese were attempt-
ing to secure increased represen-
tation.

At noon today nominations
closed at the Administration
Building, and it was found that
exactly nine names had been re-
ceived for the nine posts of for-
eign members of the Council, so
that no poll will be necessary.

The American representatives
are unchanged from those serving
at present. They are Messrs.
C. S. Franklin, the present chair-
man, and A. C. Cornish.

Japanese Unchanged

The two Japanese representa-
tives are also those who are serv-
ing at present. They are Messrs.
O. Okamoto and T. Sugisaka.

In the ranks of the Britons the
representatives picked in the re-
cent straw vote are the five no-
minated. They show two changes
from the present council, as Bri-
gadier-General E. B. Macnaghten
and Mr. F. N. Matthews have
dropped out, and Messrs. G. A.
Haley and T. S. Powell come in to
replace them, while Messrs. G. E.
Mitchell, W. J. Keswick and R. G.
MacDonald are reelected.

Chinese Councillors

These nine, together with the
five Chinese councillors whose
election has not yet been notified,
will form the Council for the
forthcoming municipal year.

The election of the Chinese
councillors is to take place within
the next fortnight. From present
indications it seems that there
will be no change in the present
representation of Messrs. W.
Cockson, Yulin Hsi, Eugene Y. B.
Kiang, L. T. Yuan and Yu Ya-
ching.

Today at noon Mr. R. D. K. Silby
also was declared elected as Land
Commissioner for 1939. His name
was the only one put forward by
registered land commissioners for
the post and in this instance also
no poll is necessary.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》
03578
1939年4月4日

1939年董事
于今日中午
整体当选

本市日本居民
未提出额外提名

五-二-二
比例不变

英国人选遵循
近期意向投票
的结果

今年将没有市政选举。尽管过去几个月流传着日本人试图争取更多代表权的谣言，上海工部局将继续由五名英国人、两名美国人和两名日本人组成，外加五名中国人。

今天中午，行政大楼的提名截止，结果发现正好收到九份提名，对应工部局外籍成员的九个席位，因此无需进行投票。

美方代表与现任者相同。他们是现任主席 C. S. Franklin 先生和 A. C. Cornish 先生。

日方人选不变

两名日本代表也是现任者。他们是 O. Okamoto 先生和 T. Sugisaka 先生。

在英国人选方面，近期意向投票中选出的五人即为被提名人。与现任董事会相比有两处变动，因为 E. B. Macnaghten 准将和 F. N. Matthews 先生退出，由 G. A. Haley 先生和 T. S. Powell 先生接替他们，而 G. E. Mitchell 先生、W. J. Keswick 先生和 R. G. MacDonald 先生获得连任。

中国董事

这九人，加上选举结果尚未通知的五名中国董事，将组成下一个市政年度的董事会。

中国董事的选举将在未来两周内进行。从目前的情况来看，现任代表 W. Cockson 先生、奚玉麟（Yulin Hsi）先生、江一平（Eugene Y. B. Kiang）先生、袁履登（L. T. Yuan）先生和虞洽卿（Yu Yaching）先生似乎不会有变动。

今天中午，R. D. K. Silby 先生也被宣布当选为1939年度地政专员。他的名字是注册地政专员为该职位提出的唯一人选，因此在这种情况下也无需投票。

SUCCESSOR TO MR. SUGISAKA, JAPANESE REPRESENTATIVE

Mr. Miura, Japanese Consul-General, who has failed to persuade Mr. Funatsu to succeed Mr. Sugisaka retiring member of the S.M.C. is reported to have asked Mr. Hanawa, manager of the local Mitsui Company, but the offer was declined. Our authorities are anxious to select a Japanese representative as quickly as possible because the S.M.C. has to deal with many delicate affairs, such as the outside Settlement Roads' issue and finance. April 18, 1939.

MAINICHI

THE RATEPAYERS MEETING OF THE INTERNATIONAL
SETTLEMENT

The election of Councillors
of the S.M.C. has passed off smoothly. The annual
ratepayers meeting of the International Settlement
will be held at the Grand Theatre at 2 p.m. April 19.
The ratepayers meeting is the only general meeting at
which Japanese, British, Americans and other nationals
residing in the Settlement are represented. Great
importance is attached to the meeting because of the
nature of the organization; but it will be nothing
more than a formal affair like other meetings in the
past.

Shanghai is involved in the
Sino-Japanese hostilities to an extent it had never
experienced before yet there are no indications that
the forthcoming ratepayers meeting will discuss measures
to deal with the situation.

Among the resolutions to be dis-
cussed at the meeting is one which draws attention
to the increase in the Municipal rate. Foreigners,
except Japanese, and Chinese residents have been
voicing their opposition against this increase and it
is expected that they will raise an objection at the
meeting. It is reported that the Japanese ratepayers
will adopt a calm attitude at the ratepayers meeting
in connection with the increase of the Municipal rate
because it is revealed that a considerable part of the
revenue collected from Japanese residents is being used
for the benefit of the Japanese community.

At any rate it is believed that
the meeting will be given to understand that an increase
in the Municipal rate is inevitable and the meeting
will pass it without any trouble.

Mr. Hayashi, Chairman of the
Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions,
has made the following statement:-
"Only the question of the
increase in the Municipal rate is attracting public
attention. The Japanese ratepayers will keep a calm
attitude over the matter. I hope that all Japanese
ratepayers will attend the ratepayers meeting, but I
fear that not many of them will attend because the
resolutions to be discussed are of little interest to
them."

1939年4月18日。

《每日新闻》

国际公共租界的纳税人大会

工部局董事选举已顺利进行。国际公共租界的年度纳税人大会将于4月19日下午2点在大戏院举行。纳税人大会是唯一一个有居住在租界内的日本人、英国人、美国人及其他国籍人士代表的全体大会。鉴于该组织的性质，此次大会备受重视；但这将不过像过去的其他会议一样，只是一场形式主义的活动。

上海卷入中日敌对行动的程度前所未有，但目前没有迹象表明即将到来的纳税人大会将讨论应对局势的措施。

将在大会上讨论的决议中，有一项提请人们注意市政捐税的增加。除日本人外的外籍人士和中国居民一直对此增税表示反对，预计他们将在会议上提出异议。据报道，日本纳税人在纳税人大会上对市政捐税增加一事将采取冷静态度，因为据透露，从日本居民那里征收的相当一部分收入正用于造福日本社群。

无论如何，相信大会将被告知增加市政捐税是不可避免的，并且大会将毫无困难地通过该决议。

日本街道工会联合会主席林先生发表如下声明：
“只有市政捐税增加的问题正在吸引公众的注意力。日本纳税人在此事上将保持冷静态度。我希望所有日本纳税人都参加纳税人大会，但我担心出席者不会多，因为待讨论的决议对他们来说没什么吸引力。”

Shanghai Public Daily News (市民日报) publishes the following
editorial comment :-

ADVICE TO MR. FRANKLIN

When interviewed by newspaper reporters the
other day, Mr. C.S. Franklin, the newly elected Chairman of
the S.M.C., said that during his term of office he would
endeavour to secure closer co-operation from the various
public organizations regarding affairs in the Settlement.
He added: "I regard Shanghai as my second native place and
I shall always live here. Perhaps my sons will follow my
example and reside here. Will I not do my best to make
Shanghai a better city?" Mr. Franklin sincerely expressed
his wishes and promised to make every endeavour to improve
the municipal administration in future.
There are a number of municipal questions
waiting to be solved, the most important of which is the
educational problem. The ratepayers in the Settlement are
paying annually a large sum of money in rates to the S.M.C.,
but their children still do not get the chance to receive an
adequate education, not to speak of the children of the poor
who are left illiterate and wandering in the streets. At
the Annual Meeting of Foreign Ratepayers held on April 14,
Mr. J.S. Barr took the platform and made a speech in which
he hoped that the S.M.C. would curtail the unnecessary
expenditure in various Departments but at the same time make
an ample grant for educational expenses. Mr. Barr's words
honestly represent the wishes of the ratepayers in general.
Speaking on the Council's educational policy,
Mr. Franklin said that the moment had not come to make it
public as the new Councillors had had no time to study the
reports on this problem. What we wish of Mr. Franklin is
that the Council, in spite of its financial stringency, will
appropriate an ample sum for educational purposes, establish
more schools in various districts of the Settlement, issue as
great a grant-in-aid as possible to Chinese private schools
so as to accommodate those children who are at present deprived
of the chance to go to school, and modify the standard measures
to be observed by those schools in receipt of the grant-in-aid.

1937年4月19日。下午译文。

最初的要求是撤销增税令。因此，外籍纳税人年度会议的结果令我们大失所望。
有句谚语说：“天助自助者”。如果我们希望有效地取消这次增税，我们唯一的途径就是团结起来，以加强我们的反对力量，并一致推迟缴纳捐税，无论我们必须做出何种牺牲。
即使工部局动用其全部警力，我们认为它也无法控制国际公共租界内的200万中国居民。让我们提醒公众，为了实现我们的目标——取消市政捐税的增加——我们应该捂紧钱袋子。

《市民日报》发表以下社论评论：

致富兰克林先生的建议

日前在接受记者采访时，新当选的工部局主席C.S.富兰克林先生表示，在任期内，他将努力争取各公共组织在租界事务上更紧密的合作。他补充说：“我把上海视为我的第二故乡，我将永远住在这里。也许我的儿子们会效仿我，在此居住。难道我不会尽力让上海成为一座更好的城市吗？”富兰克林先生真诚地表达了他的愿望，并承诺将尽一切努力改善未来的市政管理。
有许多市政问题等待解决，其中最重要的是教育问题。租界内的纳税人每年向工部局缴纳巨额捐税，但他们的孩子仍然没有机会接受充分的教育，更不用说那些贫困家庭的儿童，他们沦为文盲并在街头流浪。在4月14日举行的外籍纳税人年度会议上，J.S.巴尔先生上台发言，希望工部局削减各部门不必要的开支，但同时拨出充足的经费用于教育支出。巴尔先生的话诚实地代表了广大纳税人的愿望。
谈到董事会的教育政策时，富兰克林先生表示，目前尚未到公开的时候，因为新董事们还没有时间研究有关此问题的报告。我们对富兰克林先生的期望是，董事会尽管财政紧张，仍应拨出巨款用于教育目的，在租界各区建立更多学校，尽可能向中国私立学校发放大量补助金，以容纳目前失学的儿童，并修改领取补助金的学校须遵守的标准措施。

As regards the Extra-Settlement Roads question,
the Yu Koh Tsung affair has caused a bad impression. As
an eminent lawyer, Mr. Franklin is naturally aware that the
Council has no legal ground to monopolize the extra-
Settlement roads, an act likely to estrange the sympathies
of the Chinese. These roads should be handed over to the
Shanghai City Government.
Mr. Franklin has also not yet drawn up any definite
plans regarding the Council's financial problem; he merely
expressed his great concern over it. Frankly speaking,
it will become almost an impossibility for the Council to
increase the Municipal Rate as a means of balancing its
budget, in view of the strong opposition from the ratepayers
in the Settlement. Should the Council rashly attempt to
increase the rate, who will be held responsible for any
serious consequences that may take place? We sincerely
hope that Mr. Franklin will adopt and put into force the
suggestions on retrenchment made by the Chinese Ratepayers'
Association, a body representing 64% of the total rates
paid and over 95% of the whole population in the Settlement.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, APRIL 16, 1937

MR. C. S. FRANKLIN IS
NEW CHAIRMAN
Mr. H. Porter Elected
Vice-Chairman For
1937 Council

Following the customary procedure, the first meeting of the incoming Shanghai Municipal Council was held yesterday at noon, when the only business was the election of Chairman and Vice-Chairman for the ensuing year.
On the motion of Mr. Yu Yaching, seconded by Mr. V. St. J. Killery, Mr. C. S. Franklin was elected Chairman. He was Vice-Chairman during the former Council.
On the motion of Mr. E. Y. B. Kiang, seconded by Mr. T. Yamamoto, Mr. Harold Porter, c.M.G., was elected to the post of Vice-Chairman.

CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, APRIL 16, 1937
“SQUANDERMANIA” AND PUBLIC APATHY

THE Annual Ratepayers’ Meeting held on Wednesday proved to be one of the most inconsequential in recent years. The report which Mr. H. E. Arnhold submitted is but a resume of various municipal problems which have been public knowledge for months past, and though it is a thoughtful document, comment extended at this juncture may be sheer repetition.

Besides the Chairman, the meeting was addressed by two ratepayers. Mr. J. S. Barr, of Medhurst College, whose interest in social welfare has been long noted, made an eloquent plea for continued support of foreign schools from the Shanghai Municipal Council. The subject indeed is deserving of serious consideration and, in our opinion, should not be made heir to petty economy schemes. Doubtless, the authorities of the schools whose grants from the Council may be withdrawn will be able to address themselves to the public and to command sufficient favorable sentiment to remove the possibility of rash decision or action on the part of the Council.

What immediately interests the public is the short proposal delivered by Mr. Ranald McDonald, British attorney, in the following words:

Would it be in order to suggest a vote of thanks to the people who have been practically responsible for the extraordinary squandermania of the last eight or nine years since they received $81,000,000 from an American company who took over the power company?

The proposal, whether offered in earnest or in jest, is provocative of mature deliberation. There is no doubt but that the Council has in the past been unduly liberal in dispensing its reserves, and it is also easy, as an afterthought, to show the Council how and where it could have saved money or economised on different items of expenditure. The “squandermania” as charged by Mr. McDonald, even if true, cannot be blamed on the Council alone; in fact, the public is as much to blame for permitting it to rear its head as the Council for indulging in it.

The Council has been generous with its money not for one year or two years but ever since its sale of the Electricity Department to the Shanghai Power Company. At the close of each successive fiscal year the Council submitted to the Annual Ratepayers’ Meeting a budget for approval, and in addition the Council has had annual reports printed for general perusal. If the ratepayers had assumed the responsibility together with the voting prerogative, they should have long ere this noticed the Council’s tendency toward extravagance and, having so noticed, should have taken steps to stop it in time. There is nothing to be gained over spilt milk; and one can add little to the municipal coffer after its depletion.

Judging by the poor attendance at the annual meeting Wednesday, ratepayers were conspicuous by their overwhelming absence. Out of 3,000 only 300 were present. And of the meager ten per cent no one except Mr. Barr even took the trouble to introduce any municipal problem. Their voting like their attendance was rather perfunctory; and when the ratepayers are inclined to show no interest in what the Council has done or is proposing to do, can there be any wonder that the Council, like all other public organisations, is constantly tempted to practice what Mr. McDonald has described as “squandermania?”

The root of the trouble lies both with the Council and with the public. On the one hand, the Council, dedicated to a policy of “discretion,” has seldom taken the public into confidence, and the public, denied confidence, has seldom sought to assert its right to demand confidence. The Council is happy to let the public alone except in the collection of municipal rates, and the public as represented by ratepayers whose future lies beyond China is happy to be left alone. The one is guilty of commission and the other of omission.

《字林西报》，1937年4月16日，星期五
“挥霍症”与公众的冷漠

周三举行的年度纳税人会议证明是近年来最无足轻重的会议之一。H. E. 安诺德先生提交的报告不过是对过去几个月已为公众所知的各种市政问题的综述，尽管这是一份经过深思熟虑的文件，但在此时此刻加以评论纯属老调重弹。

除主席外，还有两名纳税人向会议发了言。麦赫斯特学院（Medhurst College）的J. S. 巴尔先生长期以来一直关注社会福利，他雄辩地呼吁上海公共租界工部局继续支持外籍学校。这一主题确实值得认真考虑，在我们看来，不应使其成为 petty economy schemes（小气节约计划）的牺牲品。毫无疑问，那些可能失去工部局拨款的学校当局将能够向公众陈情，并赢得足够的好感，以消除工部局做出草率决定或采取行动的可能性。

直接引起公众兴趣的是英国律师拉纳德·麦克唐纳先生提出的简短建议，其措辞如下：

是否适宜提议对那些实际上对过去八九年来的 extraordinary squandermania（异常挥霍症）负责的人表示感谢？自从一家接管电力公司的美国公司向他们支付了8,100万美元以来，这种挥霍症便一直存在。

这项提议，无论是严肃提出还是开玩笑，都引发了成熟的审议。毫无疑问，工部局在过去动用储备金时过于慷慨，而且事后很容易指出工部局本可以在哪些方面以及如何节省资金或在不同支出项目上厉行节约。正如麦克唐纳先生所指控的那样，“挥霍症”即使属实，也不能只归咎于工部局；事实上，公众允许其抬头，与工部局沉溺其中一样，都难辞其咎。

工部局在金钱上的慷慨并非仅一两年，而是自将其电气处出售给上海电力公司以来一直如此。在每个财政年度结束时，工部局都会向年度纳税人会议提交预算以供批准，此外，工部局还印制年度报告供大众阅览。如果纳税人在拥有投票特权的同时也承担起责任，他们早就应该注意到工部局的奢侈倾向，并且在注意到之后，本应及时采取措施予以制止。覆水难收；在市政库藏耗尽之后，很难再为其增添多少收入。

从周三年度会议的出席人数寥寥来看，纳税人的缺席显得格外引人注目。3,000人中仅有300人出席。在这微不足道的百分之十中，除了巴尔先生外，甚至没有人费心提出任何市政问题。他们的投票如同他们的出席一样相当敷衍；当纳税人对工部局已完成或拟议完成的工作表现出毫无兴趣时，工部局像所有其他公共组织一样，不断受到诱惑去实践麦克唐纳先生所描述的“挥霍症”，这又有什么奇怪的呢？

问题的根源在于工部局和公众双方。一方面，致力于“酌情处理”政策的工部局很少向公众坦诚相待；而公众因被排除在信任之外，也很少试图主张其要求获得信任的权利。除了在征收市政捐税时，工部局乐于让公众自便；而以未来不在中国的纳税人为代表的公众也乐于不被打扰。一方犯作为之过，另一方犯不作为之过。

档案

212:9

In order to put an end to this anomalous state of
affairs a radical change in the system and whose future is
inevitably bound with that of Shanghai should be given the
majority vote. In this respect, the Chinese more than any
other national group or all other national groups com-
bined, should be given the same privilege to pass on the
municipal budget as well as other problems of importance
confronting the Council.
It is only logical to suggest that a ratepayers' as-
sociation be formed of all residents regardless of nation-
ality, and that this association shall elect a group of re-
presentatives to exercise the voting prerogative on behalf
of the entire community. Since the major burden of
taxation falls on the Chinese and since the Chinese also
constitute the majority of the population and of owners
of real property and industrial plants, they can be counted
upon to take a deep interest in the affairs of the Settle-
ment. Thus a representative attendance will be assured at
each annual meeting and an intelligent control over the
municipal administration may be exercised judiciously.
Until the interests of all ratepayers are pooled to-
gether, the annual meeting will have little meaning for
the public and will draw little attention from the ratepay-
ers. Mr. McDonald has pointed out only one of many features
which require adjustment, but there is no use in pointing
out anything unless the public is prepared to evolve a
fundamental solution in the basic organisation for the
ratepayers.
page_data.zh:
212:9

为了结束这种反常状态，必须进行彻底的制度变革，并且那些未来必然与上海命运紧密相连的人应获得多数投票权。在这方面，中国人比任何其他国籍群体或所有其他国籍群体的总和，更应享有同样的特权，对市政预算以及工部局面临的其他重要问题进行表决。

建议成立一个由所有居民不分国籍组成的纳税人协会，并由该协会选举一组代表，代表整个社区行使投票特权，这在逻辑上是合理的。由于税收的主要负担落在中国人身上，且中国人也构成了人口、房地产和工业厂房业主的大多数，可以指望他们对租界事务深感兴趣。因此，每次年度会议都能保证有代表性的出席人数，从而可以对市政行政进行明智而审慎的控制。

在所有纳税人的利益汇聚在一起之前，年度会议对公众而言意义不大，也不会引起纳税人的多少关注。麦克唐纳先生仅指出了许多需要调整的特征之一，但如果公众不准备在纳税人的基本组织结构中寻求根本解决方案，那么指出任何问题都是无用的。

April 16, 1937.    Morning Translation.

Le Journal de Shanghai published the following leading
article on April 15 :-

THE SETTLEMENT RATEPAYERS' MEETING

The foreign ratepayers of the Settlement
yesterday held their annual meeting at the Grand Theatre.
It will be recalled that last month there were no municipal
elections, the number of candidates being equal to the
number of seats. Only Messrs. Porter, Urabe and Yamamoto,
outgoing councillors, figure on the list for 1937 which
has been passed en bloc in conformity with Article 18
of the Land Regulations. It was thought at one time,
following the refusal of Messrs. Urabe and Yamamoto to
renew their candidature under divers pretexts which brought
forth the fire of the Japanese press against the municipal
authorities, that the electoral battle would be violent
and the ratepayers' meeting a stormy one.
But, as by a miracle, all passed off in order.
The elections took the form of a mere communique which
the S.M.C. remitted to the Press on March 26th. Yester-
day's meeting was as flat and depressed as one could wish,
not to say boring in the extreme.
Last year, the fate of the Municipal Orchestra
was in the balance. All those, and they are numerous, to
whom the Sunday concerts are a real artistic joy, wished
to retain the musicians. Rarely in the memory of the
ratepayers had there been such a controversy. The letters,
literary and humorous, which appeared in the columns of
our English contemporaries, kindled the sacred fire among
the justly enthusiastic melomaniacs. And at zero hour
the Grand Theatre was stormed by a crowd who had forgotten
the world crisis and the budgetary difficulties of the
Settlement:
At yesterday's meeting a report was read on the
financial and economic standing of the Settlement for the
year 1936. There is no doubt that the depression which is
still being felt in Shanghai has affected the income of
the Council. In spite of the economies effected last year
by the S.M.C., there is a large budgetary deficit which
cannot be allowed to accumulate at any price.
Shanghai knew good times up to the end of 1931.
In 1929 commerce and industry were flourishing. The S.M.C.
then sold to the Shanghai Power Company its electricity
department for the sum of 81 million dollars which was
placed in the reserve fund. The Municipality was rich and
knew it. In a fit of generosity, the chairman of the
ratepayers' meeting proposed to reduce the Rate from 16
to 14 per cent. Needless to say this motion was adopted
unanimously.
The incidents of 1932 which for several months
completely deranged affairs in Shanghai aggravated still
more the depression which, after passing through America
and Europe, hit China with full force.
But the reserve funds were still intact. The
Municipal Council was able to face the storm. And,
according to Mr. Arnhold, the outgoing chairman, the budget's
equilibrium has been maintained since 1929 by the aid of
these 81 millions.

《上海日报》（Le Journal de Shanghai）于4月15日发表了以下社论：

租界纳税人会议

租界的外籍纳税人昨日在大光明大戏院举行了年度会议。回想上月，并未举行市政选举，因为候选人数与席位数量相等。只有波特（Porter）、浦边（Urabe）和山本（Yamamoto）三位离任董事出现在1937年的名单上，该名单已根据《土地章程》第18条整体通过。曾有一段时间，鉴于浦边和山本先生以各种借口拒绝再次参选，引发了日本报刊对市政当局的猛烈抨击，人们以为选举战将会激烈，纳税人会议也将充满风暴。

但是，仿佛奇迹一般，一切井然有序地过去了。选举仅仅表现为工部局于3月26日向新闻界发布的一份公报。昨日的会议平淡且压抑至极，甚至可以说极其无聊。

去年，工部局乐队的命运悬而未决。所有那些——为数众多——将周日音乐会视为真正艺术享受的人都希望留住音乐家。在纳税人的记忆中，很少有过如此激烈的争论。刊登在我们英文同行报刊专栏中的那些富有文学性和幽默感的信件，点燃了那些热情正当的音乐爱好者心中的神圣之火。在关键时刻，大光明大戏院被人群涌入，这些人忘记了世界危机和租界的预算困难：

在昨日的会议上，宣读了一份关于租界1936年财政和经济状况的报告。毫无疑问，上海目前仍在感受到的萧条影响了工部局的收入。尽管工部局去年实行了节约措施，但仍存在巨大的预算赤字，无论如何都不能让其累积。

上海的好日子一直持续到1931年底。1929年，工商业繁荣。当时，工部局将其电气处以8,100万美元的价格出售给上海电力公司，这笔款项被存入储备基金。市政当局很富有，并且对此心知肚明。在一阵慷慨冲动中，纳税人会议主席提议将捐税率从16%降至14%。不用说，这项动议一致通过。

1932年的事件使上海的事务在数月内完全混乱，进一步加剧了萧条，这场萧条在席卷美国和欧洲后，全力冲击了中国。

但储备基金依然完好无损。工部局得以应对风暴。而且，据离任主席安诺德先生称，自1929年以来，正是依靠这8,100万美元的帮助，才维持了预算平衡。

April 16, 1937. Morning Translation.

It is obvious that, under these conditions, the reserve funds have been considerably reduced.
The S.M.C. realizes without doubt that the rate-payers are not going to be taxed without mercy. But it must balance its budget without disbanding its last line of defence, of which it may have need in extraordinary and unforeseen circumstances.
Expenses last year were cut down to the limit, and to assure the normal working of the administrative machine and at the same time to maintain order in the Settlement, it is impossible to-day to reduce any further the salaries of the heads of departments and other employees. One has seen recently the violent controversy caused by the sad cuts made in the pay of the municipal personnel.
It was in these conditions that Mr. Arnhold proposed to raise the rate from 14 to 16 per cent and the tax from 0.7 to 0.8 per cent from 1st July next.
This increase would bring the Council $1,258,000 more revenue and it would be equivalent to an extra charge of one dollar on each ratepayer.
During the last few days there has been great opposition from the Chinese ratepayers, comparable to that in 1927 when the rate was raised from 14 to 16 per cent.
Incidents were feared, and the new councillors searched for a compromise. The increase will now not take place until 1st January 1938. In the meantime the S.M.C. is authorised to meet its obligations by dipping still further into the reserve fund. If conditions improve, as is hoped, the new municipal tax should not lead to serious opposition. But, if no improvement develops, the risk will be considerable. But the S.M.C., under the burden of necessity, will no longer hesitate to proclaim that the ratepayers must be taxed to a degree commensurate with the administrative and financial security of the Settlement.

显而易见，在这种情况下，储备基金已大幅减少。
工部局无疑意识到，纳税人不会接受无情的征税。但它必须在不解散其最后一道防线的情况下平衡预算，因为在特殊和不可预见的情况下，它可能需要这道防线。
去年的开支已削减至极限，为了确保行政机器的正常运转，同时维持租界秩序，今天已不可能进一步降低各部门主管和其他雇员的薪水。人们最近看到了因市政人员薪资悲惨削减而引发的激烈争议。

正是在这种情况下，安诺德先生提议从明年7月1日起，将捐税率从14%提高到16%，将市政税从0.7%提高到0.8%。
这一增加将为工部局带来1,258,000美元的额外收入，相当于每位纳税人额外承担一美元的费用。
在过去几天里，中国纳税人强烈反对，其程度可与1927年捐税率从14%提高到16%时的反对相比。
人们担心会发生事变，新任董事们寻求妥协方案。现在，增税将推迟至1938年1月1日实施。与此同时，授权工部局通过进一步动用储备基金来履行其义务。如果情况如所愿改善，新的市政税不应导致严重的反对。但是，如果情况没有改善，风险将是巨大的。但在必要性的重压下，工部局将不再犹豫，宣布必须对纳税人征收与租界行政和财政安全相称程度的税款。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, APRIL 15, 1937

Barr Hits Council's
School Policy At
Convention

S. M. C. SAID
LOOKING BACKWARD

Education Of Children
Seen As Moral Duty
Of Administration

Sounding the keynote of an issue which is likely to dominate the activities of the Shanghai Municipal Council this year, Mr. J. S. Barr of the Medhurst College criticised, in a speech before the Foreign Rate-payers' Meeting yesterday, the report of the Special Committee on Education, which had recently recommended the handing over of Settlement foreign schools to national groups.

In essence, Mr. Barr said that the Committee's recommendation, motivated by the Council's desire for stringent economy, embodies a "backward-looking spirit." He pointed out that if the various foreign schools were handed over to national groups, the Council would be shirking from its own responsibility.

Mr. Barr's attack on the proposed change in the Council's educational policy was directed toward a report recently made public in which it was stated that the S.M.C. should reiterate the basic principle on school systems as set forth in the 1922 report.

This 1922 policy embodies three main points: namely, that the Council does not intend to assume the responsibility of educating all children in the Settlement that by the Land Regulations the Council is not compelled or obligated to educate children and that the Council has only a moral obligation to spend public money to operate schools.

Implicit Function

Using these points of the 1922 report as a basis, the Special Committee report recommended that measures should be devised whereby national groups might assume a greater responsibility for education, and that a more equitable distribution of grants-in-aid to school be provided. It also proposed that the majority of Council foreign schools should be handed over to the national groups, leaving only two schools for children of unorganized national residents.

In criticising the basic principle of the Committee's report yesterday, Mr. Barr pointed out that while the primary function of the Council is to maintain law and order and to govern, it is also the duty of the Council to serve the community living within its territorial jurisdiction. Education, he continued, is therefore an implicit function which it should carry out.

"Undoubtedly finance is an all-important factor, but if we spend too little on education today we shall probably rue it in the future. If we had municipal provision for more education instead of less....in the long run we would probably find that we were saving money in the budget....because we had produced good citizens."

Chinese Angle Cited

Touching on the status of Chinese S.M.C. schools, Mr. Barr pointed out that if the proposed principle in the Committee's report is carried into effect, it will have a definite bearing on Chinese education.

This important connection between the recommendation and the Chinese educational facilities in the Settlement, Mr. Barr said, is neglected and under-emphasised by the report.

Mr. Barr referred to Mr. Justice Feetham's report regarding the need of future development of educational facilities for the Chinese, pointing out that the question can be better solved by a closer co-operation among the administrative authorities of the three municipalities.

Up To Ratepayers

Before concluding his speech, Mr. Barr said that in his opinion the selection of the members of the Special Committee on Education by the Chairman of the Council was badly handled. He averred that experts should be included in the committee to study a question on policy of such importance.

He asked the Council to give an assurance that before any drastic change was made in educational policy, the question be submitted to the approval of the ratepayers.

In replying to his question, Mr. H. E. Arnhold, the outgoing chairman, pointed out that the recommendations and the entire educational problem are now in the hands of the new Council and that he is in no position to give assurance as to what that new governing body will do. However, he said, educational policy will be treated carefully by the new Council.

Mr. Barr's criticism of the Committee recommendation yesterday brought to the fore a question which is likely to become one of the political footballs of Settlement affairs during 1937 and 1938. The Committee's proposals for handing over municipal schools to national groups are in essence similar to the chief points of a campaign conducted on the subject by the local Japanese residents.

Others Nationals Silent

Other national groups have not yet made any official comment on the subject. It remains to be seen whether the recommendation for the Council to abdicate from educational affairs of the Settlement will be acceptable to the leading foreign residents of the city.

Meantime, the Chinese ratepayers are also watching closely which way the Council's education is likely to turn. It was indicated that the Chinese ratepayers are against the national group idea and that they believe as soon as foreign schools are placed on that basis, the Chinese schools will follow suit. At present, however, the Chinese ratepayers are too engrossed by their campaign against the Council's spending policy to have much time to start a drive on the educational plank.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1937年4月15日，星期四

巴尔在纳税人大会上抨击
工部局学校政策

工部局被指
目光短浅

视儿童教育为
行政当局之道德义务

麦赫斯特学院（Medhurst College）的J. S. 巴尔先生（Mr. J. S. Barr）在昨日的外国纳税人大会上发表演讲，对教育特别委员会的报告提出批评。该报告最近建议将租界内的外国学校移交给各国侨民团体管理。巴尔先生的发言为本年度可能主导上海公共租界工部局活动的一个议题定下了基调。

巴尔先生指出，该委员会的建议本质上是出于工部局厉行节约的愿望，体现了一种“向后看的精神”。他指出，如果将各所外国学校移交给各国侨民团体，工部局便是在推卸自身的责任。

巴尔先生对工部局拟议的教育政策变更的抨击，针对的是最近公布的一份报告。该报告称，工部局应重申1922年报告中关于学校制度的基本原则。

这一1922年的政策包含三个要点：即工部局不打算承担教育租界内所有儿童的责任；根据《土地章程》，工部局并无强制或义务去教育儿童；工部局仅负有动用公款办学的道德义务。

隐含职能

特别委员会的报告以1922年报告的这些要点为基础，建议制定措施，让各国侨民团体承担更多的教育责任，并提供更公平的学校补助金分配方案。报告还提议，应将工部局所属的大部分外国学校移交给各国侨民团体，仅保留两所学校供无组织之各国侨民子女就读。

在昨日批评委员会报告的基本原则时，巴尔先生指出，虽然工部局的主要职能是维持治安和管理行政，但其也有义务服务于其管辖区域内的社区。他接着说，因此，教育是其应履行的一项隐含职能。

“毫无疑问，财政是一个至关重要的因素，但如果我们今天在教育上投入太少，将来可能会后悔。如果我们市政当局提供更多而非更少的教育设施……从长远来看，我们可能会发现我们在预算上节省了资金……因为我们培养出了良好的公民。”

提及华人角度

谈及工部局所属华校的地位时，巴尔先生指出，如果实施委员会报告中提出的原则，将对华人教育产生明确的影响。

巴尔先生说，报告忽视并低估了这一建议与租界内华人教育设施之间的重要联系。

巴尔先生提到了费瑟姆法官（Judge Feetham）关于未来需要发展华人教育设施的报告，指出通过三个市政当局行政机构之间的更紧密合作，可以更好地解决这一问题。

取决于纳税人

在结束演讲前，巴尔先生说，他认为由工部局主席挑选教育特别委员会成员的做法处理不当。他断言，委员会中应包括专家，以研究如此重要的政策问题。

他要求工部局保证，在对教育政策进行任何重大变更之前，应将此问题提交纳税人批准。

在回答他的提问时，即将离任的主席H. E. 安诺德先生（Mr. H. E. Arnhold）指出，各项建议及整个教育问题现在掌握在新任工部局手中，他无法就新管理机构将采取何种行动做出保证。然而，他说，新任工部局将慎重处理教育政策。

巴尔先生昨日对委员会建议的批评，使一个可能在1937年和1938年成为租界事务政治皮球的问题浮出水面。委员会关于将市立学校移交给各国侨民团体的提议，本质上与当地日本居民就此主题开展的运动的主要观点相似。

其他国籍人士保持沉默

其他各国侨民团体尚未就此问题发表任何官方评论。工部局放弃租界教育事务的建议是否能被本市主要外籍居民接受，仍有待观察。

与此同时，中国纳税人也在密切关注工部局教育政策的可能走向。有迹象表明，中国纳税人反对“各国侨民团体”这一构想，他们认为一旦外国学校以此为基础运作，华校也将效仿。然而，目前中国纳税人正全神贯注于反对工部局开支政策的运动，无暇发起关于教育纲领的运动。

Afternoon Translation

Sin Wan Pao :-

ANNUAL MEETING OF FOREIGN RATEPAYERS

The apparently dignified Annual Meeting of Foreign Ratepayers in the International Settlement was held between 2.36 and 3.40 p.m. yesterday (April 14) in a manner much resembling a humourous play, in the course of which one man on the stage proposed a resolution, another stood up to explain it, a third seconded it, while finally the attendance signified their approval by raising their hands.

The venue of this meeting was the Grand Theatre on Bubbling Well Road, outside which and across the road there was a banner inscribed with the words "Annual Meeting of Foreign Ratepayers." In and around the theatre there were a great number of foreign policemen, but only between 100 and 200 foreign ratepayers were present.

Not one Chinese councillor was to be found on the stage. Judge Mossop of the British Supreme Court occupied the chair. Mr. Arnhold as Chairman of the Council sat right in front of the chairman of the meeting so as to give explanation on any subject if required. The silver-headed Secretary-General, Mr. Fessenden, sat on the left of Mr. Arnhold; he was silent throughout the meeting. In addition, there were five other foreign councillors and the Secretary of the Council.

Right below the stage were the seats reserved for the Press which was represented by about ten foreign and four Chinese reporters. In spite of the grave atmosphere prevailing over the meeting, these gentlemen of the Press laughed with each other at the sight of the drama being mechanically performed on the stage.

The whole drama centred around Judge Mossop, Mr. Arnhold and Mr. Franklin.

When the resolution for an increase in the tax for the purpose of enabling the Council to balance its Budget was proposed, a foreign ratepayer named Mr. King took his stand on the stage and moved the following amendment :-
"That the increases in Land Tax, General Municipal
"Rate and Special Rate shall take effect as from
"January 1, 1938, and that the Council be authorized
"to take such measures for the balancing of the
"Budget as may be necessary in respect of a resulting
"shortage of approximately $1,258,000, either by an
"additional appropriation from reserve or by such
"further economies as may be possible, or both."

The amendment was unanimously carried because it was considered to be the most suitable way of appeasing the opposition. This matter was settled in a few minutes and marked the victory of the opposition raised by the Chinese ratepayers from the Chinese councillors down to the poorest residents. However, we must not be satisfied with this victory. We must make a greater effort in conjunction with our government and we must struggle for the abolition of consular jurisdiction, rendition of settlements and recovery of all lost territory. Long live the Chinese Republic!

下午译文

《新闻报》：

国际租界外国纳税人年会

国际租界外国纳税人年会表面上庄重严肃，实则于昨日（4月14日）下午2时36分至3时40分之间举行，其过程颇似一出幽默剧。期间，台上一人提出决议案，另一人起立解释，第三人附议，最后出席者以举手方式表示赞成。

会议地点位于静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的大光明大戏院（Grand Theatre）。戏院外及马路对面悬挂着写有“外国纳税人年会”字样的横幅。戏院内外有大量外籍警察，但出席的外国纳税人仅在100至200人之间。

台上未见一名华董。英国最高法院莫索普法官（Judge Mossop）担任主席。工部局主席安诺德先生（Mr. Arnhold）坐在会议主席正前方，以便在需要时就任何议题作出解释。白发苍苍的总办费森登先生（Mr. Fessenden）坐在安诺德先生左侧；他在整个会议期间保持沉默。此外，还有另外五名外籍董事和工部局秘书在场。

舞台正下方是为记者预留的座位，约有十名外籍记者和四名华籍记者出席。尽管会议气氛严肃，但这些记者看到台上机械地上演这出戏剧时，彼此相视而笑。

整出戏剧围绕莫索普法官、安诺德先生和富兰克林先生（Mr. Franklin）展开。

当提出增加税收以使工部局平衡预算的决议案时，一位名叫金先生（Mr. King）的外国纳税人上台提出了以下修正案：
“土地税、一般市政捐及特别捐的增加应自1938年1月1日起生效，并授权工部局采取必要措施，通过从储备金中追加拨款或实行进一步可能的节约措施，或两者兼施，以弥补由此产生的约1,258,000元的短缺，从而平衡预算。”

该修正案一致通过，因为它被视为平息反对意见的最合适方式。此事在几分钟内得以解决，标志着从华董到最贫困居民的中国纳税人所提出的反对取得了胜利。然而，我们不能满足于这一胜利。我们必须与我国政府共同努力，必须为废除领事裁判权、交还租界及收复所有失地而奋斗。中华民国万岁！

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY.
Afternoon Annotations
Date / /
Shanghai Public Daily News (市民日報) publishes the
following editorial comment :-

At the annual meeting of foreign ratepayers
in the International Settlement held on April 14, a
resolution was passed that the Municipal Rate be increased
as from January 1, 1938.
Following the approval by the S.M.C. of the
recommendation for an increase in the Municipal Rate,
various public bodies and residents in the Settlement
unanimously voiced their opposition. The Chinese
Ratepayers' Association held a meeting of representatives
on April 12 when it was decided that the subject concerning
the proposal by the S.M.C. to increase the Municipal Rate
from July 1, 1937 be postponed to 1938 for further
discussion and that the S.M.C. be ordered to exercise
practical economy towards all unnecessary expenses and
to press for unpaid rates.
The intention of the Chinese Ratepayers'
Association is very clear and in its opinion there is
no ground to discuss an increase in the Municipal Rate
since local commercial conditions have not returned to
normal and since the S.M.C. has not done its utmost in
economizing in its expenses. If the Council respects
the opinions of the Chinese Ratepayers' Association and
introduces practical economy by rescinding all lavish
expenditure, it can balance its budget without increasing
the rates.
The annual meeting of foreign ratepayers paid
no heed to public opinion and disregarded the intentions
of 95% of the whole population of the Settlement. It
eventually authorized the Council to raise funds to cover
special expenses and also approved the proposed increase
in the Municipal Rate from January 1, 1938. This surprises
us. The impression in the minds of the Chinese residents
that the meeting of foreign ratepayers is becoming a
puppet organization of the S.M.C. is increasing daily.
It seems that the meeting instigates the Council to impose
upon the ratepayers.
"We believe that the present financial
difficulties of the Council are the general results of
its lavish expenditure over many years" is the word of
warning contained in the open letter of the Chinese
Ratepayers' Association addressed to the foreign ratepayers.
Not only does it point out the cause of the poor financial
condition of the S.M.C., but it also tells us of ways and
means to be adopted hereafter to deal with the unreasonable
"squeezing" by the Council. Since the meeting of the
foreign ratepayers has passed the increase in the Municipal
Rate, we can only turn down its decision on January 1, 1938
as a reply to Mr. Arnhold, Chairman of the Council, and
those who suggested the increase.

Lih Pao (comment) :-

We cannot agree to a mere delay of six months
in the enforcement of the increase in Municipal Rate.
We are of the opinion that if the Council would
only cut down its expenses wholeheartedly, there would be no
necessity to increase the rate at all.
We are also of the opinion that if the Council
would seriously demand payment of outstanding rates from the
subjects of a certain nation, there would also be no neces-
sity to increase the rate.

工部局登记处。
下午注释
日期 / /
《市民日报》刊登如下社论：

在4月14日举行的国际租界外国纳税人年会上，通过了一项决议，规定自1938年1月1日起增加市政捐。

继工部局批准增加市政捐的建议后，租界内各公共团体及居民一致表示反对。中国纳税人协会于4月12日召开代表会议，决定将有关工部局提议自1937年7月1日起增加市政捐的事项推迟至1938年再行讨论，并责令工部局对所有不必要的开支实行切实的节约，并催缴欠款。

中国纳税人协会的意图非常明确，其认为，鉴于当地商业状况尚未恢复正常，且工部局未在节约开支方面竭尽全力，因此没有理由讨论增加市政捐。如果工部局尊重中国纳税人协会的意见，通过取消所有奢侈支出来实行切实的节约，它可以在不增加捐税的情况下平衡预算。

外国纳税人年会无视舆论， disregarding 租界总人口95%的意愿。它最终授权工部局筹集资金以支付特别费用，并批准了自1938年1月1日起增加市政捐的提议。这令我们感到惊讶。中国居民心中认为外国纳税人年会正日益成为工部局的傀儡组织的印象与日俱增。看来，该会议正在煽动工部局向纳税人施加压力。

“我们认为，工部局目前的财政困难是其多年来奢侈支出的普遍结果”，这是中国纳税人协会致外国纳税人的公开信中包含的警告之语。这不仅指出了工部局财务状况不佳的原因，也告诉了我们今后应对工部局不合理“压榨”的方法和手段。既然外国纳税人年会已通过增加市政捐，我们只能以在1938年1月1日拒绝执行其决定，作为对工部局主席安诺德先生及那些建议增税者的回应。

《立报》（评论）：

我们不能同意仅仅将市政捐增加的实施推迟六个月。
我们认为，如果工部局能真心实意地削减开支，就根本无需增加捐税。
我们也认为，如果工部局认真向某国臣民追缴拖欠的捐税，也就无需增加捐税。

April 15, 1937.
Afternoon Translation:

MAINICHI

FOREIGN RATEPAYERS' MEETING ACCEPTS MUNICIPAL
BUDGET

The Mainichi publishes the
following leading article:-
The foreign ratepayers' meeting
of the International Settlement was held at the Grand
Theatre at 2.40 p.m. April 14 with an attendance of
only 248 probably due to the fact that the meeting was
held on a week day. The important proposal for an
increase in the Municipal rate has been postponed for
six months and there were no interesting resolutions
passed.
Mr. Arnhold, Chairman of the
Council, delivered a speech lasting 20 minutes reporting
on Municipal affairs. The ratepayers accepted the
huge budget of $24,000,000, satisfying themselves with
the explanation of the chairman to the effect that the
deficit of $1,250,000 in the Municipal budget will be
met by a part of the Municipal reserve fund and money
saved through further economy measures.
In the course of his speech,
Mr. Arnhold gave an explanation to the effect that a
city in Great Britain which has a population equal to
that of Shanghai imposes a rate of 64% upon its rate-
payers and the rate paid by Shanghai residents is very
small in comparison.
Mr. Arnhold's explanation
simply exposed his ignorance regarding the circumstances
of Shanghai residents and the wrong idea of the British
people regarding the International Settlement. We are
opposed to such an attitude and we hope to have a real
international administrative organization which
distributes suffrage among residents properly and
carries out administration in the interests of all the
citizens.
The British police officers,
who draw large salaries from the S.M.C. are engaged
to protect British interests and enterprises conducted
with British capital. For instance, the British
Consulate-General has a court, but no police officers,
while the Japanese Consulate-General employs a large
number of policemen. The British Government freely
uses the British police officers of the S.M.C. The
British police officers draw higher salaries and occupy
higher position than other nationals. They are paid
with the money collected from the residents in the
International Settlement and a large number of other
British residents are making their living in the S.I.C.
We must first consider whether
every national in the International Settlement receives
equal benefit from the S.M.C. British administrative
policy cannot be applied here as the characteristics of
the Shanghai Municipal organization are quite different
from those of Great Britain. The S.M.C. will be
regarded as an organization formed for the purpose of
advancing British interests unless a proper administration
is introduced by the S.M.C.
We hope that the S.M.C. will
do its best for all the residents.

《每日新闻》

外侨纳税人大会通过市政预算

《每日新闻》发表以下社论：——
国际公共租界的外侨纳税人大会于4月14日下午2时40分在大光明大戏院举行，出席者仅248人，这可能是因为会议在工作日举行。关于增加市政捐税的重要提案已推迟六个月，会上未通过任何引人注目的决议。
工部局董事会主席阿诺德（Arnhold）先生发表了长达20分钟的演讲，报告市政事务。纳税人接受了高达2,400万美元的巨额预算，他们对主席的解释感到满意，即市政预算中125万美元的赤字将由部分市政储备基金以及通过进一步节约措施省下的资金来弥补。
在演讲过程中，阿诺德先生解释说，英国一个人口与上海相当的城市向其纳税人征收64%的捐税，相比之下，上海居民缴纳的捐税非常少。
阿诺德先生的解释仅仅暴露了他对上海居民状况的无知，以及英国人对国际公共租界的错误观念。我们反对这种态度，我们希望有一个真正的国际行政机构，在居民中适当分配选举权，并为所有市民的利益实施行政管理。
从工部局领取高薪的英国警官受雇保护英国的利益和以英国资本经营的企业。例如，英国总领事馆设有法庭，但没有警官，而日本总领事馆则雇用大量警察。英国政府随意使用工部局的英国警官。英国警官的薪俸高于其他国籍人士，职位也更高。他们的薪水是用从国际公共租界居民那里收取的钱支付的，还有许多其他英国居民靠工部局谋生。
我们必须首先考虑国际公共租界的每个国民是否都从工部局获得平等的利益。英国的行政政策不能在此适用，因为上海市政组织的特征与英国截然不同。除非工部局实行适当的行政管理，否则它将被视为一个旨在推进英国利益的组织。
我们希望工部局为所有居民尽力而为。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, March 22, 1937

Chit To “Samurai”
“SAMURAI,” writing in the Shipping Review, wants to know how taipans can represent the small or non-salaried man on the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Dear Samurai: Don’t be silly. Taipans do not represent the small or non-salaried man. So far as we are aware they make no pretense of so doing. Shanghai is oligarchic, not democratic. Why should anyone say or think otherwise? The system may be outmoded and it may be wrong. But the system functions beautifully within its own natural limits; a true proof of how smooth-running a bit of fine old machinery can be if the proper oil is regularly applied.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 17, 1937

JAPANESE MEMBERS
OF COUNCIL
Final Effort To Induce
Urabe And Yamamoto
To Run

Assembled in an emergency meeting, 37 of the 40 newly-elected members of the Council of the Japanese Residents' Corporation yesterday afternoon unanimously adopted a resolution urging Mr. Takue Urabe and Mr. Takeo Yamamoto, official Japanese nominees for the Municipal Council, to reconsider their decision not to seek re-election.
This was interpreted by the local Japanese press as representing a final effort of the leaders of the Japanese community to break the 10-day deadlock precipitated by the refusal of Mr. Urabe and Mr. Yamamoto to run.
Mr. Masusaburo Amano, President of the Residents' Corporation, and Mr. Itsuji Hishida, chairman of the Council, will call on Mr. Yamamoto and Mr. Urabe to inform them of yesterday's resolution, the Japanese press said.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1937年3月17日，星期三

工部局
日本董事
促使浦边和山本
参选的最后努力

日本居留民团董事会新当选的40名成员中有37人昨天下午召开紧急会议，一致通过一项决议，敦促工部局日本官方提名人浦边卓（Takue Urabe）先生和山本武雄（Takeo Yamamoto）先生重新考虑其不寻求连任的决定。
当地日文报纸将此解读为日本社区领导人为打破因浦边先生和山本先生拒绝参选而导致的为期10天的僵局所做的最后努力。
日文报纸称，居留民团总裁天野增三郎（Masusaburo Amano）先生和董事会主席菱田伊次（Itsuji Hishida）先生将拜访山本先生和浦边先生，向他们通报昨天的决议。

March 17, 1937.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE CANDIDATES FOR MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS

At 12.30 p.m. yesterday the
Councillors of the Japanese Residents' Corporation held
a meeting at the Japanese Club to consider the nomination
of Japanese candidates for the Municipal elections. The
meeting decided to endeavour to persuade Mr. Yamamoto and
Mr. Urabe to change their minds and accept the nomination.

At 3 p.m. Mr. Amano, Chairman
of the Corporation, and Mr. Hishida called on Mr. Kawai,
Japanese Consul-General, reported the result of the
meeting and requested him to persuade Mr. Yamamoto and
Mr. Urabe to accept the nomination.

In reply Mr. Kawai informed
them that he would do his best to carry out their wishes.

Five British
Candidates In

ONLY ONE COUNCILLOR
SEEKS RE-ELECTION

Porter, MacDonald, Killery,
Matthews And King Are
To Face Voters

As the result of the straw
vote conducted by the British
Residents' Association during
the past week it was announc-
ed yesterday that five British
candidates for the 1937 Shang-
hai Municipal Council had been
chosen by popular vote. Of
the five selected British
nominees only one is at present
a Councillor, the other four
incumbents having decided not
to offer themselves for re-
election for various reasons.

The five British residents who
will offer themselves for election
by Settlement ratepayers on April
5 and 6 are:
Mr. V. St. J. Killery, Imperial
Chemical Industries (China), Ltd.
Mr. W. S. King, Messrs. Harrisons,
King and Irwin, Ltd.
Mr. R. G. MacDonald, Messrs. Dod-
well and Co., Ltd.
Mr. F. N. Matthews, Messrs. Lowe,
Bingham and Matthews.
Mr. Harold Porter, C.M.G., former-
ly H.B.M. Consular Service in China.
The five residents who offered
themselves for selection by mem-
bers of the British Residents' As-
sociation and who failed to qualify
were:
Mr. Ernest F. Harris, Sun Life In-
surance Company of Canada.
Mr. S. C. Miskin Asiatic Petroleum
Company (North China), Ltd.
Mr. H. A. Et 's, Messrs. Ellis and
Hays.
Mr. F. R. Smith, Metropolitan Land
Company, Limited; International
Assurance Company, Limited.

Only One Incumbent

Of the five candidates who are
running on the British ticket Mr.
Harold Porter is a member of the
present Council and Mr. Killery
has previously held office. The re-
maining three, although well known
here as prominent businessmen
with considerable experience in
many civic movements, are all
newcomers to the Municipal field.

The vote in the Ballot represent-
ed 70 per cent. of the number of
papers sent out.
British members of the Muni-
cipal Council who are not seeking
re-election are: Messrs. E. H. Arn-
hold, W. J. Keswick, G. E. Mitchell
and Brig.-General E. B. Macnaghten.
Everything at the present time
tends to the belief that a ballot
will not be necessary this year as
the present ratio of American,
British and Japanese candidates is
expected to be maintained. Al-
though there is still some uncer-
tainty regarding the Japanese re-
presentatives, it has been indicated
that they will only seek to main-
tain their present two seats. The
American community has already
announced their two candidates,
namely, Messrs. C. S. Franklin, a
sitting member, and W. H. Plant,
a newco r.

Scrutineers Named

Messrs. H. C. A. van Someren, of
the Java Sea and Fire Insurance
Co., Ltd., and H. S. Poulsen, Gen-
eral Manager of the Great North-
ern Telegraph Co., Ltd., have ac-
cepted invitations from the Muni-
cipal Council to serve as scruti-
neers at the election of foreign mem-
bers of the Council for the muni-
cipal year 1937.
The dates of the election are
Monday and Tuesday, April 5 and
6. The closing date for nominations
is March 27 at noon when it will
be known whether an election will
be necessary or not.

1937年选举中的
五名英国
候选人

九名提名人中经
模拟投票选出
五人组合

仅有一名董事
寻求连任

波特、麦克唐纳、基勒里、
马修斯和金将
面对选民

鉴于英国居留民团在过去一周进行的模拟投票结果，昨日宣布，通过普选选出了五名1937年上海工部局董事会的英国候选人。在五名获选的英国提名人中，目前只有一人是现任董事，其他四名现任董事因各种原因决定不寻求连任。
将于4月5日和6日由租界纳税人选举的五名英国居民是：
V. St. J. 基勒里（Killery）先生，帝国化学工业（中国）有限公司。
W. S. 金（King）先生，哈里森、金和欧文有限公司。
R. G. 麦克唐纳（MacDonald）先生，多德韦尔有限公司。
F. N. 马修斯（Matthews）先生，洛、宾厄姆和马修斯公司。
哈罗德·波特（Harold Porter）先生，C.M.G.，前英国驻华领事馆人员。
向英国居留民团成员自荐参选但未获资格的 five 名居民是：
欧内斯特·F. 哈里斯（Ernest F. Harris）先生，加拿大太阳人寿保险公司。
S. C. 米斯基恩（Miskin）先生，亚细亚火油公司（华北）有限公司。
H. A. Et 's 先生，埃利斯和海斯公司。（原文不清）
F. R. 史密斯（Smith）先生，大都会地产有限公司；国际保险有限公司。

仅有一名现任者

在英国阵营参选的五名候选人中，哈罗德·波特先生是现任董事会成员，基勒里先生此前曾任职。其余三人虽然作为知名商人在此间广为人知，并在许多市政运动中拥有丰富经验，但都是市政领域的新人。
投票箱中的选票代表了发出选票总数的70%。
不寻求连任的工部局英国董事有：E. H. 阿诺德（Arnhold）先生、W. J. 凯思威克（Keswick）先生、G. E. 米切尔（Mitchell）先生和E. B. 麦克纳格滕（Macnaghten）准将。
目前的一切迹象都使人相信，今年无需进行投票选举，因为预计美国、英国和日本候选人的现有比例将得以维持。虽然日本代表方面仍存在一些不确定性，但已有迹象表明，他们将只力求保持现有的两个席位。美国社区已宣布其两名候选人，即现任成员C. S. 富兰克林（Franklin）先生和新成员W. H. 普兰特（Plant）先生。

指定监票人

爪哇海火灾保险公司有限公司的H. C. A. 范·索默伦（van Someren）先生和大北电报有限公司总经理H. S. 波尔森（Poulsen）先生已接受工部局的邀请，担任1937市政年度工部局外籍董事选举的监票人。
选举日期为4月5日（星期一）和6日（星期二）。提名截止日期为3月27日中午，届时将知晓是否需要进行选举。

The time of the election of the Shanghai 
Municipal Council is approaching. 

the “city fathers" are already agitated and 
worried by the question of whether or not they will 
remain at the helm for another year and keep their 
comfortable and lucrative positions. The new British

They will need you at the time of elections

You want proof? Here are a few facts both 
from the recent past and from the present time, to 
recall which would not be out of place :- 

Following the conclusion of the civil war in 
Russia, White Russians sought refuge in Shanghai. 
The Municipal authorities did not allow them te land 
here. Those who succeeded in landing were received

Employers began to engage Russians to do certain 
low paid work and the city fathers authorised the 
recruiting of Russian policemen and the formation of 
Russian Volunteer Regiment. On the face of it one 
would think that they did so solely in the interests 
of Russians and not in their own interests. However, 
this was not the case. 

Russians were engaged to work in factories and 
offices because reliable and efficient workers were 
required, tovhom it was necessary to pay only a little 
more than one had to pay Chinese. In the Police, 
Russians were required to deal with Russian affairs, 
which the guardians of law, being unfamiliar with the 
Russian language, were unable to handle. However, 
having engaged Russians to fill the lower positions, 
representatives of perfidious Albion did not promote 
them above the rank of Sergeant or, at the most, above 
the rank of Sub-Inspector. 

Where, then, is the equal treatment to which 
all residents of Shanghai are supposed to be entitled

Regiment was an act of consideration to Ruesians - 
just to give them some employment? Nothing of that
